*My eyes flicker open.*
*I wake up in the compartment of a train. My head is leaned back against my seat, a strand of drool dripping from the corner of my mouth.*
Atcchan: "Urgh... What...?"
*Wincing, I wipe it away with the back of my hand.*
*Drooling, at my age? That isn't very mature. I thought I stopped doing that when I was a kid.*
*I need to get it together. Act more like an adult. That's what I keep telling myself, but... it never seems to work out.*
*That's partially why I decided to take this trip alone. This isn't some kind of crazy, coming of age, 'quest for maturity' kind of adventure, though.*
*I'm not going to go to far-off lands and slay dragons, or pull swords from stones or anything. I doubt I could do that even if I tried.*
*I'm just going to visit my grandparents, who live all the way out in the countryside. That's all.*
*Still... I think it'll be nice, going back home. I've only been away for two years, but it almost feels like a whole lifetime.*
*I wonder if anything will be different. Two years might seem like a short amount of time - miniscule when you consider how old the Earth is - but a lot of things can change over a period of only a few days, let alone years.*
*I hope Amu's okay. It'll be strange seeing her face again. She sent me some photographs, but a photo isn't the same as seeing a person in real life.*
*And, I wonder...*
*...*
*I lean my head against the window, staring outside. The rough movement of the train jerks my head against the glass, bumping my forehead and knocking my teeth together so they chatter, but I disregard it.*
*I can see fields, dyed dark blue under the evening sky.*
*I'm not in the city anymore. I'm far away from my new house, my new school, my new friends. Saki, Miho, and Yuuna.*
*What are they doing right now?*
*Saki, with her love of  horror stories. Miho, who always scores the highest in karaoke. Yuuna, who wears red ribbons in her hair and keeps falling asleep in class.*
*But these idle thoughts soon fade away.*
*I'm going back home. And maybe...*
*Maybe I'll see her.*
*She was always so quiet, never talking to anyone other than me. Will she be any different now? I hope she's at least made a few new friends. If she hasn't, then...*
*Would it be my fault?*
*... No, that's no good. Why am I worrying already? I haven't even made it to the village yet.*
Atcchan: "Stupid."
*I chastise myself, shaking my head in an attempt to dissuade my steadily mounting feelings of guilt. I don't want to ruin my trip before it even begins. But if I did... it wouldn't be too surprising.*
*Maybe I deserve to feel bad.*
*I should have told her.*
*Why didn't I tell her?*
Atcchan: "Because you were scared."
*I mutter this under my breath. It doesn't matter. Nobody can hear me.*
*I'm the only person on the train, after all.*
Grandma: "Darling! Welcome back!"
Grandpa: "It's good to see you again, lad! You want a hand with your luggage?"
*I stand outside the small, dilapidated train station, gripping my single suitcase tight in my hand.*
*Since I'm only going to be here for three days, I didn't bother to pack much. I can make do with only a few pairs of underwear and my pajamas. I don't need anything else.*
*My grandparents are standing before me. They've come to greet me at the station with wide smiles, comforting in their familiarity.*
*Their home is only five minutes away from the station so they didn't need to bring the car. This is probably a good thing.*
*My mother keeps saying my grandfather's eyesight is getting worse and worse. Nowadays he can hardly read the newspaper without the aid of his thick glasses - which he hardly ever wears, given he keeps losing them.*
*And yet he's still allowed to drive a car - something he frequently does (according to my mother) just so he can feel superior to other people...*
*At least this is a fairly rural area so there aren't all that many cars around to hit.*
Atcchan: "You don't need to carry anything, Grandpa. I'm good."
*I return my grandfather's smile and make a show of lifting my suitcase, trying to prove that I can handle it. He, however, seems skeptical.*
Grandpa: "Nonsense! You made all the effort to come out here - and on that blasted train, too! You must be exhausted."
Atcchan: "I'm fine. I'm not a child anymore."
*Grandfather peers at me, frowning. Maybe he's trying to verify the validity of my statement.*
*I wonder if he's forgotten how old I am.*
Grandpa: "Hm? What's this? You still look like a youngster to me!"
Atcchan: "Hey. I am sixteen."
Grandpa: "And I'm older than sixty! The gulf between us is as wide as the Kitakami river!"
*My grandmother giggles.*
Grandma: "Come now, dear, don't be silly. You're getting old and your eyes aren't what they used to be."
Grandpa: "Nonsense! My eyes are just fine, Chiyo!"
Grandma: "And yet you keep wearing that ugly shirt..."
Grandpa: "This shirt isn't ugly! It's very cutting edge, I'll have you know! All the youngsters are wearing them!"
Grandma: "Our dear grandson isn't wearing one."
Grandpa: "To his detriment! It enhances a man's natural charm and shows off his true character!"
Grandma: "It shows he's starting to get senile, perhaps..."
Grandpa: "Chiyo... You can be a very cruel mistress."
Grandma: "Fufufu~ "
Grandma: "Now, don't bully Atcchan too much, you old bore."
Grandpa: "I'm just saying it like I see it, Chiyo! To me, he'll always be a brat!"
Grandma: "On the contrary, I think he's grown up to be rather handsome."
Atcchan: "Handsome...? I don't know about that..."
Grandma: "Well, you know what they say. Good things come in small packages. The way I see it, you're just being modest!"
*I don't know if being short is the same thing as being modest. My lack of height wasn't a conscious decision I made. If anything, I'd like to be a couple of inches taller. That way, I wouldn't get teased so much.*
*Being the shortest boy in your class can be pretty depressing. Nobody likes being picked last when teams are being formed in P.E., and nobody likes being laughed at.*
*Haa...*
Atcchan: "I... I'm not really modest, you know?"
Grandma: "I think you are. You're just proving my point, dear."
Atcchan: "Well..."
Grandma: "Hohoh~ Our Airi has raised you well~ You're such a little gentleman!"
*'Little' being the operative word...*
Grandpa: "He must get it from your side of the family, Chiyo. You've always been tiny, haven't you?"
Grandma: "Yes, yes. I simply have a weak constitution~"
Grandpa: "See? Even though he's two years older now, he's still a runt. I think you should let me carry your case, lad - it's for your own good!"
Atcchan: "No, I'd feel bad. You don't need to put yourself out for me."
*Grandmother grins, beckoning me close. I follow her crooked finger and she leans in towards me, whispering in my ear.*
Grandma: "Don't mind him, dear, he just wants to show off. Let him carry your case. It'll give him something to boast about with the neighbors later."
Atcchan: "Oh... Well, if that's how it is..."
Grandma: "Hohoh~ No matter how old this man gets, he's just a child at heart."
*Grandmother and I laugh together, co-conspirators, before I turn my attention back to my grandfather.*
Atcchan: "All right, I reconsidered. I guess I am a little tired from the journey, so you can carry my case if you want."
Grandpa: "Excellent! I see you talked some sense into him, Chiyo? You used your feminine charms, did you?"
Grandma: "Mmhmm. Even at the age of eighty, I still have it in me. It must be all the homegrown vegetables we eat. They're good for your skin - better than the vegetables at those so-called 'supermarkets.'"
Grandpa: "You got that right! No tomatoes taste as good as yours, Chiyo! Wahaha!"
*As my grandparents laugh together, sounding so carefree, I feel something lift from the pit of my stomach. Could it be anxiety?*
*I started to get worried during my journey here, but... maybe those fears were unfounded. Simply seeing my grandparents has made me feel more at ease.*
*I guess I really do belong here.*
*It's where I was born, after all.*
Grandma: "How was the journey here, darling?"
Atcchan: "It was fine. It took a while, so it was a little tiring, but other than that..."
Grandma: "Yes, yes. It really is a long journey. It's six hours or so, isn't it?"
Atcchan: "Something like that. I had to change a few times, though, and wait around for a while... so maybe it was more like seven."
Grandma: "Seven hours?"
*My grandmother tuts disapprovingly.*
Grandma: "Your poor dear, it must have been dreadful. You need to eat more - here, take this."
Atcchan: "A-Ahaha... T-Thanks..."
*I look at my loaded plate with suspicion. Even though Grandmother said all that stuff about me being grown up and handsome... did she really believe it?*
*If she did, why did she make me so much food? It's almost like she's trying to feed up a starving kitten...*
Atcchan: "There weren't many people on the train, though. For the last two stations, I was the only one. It wasn't too stressful."
Grandpa: "Ah well, this is a very small village. Not many people come up here, and more and more people have been leaving."
Atcchan: "Huh? But why?"
Grandpa: "Because there aren't enough jobs to go around. Means there's no reason to stay. Now, most of what's left here is just us old people."
Grandma: "It's sad really. I don't think I should ever like to leave. It's just so peaceful."
Grandma: "And the green beans that grow in these parts are the best you can find, hohoh~"
Grandpa: "I even hear they're going to discontinue the train line here. Guess it makes sense, since it's hardly ever used, and the current track is getting old."
Atcchan: "Huh. That really is sad..."
*I pick at my dinner despondently.*
*Even though I don't live here anymore... hearing that this village is starting to decline is just a little depressing.*
*All of my childhood memories were created here; every single precious moment of my youth.*
*Going out for walks in the forest... Catching cicadas in the summer with a net and an empty mayonnaise jar... My extravagant and slightly unrealistic plans to build a tree house with Amu, which never managed to become a reality...*
*And... of course, there was her.*
*My best friend.*
*Noelle.*
Saki: "Hey, Atcchan. God, it's been too long."
*Saki's voice, wry and quietly sarcastic as ever, comes through to me from the other end of the phone.*
*The phone in my grandparents' home is fairly old, more of an antique than a fully functional means of communication, and it distorts her voice, just as ripples across water can mar a reflection.*
*Even so, I recognize it. How could I not?*
*That kind of tone could only belong to the Saki I know and (sort of, with a certain amount of fear) love.*
*I smile, shaking my head. She's acting like she hasn't seen me in years.*
Atcchan: "It hasn't been that long. Only a couple of days."
Saki: "But it feels like an eternity. I've been so bored."
*I'm sitting on the floor, cross-legged, the cord of the phone snaked about in my lap. My hair is damp from the bath and my face feels slightly flushed. I think I used a little too much hot water.*
*I've always loved hot baths ever since I was kid, but sometimes I go overboard and emerge from my long soaks on uneasy legs, my skin bright pink and puckered like a prune.*
*I yawn, holding one hand up against my mouth, and shift slightly; balancing the phone against my shoulder, in the crook of my neck.*
Atcchan: "How can you be bored? You have all those brothers and sisters to look after, don't you?"
Saki: "Urgh. Don't remind me. I only just got them all off to bed."
Saki: "It's so unfair. If my parents wanted to go off on a romantic holiday, they should have thought twice before having so many kids. Why should I have to stay behind and look after them just because I'm the oldest?"
Atcchan: "But you wouldn't have wanted to go on holiday with them either, would you?"
Saki: "With my parents? Of course not. I'd rather die."
Saki: "Did you know they've gone to Okinawa? Who wants to go to Okinawa?"
Saki: "I went there on a school trip a few years ago, and it's a complete tourist trap. Tacky merchandise everywhere - and it's all so bright and noisy. Not to mention the weather..."
*Saki has a very pale complexion, which she guards jealously. She always slathers on sunscreen, inches thick, whenever so much as a single glint of sunshine can be seen peeking out from behind a cloud.*
Atcchan: "Then I don't know why you're so unhappy. If you didn't want to go with them in the first place then there's no problem, right?"
Saki: "It's the principle of the thing, that's all. I'm hurt. They didn't even invite me."
Atcchan: "Because they knew you wouldn't want to go."
Saki: "But I still would've liked an invitation. It would at least have given the vague illusion that my company is in high demand this holiday."
Atcchan: "What about Miho and Yuuna?"
Saki: "Yuuna went to stay with her big sister for a few days and Miho's out camping with her parents."
*Saki sighs.*
Saki: "This is so pathetic. I'm the only one who doesn't have anything to do. Not a single thing."
Atcchan: "But taking care of your siblings is a noble job!"
Saki: "Hahaha, yeah. Noble."
*Saki laughs dryly, without any trace of humor.*
Saki: "If you think watching reruns of Heidi for hours on end is noble, then sure."
Atcchan: "I kind of liked Heidi..."
*I had the whole series on VHS, and I used to re-watch it regularly, even up until my early teens, when I was feeling bad.*
*That is, until my mother rummaged through my bedroom when I wasn't home and threw all my old VHS tapes out...*
*I was pretty sore about that at the time - and I still am, actually. Most of those shows don't get aired on TV anymore.*
Saki: "I liked it too, but that was when I was about five."
Atcchan: "But most of your siblings are five."
Saki: "I know. It's so depressing I could scream. However, I will refrain, because that would wake those monsters up again."
Atcchan: "It sounds rough."
Saki: "You have no idea. You haven't known true torture until you've had the task of putting four young children to bed."
*Having met Saki's siblings several times during my trips to her home, I know better than to berate her.*
*Although I genuinely like young children, Saki's siblings are something else altogether. They're more like gremlins than cute kids - and they're so loud, too.*
*It's no wonder Saki always has such dark bags under her eyes. Living in a small home filled with tiny children, prone to waking up in the very early hours of morning and slipping into their big sister's bed, must be incredibly exhausting.*
Saki: "It's getting so bad that I'm starting to think Okinawa would be better after all. Okinawa."
Saki: "What a joke. Why couldn't they go somewhere classy, like France or Italy? And if it absolutely has to be Japan, then Ginza would definitely be the best choice."
Saki: "My parents have, like, no sense of style - none whatsoever."
*A sigh.*
Saki: "Anyway. I hope you're having a good time, at least."
Atcchan: "I'm not entirely sure yet. I only just got here."
Saki: "Your train journey was that long?"
Atcchan: "Yeah. Like, seven hours or so."
Saki: "I would hate that so much, being cramped up on a train with strangers coughing on me."
Atcchan: "It really wasn't that bad. It was pretty quiet, really."
Saki: "Hn. That's good, I suppose. More than can be said for my day."
*A pause.*
Saki: "Hey, Atcchan."
Atcchan: "What is it?"
Saki: "I hope you have a good time on your trip. Honestly. I'm not just saying it."
Atcchan: "Yeah. I know."
Saki: "I hope you get along well with your friends. Your old friends. And, um..."
*I shuffle around, trying to get comfortable. My bare feet, toes twitching, are starting to feel strange, slightly heavy. Have they gone numb from sitting cross-legged on the wooden floor for so long?*
Saki: "If you ever feel overwhelmed, you can always call me. I probably won't be doing anything interesting. If anything, I'd appreciate having somebody to talk to other than the mothers at the local playground."
Atcchan: "Sure. I'll try to keep in contact, if I have time. But I am going to be back in three days. Just try to hold out until then!"
Saki: "I'll do my best. Three days of endless Heidi reruns and pillow fights and take-out pizza... I'll have to grin and bear it, I suppose."
*Not that Saki grins very often. That would conflict with her pale-skinned, dark-eyed, 'eternal queen of the night' appearance.*
Saki: "Oh, and one more thing."
Atcchan: "Hm?"
Saki: "Make sure you bring me back a souvenir. I need some kind of excitement lingering on the horizon to get me through this living nightmare."
Saki: "Otherwise, I might snap and stab myself in the eye with a wax crayon."
*I lie in my futon, staring up at the living room ceiling.*
*Since my grandparents' house is pretty small, there was nowhere to put me other than here. Still, I don't mind. It reminds me of the times when I was a child, and I used to stay here overnight when my parents were busy.*
*I would lie on this same futon, in this same living room, with the light turned on, reading comics and eating slices of stolen tangerine.*
*My fingers would always get stained with yellow from the rind of the tangerine, and I never had the foresight to wash it off before I went to sleep.*
*My grandmother would see my yellow fingers in the morning, and see the missing tangerines, but she never scolded me. Instead, she asked, in an overly theatrical tone of surprise, "Where have the tangerines all gone?" and I'd say "I don't know - maybe it was a bear!"*
*They really were fun times...*
*But I'm not ten anymore.*
*I'm getting older and I'm too big for this futon now. The tips of my toes are poking out from under the sheets.*
*I close my eyes and curl up into a ball, listening to the sounds of the cicadas outside.*
*The windows are all shut but I can still hear them.*
*This is something I forgot after living in the city for so long. The small details vanished from my mind, as though they were never there at all.*
*No matter where you live, there's always background noise. In the city, it's cars and drunken arguments at 2:00 a.m. outside your apartment. In the countryside, it's cicadas. Cicadas and the wind.*
*I snuggle under my blanket. For some reason, I feel cold - and not just my toes. All of me; my whole body.*
*I shiver.*
*Maybe it isn't the weather. Maybe it's my mind.*
*I'm probably overthinking things. I always do.*
*Thinking about tomorrow.*
*Thinking about her.*
*I should have told her.*
*Why... didn't I tell her?*
*That's the last thought I have... before I fall into a deep, dreamless sleep.*
*Sunlight streams through the window. I can feel it brushing against my face, trying to snake itself through my closed eyes.*
*I curl up even tighter into a ball like a hibernating hedgehog. The new day crept upon me far too fast. I haven't had any time to prepare myself yet. I'm still tired and my feet are cold.*
*That's what I get for sleeping on a futon slightly too small for me, I guess.*
*I can't hear any cars. I can't hear any people. Everything is still, quiet. Maybe too quiet.*
*I start to fantasize, making up imaginary scenarios of natural disasters, nuclear wars, a zombie apocalypse.*
*Where have all the people gone?*
*It takes me a few moments to remember where I am.*
*I'm not in the city anymore.*
Atcchan: "Haa..."
*I sigh, breathing in the cool country air. It's invigorating, waking me up more thoroughly than a bucket of cold water could.*
*Now then...*
*Where should I go...? Who should I see...?*
*Amu told me, in a letter I received a few days ago, that she was going to spend most of Golden Week working in her parents' café. Since it's only 11:00 a.m., it seems likely she'll be there.*
*In that case, if I want to pay her a visit, I should dig my old bike out from my grandparents' back garden and take it for a ride. It takes about forty minutes to reach the town where that café is by bike, probably slightly longer if I walk.*
*I haven't been on a bike in a long time. Thinking about it makes me feel a bit nostalgic.*
*The wind in my hair, the scent of the flowers in the fields, the earth under my tires... It's an enticing idea.*
*But on the other hand... there's always Noelle.*
*I probably - no, I definitely - owe her a visit. And yet, it's been so long... I can't help but feel anxious.*
*But I know one thing is certain. If I keep deliberating like this I'll never get anything done.*
*I stand in front of that house for the first time in two years. It feels almost unreal, like a dream.*
*The only thing that reassures me that this is reality is the anxious beating of my heart, the knot of worry coiled up inside my chest.*
*I want to turn. I want to run. But I know I'd despise myself for it.*
*I've come this far already... so I can't turn back.*
*I need to focus my breathing. Steady my heart. Breathe in, breathe out.*
*Look at the house. Look at the house and remember.*
*This is an old village, with roots that can be traced back centuries. Most of the houses here are wooden, long-lasting remnants on an older time, constructed almost a century ago.*
*In comparison, Noelle's home is strikingly modern, a large structure with glass windows and a garage. To my younger self it seemed almost like a palace, a home for a princess.*
*I used to come down this path on my bike every few days when I was young, often with Amu. We'd watch this home being constructed bit by bit - staring from a distance with wide eyes as it all came together.*
*To me it seemed like magic.*
*But now...*
*The house doesn't look as grand as I once remembered. It seems smaller - somehow shrunken. That's probably because I've been exposed to so many towering skyscrapers in the city.*
*I don't think that's the only thing, though...*
*Somehow, the house looks... a little bit like a shell. A fossilized remain. Maybe I'm just being sentimental, but... the atmosphere feels a little 'off.'*
*It's cold. There's no warmth here.*
*And, in the garden... there's a sign.*
*A sign that reads, quite plainly, in large characters: 'FOR SALE.'*
*This unexpected news makes my eyes open wide.*
*The house is for sale...? I had no idea. Amu never mentioned this in any of her letters.*
*Does this mean... Noelle is moving?*
*Did something happen...?*
*Maybe Noelle's sick. She's ill and her parents don't want to stay in a small village like this any longer, so far away from a hospital.*
*Or, it's her parents. Maybe something unfortunate happened to them - an accident? - and they're in critical care, or worse, dead. Noelle will have to stay with distant relatives while her old, beautiful home goes to ruin...*
*No, that's ridiculous. Way too over the top. Then maybe...*
*Her parents got remarried? They're getting divorced and they're selling the house. In that case, Noelle will end up living with a new stepparent - maybe they're cruel? - and some wicked stepsisters, or-*
*... But if I keep going down this line of thought it'll end up like a fairy tale.*
*Something simpler, then. Something more likely to have actually happened in reality, and not inside my overly anxious, melodramatic mind that's been warped from watching too many TV dramas.*
*Her parents probably got a new job. That seems like the most likely option.*
*My grandparents did say more and more people were leaving this village. It is a small place, after all, even if it is very pretty. There just aren't that many jobs here, and driving forty minutes to work every day isn't practical.*
*And yet, even though I know it's foolish... I can't help but worry.*
*Noelle was always so quiet, so shy, so reclusive. Even though there were only thirty-three students in our whole school, she hardly ever spoke a word to anyone other than me.*
*If Noelle's parents are moving to a larger town... how will she cope?*
*What will she do?*
*But it's not my place to worry. I scoff at myself, shaking my head.*
*I don't deserve to act so righteous, pretending to be oh-so-concerned for Noelle's happiness. If I was, I would have told her.*
*If I really valued our friendship... I wouldn't have let it fall apart so easily.*
*My legs remain frozen to the spot. I have to exercise a great deal of willpower to get them to move.*
*Feeling as though I could fall over at any moment, I make my way up to the front door.*
*I knock on the door... and wait.*
*I wait... and wait... and wait...*
*The seconds go by slowly, agonizingly, like trying to squeeze the very last remnants of toothpaste out of a tube.*
*When the act of waiting gives my brain enough free time to start panicking, I knock on the door again, just to give myself something to do.*
*But there's still no response.*
*There's nobody home. Noelle isn't there, and neither are her parents.*
Atcchan: "Well, that would explain why their car isn't in the drive..."
*No car. No people. I can't hear a single sound, not even from a stray bird or a lonesome cicada. There's nothing.*
*It really does feel desolate here.*
Atcchan: "I guess there isn't much I can do, then..."
*I say this aloud, attempting to organize my thoughts. It might be easier to do so in words, rather than in the stifling confines of my own skull.*
*I'm not sure whether I'm relieved or not that Noelle isn't home. At least it means I don't have to face her. For now.*
*This gives me a little more time to prepare myself and figure out what to say.*
*It's difficult, though. I don't know if there's anything you can say after abandoning your best friend for two years without a single word of explanation.*
*Well then...*
*I guess, since Noelle isn't in, this means I can pay a visit to Amu.*
*I turn away from Noelle's home and make my way back to my grandparents' house.*
*I know my old bike is being stored somewhere in their back garden, waiting for me to ride on it once more.*
*It doesn't take long for me to make up my mind.*
*Although I feel a twinge of guilt at brushing Noelle aside like this... I think it might be for the best.*
*I know, in my heart, I should at least try to visit her. I should try to repair our relationship. I owe her that much - and this might be the only chance I have. But...*
*I'm not going to be here for very long, and I don't know if I'll have enough time.*
*It seems far more realistic to spend these few days having fun with my first best friend, rather than trying to rekindle a relationship that might never spark again. At least I know that Amu will be happy to see me.*
*And so, trying to justify this cowardly line of thought to myself... I go into my grandparents' back garden and dig up my old bike.*
Atcchan: "Haah... Haaah..."
*It's taking longer to reach the next town than I thought it would.*
*I'm slumped over the handlebars of my bike like a slab of freshly cut meat. My face is just as red.*
*I pant heavily, trying to get my breath back. Sweat beads on my forehead, dripping down the contours of my face and off the tip of my nose.*
*This gradual degradation must be what happens when you move to the city.*
*Since everything was all so convenient I stopped walking and cycling everywhere, and instead started to rely on the godsend that is public transportation.*
*I took the train to and from school. When I wanted to go shopping, I went on the bus. I hardly ever had to walk, unless it was to the convenience store - and that was only three minutes away.*
*My heart burns. My face is on fire.*
*At least one good thing's come out of all this. When I blush, my face gets so red it helps to obscure my freckles. I've never liked them.*
*I've wondered about wearing make-up to conceal them before, but... it might be kind of strange asking my female friends for advice about that. I don't know if they'd tease me, but...*
*Well. Even if I wanted to reinvent myself, it's already too late. The people at my new school already know about my freckles, so what's the point? I wouldn't be able to fool them.*
*I'm just the same as I used to be, all those years ago - or am I?*
*If that were really true... then why has cycling suddenly become such a chore?*
*Could I have changed more than I thought?*
*My legs hurt. After that strenuous cycle here, I don't even want to look at my bike, let alone ride it.*
*Unfortunately, I can't just abandon it somewhere along the street. That would be irresponsible, and somebody might trip over it.*
*Burdened by my own code of ethics, I end up towing the wretched thing along behind me, holding it by the handlebars.*
*Maybe it wasn't my fault I got so tired. After all, this is an old bike. Perhaps one of the tires is flat or something - and the brakes aren't very good, either.*
*It's not my fault. It really, truly isn't.*
*Or, at least... I don't want it to be.*
Atcchan: "Geez..."
*Trying to distract myself from my concerns over my physical fitness (or lack of it), I take a look around at my surroundings.*
*Come to think of it, I really should be paying more attention, given I'm wheeling along this unwieldy vehicle. I don't want to run over any small children.*
*The streets are pretty crowded. Since it's a warm day, the whole street is flooded with life: young men and women strolling along hand-in-hand; parents pushing baby strollers; old men and women shielding from the sun under the bus shelter, laughing over private jokes.*
*There are young children clinging to their parents, wailing for ice cream; a group of teenage boys with their hands thrust deep into their pockets sporting backwards baseball caps; a gaggle of girls with fake tans and long fingernails laden down with shopping bags.*
*Everywhere I look, I can see something happening - and almost everybody seems to be smiling. Is that because of the warm weather?*
*This town really does have everything. Large businesses, buildings with more than three floors! A library, a hospital, a police station, a church, several shops, an elementary school, middle school, and a high school; not combined into one classroom like the school in my old village.*
*There are even ice cream vendors in the street, a couple of fast food restaurants, and a movie theater. Truly, this place is a metropolis...!*
*At least, that's what I thought when I was little.*
*Littler than I am now, I mean.*
*Now I know that isn't really true. This is only a small town, with a population of about 30,000. It's not nearly as cosmopolitan as I thought.*
*When you get older, your perspective really does change. The five-story company buildings that were once so impressive are less grandiose now; the single library sadly understocked; the ice cream vendors nothing special. In bigger cities you can also buy crêpes, yakisoba, and takoyaki in the street.*
*Hm... Now, where was the café again?*
*If I remember correctly, it was just down this street and then to the left. Not too far away.*
*This is only a small town, so of course it isn't too far away. Nothing is.*
*I feel a little bit worried about my disheveled hair and sweaty brow, though.*
*If I go to see Amu looking like this it won't make a very good first impression. I bet she'll make fun of me.*
*Should I try to find a public restroom somewhere, so I can freshen up? I'm not so sure. It sounds like too much hard work.*
*If it's Amu, she'll make fun of me no matter what I look like. That's just her thing.*
*If Amu laughs at me, she laughs at me. I don't think I'll mind. It's how she communicates with people.*
*I think, right now... all I want to do is see a friendly face.*
*Coming back here after so long feels stranger, more unsettling, than I thought it would.*
*However...*
*I take a lock of my hair between my thumb and forefinger, squeezing it. It feels slippery to the touch, like handling a fish fresh out of the water.*
*Do I really want to meet Amu looking like I've just crawled out of a vat of lard? I don't think that'd make for a particularly good first impression...*
*It has been two years since I last saw her. Shouldn't I greet her looking my best?*
*Find a public restroom and cool yourself down.":
*Visit the café the way you are.":
*I bend over the sink, splashing cold water onto my face. I don't know if it's making a whole world of difference, but at least I feel somewhat refreshed.*
*When I look at my reflection in the mirror over the sink, I'm relieved to note I look slightly less bedraggled than before. My hair is still damp, but it doesn't look as greasy, and my face isn't as red as once it was.*
*I hope Amu doesn't make fun of me now.*
*... Yeah, right.*
*Since it's Amu, she's going to make fun of me no matter what I look like. I'm not that naïve. But still...*
*She might tease me less than she potentially could, which is good enough for me. At least I've managed to minimize the potential damage.*
*I mop my forehead with a tissue, then crumple it up and throw it in a nearby toilet. At the same time, I can't help but wonder.*
*Why am I getting so concerned about my appearance anyway? It doesn't make any sense. I've known Amu ever since I was a kid. We used to make mud-pies in the forest, go paddling in the river, climb trees together.*
*We've both seen each other in so many embarrassing situations in the past I can hardly count them on my fingers. Why should I worry so much about how I look now...?*
*Am I growing up...?*
*Or, could it possibly be... something more than that...?*
Atcchan: "Ha. That's stupid."
*I shake my head, trying to dispel that ridiculous thought.*
*Why should I care what Amu thinks about me? We've been friends forever (not literally, but close enough). If I liked her in any way other than that, surely I would have realized it by now.*
*I don't like her like that. Not at all. Not one bit.*
*Aah... B-But now that I've denied it so much...*
*D-Doesn't that make it sound even more suspicious?*
*And so I've finally made it back here... Back to this familiar café.*

*And the waitress who comes to greet me...*
Amu:  "Hello, Sir, and welcome to Amu Café! Will you be dining alone today? Is there anywhere in particular you would like to-"

*Aah... No way! That's no fair!*
*She's grown over the last couple of years, too.*
*I may have entertained some wild fantasies of one day overtaking her, being able to rest my elbows on the top of her head just as she always did with me - but, of course, it didn't work out like that.*
*The best laid plans never do.*
*I didn't grow at all these last two years, but Amu... she's shot up just like a stick of bamboo.*
*She's still taller than me. A lot taller than me, actually.*
*How depressing...*
*Amu looks at me in surprise. It takes a few moments until, finally, she's able to greet me.*

Atcchan: "But you're not a kid."
Amu: "Huh?"
Atcchan: "Aren't you a little too old to order from the children's menu?"
Amu: "Huh? That? Oh, well..."

Amu: "I'm still a child at heart, so it's okay~! Ehehehe~"
*Amu places her hands against her cheeks and bats her lashes in what, perhaps, is supposed be an alluring manner. However, given there is a streak of ketchup smeared against her lower lip, the effect is slightly ruined.*

Amu: "Okay! Since you haven't been here for a while, stranger, how about a tour 'round this town?"

Amu: "Why, it's almost like you can read my mind!"
Amu: "Ooh... I can't believe they have the next volume of this out already!"
Atcchan: "Hey, be careful with that!"
*I eye Amu with concern, in the same way a mother might fuss over a particularly spirited child.*
*Amu stands in a corner of the bookstore, flipping through the pristine pages of a brand new manga with such speed I'm worried she'll crease them.*
*I did wonder why she wanted to drag me to a bookstore of all places, given she isn't one for reading a lot... but now I know why.*
*I didn't know this store sold manga too. I wonder if this diversification is a recent thing...*
Amu: "Hehe~"
*Amu giggles, sticking out her tongue.*
Amu: "Fret not, oh ye of little faith. I'm not a complete klutz like you."
Atcchan: "Che..."
*I click my tongue against the roof of my mouth. I want to retort, but I know it'd be for nothing. Amu's right. When it comes to discussions of my shortcomings (of which there are many), Amu is always right.*
*If I were bickering with Saki, maybe I would be able to defend myself, but Amu's known me for too long and has too much material to work with. She even knows about that one time in class, with the cockroach...*

Atcchan: "What are you looking at, anyway?"
Amu: "This? Why, Atcchan, I thought you would've been able to guess! It's a strange new invention we call a 'book.'"

Amu: "There's a lot about me you don't know, Atcchan~ We women are mysterious creatures~"
Atcchan: "And yet you seem to know everything about me..."
Amu: "Well, of course. That's also part of our mystery. Kukuku~"
Atcchan: "Haa... If you say so."
*I sigh, stretching, the joints at my elbows clicking.*
*While Amu flips through various volumes of manga (I have half a mind to tell her 'This is a book store, not a library.' but I'm sure she'd laugh at me), I ponder. Didn't Saki ask me for a souvenir yesterday?*
*I don't really know what kind of 'souvenir' she's expecting, though. It's not like I've gone to visit some famous tourist destination - this is only a tiny little town near a tiny little village.*
*I suppose I could get her something to eat. Everybody likes chocolate, don't they? Even Saki, with her admiration for any and all things gothic, who only ever drinks tomato juice with her school lunch, likes chocolate.*
*Chocolate isn't a very special gift, though. You can buy chocolate everywhere (which, to me at least, only attests to how incredible it is - but not everybody sees it that way). It doesn't have much 'heart.'*
*What would Saki like, though? Knowing her and her ghoulish tastes, she'd probably appreciate something suitably morbid, like a badger's skull or a taxidermy bat, but I don't know if there are any specialist stores around here where I'd be able to pick up such questionable items...*
*Feeling a little like I'm cheating, but genuinely curious for an answer, I turn to look at Amu, who is still preoccupied with her manga.*
*There's something strangely relaxing about watching Amu read. Although she claimed all girls are made of mysteries earlier, she's very open about her emotions most of the time.*
*She must have reached a particularly dramatic twist in her story, because her eyes are startlingly wide, her eyebrows raised so high they've disappeared into her hairline.*
*I smile, shaking my head. I can't help but be amused.*
Atcchan: "Hey, Amu?"
Amu: "Huh?!"
*Amu jumps at the sound of her name, her voice a little more pitchy than usual.*
*I laugh.*
Atcchan: "That manga must be pretty engrossing, huh?"
Amu: "O-Oh yeah... It's not that bad, I suppose..."
Atcchan: "I'm sorry. Did I startle you?"
Amu: "N-No, not really. Jougasaki Amu doesn't get startled by anything! I'd remain completely cool even in the event of the apocalypse! Hohoh!"
Amu: "Anyway, what were you calling me for? Do you have a question?"
Atcchan: "Yeah, um... Actually, I was wondering..."
*I frown, rubbing one hand against the back of my head.*
Atcchan: "This might sound kind of weird, but... Do you know what kind of gift a girl would like?"
Amu: "A girl? Well, well..."
*A devious smile begins to form on Amu's face.*
Amu: "Atcchan, you sly old dog, you! When were you planning to tell me this piece of breaking news, huh?"
Atcchan: "O-Ow...!"
*I wince as Amu elbows me in the stomach, hard. Was she trying to hurt me, or is that just my imagination...?*
Atcchan: "W-What are you talking about?"
Amu: "I'm talking about you getting a girlfriend, of course!"
Atcchan: "G-Girlfriend?"
Amu: "Yes! And in only two years, too! I never would've believed it of you!"
*I stare at Amu, my mouth falling open in a small 'o'. Of course, I should've known she'd react like this...*
*And why does she have to be so loud about it? It feels like everybody in the bookstore is staring at me...*
Atcchan: "S-Saki isn't my girlfriend. She's just a friend."
Amu: "Ooh. Her name is Saki, is it? How cute!"
Atcchan: "I don't know if 'cute' would be the best way to describe her..."
Amu: "Ohoh? So, how would you describe her?"
Atcchan: "I don't know. Maybe 'scary'..."
Amu: "So you like sadistic girls, huh? Of course you do, I should have known~ You always enjoyed those punishment games we used to play when we were younger, didn't you?"
Atcchan: "I-I didn't enjoy them! I didn't enjoy them at all! A-And anyway, Saki isn't my girlfriend!"
Amu: "Okay, Atcchan. Whatever you say~ "
Atcchan: "I'm telling the truth!"
*Amu smirks. I don't know if she really believes Saki is my girlfriend or not, but it's clear she's going to continue to frame it that way just to unsettle me.*
*Is this revenge for making her jump earlier? If so, it seems a little harsh...*
Amu: "Anyway. Why are you so hung up on buying this girl 'friend' a present?"
Atcchan: "I... She asked for one, that's all. I think she's been feeling a little down lately, so I thought it might cheer her up."
Amu: "Hm. You must really like this girl, then?"
Atcchan: "I... I like her enough, I suppose. Why are you asking?"
Amu: "Well..."
*Amu pauses, tugging at the end of her pink ponytail in a strangely distressed manner. Although she's still smiling, her expression looks slightly less cheery than before.*
Amu: "I find it kind of hard to believe that you're soooo desperate to buy a present for a girl who's simply a 'friend' when you wouldn't even buy me - one of your bestest buds - a measly ice cream."
Atcchan: "H-Hey now..."
*I thought she'd gotten over that. Is she still holding a grudge?*
*Amu can be such a kid sometimes.*
Atcchan: "It's not that I like Saki more than you. It's just... different."
*Amu pouts, sticking out her lower lip.*
Amu: "Different? How is it different?"
Atcchan: "Well... Because I've bought you loads of things in the past, but I've never really bought Saki anything before. She doesn't usually ask for favors from people."
Amu: "And you're saying I do?!"
Atcchan: "You do try to get me to buy stuff for you quite a lot..."
Amu: "But I haven't in ages! Not for, like, two whole years!"
Atcchan: "Because you haven't seen me for two whole years!"
Amu: "Ha... You might have a point there. Ehehe..."
*Amu laughs, though it lacks a certain kind of buoyancy. Her eyes are unusually downcast, her smile strained.*
*If I didn't know any better... I'd say she really was jealous.*
*I wonder...*
*In this kind of scenario, is it really all right for me to put Saki before Amu? Amu does have a point - I have known her for far longer. But...*
*...*
Amu: "You know..."
*Amu's fiddling with the hem of her skirt, her eyes directed downwards, towards the ground.*
Amu: "Um... if you want to buy her a present, then... it's fine."
*I blink at Amu, surprised. It isn't often she backs down like this - and of her own free will, no less.*
Atcchan: "Are you sure?"
Amu: "Yeah. It might be a good lesson for me."
Atcchan: "Lesson?"
Amu: "Mm. I think I'm just feeling kind of clingy - like, 'I knew Atcchan first, so he's all mine!' Ehehe..."
*A sheepish smile.*
Amu: "I know that's kind of unhealthy, though - and it isn't fair to you. You have a new life now. New friends."
Amu: "If you really want... you can go and buy the girl a present. Please don't mind me. Ehehe~"
*So she says, but... I can tell, despite her bravado, she isn't happy about it. I've clearly hurt her feelings.*
*Ah... Now I feel conflicted. What should I do...?*
*And what kind of present would Saki like, anyway?*
Amu: "Oh! How noble!"
Atcchan: "So... Do you have any ideas? About what a girl might like?"
Amu: "Hmm... Well, it's a lot trickier than that. Girls are all different, you know? We like different things."
Amu: "And I don't even know who this Saki person is. I'm probably the least qualified to tell you what she'd like."
Atcchan: "Yeah. I thought it might have been a bit of a broad question."
*I sigh, rubbing my side. It still aches after being unceremoniously gouged by Amu's elbow like that.*
Atcchan: "I just thought... is there any gift in particular you'd like to receive? Anything you really want?"
Amu: "Well now... Then it would become a case of what I would like, rather than what Saki would like, and that isn't what you want to know, is it?"
Atcchan: "You're right. I'm sorry for asking something so pointless."
Amu: "Hey now, it's not pointless. I'm sorry I can't be of further use, lover boy~ "
Atcchan: "L-Lover boy?!"
Amu: "Kukuku~"
*Damn that Amu... My face feels so hot you could fry an egg on it...*
*A present for Saki, though... What would she want? I don't know if I'd be able to find it in this bookstore.*
*Saki does like to read, but she prefers the Victorian gothic to cute manga, and I don't know which books she's read and which ones she hasn't.*
*Hmm... A present for Saki... A present for Saki... A present for Saki...*
*Ah...!*
*A sudden flash of inspiration crosses my mind, illuminating my thoughts more clearly than a clap of thunder.*
*There was that store, wasn't there? I used to go there with Noelle all the time, back when we were younger.*
*The old man who worked there was really nice - until he got replaced by that eerie woman with the long fingernails and the perpetual look of arch disdain. Just thinking about her is making my skin crawl.*
*Besides... This store is a little off the beaten track. It's not one of the stores situated on the main street.*
*It's tucked away amongst a rabbit warren of residential homes, difficult to find unless one knows where it is.*
*Could I really go there? Would it be worth it?*
Amu: "Hey, what's this? Do you have an idea, Atcchan~?"
Atcchan: "Well, um..."
*I frown, looking down at my shoes.*
*Could I really drag Amu along on an excursion like that, just to find a gift for another girl back at home?*
*Didn't I come here so I could spend time with my old friends, rather than fussing over the new? I don't want to upset Amu...*
*I do have an idea.":
*It's fine, I'll just leave it.":
Amu: "Whoa... I don't think I've ever been to this place before."
Atcchan: "I'm not surprised. I don't know if many people have."
*After all, this place is hard to find, tucked away amongst a bunch of residential houses. It took Amu and I twenty minutes to get here. I'm surprised I didn't get lost on the way.*
*From what I remember during my trips here with Noelle, the items in this store weren't so much 'antiques' as 'bits of old junk', and I'm not surprised to see this hasn't changed in the last two years. The interior of this store is piled high with junk, but I can't imagine much of it has any practical use.*
*With just one cursory glance around I can see several cracked mirrors, an old grandfather clock, display cases filled with dolls, a wooden table missing a leg, a birdcage with a broken lock, an ancient iron teakettle, and a mask that seems to be aping the Noh theater tradition, but it's been very crudely carved and painted. Maybe it would look good for Halloween, but I can't imagine anybody would want it hanging on their living room wall for decorative purposes. They'd have to have pretty warped sensibilities if that was the case...*
*Although I don't have much interest in things like this, Noelle has always been very keen. I'm not sure why, but she has some inbuilt, magpie-like obsession over collecting junk.*
*I don't think Saki and Noelle are very similar, not by any stretch of the imagination, but Saki also has a fondness for curious old objects. I think she likes the mystery and the romance of it - although, personally, I don't find broken plates and old jewellery 'romantic.'*
*Maybe I have no sense of imagination? But I worry about almost everything all the time, so I must have some capacity for it. I guess being 'overly anxious' and 'imaginative' are two distinctly different things...*
*The air is thick with dust, so heavy I have to stifle my coughs with one hand. It's nice to know this place hasn't changed at all. It's just as disorderly as I remember.*
*I cast my mind back to the sign displayed outside the door, written in red pen in angry strokes. The sign that reads, for all to see:*
Note: "TO MY BELOVED CUSTOMERS: PLEASE WOULD YOU KINDLY CLOSE THE DOOR WHEN YOU ENTER THE SHOP, FOR THAT IS WHAT A DOOR IS FOR. THANK YOU :)"
*I thought the shopkeeper might have removed that sign during the last two years I was away in the city, but I guess not. The passive aggressive nature of that warning must be doing wonders for this little store's business, though, because it's completely empty - not a soul in sight, save for the shopkeeper.*
*She's sitting at the counter, leaning over something, a pencil clutched in one hand. Her dark blue hair falls in front of her pale face, obscuring her features.*
*I don't know whether she's even realized there are other people in her store - or if she has, she evidently doesn't care.*
*Not even the sound of the bell ringing as Amu and I entered was enough to get her attention.*
*I wonder what her name was...*
*I'm sure I've seen her somewhere else before - and not just behind the counter of this store. Didn't she used to go my school?*
*I turn to Amu for confirmation. She's surveying the young woman behind the counter with an uneasy look.*
Atcchan: "Do you know who she is?"
*I whisper under my breath.*
*Amu nods her head.*
Amu: "Mm. It's Eri's big sister, Tsuzumi."
Atcchan: "Eri...?"
*I blink, casting my mind back. Eri, Eri...*
*Ah. I remember Eri. She went to my school, lived in the same village. The blond girl with the corkscrew pigtails, who always used to wear the most beautiful clothes.*
*I think I let her borrow my umbrella once, during a particularly bad downpour, when she had left hers at home.*
*The expression on Amu's face really is curious. She looks as though she's swallowed a lemon, whole.*
Atcchan: "What's wrong? Weren't you friends with Eri?"
Amu: "I... I was at some point. Now, however..."
*She winces.*
Amu: "It's a little complicated, and I'm not sure whether her big sister will appreciate me hanging around here..."
Atcchan: "You mean you had an argument?"
Amu: "You could call it that. Personally, I think she was just being stubborn, but..."
*Amu sighs, letting her shoulders sag.*
Amu: "If you really want to buy something from here, I won't stop you, but... is it all right if I wait outside? I don't want the big sister to spot me."
Atcchan: "Is she really that bad?"
*From what I remember of Tsuzumi, she was only ever rude and sardonic towards me, but maybe she was just having a bad day. A couple of bad days. And we all have moments in our life like that.*
*It wouldn't be fair to condemn somebody based on a mere handful of interactions.*
*Judging by Amu's expression, however, you'd think I'd dragged her up before a guillotine, rather than into an antiques store.*
*I don't think I've ever seen Amu, brave and fearless Amu, capable of facing down the apocalypse without so much as a sniffle, look so pale before.*
*Maybe Tsuzumi really is that bad...*
*Now I feel guilty for bringing Amu here. Guilty, and ever so slightly frightened for my safety. Still, I came here to buy Saki a gift, and it would be silly to leave after coming all this way...*
*I square my shoulders and draw in a deep breath, trying to compose myself.*
*I can do it, with or without Amu's support. I can.*
Atcchan: "Okay. You can wait outside. I'll try to be quick."
Amu: "Thank you, Atcchan."
*With a small smile, Amu gives me a wave, and then ducks back out of the shop; the opened door letting a brief sliver of sunlight creep down the very ugly patterned carpet, before it is finally extinguished with a slam.*
*Somehow, the disappearance of that light seems strangely symbolic - as though my own hopes of escaping here alive have similarly been extinguished...*
Tsuzumi: "Hmph... What a racket..."
*The sound of the door slamming finally rouses Tsuzumi from her stupor. She lifts her head, glaring, eyes framed with dark lashes.*
*I whimper. The look on her face... I have no doubts it could bore through solid steel.*
Tsuzumi: "Are you trying to give me a headache? I put that sign outside the door for a reason, you know!"
Atcchan: "S-So... So people would remember to close it?"
Tsuzumi: "Yes, but that's only part of it. I thought a notice like that would be enough to scare away brats like yourself, but I suppose not."
Tsuzumi: "What can I do so you people get the message, short of nailing the corpse of a dead dog to the door?"
Atcchan: "Ah... W-Well, um..."
*I can feel the color draining out of my face, as though a plug has been pulled somewhere on the soles of my feet.*
*I must look ashen. I feel ashen, too, if it is even possible to feel such a thing.*
Tsuzumi: "Oh... Now, wait one moment..."
*Tsuzumi's eyes soften slightly, one finger (I notice, with a gulp, her fingernails are remarkably long and pointed) tapping against her lower lip.*
Tsuzumi: "I think I recognize you."
Atcchan: "Y-You do?"
Tsuzumi: "Yes. That's right. You're not just any old impudent brat after all. Hm, hm."
*She nods, as though reassuring herself of this fact.*
*The two little buns, pinned neatly at either side of her head, bounce slightly as she moves, in a manner that could almost be considered charming.*
*Almost.*
*If her fingernails weren't so very, very sharp, her gaze so disconcerting, her smirk so distinctly unpleasant.*
Tsuzumi: "You used to live here, didn't you? In the village, I mean. You went to my school - though you must've been even littler back then than you are now."
Atcchan: "A-Ah, um... Y-Yes, that... T-That's right..."
Tsuzumi: "Fufu. Atcchan, isn't it?"
Atcchan: "Mm..."
*I look down at the floor, hardly daring to meet this woman's eyes.*
*It's a mark of just how ingrained on my subconscious that nickname is that I respond to it almost as though it's my real name. By this point, given everybody refers to me as such (even my teachers), it might as well be.*
*If everybody starts referring to me with this diminutive, and nobody uses my birth name, will that rewrite my whole identity? Will the 'me' I used to be before Amu arbitrarily assigned this nickname to me disappear completely?*
*But, then again, I was only three or four when I got this nickname. There wasn't really all that much of 'me' that existed before then anyway.*
*I guess it doesn't matter that much after all.*
Tsuzumi: "My little sister has told me about you. She said your family got bored of the country and decided to move out to the big city."
*Although she's simply stating a fact, it feels as though she's judging me. Behind her eyes, I can see the unspoken words, loud and clear. Traitor.*
Atcchan: "Y-Yeah, they, um... My dad got a new job, so... My parents decided to move."
*For some reason, I feel like I have to defend myself, even though she hasn't actually made any kind of accusation out loud.*
Atcchan: "B-But I-I didn't want to move! I... I-I was really against the whole idea...! I tried to talk my parents out of it, but... But they didn't listen..."
Tsuzumi: "How sad. My heart bleeds for you."
Tsuzumi: "Anyway. If you want to buy something, do it quickly. I'm in the middle of something, and your presence is distracting me."
Atcchan: "In the middle of something?"
*I look at Tsuzumi curiously. I can see several sheets of paper spread out across the top of the counter. It looks like she's drawing something, but I can't tell what.*
*I wonder... Just what is it she's working on?*
*And... Do I have any right to ask?*
*The expression on Tsuzumi's face... is kind of scary...*
*Ask her what she's drawing.":
*Don't ask her.":
*No. I can't do it. Just one look at her eyes makes me feel numb; my whole body paralyzed with fear.*
*But I'm still curious. We humans always are - damnably so.*
*Maybe, if I just tilt my head to one side, I'll be able to get a better look? Just what is it she's drawing, anyway...?*
Tsuzumi: "Hey."
*O-Oh no...*
*At this simple sound, this single syllable, my blood turns to ice in my veins.*
*She's spotted me.*
*I guess I'm not very good at being discreet...*
Tsuzumi: "Did I tell you you could peek at my private affairs, you nosy little swine?"
Tsuzumi: "Now, now. Did I tell you that you could try to sneak a peek at my private affairs?"
Atcchan: "P-Private...?"
Tsuzumi: "That's right. What I'm working on is top secret. An uncouth boy such as yourself could never comprehend it."
Atcchan: "I-I, um... I-I'm sorry...! I-I wasn't try to look, I-I was just curious...!"
Tsuzumi: "And it was curiosity that killed the cat, as they say."
*I bet this woman wouldn't wait a single heartbeat before killing me. With those sharp claws, I wouldn't stand a chance...*
Tsuzumi: "Now, would you kindly get out of my sight? Run along, little boy. Shoo, shoo."
*Tsuzumi makes a dismissive motion with her hands. I'm more than happy to oblige. My face burning bright red, I turn about on my heels, venturing into the deeper, darker depths of the store.*
*I just hope Saki appreciates her present, whatever it ends up being. I feel as though this gift may very well end up costing me more than mere money...*
Tsuzumi: "Hm? Is this what you want?"
Atcchan: "I-I, um... Y-Yes, please..."
*Tsuzumi picks up my planned purchase in one pale hand.*
*I note, with a start, her skin might be just as white as Saki's. Is that because she stays in this dimly lit shop, bat-like, for hours on end? Or maybe it's something more sinister than that...*
*Wasn't there that one countess who stayed young forever by bathing in the blood of young, virgin girls...?*
*I shudder.*
*The item Tsuzumi is turning over, examining with a critical gaze, is something that certainly supports my 'sinister' theory. It's a pack of tarot cards.*
*I'm surprised I was able to find such a Saki-like gift in here, nestled away on a shelf amongst an old board of Go and a set of nesting dolls. Stumbling across this really was a stroke of luck.*
*The cards are fairly large, about the size of my palm, printed on thick paper that doesn't yield easily when bent. The prints on them are fairly abstract, with lots of flowers and skulls and gnarled trees, but I think Saki would prefer that.*
*It's just a pity there isn't any 'vampire' card - but the odd, goblin-like creature grinning unpleasantly up at me from the 'devil' card seems gothic enough.*
*The cards are a little ragged at the edges, slightly worse for wear, and it makes me wonder just how old they are, how long they've been festering away in some corner of this store. Maybe for years and years.*
*Somehow, the knowledge that I may be the first person to handle these cards for five, ten, maybe twenty years, makes me feel a little excited. Is this why Noelle enjoys collecting 'antiques' so much? The thrill?*
*After finishing her appraisal, Tsuzumi gathers the cards together and slots them back into the slightly moth-eaten box where they belong.*
Tsuzumi: "Hm... These are pretty nice. There's only the major arcana, but I don't think any of them are missing."
Atcchan: "You know about tarot cards?"
Tsuzumi: "Just a little. You pick up lots of random bits of knowledge when you write things."
Atcchan: "You write books?"
*Once more, the sheets of paper strewn across the counter pique my interest. Are these pages from Tsuzumi's novel? Did she get mad at me because I was distracting her from her writing? Is she actually a famous author?*
*Maybe that's how this store is able to stay open, despite the evident lack of customers...*
*But Tsuzumi snorts, destroying this little fantasy in a matter of moments.*
Tsuzumi: "Not books, no. It's something far more exciting."
Atcchan: "Exciting...?"
Tsuzumi: "Mmhmm. But don't start prying now - it isn't your place."
*I look down at the floor, my face flushing.*
Atcchan: "I... I-I'm sorry..."
Tsuzumi: "Heh. You apologize an awful lot, don't you?"
*O-Only because your withering gaze and pointed comments make me feel like I should apologize!*
Atcchan: "I... I'm sorry...?"
*Tsuzumi sniggers.*
Tsuzumi: "Well, I should've expected as much. It's just a shame you couldn't have shown a little bit of that humility towards my little sister."
Atcchan: "Y-Your little sister? You mean Eri?"
Tsuzumi: "Is there any other? How could you forget my dear Eri when she is the cutest, sweetest, most sensitive creature in the whole world?"
Atcchan: "I... I-I didn't forget her. I just..."
Atcchan: "I... I didn't know I'd ever done anything wrong to her...?"
Tsuzumi: "Of course you wouldn't remember. Men never do. They're so pigheaded and unreliable."
Atcchan: "I'm sorry...?"
*Tsuzumi raises an eyebrow.*
Tsuzumi: "You're apologizing for being born as a man now?"
Atcchan: "I... I-I guess so..."
*Although it sounds kind of sad when she puts it that way.*
Tsuzumi: "Fufu~ "
*With a devious little giggle, Tsuzumi leans across the counter.*
Tsuzumi: "You know, if you ever get tired of being a man... I can help you out~ "
Atcchan: "W-What do you mean?"
Tsuzumi: "I mean... I have a way to end that masculinity, forced upon you by birth, forever. When I'm through with you, nobody could recognize you as one of those disgusting, shameless pigs again... Fufufu~"
*W-Waah...*
*I feel a chill run down my spine, ice cold, as though somebody has just slipped an eel down the back of my shirt.*
*F-For all I know, Tsuzumi could be talking about giving me a make-over, but... somehow, I doubt it. I think her motives might be rather more unpleasant than that...*
Atcchan: "I... I-I'll think about it...!"
*In my nightmares.*
Atcchan: "C-Can I just pay for the cards, please?"
Tsuzumi: "Hm? Oh, these?"
*Tsuzumi turns her attention back to the pack of cards, resting innocently on her desk.*
Tsuzumi: "Well... I don't particularly like selling my stock to irritating little boys who are so stupid they can't even repent when they've done something wrong. You don't really deserve it, you know?"
Atcchan: "I... I know! I'm sorry!"
Tsuzumi: "But... Since I am busy with my work, and I don't particularly want to be disturbed... I suppose, if it will be the quickest way to make you leave, I can acquiesce. Just this once."
Atcchan: "So you... you'll sell them to me?"
Tsuzumi: "That's right. And for a discounted price, too - if you promise to take them and get out as soon as possible."
Atcchan: "I... I-I will...! I-I won't come back, I promise!"
*As if I'd want to. I'd rather gnaw off my own arm.*
Tsuzumi: "Good, good. Then I'm glad we understand one another. Fufufu~"
*W-Wah... That cold, empty laugh of Tsuzumi's... it's making my whole body shudder. I'm starting to feel sick.*
*In her dark clothes, with those long fingernails, with that laugh, she fits the role of a wicked witch almost perfectly!*
*I wouldn't be at all surprised if this store turned out to be a front for her to carry out her witch-like activities, sacrificing animals at altars and bathing in pig's blood and praying to Satan.*
*Maybe she's cast some kind of curse on me, and when I go to sleep tonight all my flesh will slowly start to peel away from my bones?*
*No, I don't want that! Anything but that!*
*Saki... I really, really hope you appreciate your present...!*
Amu: "Finally done, huh?"
Atcchan: "Yeah. I'm sorry. It took a little while to find something I wanted, and then I got distracted talking to the shopkeeper..."
*Being threatened and insulted by her, more like.*
*Is casting curses on people illegal? Maybe I should report her. But, ah... if I did, she'd probably inflict me with the black plague...*
Amu: "Kukuku~"
*Amu grins. Her light smile is able to combat some of the unease I felt earlier, making my body feel more relaxed.*
*If Tsuzumi is some kind of demon... then, does that make Amu an angel...?*
*An angel who likes to hit people on the back a lot, and embarrass them with past memories they would much rather forget...*
*Maybe Amu isn't really an angel after all. Her company is still preferable to Tsuzumi's though.*
*Then again, this might not be saying much, given the company of a rabid wolf would still be preferable to Tsuzumi's.*
Amu: "I can only imagine. Tsuzumi is quite an intense person, isn't she?"
Atcchan: "Y-Yeah... Intense is the word..."
Amu: "You were brave going in there all on your own, Atcchan! I think living in the city has changed you!"
Atcchan: "Y-You think?"
Amu: "Mmhmm! I think you're a lot braver now! Far more confident! It's cool!"
Atcchan: "W-Well, I don't know about that..."
*I think back to my earlier exchange with Tsuzumi, flushing. Would Amu be quite so keen to call me 'cool' if she'd seen just how much I was apologizing?*
Amu: "Anyway~ What did you get your friend? What did you get her?"
Atcchan: "Oh, nothing special. Just this."
*I draw the pack of tarot cards out of my pocket. Amu examines them with interest, her ponytail bobbing as she tilts her head.*
Amu: "Aren't they, like, those cards you use to tell if people are going to die soon or not?"
Atcchan: "They... They're for fortune telling, I think. I don't know. I've never used them."
Amu: "So your friend is into demons and ghosts and creepy things like that?"
Atcchan: "A little. She does like horror movies a lot..."
Amu: "Kukuku~ Maybe that explains it then~"
Atcchan: "Explains what?"
Amu: "How you ended up becoming so brave! If you've got a friend like that, maybe her fearlessness rubbed off on you a little, too!"
Atcchan: "I don't know about that..."
*Whenever I watch horror movies with Saki, I have to put my hands over my eyes during the scary parts.*
*I don't handle graphic depictions of violence very well - especially not when it comes with gallons of bright red blood...*
Amu: "So, Atcchan. Do you want to walk back to the café? My dad said he'd pick us up and give us a ride back to the village."
Atcchan: "He did? That's kind of him."
Amu: "Yeah. And I thought, maybe you wouldn't want to walk home all the way by yourself, given it's quite a way - and you already did a load of walking just to get here. And to get to this store, too."
*It's true. My feet really are starting to ache. I think I might have stretched my stamina a little too far today.*
*Walking into town was bad enough, but the extra added journey to the antiques store might have cinched it for me.*
Atcchan: "Thanks. I would love a ride back home - if you're sure it's okay?"
Amu: "Sure? Of course I'm sure, Atcchan! Don't be silly! I don't say things I don't mean!"
Atcchan: "O-Ow..."
*Did she really need to hit my shoulder like that?*
