*I feel relieved. It seems like my words are finally getting through to her.*
Eri: "Hey. Atcchan."
Atcchan: "A-Aah...?"
*I stare, wide-eyed. I can't help myself.*
*My name. Eri actually said my name...*
*Or nickname, rather, but I suppose that's good enough. Hardly anybody addresses me by my real name. Not even my teachers.*
*Sometimes, even I almost forget what my actual name is, I'm so used to being addressed with this cutesy diminutive.*
Eri: "What are you stuttering for, peasant? You're acting as though I've done something strange."
Atcchan: "W-Well, um... I-It's just... I didn't expect you to use my name..."
*Eri's glare intensifies.*
Eri: "I-It's not as though I wanted to use your name! It's just, saying 'you' or 'moron' or 'peasant' sounds stilted, and I dislike jarring conversation."
Eri: "I'm going to call you Atcchan because you are Atcchan. That makes sense. There's nothing strange about it, okay?"
Eri: "If you dare make any kind of comment, I'll murder you!"
Atcchan: "Ah, um... I was just surprised. If you want to call me that, I don't mind. If anything, it makes me happy..."
Eri: "Ew. Gross."
*I didn't realize my happiness was something so unpleasant to Eri. Maybe I should try to avoid smiling around her...*
Atcchan: "Then... what should I call you? If 'Onodera' and 'Eri' are out, then-"
Eri: "Eri is fine."
Eri: "Even though it pains me, hearing an uncouth commoner like you use it so carelessly. But, as you offered to help me find Shiro tomorrow, perhaps you deserve at least that much."
Eri: "This isn't a fairytale though. I'm not going to pay you in kisses. If I did, I'd have to scour my own tongue with a brush."
Eri: "Besides, even if a beautiful woman like myself were to kiss you, you still wouldn't turn into a handsome prince. That kind of thing never happens in reality."
Eri: "Men shouldn't rely on the love of women to reform them. I have better things to do with my time, so don't get your hopes up!"
Atcchan: "I-I wasn't going to..."
*And, sadly, I know she's telling the truth. I don't think even ordering shady growth enhancement drugs from dubious magazines could turn somebody like me into a tall, dashing prince...*
*Still... Didn't Eri slip something strange in there, amongst her words? What did she say?*
*'As you offered to help me find Shiro tomorrow...'*
*Did I really make that offer? Or has Eri made that offer for me?*
*I open my mouth, ready to ask, but Eri doesn't let me. She pre-empts my question and cuts me down before I can even utter a syllable.*
Eri: "I want you to wait for me by the sunflower field at 9:00 a.m. sharp, tomorrow morning. We're going into town together."
*I feel like saying something, but I don't know what that 'something' should be. Instead, I can only nod my head meekly.*
Atcchan: "W-Well... A-All right... W-Whatever you say."
Eri: "Good. And make sure you bring some money. We're going to need it."
*With that parting comment, she turns on her heel and walks away.*
*I stare at her retreating back as it fades away into the darkness.*
*It's only when she disappears altogether that I allow myself to sigh, expelling the air that was bottled up deep, deep inside my lungs.*
*It feels like I've gotten myself caught up in something complicated.*
*When I get home it's already dark.*
*Dinner is waiting for me on the table, carefully prepared by my grandmother.*
*And so I end up getting a lift home with Amu's dad.*
*Although I know very little about cars, I know enough to realize this car is pretty old. The interior smells funny, and the seats look worn and frayed.*
*It doesn't help that Amu's dad seems to be driving too quickly. As the car speeds along down the country roads, I feel myself being jerked about in the back seat, my body shaking like a pinball.*
*Sitting in the front of the car beside her Father, Amu complains bitterly, her arms folded.*
Amu: "This car is such a piece of junk. Why don't you get a new one, Dad?"
Mr. Jougasaki: "Because times are hard, sweetheart, times are hard. We've gotta make every penny count! Wahahahahaha!"
Amu: "If that's the case, maybe you shouldn't be driving so quickly."
Mr. Jougasaki: "Nonsense, nonsense! Drivin' fast is part of being a man! It makes me feel young again!"
Mr. Jougasaki: "Besides, I've been with Yukiko for almost twenty years now. She can handle it. She's a reliable kind of woman!"
Atcchan: "Y-Yukiko...?"
Amu: "Dad calls the car Yukiko. It's his thing."
Mr. Jougasaki: "Wahahaha! That's right! I could never part with her! She's like the wife I never had!"
Amu: "You do have a wife, though. You're married to her."
*Amu's dad laughs, slapping the steering wheel of the car in good humor. His hands are so large I worry he might split the wheel in two.*
Mr. Jougasaki: "Wahahahaha! Too true, too true. Your mother is a good woman, dear, but she isn't quite the same as ol' Yuki here!"
Mr. Jougasaki: "A man and his car, they have a special bond, you see? Sometimes, that bond is even tighter than the bond between a man and his wife! Wahahahaha!"
Mr. Jougasaki: "Anyway, my boy..."
Atcchan: "Y-Yes...?"
Mr. Jougasaki: "I'll tell you a story. An exciting tale. A story about men, for men!!! It'll really get your blood pumping!"
Amu: "Oh geez."
*Even though I can't see her face, I'm sure Amu's rolling her eyes.*
Mr. Jougasaki: "I keep tryin' to tell Amu here, but she just doesn't get it! She's not a man, I guess. Doesn't think like one! Even though she acts like one! Wahahahaha!"
Amu: "Come on, Dad, cut that out. It's annoying."
Mr. Jougasaki: "Wahahahaha! Now, now, dear, some people are interested in stories like this."
Mr. Jougasaki: "So, so. I'll tell you a tale. A tale about a man and a trout..."
*And so Mr. Jougasaki launches into a very long, very detailed, very boring, and very loud rendition of his heroic fishing feats.*
*I sink lower and lower in my seat the whole while, muttering things like 'I see.' and 'How interesting.' so he knows I'm listening, but I don't think he'd care even if I wasn't.*
*It's clear Mr. Jougasaki isn't interested in having a conversation. He just wants somebody to talk at and boast to. Now that I'm in his car, trapped, with no means of escape... I have no choice but to listen.*
Mr. Jougasaki: "So, lad, do you know how large that fish was? Well, do you? Do you?"
Atcchan: "U-Um, I... I don't know how big the fish you caught was... I couldn't possibly imagine, Sir..."
Mr. Jougasaki: "Wahahahahaha!!! There's no need to be so polite! There's no need to call me 'Sir!' Plain ol' 'Kentaro' will do!"
Atcchan: "O-Oh, um... Y-Yes... O-Of course..."
*But I still don't call Mr. Jougasaki that. It would seem wrong, somehow, given he's such a towering figure... It'd be like calling a mountain a molehill.*
Mr. Jougasaki: "Aah, so, about that fish. It was a trout, you know? A big'un!"
*Amu rolls her eyes.*
Amu: "Dad, do you have to? You've told me this story about a million times already."
Mr. Jougasaki: "Now, now, Amu, don't exaggerate! It's more like five or six, maybe seven, at a push..."
Mr. Jougasaki: "But I'm not being prideful. I'm not being arrogant. I'm simply sharing a darn exciting story, that's all - and you've got to admit, it is darn exciting! Wahahahaha!!!"
Mr. Jougasaki: "You wouldn't understand, Amu. Fishing is a man's world, you know, and only men like me and this young lad here can understand it. You know what I mean? Wahahahahaha!!!"
Amu: "I'm wondering how Mom even puts up with you."
Mr. Jougasaki: "Wahahahahahaha!"
*And so I spend the entirety of the awkward car journey being shouted at by Mr. Jougasaki, as he tells me the 'darn exciting story' of his various fishing exploits...*
*When I get back, it's already starting to get late.*
*I talk to my grandparents for a while, then sit down for another family meal.*
*Grandma really is pulling out all the stops now that I'm back with them. The meals aren't exactly extravagant or complicated, but the quantity of food really is ridiculous.*
*Did Mother tell her I was particularly gluttonous before I came back here? Maybe she's playing a practical joke on me, trying to pay me back for the time I accidentally over-watered her beloved gardenias...*
Grandma: "I hope you like it, dear. Miss Tachibana brought over those spring onions, you know? She grew them in her own garden."
*Aaah, Miss Tachibana... I remember her. She used to be my teacher - the only teacher in the whole school.*
*As my grandmother talks fondly of our neighbors, I start to feel the color rising to my cheeks. It's kind of embarrassing, but... when I was younger I kind of, sort of, maybe just a little, had a tiny bit of a crush on her.*
*I eat my food with a red face, staring down resolutely at the floor.*
*Noticing my discomfort, my grandmother laughs. I wonder if she knows...*
*Even though I never told her about my childhood crush, I wouldn't put it past her. That woman knows everything.*
Grandma: "Come on, dear, eat up! Let's put some more meat on those bones!"
Atcchan: "T-Thanks, but... I..."
*I sigh.*
Atcchan: "I'm not really hungry."
Grandma: "That might be the case, dear, but this is for your own good! If you eat my delicious, rejuvenating food you'll never grow old!"
Grandma: "That's how I've maintained my good looks over the years! And besides..."
*She smiles at me craftily.*
Grandma: "If you eat a lot, you'll become even handsomer, and then you'll have all the girls chasing after you~! "
Atcchan: "G-Grandma...! I-I'm too young to think about that kind of thing!"
Grandma: "Hohohohohoh~"
Grandpa: "Ha! A likely story! I got married to Chiyo here when she was only seventeen, and I haven't regretted it since! Too young indeed!"
Atcchan: "B-But... I-I'm not even seventeen yet, s-so that's still far too early..."
Grandma: "It's never too early to start planning ahead~ The early bird catches the worm!"
Atcchan: "I-I don't know if I should think about girls as worms..."
*And I don't think you should start counting your chickens before they've hatched, either.*
Grandma: "Hohoh~ Yes, yes. You just have to do your best~ Your grandma will be rooting for you~ "
Atcchan: "I appreciate the sentiment, but... rooting for me in what?"
Grandma: "Well, you know... This old woman hopes to live to see the birth of some cute great-grandchildren one day, you know?"
Atcchan: "G-Great-grandchildren?!"
Grandma: "Yes, yes~ I've started to knit some little socks already~ It's the only thing that keeps me going, hohoh~"
Grandpa: "Mm hmm. It'd be nice to have some little nippers around again. You're getting so old already..."
Atcchan: "I-I'm not old! I can't even drink yet!"
Grandma: "You're not as cute as you used to be."
Atcchan: "H-Hey!"
Grandma: "It would use up far too much wool if I tried to knit you socks now, at your age. A frail old lady such as myself might keel over before she could finish a single pair~"
*I'm not sure if I'd describe my grandmother as 'frail.' Even though she is around eighty, she's as energetic as a small child passing notes and giggling in class.*
Grandpa: "For Chiyo's sake, you'll have to do your best, lad!"
Atcchan: "Uwawawa..."
*Why do old people like to tease their grandchildren so much about marriage? Are they really so starved for drama they have to resort to something that cruel?*
*Why can't they just watch TV soap operas like everybody else? Some of them are really good!*
*Aah... It just isn't fair at all!*
Atcchan: "Haa... The fresh air feels good..."
*I breathe in deeply. Although it sounds cliché, the air in the country really does feel more refreshing than the air in the city.*
Atcchan: "Maybe that's why my grandparents still act like children. H-Honestly, teasing me like that..."
*It's dark outside. I think it must be around 8:00 or 9:00 p.m. - I'm not entirely sure.*
*There are no large roads that run through this small village. As such, there's no need for streetlamps. That means when it starts to get dark here, it gets really dark.*
*One would think it unsafe to wander around at night, the only visibility coming from the moon... but that isn't really true.*
*Because so few people live here and everybody knows everyone else, the environment is safe. I don't feel any particular worry.*
*In actuality, I was feeling more concerned sitting in the living room with my grandparents, being teased about great-grandchildren and tiny, knitted socks for tiny, newborn feet...*
*I shudder.*
*I know my grandparents got married when they were only seventeen, but I can't imagine starting a family that young.*
*I do have my friends back in the city - Saki, Miho, and Yuuna - but I wouldn't consider marrying them. The thought hadn't even crossed my mind.*
*More importantly, I'm sure none of them would want to marry me either. I can't think of anything particularly attractive about me that would make me appealing to girls, and I'd be more surprised than anything else if one of my female friends did decide to confess to me. In fact, I'd probably assume it was all some kind of joke.*
*Then there's Amu. I like her a lot - I always have done - and we've known each other ever since we were little. But thinking about that seems kind of strange.*
*It is true that I like her, but I've known her for far too long. She feels like a sister to me.*
*I'm sure if Amu knew I was seriously considering being in a relationship with her, she'd just laugh in my face.*
*And then... there's Noelle...*
Atcchan: "N-No... N-No way..."
*But the moment I think this, I start to feel guilty. I have to reprimand myself verbally, shaking my head at my own thoughts.*
*It is true that Noelle was my closest friend for a very long period of time but...*
*T-That is something... I don't want to think about.*
*After a few moments of musing, trying to force my brain to think about something less embarrassing than potential wives, I come to my senses.*
*I realize, without being really conscious of my own actions, that I've ended up here.*
*I've arrived at a small wooden building, separated from the rest of the village by fields and trees. It's a worn, ramshackle structure that stands all alone, seeming to creak and moan in the wind.*
*It's the school. The only school in the village.*
*My old school: elementary, middle, and high school combined.*
*In the gathering dark, with the pale moon beginning to rise, the building looks like something from a ghost story - eerie, sinister.*
*I shiver, a cold wind snaking up my spine, through my jacket.*
*I didn't notice before, but it's getting pretty chilly.*
*Maybe that's why I can't hear the cicadas. It's too cold for them, so they're all hiding.*
*It makes the atmosphere feel strangely melancholy, as though something vital is missing.*
*Haa...*
*I don't really like being here. It's making me feel uneasy.*
*I want to go back.*
*I turn around, ready to retrace my steps, when-*
Atcchan: "H-Huh...?"
*I hear it.*
*It's a faint creaking sound, carried over some distance.*
*If I were in a horror movie, this would be the noise that would signal my impeding demise at the hands of some apparition from Hell. However, even though I'm easily startled, I do know better than that.*
*Although I don't like ghost stories, I'm sensible enough not to believe in them - even though, as a child, I did used to check in my wardrobe for monsters every night before I went to bed.*
*It isn't a completely alien noise. In fact, I recognize it.*
*When I was younger, it was a sound I heard a lot.*
*It's the sound of a swing.*
*To be more precise, it's the sound of the old, rusty swing situated in the small playground around the back of the school.*
*That playground, overgrown with grass and flowers, was where I used to play during break time at school. Even though it only contained a few swings and a slide, I still found it fun.*
*Because there was so little playground equipment, a lot of the bigger children would get there first, shoving the younger ones out of the way.*
*I remember, during that time, the twelve year old Amu was remorseless. She would shout at the older kids and threaten to hit them, so they ran away in fear. That way, the younger children could play.*
*I think the little kids saw Amu as some kind of hero because of her exploits.*
*That really does take me back...*
*But who is playing on those swings at night? I bet it's one of the kids from the village - though they can't be too young, or else they wouldn't be allowed out by themselves.*
*Even though this village is relatively safe, no parent would want their child out by themselves in the cold. Not at this time.*
*So... who could it be?*
*I'm curious...*
*Silently, I walk around the back of the school building. I take great care where I place my feet, trying not to make any noise.*
*I don't know why, but... I feel kind of excited... and, also, a little bit scared.*
*My heart pounds in my chest. My thoughts tick over quickly, running through a list of possibilities.*
*Maybe it is a ghost after all. The ghost of a young child, playing on a swing in the middle of the night, under the full moon.*
Atcchan: "Y-Yeah right. As if I'd believe in something like that."
*I creep over to the small park quietly. The wind rustles through the long grass, the surrounding trees. An owl hoots overhead.*
*I walk closer. Closer. And closer.*
*And then my breath catches in my throat.*
*On the rusty swing, moving backwards and forwards through the air... I see her.*
*A figure with pale skin, shining under the moonlight. She's wearing a white dress, sleeveless; far too exposing for this weather, surely...?*
*Her arms are long and slender. Even at a distance they look too thin, worryingly so, as though they could snap in two at the slightest bit of pressure.*
*Her white skirts billow out around her bare legs. Her hair flutters around her shoulders, caught in the wind as she moves back and forth.*
*With each movement, I can hear it; the sound of the old swing set creaking in protest. An eerie kind of wail, mixed with the sound of the wind.*
*She really does look like a ghost. Dressed entirely in white, with that pale hair and pale skin...*
*One could be forgiven for letting out a cry of alarm, taking an involuntary step backwards out of fear; their hearts stopping in their chests, eyes widening in surprise.*
*A ghost girl playing on the swing in the darkness, under the full moon. An aesthetic experience that would make for a beautiful photograph or frightening campfire story.*
*But I know it isn't true. This is no ghost.*
*Even at a distance, even after two years, I know her. I recognize her face almost as quickly as I would recognize my own in a mirror.*
*It's Noelle.*
*I don't think she's seen me. She's still swinging; back and forth, back and forth, like a metronome.*
*Should I go up to her? But what would I say?*
*It's been two years. Two whole years. That's a long time.*
*Will she forgive me? Do I deserve to be forgiven? Is she angry, is she upset, does she feel betrayed...?*
*Or, worst of all... does she feel indifferent? Does she no longer care for me at all?*
*She certainly won't be the same girl who used to hide behind my back, clinging to my shirt. Too much time has passed.*
*But she's still Noelle.*
*She's still my best friend. No matter how much time passes... That will never change... Right?*
*But, if that's really true... then why is my heart pounding so hard?*
*Approach Noelle.":
*Just go home.":
*I don't want to do this. It's too early for me to face her.*
*Thinking about what kind of expression she might make after she sees me... makes me feel queasy.*
*Just how hurt will she be?*
*I don't know. It isn't something I want to face. It's something I don't even want to think about.*
*Feeling even more cowardly than before... I make my shameful, dejected way back home.*
*The sound of the old, rusty swing fades into the background... until I can longer hear it.*
Atcchan: "Hey... What are you even thinking? As if you can just turn around and leave now."
*I mutter this under my breath, speaking harshly, as though trying to chastise myself.*
*I can't turn around and leave. Not now.*
*I know this... even though I still feel nervous. But I can't let that worry get the better of me.*
*I've been worrying about this... for far too long.*
*I need to move forward.*
*The sounds of my footsteps, weak and hesitant, mingle with the noise of the swing, creaking in the breeze.*
*My heart feels heavy, as though it's made of lead, dragging my body down. But I don't succumb. I can't.*
*If I gave up now, what would she think?*
*She would probably hate me more than she does already.*
*I can't afford to let her down. Not again. I don't want to betray her expectations.*
*With this thought in mind, I enter the park. It's eerie, lit only by the light of the moon. I've only ever been in here during the day before.*
*Although I've known these friendly, familiar surroundings ever since I was little, they seem strange now. Foreboding. Almost like an alternate reality.*
*I make my way over to the rusty old swing set... and sit down on the spare swing beside Noelle.*
*By this point, she must have seen me. There's no way she couldn't. But she doesn't say anything.*
*She just continues to swing; back and forth, back and forth.*
*Her eyes look misty and far-away. Her pale hair shimmers in the moonlight.*
*I can't help but think, even now... this must be some kind of mirage.*
*It's all a dream.*
*If I were to reach out and touch her... I feel as though my fingertips would poke right through her, out the other side.*
*In that case, if it's a dream... it doesn't matter what I say.*
*Summoning my courage - even though my heart is beating so fast it's a wonder it doesn't leap out of my mouth - I start to talk.*
*After two years... I introduce myself anew.*
Atcchan: "Hey... Um... Noelle...? It's me."
*My voice is quiet, but she still hears me.*
*Seeming to snap out of her trance, she turns her head to one side, ever so slightly.*
*Her eyes meet mine.*
*They're large, light blue, and lined with long lashes.*
*She doesn't look surprised. Her expression doesn't flicker. Instead, she merely nods; a very slight acknowledgment, as though I'm any old acquaintance. An utterly meaningless person.*
*But at least she stops swinging.*
*Her motions come to a halt. The grinding, creaking noise dies down; swallowed by the silence of the night, the sound of the wind.*
*Somehow, without that noise... the atmosphere starts to feel even more intense. Although I found that sound grating, now... I almost wish I had it back. That Noelle was still swinging.*
*Then the rapid thud, thud, thud of my heartbeat wouldn't sound so stupidly loud.*
Atcchan: "Noelle...?"
*I venture again, my voice shaking. In response, she nods her head.*
Atcchan: "It's really you...?"
*She gives me another nod. It's a very slight motion, one that could be easily missed, but I catch it out of the corner of my eye.*
*Noelle was always like this. Quiet.*
Atcchan: "Do you recognize me...?"
Noelle: "..."
Noelle: "Atcchan...?"
*Her voice is soft.*
*She doesn't use my real name - instead, it's that nickname; the one Amu coined for me in childhood, which stuck ever since.*
*Somehow, it feels very nostalgic... and very warm.*
Atcchan: "Y-Yeah... It's me."
Noelle: "Ah... Atcchan... You came back?"
Atcchan: "Mm... Just for a little while, but... I came back. I-I... I..."
Atcchan: "I was still thinking of you the whole time, though. I missed you..."
Noelle: "Atcchan... Atcchan..."
*Noelle looks at me with her large, light blue eyes. Some people say that her intense gaze is disturbing, but I've never thought that.*
*...*
*The silence encircles us. It takes Noelle a short while to piece together her thoughts and feelings. That's hardly surprising. It has been a long time since we last saw each other.*
*A small smile, barely visible... begins to bloom on her lips.*
Noelle: "Atcchan... Welcome home."
*The two of us sit there for a while, neither saying a word. The cold wind brushes against my skin, making me shudder.*
*It takes me a while before I can find the words; dredging them up out of my head, into my mouth. They're words I should have said long, long ago.*
Atcchan: "Noelle... I'm sorry."
Noelle: "Huh...? Why are you sorry? I don't understand."
Atcchan: "Y-You don't...?"
Noelle: "No."
Atcchan: "Then you... You're not angry at me?"
Noelle: "Why should I be angry...?"
Atcchan: "Because I... I..."
*I wince.*
Atcchan: "Because I left you. You were so important to me, but... I still left."
Noelle: "... I know... but I'm not angry."
Atcchan: "R-Really?"
Noelle: "Yeah. It isn't your fault that your parents moved away. Why should I blame you for that?"
Atcchan: "B-Because... Because, even though we were always so close, I... I was scared, and worried you would be upset. I didn't want to hurt you."
Atcchan: "I was a coward. I was weak and I... I never told you...!"
*That's right.*
*The reason I feel so guilty... is because of that.*
*I never told my best friend I was leaving.*
*One day I was there, eating lunch with her at school and doing our homework together... and the next day, I was gone.*
*I told everyone else, but... the one person I didn't tell was the one person who would care the most. And it was all because I was a coward, far too afraid to see her unhappy. Too afraid to break the bad news.*
*I really am... the worst...*
Atcchan: "Don't you feel betrayed...?"
Noelle: "Everything and everybody has to change at some point. Nothing stays the same forever."
Atcchan: "But you were angry, right...? W-Weren't you angry...?"
*Noelle tilts her head to one side, lips parted in a small 'o'.*
Noelle: "Do you want me to be?"
Atcchan: "Of course not, but-"
Noelle: "Then I won't be."
Noelle: "I don't like being angry. It doesn't ever change anything. It only makes things more difficult. It's a pointless emotion."
Atcchan: "B-But whether it has a point or not... I think that after what I did to you, you have a right to feel just a little bit angry."
Noelle: "..."
Noelle: "Maybe I did... feel a little bit sad. But not angry."
Atcchan: "Sad...?"
Noelle: "Mm. That our fun times came to an end so quickly. It was upsetting."
Atcchan: "I-I'm sorry... I didn't want to make you sad."
Noelle: "It's all right. I'm not sad anymore."
Atcchan: "Why not...?"
*A cold breeze runs through the park, making me shudder. The hem of Noelle's skirt ripples like ocean waves.*
*She always did dress in white, didn't she?*
Noelle: "Because you came back. You came back to me and said sorry. So there's no reason to be sad. Not anymore."
*And, with these words, Noelle smiles at me.*
*It's a gentle smile, devoid of malice.*
*The two of us sit together for a while in companionable silence, under the moon. The rusty equipment of this old park is bathed under the silver light from the moon, making the mundane look eerie and haunting.*
*This really does feel like some kind of fantasy...*
*The sharp feeling of metal against my bare fingers helps to keep me grounded. The cold burrows into my flesh, making my fingers spasm.*
Atcchan: "Aren't you cold?"
Noelle: "Not really."
Atcchan: "You sure you don't want my jacket?"
Noelle: "I'm sure."
Atcchan: "But you're wearing a sleeveless dress. That can't be comfortable, can it?"
Noelle: "I'm used to it. People can get used to a lot of things."
Atcchan: "Yeah... I guess that's true. I did move to the city, after all."
Noelle: "I don't think I'd like to live in a city."
Atcchan: "I don't know if you'd say that if you could see the convenience stores out there. You can buy almost anything you want, all around the clock. Isn't that amazing?"
Noelle: "Any... thing...?"
Atcchan: "Yeah, anything! Even those jello drinks you like so much."
Noelle: "Jello...?"
Noelle: "Do they do all kinds of different flavors?"
Atcchan: "Yeah, all different kinds. They're big convenience stores, you know?"
Noelle: "R-Really...? Really, really?"
Atcchan: "W-Well, it isn't a lie..."
*Why would I lie about something so trivial?*
*Noelle leans forward on the seat of her swing. It creaks as she does so.*
*There's a strangely happy expression on her face - one that I never usually see. Even her cheeks look a little flushed.*
Noelle: "Is there even strawberry jello?!"
Atcchan: "Of course there is. That's a common flavor."
Noelle: "And melon?"

Atcchan: "I, um... I wasn't suggesting otherwise, I was simply offering-"
Eri: "It's fine. I don't need your pity. That would not help Shiro."
Atcchan: "Then... You don't think Shiro is hiding in this convenience store, do you?"
Eri: "Don't be a fool. I'm not a small-minded country bumpkin like you."
Eri: "Perhaps you believe in conspiracy theories, such as convenience store food being made up from wild animal meat, but I refuse to buy into such notions."
*I eye the various items of food on the shelves dubiously.*
Atcchan: "I never even knew there were rumors like that."
*Eri rolls her eyes.*
Eri: "And that is the difference between you and I. One of us actually has a modicum of intelligence."
Eri: "Anyway. In case you can't work it out on your own, we came here to use that."
Atcchan: "That?"
*My eyes follow Eri's finger. She's pointing at the corner of the convenience store, next to the cashier's counter.*
*It's a photocopier.*
Atcchan: "We're using this...?"
Eri: "Yes. For this."
*Eri reaches into her pocket and procures a sheet of folded paper. Straightening it out, she thrusts it into my face.*
*Missing, Shiro - beloved pet rabbit. White, with red eyes and floppy ears. If found, return to Onodera Eri.*
Eri: "All right. Now we need to hand these out."
*Eri and I stand together on a street corner, our arms laden with photocopy prints of the homemade poster she made.*
*I have to admire Eri's dedication. The sheer amount of energy she's expending on this project is commendable.*
*It's a warm day, much like yesterday. The sunshine beats down gently, reflecting off the windows of the various small stores scattered around us.*
*I hear cars go past in a light trickle of traffic, a pleasant background noise compared to that of the city.*
*People scurry to and fro around me: alone, in couples, or in clusters.*
*For some reason, there are a lot of couples out today. Everywhere I look I see men and women of all ages; giggling over private jokes, sharing ice cream cones, clinging to one another, pointing out things in shop windows...*
*Since the weather's so nice, it must be a perfect day to go on a date.*
*And yet, somehow...*
*I lift my head, looking up at Eri.*
*She's staring down her surroundings with an intense, serious expression, lips pursed. She looks like a lion, ready to go in for the kill.*
*It guess today won't be a relaxing one spent eating ice cream, window shopping and finding interesting shapes in clouds with a significant other after all...*
*Instead, I've been strung along by this self-proclaimed princess, acting as her impromptu butler on the hunt for her missing rabbit.*
*... Well, that might be kind of exciting, too.*
*I've never been on a date before, so it's not like I'd know what to do. I'd probably just make a fool out of myself.*
Eri: "Hey! Whaddaya think you're doing?! This is no time to be spacing out, moron!"
Atcchan: "A-Ah, I'm sorry! I just got caught up thinking..."
Eri: "If your thoughts weren't about the welfare of Shiro then they're worthless."
Eri: "I bet you were thinking about pointless things, like dates and romance and ice cream, huh?"
Atcchan: "Ah..."
*I stare at Eri. Although I don't go so far as to spell my disbelief out in words, it must be fairly apparent on my face, because Eri snorts.*
Eri: "You had a stupid look in your eyes. A cowy look."
Atcchan: "Cowy...?"
Eri: "Yes. Like cows in fields staring off into the distance, eating grass with empty heads. A cowy look."
Eri: "All couples have it. That dumb, vacant stare. It pisses me off."
Eri: "Listen. Don't think about any gross or unpleasant things around me, okay? If you do, I'll never forgive you!"
Atcchan: "Ah... I... I won't, I promise."
Eri: "Good. And we need to give these out. Do it quickly."
*I bow my head in assent, not bothering to add any extraneous comments.*
*I worry it might provoke Eri's ire further if I do.*
*Eri and I split up, both of us handing out posters.*
*Although I find talking to strangers unnerving, I find the prospect of Eri's anger even more so.*
*And more than that... I genuinely do want to cheer her up. Even though Shiro is only a rabbit (with a poorly chosen name), I know how much Eri cares for him. It would be cruel of me to give up now.*
*I visit various shops along the street, asking the people behind the counters if they'll display the poster in their windows.*
*I also hand a few out to random people on the street, and buy some tape from a craft store to put them up on walls and street lights.*
*Eventually, I make my way back to the main street, right back where I began.*
*There's one more destination weighing on my mind, however... and this one isn't solely related to Shiro.*
Amu: "Hello, customer! Will you be dining alone today? Is there - oh. Hello, stranger."
*Amu greets me with a small smile.*
Atcchan: "Ah... Hey there, Amu. Fancy seeing you here."
Amu: "Ehehe~ I could say the same about you."
*Despite her cheery tone, Amu sounds tired. Her ponytail is even more disorderly than usual, and her face is slightly flushed.*
*Being cramped inside a small building on such a hot day, forced to wait tables with a polite smile on standby, must be quite challenging...*
Atcchan: "You look tired. Are you all right?"
Amu: "Kukuku~ Silly Atcchan, that's ru~ude~"
Atcchan: "It's rude to worry about your health?"
Amu: "No, not that. I'm actually quite flattered by your attentions."
*She says it with a wink which would cause anybody's heart to flutter. I think, for a few brief seconds, mine actually does.*
Amu: "However, it is impolite to tell a lady she looks tired! You might make her feel bad!"
Atcchan: "O-Oh, I'm sorry. I hope I didn't hurt your feelings?"
Amu: "Nah, it's okay. At least when I smile at you, I actually mean it. Unlike when I have to look at the other customers! Wahaha~!"
*At Amu's mutinous words, I hear an offended gasp, emitting from a well-turned out family sitting at a nearby table.*
Atcchan: "Amu... I think they heard you..."
Amu: "Ah... I'm sorry. My bad. Ehehe..."
*Amu apologizes awkwardly to the family, giving them a small bow.*
*When she turns back to me, however, she's sighing. I wonder how sincere that apology was...*
Amu: "Man... This always happens. Dad scolds me all the time for upsetting the customers..."
Atcchan: "Then... don't you think you should cut it out? Or try to be offensive a little more quietly...?"
*Amu sighs, clicking her neck with a noise so piercing it makes a young girl eating an ice cream sundae jump in alarm.*
Amu: "But if I can't vent my frustrations I'll get so keyed up I might explode!"
Atcchan: "A-Ahaha... W-Well, I wouldn't want that either..."
Amu: "Besides, I'm not the only one who looks worn down! You seem kind of rough around the edges too!"
*She's right, of course. I've been in a heightened state of frantic anxiety all day, rushing around after Eri.*
*Now that I'm in familiar territory, conversing with a friendly(?) face, I'm starting to feel more relaxed.*
*The soothing smell of coffee beans, deep and rich, helps. It mingles with various other comforting scents, of cake and cookies and fresh bread, bringing a smile to my lips.*
Amu: "Come on, you can go sit at the back. I'll get you some fruit juice or something. You look like you need to cool down!"
Atcchan: "Ah... T-Thank you..."
*Touched by Amu's unexpected kindness, my face turns pink.*
*I follow her retreating back through the café, navigating around tables containing families and - of course - couples out on dates.*
*Amu leads me to a small, secluded spot at the back of the café, away from the other patrons.*
*This is another unexpected gesture of kindness. I feel touched that she factored my inherent dislike of crowds into my seating arrangement...*
Amu: "Kukuku~ Don't start thinking sappy stuff, now, Atcchan."
Atcchan: "H-Huh...? What do you mean?"
*Amu grins.*
Amu: "When I said I'd get you that juice, I didn't mean it was on the house. Just because you're my friend, that doesn't mean you get a discount~ "
*Ah...*
*Has my own childhood friend lured me into her café under false pretenses, solely to steal my money?*
*My poor wallet must be crying right now. It's suffered far too many indignities for one day...*
*Even after Amu writes down my order, it takes a while for her to actually serve me my juice.*
*She looks rushed off her feet. The tables in here are positively crammed with people, chatting together noisily; all demanding this, that or the other.*
*A sulky looking little boy knocks his food onto the floor. An old woman complains that her tea is too hot. A young man asks Amu if she wouldn't mind writing a cute message on his omelet rice in ketchup, which makes Amu's face go unusually red.*
*I thought that kind of thing was only for maid cafés? But when Amu tries to argue the point, the man reminds her, leering unpleasantly, 'The customer is always right.'*
*The minutes go by slowly.*
*With each passing second, Amu looks more and more disheveled - like a slowly rotting watermelon (not that that's a very flattering comparison). More strands of hair worm their way free from her ponytail, beads of sweat gathering on her forehead.*
*I never knew working at a café could be so difficult.*
*Finally, some ten minutes after I placed my order, Amu delivers my drink.*
Amu: "Sorry for the slow service, Atcchan. You're my friend, so I thought it'd be okay if I slacked off on your order a little. Kukuku~"
*Although she's laughing her usual laugh, it sounds strained and less lighthearted than usual.*
*I think being forced to write that cute message - adding hearts, no less - on that man's food might have been the final straw.*
Atcchan: "Is working here always so hard?"
Amu: "Ehehe... It depends on what customers you get. Some people can be pretty entitled."
Atcchan: "Yeah, I noticed."
Amu: "Geez. I'd like to slam some of their heads against a wall. Or hit them with a baseball bat. Give them a really good beating, you know?"
*Amu's threat is made all the more disturbing by the fact she's rolling up her sleeves...*
Atcchan: "A-Ahaha... Maybe you should try to keep that impulse under control for now?"
*She pouts.*
Amu: "I do my best. But if I snap one day, and reduce this whole place to a sea of blood I won't be held accountable for my actions!"
Amu: "I'm sick of hearing young children cry all the time, you know?"
Amu: "You'd think their parents would have some pity on poor people like me, who have to work at crappy places like this for virtually no money, and have the decency not to bring their little kids along when they're teething..."
Amu: "I'm never going to have any children, Atcchan. Never."
Amu: "If I hear another wailing brat I might lose it."
*Amu leans against the wall, arms folded, head hanging. Despite the violence of her words, she seems far too tired to actually carry her threats out.*
*This, I decide, is probably a good thing. I wouldn't want Amu to become a murderer over something so petty.*
*I take a sip of my orange juice, relishing the soothing sensation as it slides down my throat. Then I offer the glass to Amu.*
Atcchan: "You want some?"
Amu: "Huh? Are you offering me an indirect kiss, Atcchaaan?"
Atcchan: "H-Huh? N-No, I, um... A-Aah..."
Amu: "Kukuku~ I had no idea you were so bold! "
Atcchan: "A-Aah...! T-That is, I-I mean-"
Amu: "I guess that's what happens when you move to the city! You get surrounded by all these super confident city girls and you start to lose your inhibitions!"
Atcchan: "W-Waah... I-It's not like that... I-I just thought maybe you would like a drink...?"
Amu: "Nah, it's okay. In warm weather, drinking something hot is actually better for you."
Atcchan: "Really...?"
Amu: "Yeah. Hot drinks make you sweat. When the sweat evaporates, you cool down quicker."
Atcchan: "I didn't know that..."
Amu: "Mmhmm~ Tea really is the best drink for any occasion, you know? If you're Japanese, you can't not love tea!"
*Even though I've known about it for years, Amu's love for traditionally Japanese food and drink always strikes me as odd. It seems out of character, somehow...*
Amu: "But anyway, that's enough about me. Talking about work is way too depressing. How 'bout you, Atcchan?"
Atcchan: "Oh, um..."
Atcchan: "Actually... I've been working too."
Amu: "You have? Where? And why?"
Atcchan: "Oh... Somebody forced me into it, and I thought it would be mean to say no..."
Amu: "Is that what these are for?"
*Amu picks up one of the photocopied posters, left in a neat pile on the top of the table, and examines it.*
Atcchan: "Yeah. I got dragged into helping this girl search for her rabbit. I'm sure you know her, it's-"
*But the look on Amu's face makes the words die in my throat.*
*Amu lets the poster drop to the ground carelessly. It flutters through the air like a leaf caught in the breeze; landing, not on the table, but on the floor.*
*Somehow, this very simple act... seems strangely aggressive.*
*Maybe it's because Amu was talking about smashing in skulls so freely a few seconds ago. Am I just being paranoid?*
Amu: "Eri? Why're you helping her?"
*The guile in Amu's tone is unmistakable.*
Atcchan: "Ah... You... You don't like Eri...?"
Amu: "No, I don't. I can't stand her."
Atcchan: "But... I thought you two used to be friends? Even though you argued a lot you still got on, right...?"
Amu: "We don't now. Not anymore."
Amu: "It's not even worth talking about. Just thinking about her is making me mad."
*I know Eri is annoying, but that's kind of harsh...":
*I don't think Eri is a bad person, though.":
Amu: "You don't, do you?"
*Amu glares, hands on her hips, but I try not to waver.*
*I don't really know why I'm defending Eri. I just... I don't think she's so bad - not really. Sure, she says some pretty mean things, and can be quite harsh, but...*
*Being with her is kind of fun, I suppose - in a weird way.*
Atcchan: "A-Ah, no... I don't..."
Amu: "But she acts so spoiled and selfish, always putting on such ridiculous airs and graces! It ticks me off!"
Atcchan: "Well... She is quite stubborn, and sometimes she says rude things, but-"
Amu: "But what? Why are you trying to make excuses for somebody you barely know? I thought I was supposed to be your friend?"
*Ah... I don't understand...*
*Amu looks so mad  now, but she and Eri... even though they used to squabble about petty things all the time, they got along well.*
*Didn't they used to be friends...?*
*I'm not remembering it wrong, am I?*
*I open my mouth, ready to ask, when-*
Amu: "If you know she's annoying then why are you hanging out with her?"
*I guess that's a fair question. Because I was roped into it? I have always been bad at saying no. Whenever people in the street try to talk me into donating for X charity, or accepting packs of pocket tissues, I'm incapable of saying no...*
*I think the worst time was when I got held up by a young woman trying to champion a new animal shelter for a whole hour. After that, I almost always tried to go out with Saki, Miho or Yuuna by my side, to protect me...*
*But... Maybe there's more to Eri's appeal than that.*
*I simply couldn't leave her alone. Not when she was searching, so earnestly, for something so dear to her. I think that kind of passion is... admirable.*
*It actually reminds me a little of Amu. She can be stubborn like that, too.*
*I open my mouth, but... the words stick inside my throat.*
*Amu's expression... really is scary...*
*But before I can respond-*
???: "There you are! I thought I'd find you slacking off in here!"
*There, standing in the entrance of the café, hands on her hips and a dangerous glare on her face...*
Amu: "Hello, customer. Will you be dining alone today? Or perhaps I should just assume you will be. I can't imagine anybody would want to sit with you."
*It's Eri.*
*When the doors behind her swing closed with a thud, dead silence falls upon the café.*
*People stop talking. Chairs stop scraping. Chopsticks stop moving.*
*Even little toddlers and irritable young children fall quiet, their mouths open mid-scream.*
*It's so quiet I swear I can hear the separate dust particles swirling about in the air.*
*The customers look at Eri. Then at Amu. Back to Eri. Back to Amu.*
*Over and over again, their eyes traverse the full length of the café, from one side, to the other.*
*They wait with baited breath, like a vast crowd at a festival, preparing themselves for the moment when the fireworks are launched.*
*Any second now, they'll see sparks. That's what they want. I'm sure of it.*
Eri: "Hello, Amu. I see you're just as rude as you ever were."
Amu: "And I see you're just as arrogant."
Eri: "Hmph."
*Eri makes her characteristic snort of derision, turning her nose up in the air.*
*Amu cracks her knuckles together. The sound splits through the silence of the café like a gunshot.*
*The two of them continue to stare each other down like cowboys in a Western. Any second now, I fear one of them will draw their gun and shoot.*
Eri: "I don't have enough time to talk to a mere waitress such as yourself, Amu. Step aside, please. I have some business with that person over there."
Amu: "I'm sorry, but 'that person over there' has a name. Atcchan has no reason to follow your commands if he doesn't want to."
Eri: "And yet, for one supposedly so concerned about her friend, you haven't asked him what he wants to do either, have you?"
Amu: "That's because you're such an unpleasant person nobody in their right mind would want to spend a second in your company!"
Eri: "Hohoh? That's funny. I could say the same about you."
*Eri's voice is cold, hard as iron. She fills her voice with as much malice as possible, like loading a bullet into the chamber of a gun.*
*When the word leaves her lips, it fires and explodes in Amu's face with a shower of malice.*
Eri: "Traitor."
*But Amu is strong.*
*Even though she recoils, she does not stumble.*
*Eri has used up her own ammunition - and now it's Amu's turn.*
*Eri can only watch, unable to defend herself, as Amu prepares to take her own shot.*
Amu: "I didn't do anything wrong. I told you that already. If you can't get that through your thick skull then there really is no hope for you."
Eri: "Maybe you're right. Maybe I was foolish. But you are a liar, Amu."
Eri: "You are a liar and you are a traitor, and if you refuse to admit to it that is simply proof of your own rotten heart."
*Amu glares at Eri, staring her down.*
*Her gaze is so intense even Eri falters, taking a small step backwards.*
*And, in this moment... I know.*
*Amu knows. Eri knows.*
*Everybody in the café knows.*
*It's a foregone conclusion.*
Amu: "So. My heart is rotten, is it?"
Eri: "Yes. That's exactly what I'm saying, you traitor."
*Eri makes a halfhearted attempt to fight back, but... at this stage, it's impossible. She's already used her best shot. She has no way to defend herself.*
*All she can do now... is wait for the inevitable.*
Amu: "Heh. If my heart really is rotten, then surely I wouldn't be the one Atcchan is sitting with right now."
Eri: "Grrr..."
Amu: "And, moreover..."
*Amu's lips quirk upwards. Her smile is merciless, demonic.*
*Here it is. I can feel it. Amu's last move. The ace up her sleeve.*
Amu: "If you really are such a kind, gentle lady..."
Amu: "... then your rabbit wouldn't have abandoned you to begin with."
Eri: "Haa..."
*Eri's eyes widen. The words strike her, sharply, across her face.*
*Placing one hand against her cheek, flushed red, she whimpers.*
*It's a noise of absolute defeat.*
*There it is. A perfect victory.*
*I almost expect the crowd to start cheering. Who knows? Maybe they will.*
*Maybe they would have done, at least. Until...*
*.........*
*White and pink stripes.*
*Standing right behind Amu is a young boy, around five or six years old... pulling up her skirt.*
Amu: "Wa... Wawawa... Waaaa..."
*Amu stands there for a while, trembling, hands clasped at her front. Her face is bright red.*
*And then, finally...*
Amu: "K-Kyaaaaaa...!"
*She screams.*
*At this moment, all hell breaks loose.*
*The people sitting at the tables, once so quiet, break out into chatter causing sound to bubble through the cafe like a tidal wave.*
*Almost at once, the babies resume crying. A young girl knocks her omelet rice on the floor, the plate splintering into several pieces with a crash. A few concerned onlookers approach Amu, asking after her well-being.*
*A young, well-dressed woman - presumably the little boy's mother - leaps forwards, grabbing hold of her son's arm.*
Well-dressed woman: "I'm sorry, Miss, I'm so sorry!"
Young boy: "Nooo! Wanna see the lady, wanna see!"
Well-dressed woman: "Stop that, Taro! I'm sorry, Miss! I thought I'd brought him up better than that, he-"
Young boy: "Wanna see the lady! Wanna see the lady!"
Well-dressed woman: 1 "Are you all right, dear?"
Well-dressed woman: 2 "Must have been a dreadful shock, I'm sure...!"
Young boy: 2 "Ahahaha, cool! I didn't know you got that kind of service here!"
Young boy: 3 "Hey, don't say that, dude - can't you see she's upset?"
Young boy: "Wanna see the lady! Wanna see the lady! Wanna plaaaay!!"
Well-dressed woman: "No, Taro, you can't play like that! It's not allowed! Bad!"
Young boy: "Wanted to hide. Wanted to play circus!"
Well-dressed woman: "A woman's skirt is not a circus tent, Taro!"
Young boy: "But, mommy...!!!"
Well-dressed woman: 1 "Do you need a drink, dear? Do you want to sit down?"
Young boy: 2 "But they were pink and white stripes... Pink and white...!"
Young boy: 3 "You're a really unpleasant person, aren't you...?"
Young boy: "Wanna play! WA-NNA PLAAAAAAAAY!"
Amu: "Wa... W-Wawawawa..."
*Amu recoils under their curious stares, pressing her hands against her face to shield it from public view.*
*At the same time, I feel a warm, soft sensation grip my hand.*
*It's Eri.*
Eri: "Come on. Let's go."
Atcchan: "B-But Amu is-"
Eri: "I said, let's go."
*And so, in the chaos and confusion, Eri drags me away. We flee together, like two criminals escaping a crime scene.*
*The two of us end up at the small park I visited yesterday.*
*This park is a peaceful place. Cut off from the main road by a large canopy of trees, almost all the noise from the outside world is obscured by the gentle ambience of nature.*
*The wind runs through the trees, making the leaves shake. A few birds twitter amongst themselves, as though in conversation.*
*Some pieces of discarded litter, the pages from a newspaper and the packaging of a convenience store sandwich, roll along the ground.*
*It is in this quiet, secluded area, surrounded by greenery, bathed in gentle light...*
Eri: "U-Uuu..."
*That Eri starts to cry.*
*Was she holding those tears back throughout our walk here? Is that why her lips were pursed so tight, her face so stony?*
Atcchan: "Ah..."
*I reach forwards ineffectually, my hand hovering over her shoulder, unsure whether to pat it or not. I don't know if she'd appreciate it. Maybe she'd think I was pitying her.*
Atcchan: "A-Are you... all right...?"
Eri: "Do I look like I'm all right?"
Atcchan: "No... I guess not. That's why I was asking..."
Eri: "I-If you can see it for yourself... why should I have to spell it out for you? A-Are you trying to... make fun of me..?"
*Eri's voice is punctuated by sniffles. She pauses to wipe her eyes with the backs of her hands.*
*For a person like Eri, who seems so concerned about her outward appearance, I worry she might find this candid display of emotion embarrassing.*
*I fish around in my pocket and procure some paper tissues. I'm never without these paper tissues. I'm always prepared, for any eventuality. Except, perhaps, a time slip.*
Atcchan: "Here. You can use this, if you want."
*Eri glares at me. It's impressive she's able to transmit that much hatred through her teary eyes.*
Eri: "What? You want me, Onodera Eri, to wipe my eyes with those snotty tissues that have been in your pocket for who knows how long?"
Atcchan: "I-I just thought you might appreciate it... And they're not snotty."
Eri: "Hmph. Why should I appreciate it? I never asked for them."
*I try to assume a friendly, yet polite and respectful, smile as I bow my head.*
Atcchan: "I do apologize for my impudence. I merely thought Milady was in the need of some assistance - and I, being but her humble butler-"
Eri: "Kyaaa..."
*Eri squeals weakly, a gentle blush rising to her face.*
*The noise is marred, however, by a tear-choked hiccough that pushes its way past her lips right after.*
Eri: "Hikk...!"
Atcchan: "Ah... A-Are you all right?"
Eri: "You already asked me that question, moron, and I am -"
Eri: "- hikk! -"
Eri: "- fine."
Atcchan: "You sure you don't want a tissue?"
Eri: "If you're offering the tissues then -"
Eri: "- hikk! -"
Eri: "- I'll take the stupid tissues."
*And with that, Eri snatches the tissues from my hand without a word of thanks.*
*Well... It's about what I was expecting, so I don't get too upset.*
*She dries her eyes and blows her nose, giving the most delicate of sniffles as she does so.*
*When she lifts her head she looks a little better than she did before, though her eyes are still rimmed with red. At least she isn't crying, though. The hiccups have stopped, too.*
Atcchan: "Are you all right...?"
Eri: "You've asked me that three times already. Don't you ever get sick of saying the same thing over and over?"
Atcchan: "A-Ah... I-I guess not?"
*I sigh.*
Atcchan: "Maybe you're right. Maybe I really am stupid..."
Eri: "..."
Eri: "Hmph. It's all right. A fool will be a fool, no matter what. Leotards can't change. Something about spots."
*Leotards...?*
Atcchan: "A-Actually, I, um... I think people can change. I-It's a natural process, I think?"
Eri: "Well, that might be true as well. Amu definitely did."
Atcchan: "I thought you two used to be friends?"
Eri: "We're not now. Not anymore."
*Eri shuts down this line of conversation swiftly, as though bringing down the blade of a guillotine. It's plain, regardless of what happened between her and Amu, she doesn't want to talk about it.*
Eri: "Hey. You."
*I blink, lifting my head. Eri has gotten to her feet, a sour look on her face.*
Atcchan: "What is it?"
Eri: "There's somewhere I want to go. Come on."
Atcchan: "A-Aah...!"
*But Eri doesn't wait for an answer. She hauls me unceremoniously to my feet, her sharp fingernails digging into my hand.*
*Where on earth is she storing all of that strength, anyway? Her arms are as skinny as drinking straws...*
*It really is a mystery...*
Atcchan: "Huh? Why did we come here?"
*I look around my surroundings with some confusion.*
*Eri has led me to a small antiques store in a secluded part of town, divorced from the steady flow of traffic and groups of people by the main road.*
*This antiques store isn't entirely unfamiliar to me. I've been here several times before with Noelle.*
*Noelle has a fascinating love for old bits of junk, dolls with missing limbs, and supposedly 'valuable' ornaments covered in dust and dented in various places, so we always used to come here together.*
*I would wait in one corner while Noelle amused herself, looking around the shelves with wide eyes, examining each and every object that caught her fancy.*
*This place is just as rundown as I remember. The shop is so old it almost looks like an antique itself - but not one of any particular value.*
*I worry one wrong movement, one misplaced foot, will send my whole body straight through the floorboards, leaving behind nothing but an Atcchan-shaped hole in the ground.*
*Although the store looks small on the outside, it's surprisingly large within. This is something I know from firsthand experience, given how much time Noelle could spend in here...*
*Almost every square inch of the floor is covered in supposed 'antiques' - although (and I'm not often a cynical person) 'junk' would probably be a more accurate term.*
*Various items are on display in cabinets. Chess sets with missing pieces, crockery and cutlery, small collections of ceramic figures, watches, fans, candlesticks - all sorts of things.*
*And... what else is over there? A card table, a large mirror, a bird house, a grandfather clock, some paintings and an old hat stand - but these are only the more notable objects. I'm sure there are more.*
*The air smells stale. The floorboards, covered by a very ugly carpet, creak ominously underfoot. There are cobwebs in the corners where the walls meet the ceiling.*

Note: "TO MY BELOVED CUSTOMERS: PLEASE WOULD YOU KINDLY CLOSE THE DOOR WHEN YOU ENTER THE SHOP, FOR THAT IS WHAT A DOOR IS FOR. THANK YOU :)"

Atcchan: "O-Ow..."

Noelle: "Are you all right?"

*And who says 'Just peachy.' in this day and age? What am I going to come out with next? 'Golly gosh?' 'Oh crumbs?' 'Fiddlesticks?' The possibilities are endless - unlike my self-esteem...*
Noelle: "Then, shall we continue with our search?"
*Why do you want to search?":
*Why do you like ghost stories so much?":
Atcchan: "Um... W-Why do you like ghost stories so much, though?"
Noelle: "Ghost stories, hm?"
Noelle: "It's hard to explain."
Noelle: "I suppose... They're comforting."
Atcchan: "Comforting?"
*I've heard a few different replies to that question, but I don't think 'comforting' was ever one of them.*
*When I asked Saki why she liked ghost stories so much, her response was more along the lines of 'They're so romantic and mysterious.' But she definitely didn't say they were 'comforting.'*
*I don't think Saki likes comforting things very much. She's a very anti-comfort kind of girl.*
Noelle: "I suppose so. In a certain kind of way."
Atcchan: "I thought liking ghost stories was just about preferences. Like, some people like romance films and some people like action?"
Noelle: "Some people like jello and some people don't?"
Atcchan: "Yeah, kind of."
Noelle: "Although the people who don't like jello are all wrong, of course."
*Ahaha... She really is passionate about that jello.*
Noelle: "Well... I can't speak for everyone. Just myself. I only live inside my own head, after all. But, for me..."
Noelle: "Ghost stories... often stem from tragic circumstances."
Noelle: "The heartbroken lover... The jilted bride... The bullied child... The person who got into an unfortunate accident..."
Noelle: "These are the kinds of stories that spawn ghosts. Most of them are born from sad or lonely or unlucky people who didn't do anything wrong."
*Noelle continues to coil that strand of hair around and around her finger, until she's almost worked her way up to her scalp.*
Noelle: "I think ghost stories are comforting. They give people who were badly treated in life a chance to come back and take revenge. Even if it is only fictional."
Noelle: "Don't you think?"
*Noelle starts to unwind that strand of hair from around her finger, letting it spring free - and, just like that, I am released from her spell.*
*Her voice... really was sincere. It sounded like a topic dear to her heart, though I'm not entirely sure why.*
Atcchan: "I... I understand. I think."
Noelle: "It's all right if you don't. Maybe I didn't explain it very well."
Atcchan: "N-No, it's okay. I get it - I do!"
Atcchan: "When you talk about ghosts like that... I start to feel a little sorry for them. Maybe I've been discriminating against them this whole time."
*Noelle smiles.*
Noelle: "I suppose they are quite tragic, aren't they? It isn't the ghosts you should sympathize with, though."
Noelle: "It's the real people who inspire the ghost stories. The flesh and blood human beings, who have been suffering for so long - and so not know what to do. They're the ones who really deserve your sympathy?"
Atcchan: "I... I suppose so."
Noelle: "When people are dead you can't help them anymore. You can only help people who are alive. So..."
Noelle: "If you see somebody alive, who is in pain... You should try to help them. It might prevent more ghost stories from being told. From needing to exist."
Atcchan: "Au... W-Why do you want to search so much to begin with?"
Noelle: "It's fun. Like looking for edible mushrooms in the forest."
Atcchan: "Y-You think this is fun?"
Noelle: "Yes. Like a scavenger hunt."
*Too bad we're not searching for nice, innocuous things, like 'a pair of glasses' or 'an interestingly shaped leaf'...*
Noelle: "Your face is all red so you must think it's exciting too, right?"
Atcchan: "Hau... Auau..."
*I whimper, looking down at the floor.*
*The only reason my face is red is because I'm embarrassed... But how do I tell Noelle that?*
Noelle: "Then, shall we go?"
*I watch, eyes widening in horror, as Noelle turns about, ready to walk away.*
*Her footsteps fill the cavernous silence, echoing through the air. The floorboards creak ominously.*
Atcchan: "W-Wait...!"
Noelle: "Hm?"
*Noelle pauses, stops, turns around, her silver hair fluttering.*
*C-Can I ask her...? Do I dare?*
*Can I hold your hand?":
*I-It's nothing...":
Atcchan: "O-Oh, um... It's fine. Don't worry about it."
Noelle: "All right."
*Noelle tilts her head to one side and gestures to the darkened corridor before her.*
Noelle: "Shall we go, then?"
*Au... Auauau...*
*I don't want to. I really, really don't want to. But, if I back down now, I'll look like a coward.*
*I've already come this far. I have to keep going.*
*If this is what Noelle wants, then... Then...*
*How could I possibly say no?*
*It's not like I believe in ghosts anyway. I'm a sensible person (or at least, I feel like I'm old enough to at least try to act sensibly). It'll be fine. Nothing will happen.*
*I just need to keep telling myself that.*
*It'll be fine. It will, won't it...?*
Atcchan: "W-Well, if it... Um... I-If..."
*I try to speak, but the words get caught in my throat. I choke, coughing; my face flooding scarlet.*
Atcchan: "I-I was wondering if... maybe, um... um..."
Atcchan: "Ifit'snottoomuchtroublecouldIholdyourhand???"
*When I finally let loose the question, my face is flushed as red as the inside of a watermelon. I can't even look at Noelle.*
*I'm an idiot. I really am an idiot...*
*...*
*...*
*...*
*The seconds go by slowly, painfully. Bit by bit, my resolve crumbles.*
*I must look... so stupid...*
*...*
*...*
*...*
Noelle: "Well, I don't mind. If it would make you feel better, Atcchan."
Atcchan: "Ah..."
*I lift my head in surprise, my eyes open a little too wide. I didn't expect that. Of all the things she could have said, I didn't expect that...*
*Is it a dream? A hallucination? Does it still hurt when I pinch my arm?*
Atcchan: "O-Ow..."
*It does.*
*When I look into Noelle's eyes, I can only see sincerity. Her lips are curved upwards into a small smile, and her eyes are soft and gentle.*
*Noelle isn't the type of person to tease others. I believe in her.*
*Right now... I trust her unconditionally.*
Atcchan: "T-Thank you..."
*I reach out in the darkness, searching for Noelle's hand with my own.*
*She takes it gently, wrapping her fingers around mine.*
*They're a little cold - maybe from being outside for so long, on that swing. Still, they feel comforting; soft and safe.*
*I worry that my own palm is sweaty, and I start to get anxious. Of course, worrying about my palm being sweaty only makes it sweat more.*
Noelle: "Are you all right, Atcchan?"
Atcchan: "H-Haah? Oh, um..."
*I'm not sure how to get my words out. It's like trying to sift potatoes through a sieve.*
Atcchan: "I-I, um... I-I think I'm not okay, maybe, but I'm slightly more okay now than I was before? I don't know, it just, um... Ah..."
Noelle: "It's all right. I'm here with you."
Atcchan: "..."
Noelle: "I'll make sure no demons or ghosts get you. Okay?"
Atcchan: "Au... Um... A-All right..."
Noelle: "And now."
*Noelle gives my hand a comforting squeeze.*
Noelle: "Let's go."
*The two of us make our way to the girls' bathrooms, located at the end of the corridor.*
*It isn't very far away. Normally, it'd only take about twenty seconds to get from one side of the school to another.*
*However... because I'm walking so slowly, almost ready to collapse with fright at every single noise I hear, it takes a great deal longer than that.*
*I think Noelle must be some kind of saint, she has so much patience. She doesn't get annoyed at my antics even once.*
*I stare at the door of the girls' bathrooms, my legs trembling.*
*I've never been in one before. Of course I haven't - I'm not a girl. Seeing inside will certainly be an 'experience' for me.*
*This whole night has been full of 'experiences', and not many of them have been pleasant. I've never broken into the school at night, either. Or gone on a ghost hunt.*
*I've never even been on a test of courage before - even though Saki was adament doing so was an integral part of any summer vacation.*
*Personally, I just think she just has ghoulish tastes.*
*I gulp.*
*What's behind that door?*
*Practically, I don't think it'll be that much different from the boys' bathroom. A single cubicle; one toilet, a sink in the corner.*
*But... But...*
*Is that all we'll find...?*
*Could there really be a ghost? The remains of a young, bullied girl, sitting on a toilet seat, sobbing?*
*If she sees me... will I get dragged down to Hell? Will she tear off my skin while I'm alive, or burst all my internal organs in quick succession?*
*In stories, ghosts can do a lot of incredible things.*
*Since I go to a larger school now, there are even more ghost stories circulating, from even more students. I've heard a lot of them (thank you, Saki). About decaying corpses and gruesome deaths - don't look in the mirror in the art room and don't count eleven steps when there are only ten...*
*But... I don't believe in that kind of stuff, do I?*
*I don't. I definitely don't.*
*So... It's okay. I'm not afraid.*
*This rapid beating in my heart is just a natural response from my body. Rationally, I know there's nothing to be afraid of. Nothing at all.*
*The creepy sounds around me... It's just the wind and my own footsteps; the thudding of my heart. Things that would be completely innocuous and innocent during the day.*
*I'm not afraid. I'm not afraid. I'm not.*
*I just need to prove this to myself.*
Noelle: "Are you all right, Atcchan?"
Atcchan: "I... I am... I-I'm all right..."
Noelle: "Are you sure?"
Atcchan: "Y-Yeah... I-It's fine."
Noelle: "You want to go inside?"
Atcchan: "Y-Yeah. Let's do it!"
Noelle: "All right. On the count of three."
Noelle: "One... two... three..."
*And, with that, she pushes the door open.*
Atcchan: "KYAAAAAAAAAAAA...!!!"
Noelle: "Are you all right, Atcchan?"
Atcchan: "N-No..."
*I'm trembling so much, I can hardly talk. My teeth chatter so hard I worry I might sand all my incisors down.*
*Even though my arms are wrapped around my middle, it's not helping me feel any warmer at all...*
*It is cold outside, but that isn't the reason why I'm trembling. It's not the reason at all.*

*A thing.*
*A thing with a half-formed face, no arms and no legs; innards exposed, black eyes staring, mouth open...*
*A horrible, disgusting, monstrous thing that fell right on top of me!!!*
*Aaah... J-Just thinking about it is making my skin crawl...*
Noelle: "I suppose that is the reason that anatomical dummy was removed from the classroom, then."
Atcchan: "O-Of course that was the reason! I-It was removed because it was terrifying! Beyond terrifying, even! My mother said it used to give her nightmares...!"
*That anatomical dummy, lurking in the dark, dingy restroom, really was something else.*
*I felt sure I'd stumbled across the carved-up corpse of a young girl; a horrible, ghoulish apparition.*
*Upon closer inspection, the dummy wasn't that convincingly realistic - but since it was dark and hard to see, and it fell right on top of me I didn't have much of a chance to react logically.*
*I look at Noelle with tortured eyes, trembling.*
Atcchan: "W-Why did you put that thing in there, of all places? Were you trying to scare me?"
*Noelle's face remains impassive. She doesn't look particularly pleased with herself, or worried about my deteriorating sanity.*
*Instead, her expression is carefully blank; the kind of look you'd wear while inspecting eggplants in the supermarket.*
*After a while, she shrugs.*
Noelle: "I just thought it would be funny."
*F-Funny?*
*If she thinks turning my hair prematurely white, or giving me a heart attack, is funny, then I guess it was a resounding success on all fronts.*
*My heart gives a few weak flutters inside my chest; flopping like a fish out of water. It hurts to breathe.*
Atcchan: "I-I had no idea you had such a cruel sense of humor..."
Noelle: "I wasn't trying to be cruel. I was just curious."
Atcchan: "Curious?"
Noelle: "Yes. I've always wanted to play a prank on somebody like that. Like Amu does to you."
Atcchan: "Amu is a bad influence. You shouldn't try to imitate her..."
Noelle: "The time she put the pail of water over the classroom door... that was funny."
*I shudder at the memory.*
Atcchan: "Maybe for everybody else... but my clothes were soaked through."
Noelle: "Perhaps I was a little too mean, then. I apologize."
*Noelle bows her head to me politely. Her silver hair shifts at the movement, her light purple ribbon catching the breeze.*
Noelle: "I did not want to be mean. I just thought it would be fun. Like a test of courage. Isn't that what friends do?"
Atcchan: "Sometimes, I guess. I think those usually take place near shrines, though..."
*And between people who've already consented to go on a test of courage. There's a difference between agreeing to mutually scare one another, and scaring somebody on your own, without asking...*
Noelle: "I see. I'm sorry if I misunderstood the concept..."
Atcchan: "Ah, no... It's okay."
Noelle: "It's just... We may not have much more time together. So, I thought... we should make more fun memories now."
Atcchan: "W-Well... I-I guess I'll survive. M-Maybe it was kind of funny... Just a little."
*Noelle nods.*
Noelle: "Yes. I'm sure you'll look back on it with fondness in a few years. You're leading a very exciting life, Atcchan."
Atcchan: "A-Ahahaha. M-Maybe it's a little bit too exciting for my tastes."
Noelle: "Still..."
*Noelle looks up towards the sky. It really is dark now. I can see the moon hovering just beyond a black line of trees; large and full.*
Noelle: "It is nice... making memories with friends. Don't you think?"
*Her words are soft and gentle; almost blowing away in the breeze.*
Atcchan: "Ah... Yeah, you're right. Making memories with friends is nice. Even if those memories will give me bad dreams..."
*Noelle giggles.*
Noelle: "Ehehe~ Sorry. Why don't you look at it as revenge, then?"
Atcchan: "R-Revenge?"
Noelle: "Mm. Because... you left me without saying goodbye."
Noelle: "This was your punishment. A punishment for doing something bad."
Atcchan: "A-Ah..."
*She's right.*
*Even though her prank was in bad taste... I did something far, far worse to her.*
*I was scared for a few seconds. Noelle, on the other hand... could have been hurting for two whole years. All because I never spoke to her. Because I never wrote to her.*
*Because I ignored her.*
*I deserve worse.*
*The fact she'd let me off with a 'punishment' so light only serves to show how forgiving she is.*
Atcchan: "I... I'm sorry, Noelle."
Noelle: "It's all right. There's no need to be sorry. I'm not mad."
Atcchan: "But I... I hurt you, didn't I?"
*Noelle smiles at me.*
*It's a very gentle smile that serves to make this dark night seem a little less unforgiving.*
Noelle: "Maybe. A little. But you've been punished now... so, I can forgive you."
Atcchan: "Y-You forgive me?"
Noelle: "Of course. You are my best friend, after all."
*Noelle...*
*I wince. The guilt in my stomach begins to bubble up, frothing like thick, muddy swamp water.*
*I feel sick.*
*I saw Noelle in the park yesterday, I know I did. It was definitely her.*
*That pale skin, that silver hair, those light blue eyes... they're impossible to mistake.*
*And yet... Even though I saw her, I ignored her.*
*I had a chance to talk to my best friend, my dearest friend - my friend that I betrayed, even though she trusted me.*
*I had a chance to apologize. But I didn't take it.*
*It's because I'm still this weak. It's because I'm a coward, unable to face the consequences of my actions.*
*And so, I made everything even worse.*
*Sometimes, I really do hate myself. But what use is that? This hatred is worth nothing. This guilt is meaningless.*
*Guilt only has worth if you can use it for a greater good. If your guilt doesn't inspire you to change, it's completely pointless - almost selfish. A useless emotion that you can wallow in at your own leisure.*
*If Noelle's angry at me... I'll understand.*
*If she hates me, I'll understand that too.*
*But I need to see her.*
*I need to apologize.*
*Maybe she's in the park again, like yesterday. It wouldn't hurt to look.*
*And so, on my way back to my grandparents' home, I make a short detour.*
*In the gathering darkness, I sit on the swing and wait.*
*I don't really know what I'm waiting for. There's no guarantee that you'll come here. But you came here yesterday.*
*Maybe you're like me. I think you're like me. But I don't know.*
*It's kind of sad that we've been friends for so long - I thought we were friends, at least - but I still don't know that much about you.*
*That's my fault, not yours. It's because I don't talk. I don't like to talk. Where does talking get you?*
*It doesn't change the past. It's pointless.*
*I think you're like me. You like routine. You like regularity. So you'll come back to this place.*
*I'm sure, just like me... you'll be led here.*
*You'll come back.*
*You will.*
*And, this time... I won't let you ignore me. Not now.*
*You can't.*
*You won't.*
*When you left, it hurt me. It hurt even more that you didn't tell me.*
*If you'd told me you were leaving... I think it would have been all right. I would have been able to manage.*
*Quietly, I could get along, like a boat bobbing on the surface of the water. Just like always.*
*But you didn't tell me.*
*You didn't tell me, and you didn't write to me.*
*Why was that...?*
*Maybe it's because you hate me.*
*I sniffle, wiping my eyes with the backs of my arms.*
*It's cold. My cheeks are wet. When the wind blows, my cheeks feel even colder.*
*Even though I go outside dressed like this all the time, I'm shivering. I thought I was used to the cold by now. I thought I could adapt to anything.*
*But I was wrong, wasn't I? Everybody has a limit.*
*I hit it once before.*
*I might have hit it again.*
*In my pocket, I feel something cool. A sharp blade.*
*Simply having it here, by my side, is comforting. It makes me feel less alone. Even though it can't talk to me. Even though it's not a real friend.*
*What would I know? I've never had a real friend before.*
*If you hated me, you should've told me. I've been told that before. I'm used to it.*
*But... pretending to be my friend... giving me a warm, happy feeling I've never had before... and then taking all that away, so suddenly, so quickly, without any warning at all...*
*That's just too cruel.*
*I think false hope might be one of the worst forms of torture in the world.*
*Ah...*
*I can hear footsteps. Is it you?*
*You stand there, looking at me. Wringing your hands. You don't know what to say, what to do. Do you even know why you're here?*
Atcchan: "H-Hey... N-Noelle, I... I, um..."
*Your voice cracks. It falters in your throat. The wind whistling around us is even louder than you are.*
*I can't hear what you're trying to say. What is it? An apology? An excuse?*
*I don't know. I don't care. I'm tired of such things.*
*I can't stand liars.*
*I get up. The swing set creaks, the metal chains old and rusty. I never got to play here when I was younger. The stronger, louder, more energetic children always got here first, and I was too shy to join in.*
*I've always been on the sidelines. Always unable to speak my mind.*
*But not this time.*
*I can speak my mind without words.*
Atcchan: "A-Are you all right? You're shaking."
*The concern in your voice makes me falter, almost.*
*But I can't be fooled again. I can't be hurt again.*
*I don't want... to be hurt...*
*So I'll have to hurt you instead.*
*Isn't that just how the world works?*
Atcchan: "Noelle, I... I... I'm sorry..."
*Sorry?*
*That isn't good enough.*
*If you really were 'sorry' you wouldn't have hurt me to begin with.*
*You're a liar.*
*A liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar a liar...!*
*And so, after acquiescing, I ended up here.*
*This antiques store has two floors. On the ground floor is the shop, where all of the wares are sold. And on the upper floor, is the space where Tsuzumi lives.*
*The upstairs of the store smells just as musty as the downstairs. Dust motes drift in the air lazily, without a care in the world, choking my throat when I try to breathe and stinging my eyes.*

Tsuzumi: "Oh dear, you look a little peaky. Would you like a cup of tea?"
*She's smiling politely, holding a teapot in her hand, but I'm not deceived. I know, behind that smile, lurks a pure and unfettered hatred for absolutely everything about me.*

*In the end, I nod my head, unable to say a single thing.*
Tsuzumi: "Ufufu~ Then here you go, you lower level life form~ "
*Uwaa...*

Tsuzumi: "It's cinnamon tea, a rather expensive blend."
Tsuzumi: "Aaah. It seems a shame to waste it on your unrefined palette, which is surely unable to distinguish between the fine subtleties of flavor woven throughout this beverage."
*With a sigh, Tsuzumi pours me a cup of tea and then passes it towards me.*
*I can't help but notice that the teacups are all chipped. Have these been taken from the cabinets in her own store...?*
*How is Tsuzumi able to make any kind of profit from this place if she overprices all her stock, scares away her customers and takes random things for her own private use?*
*I turn to my tea, sipping it slowly.*
*Thankfully, Tsuzumi hasn't done anything sinister to it, like pour in salt or bodily fluids or arsenic. It tastes fine - nice, even. Just a little too hot.*
Tsuzumi: "Well then. How is it?"
Atcchan: "Eep!"
*I cry out in alarm. I can't help it. Anybody would, after being glared at like that...*
Tsuzumi: "How does my hospitality taste? Is it good enough for you? Well, is it?"
Atcchan: "A-Ah, um... I-It, it... I-It's very good, t-thankyouforasking!"
*Eri sighs, placing her own teacup down on its saucer with a light chnk of china meeting china. I notice Eri's teacup and saucer are the only ones without any noticeable damage.*
Eri: "Big Sister, please. You're being rude."
*Tsuzumi's whole countenance twists, a sudden look of intense despair flooding her face.*
Tsuzumi: "Huh? I... I'm not being rude, am I?"

Eri: "It has helped me put things into perspective a little."

Tsuzumi: "I'm just displaying my love! I'm proving that my love for you is far, far stronger than anything this boy could display!"

*Does she really like cake that much?*
*It's kind of cute that she's getting so so enthusiastic about something so simple, even though she tries to act so mature.*
Tsuzumi: "Ehehe~ "

Tsuzumi: "I need to pick up an order I placed earlier anyway. Now, I wonder what that could have been~"

Tsuzumi: "Was it something even more exotic, like mont blanc~? "
Eri: "Wawa... M-Mont blanc...? B-But isn't that really expensive?!"

Eri: "Waah..."
Eri: "Big Sis, you're saying some pretty irresponsible things here... Y-You really should try to be more careful with your money...!"

Tsuzumi: "Ehehe~ "

*Tsuzumi turns to face me, the warmth in her face guttering out like a candle standing next to an open window.*
*The sudden shift in her demeanor... is quite unnerving...*
Tsuzumi: "You. You're coming with me."

Atcchan: "Y-You really are something special, Eri."

Eri: "A-Ahem..."

*Tsuzumi really does spoil Eri, doesn't she...?*
