Eri: "No way, stupid sister! The dice didn't roll properly so I should have another go!"
Tsuzumi: "Eri, that's not fair! You got a two - I saw it!"

Eri: "No! You're the one who's cheating, stupid sister! You are!"

Tsuzumi: "You!!!"

Atcchan: "K-Kyaaa...!"

*At least it looks like they're having fun.*
*Um... I think...*
*I lie on my stomach on the futon, flipping through a book.*
*It's not that late - only about 8:00 p.m. - but my grandparents already went to bed. It must be because they're getting old.*
*That's... kind of sad... and it makes me feel guilty.*
*Since I stayed out so late today, I hardly got to see them at all.*
*When I got back from town, on my own - Eri decided to stay overnight with her sister after all - dinner was already waiting for me, spread out across the tabletop.*

*Of course, my grandparents said they didn't mind. They said it was natural for me to spend time with my friends.*
Grandma: "You didn't come here to see us, now, did you dear?"
Grandma: "Now, don't trouble yourself with such silly worries. Would you like some more pickled vegetables?"
*... was what my grandmother said.*

*Even though I haven't been back here in so long, and I have no idea when I'll be able to see them again... I've almost completely ignored them.*
*But it hasn't just been them, though, has it...?*
*Negligence might be becoming something of a tradition with me.*
*I curl up in various positions, sitting up and then lying back down, but it's useless. No matter what I do, I still can't get comfy.*
*The words on the page don't mean anything to me. They twist and bend right before my eyes, becoming unrecognizable and alien.*
*I've been staring at the same page for the past ten minutes. I keep re-reading the same line over and over, but no matter how many times I drag my eyes across it, I can't discern any meaning from it.*
*It's just a book. They're just words. In the end, it's all meaningless. This book has no relation to my life at all.*
*I think. I can't help but think, even though I wish I didn't have to.*
*And, inevitably... I think about Noelle.*
*I saw her in the park yesterday evening, I know I did. However... I didn't go and greet her. I didn't talk to her.*
*Instead, I was a coward. I ignored her.*
*I hope she didn't see me.*
*I hope it didn't hurt her feelings.*
*It's not that I dislike her - that's never been the issue. It's just, I...*
*I don't know.*
*I'm just a coward, incapable of facing up to my own faults.*
*I knew, by abandoning her so callously, I would've upset her. And I didn't want to face that. I didn't want to feel bad.*
*So, instead of taking responsibility... I tried to run away.*
*I've always been like this. When something goes wrong, or I get scared, I try to avoid the problem... hiding from it rather than trying to solve it.*
*It's because I'm immature. It's because I'm weak. It's because hiding... is far, far easier.*
*It's because I'm like this... that I feel so terrible.*
*I sigh and set my book down to one side, closing it with a light thud.*
Atcchan: "What's the point?"
*I mutter under my breath, turning over on my futon, curling up into a ball.*
*I close my eyes tight, trying to calm myself down. I count to ten inside my head slowly.*
*One... Two... Three... Four...*
*And that's when I hear it. A steady pounding on the door.*
*It's a soft, gentle knock, not a loud or angry one. Quietly insistent might be the correct word for it.*

Atcchan: "All right. I'm coming, I'm coming..."

Noelle: "Um... It's been a while since I've been here..."
Atcchan: "A-Ahaha... Y-Yeah, it... It sure has..."

*As soon as I do this, however, I regret it.*
Atcchan: "O-Ow..."

*This green tea isn't only hot. It tastes bad. I don't know what went wrong, but it's far too weak.*
*If Amu were here right now, the great tea connoisseur that she is, she'd definitely scold me. Maybe I'd get smacked over the head for good measure.*

Atcchan: "U-Um... So, uh... What brings you here?"
Noelle: "My dad... He made curry tonight."
Atcchan: "Huh?"
*I look at Noelle, confused by this non-sequitur.*
*For my sake, she elaborates.*
Noelle: "For dinner."
*But the elaboration is completely useless, like trying to add golden embroidery to an old rag. Instead of turning it into a precious object, it just transfigures it into a source of confusion.*
Atcchan: "No, I mean... Why did you decide to come over at this time?"
Noelle: "My dad made curry tonight."
Atcchan: "I-I already gathered that much, but I don't see how it's related..."
Noelle: "He made too much curry. He asked me to take some here."

Atcchan: "Is that what's in the plastic bag? Curry?"
*Noelle nods her head.*
Atcchan: "How did he know I was here, though?"

*I should have known. Some of the neighbors must have seen me wandering around town, and gossip started to spread.*
*In a small place like this, even very small pieces of news soon become common knowledge.*
*My grandparents must have told their friends about my arrival, too. I was stupid thinking Noelle wouldn't know about it. I bet everybody else does.*
Noelle: "Anyway... The curry..."
Noelle: "You can have it if you want - but you probably don't. Your grandmother is a good cook. I wasn't trying to insult her cooking skills or anything, so... Um..."
Noelle: "I-It's not like you need to take it. I don't mind either way."
Atcchan: "A-Ah, no, um... Y-Your dad is a really good cook, too...! Really good...! I-I'd be happy to try some...!"

Noelle: "Ah... Really?"

Noelle: "That is true, but... If it's for you..."
Noelle: "If it's for you, I don't mind."
Atcchan: "A-Ah..."
*My voice sticks in my throat. I don't know what to say...*

Atcchan: "A-Ahaha... All right, all right. Give me a second."

Noelle: "You look happy, Atcchan."

Noelle: "Maybe. Just a little. But I think it suits you."
Atcchan: "Aau..."
*I flush, suddenly feeling guilty.*
*Noelle is being so friendly to me, but... do I really deserve it...?*

Noelle: "Atcchan. Are you all right...?"
Atcchan: "Huh...? Oh, um... I..."
*I blink in surprise. My face flushes.*

Noelle: "It is quite dark outside. I apologize for intruding at such a late hour. I just wanted to give you that curry, no matter what."
Atcchan: "O-Oh, no, i-it's fine. I-I already said, I don't mind! You're not intruding, you're my friend!"
Noelle: "Ah, well... I-If you're sure..."
Noelle: "I am not so good at social interactions, so... sometimes, I get unsure about simple things..."
Atcchan: "N-No, it's fine. R-Really..."
Noelle: "O-Okay. It's just..."
Noelle: "I also wanted to talk to you. We haven't seen each other in such a long while, and... Um..."
Noelle: "I missed you."

*I try to stutter back a response, but I keep tripping up over the words. My tongue feels strangely thick and heavy, and it's hard for me to talk.*
*Still... I need to tell her. Even though it's hard. Even though it's embarrassing.*
*I have to say it.*

Atcchan: "I... I missed you, too..."
Noelle: "You did?"
Atcchan: "Y-Yeah."

*I really did miss you, Noelle...*

Noelle: "E-Ehehe... It wasn't rude. You don't have to eat it. I don't want to be pushy..."
Atcchan: "A-Ah, no, that isn't it...! Y-You're not pushy...!"
Noelle: "Really?"
Atcchan: "R-Really...!"

Atcchan: "Thanks for the food."

Noelle: "Is it good?"
Atcchan: "Aah... It's delicious...! T-Thank you!"

*I smile as I watch you eat, my hands folded in my lap, knees bent underneath me.*

Atcchan: "H-Hey, Noelle... What kind of mushrooms are these?"

*After this, I won't lie anymore.*
Noelle: "Mm... I think they're just regular shiitake mushrooms. Why?"
Atcchan: "I... I-I don't know... I think they taste a little strange..."
Noelle: "I don't know why that would be. Maybe Dad prepares them differently from your grandmother, or buys them from a different place?"
Atcchan: "Ah, yeah... That's probably it. I'm sure it's no big deal."
*I watch your face carefully as you continue to eat. Even though you're not hungry. Even so, you keep eating.*
*You're doing it so you won't upset me. Even though, right now... maybe your stomach is already starting to swell. To hurt. To ache.*
*Your eyes are so innocent. Your smile is so trusting.*
*Deep down inside, I know you're not a bad person.*
*I'm not so childish to think that the world is split down the middle, between those who do good and those who do bad. I know most people are somewhere in between.*
*And I know, too, that everyone will cause harm to somebody at some point in their life. It's inevitable. It's part of being a human.*
*Most people don't cause harm out of malice. They do it out of stupidity. Or anxiety. Or selfishness. Or fear. But not hate.*
*You're not... a bad person. And you didn't mean to hurt me. I don't think you did.*
*But... that doesn't change the fact that it happened. And it doesn't change the fact that it hurts.*
*It hurts... so much...*
*If you had spoken to me yesterday, instead of running away like that... maybe it could have eased the burden in my heart. Maybe it would have stopped hurting. Just a little bit.*
*But maybe that's impossible. Wishful thinking. How could a single, brief encounter stopper up all the pain and resentment of two whole years?*
*I'm not that stupid. I'm not that naïve.*
*Even though it's sad... this may be the only way. The only way to ease my suffering.*
*The only way for me to tell you how I feel. I'll tell you without words.*
*You probably won't believe me when you find out... When you start vomiting blood. You won't believe me at all.*
*But I know the truth.*
*I didn't want to do this. Really, I didn't.*
*I don't hate you. I promise.*
*I like you more than anybody else in the whole world.*
*But that's why I had to do it.*
*I don't want you to keep lying anymore. It hurts you just as much as it hurts me.*
*I lie in my futon and stare up at the ceiling, wide awake.*
*I can't get to sleep. I can't even begin to think about the slightest possibility of sleeping.*
*My mind is filled up with the events of today; stuffed full to such an extent I fear it might burst.*
*Why does Amu dislike Eri so much? Didn't they used to be friends?*
*I never knew Amu had the capacity to dislike somebody to such a degree. I thought she was a fairly fickle, cheerful person who couldn't hold grudges for very long.*
*I guess I was wrong.*
*Because I've never been on Amu's bad side before, I never knew. I had no idea just how ruthless she could be.*
*And then, there's Tsuzumi. Eri's big sister.*
*Why does she regard me with such scorn? It makes me feel as though I've done something wrong - but I can't think what.*
*I have no idea.*
*I turn over in my futon, curled up into a ball with my knees tucked up under my chin and my arms wrapped round my legs.*
*I continue to turn, over and over. No matter what position I adopt, I can't quite get comfortable.*
*Although the air outside must be cold, in the confines of this small room it feels far too hot. I'm suffocating.*
*My whole body is melting, spoiling, turning rancid; just like a slice of cake left out in the sun for too long.*
*I shudder.*
*But... I can't give up on Eri now.*
*We haven't found Shiro yet.*
*For Eri's sake... I need to find him...*
*Wow... This house is just as large and imposing as I remember it.*
*I thought maybe my memories of this place had become skewed over time, but... I was right all along.*
*This house really is huge. It's worlds apart from the other houses in this little village, built of wood more than a century ago, seeming ready to cave in on themselves at any given moment.*
*This house defies all of that. This house defies history. It's a completely modern building, only a few years old - even younger than I am. Everything is so white and smooth and there are glass windows everywhere. The front door is so large it's almost intimidating*
*I can still remember when this house was being built. I used to come down here on my bike all the time, often with Amu. We'd sit and gawk as the construction workers bustled back and forth with their noisy machines.*
*I'd never seen anything like it before.*
*We got in the way a lot, hanging around on the construction site, and I think we got scolded a few times - but that wasn't enough to keep Amu away. She became even more determined every time we were sent home.*
*Every day after school, without fail, she dragged me here and ignored all of my feeble protests.*
*Even to me, watching the construction of this house was exciting, as it was so rare for anything in this village to change.*
*Overseeing the construction from afar became a kind of game for me and Amu.*
*Amu and I were definitely in the minority, though. Most people were upset about the construction of this large, showy house.*
*Maybe that's why this house was built so far away from the main body of the village; about a ten minute walk away. I don't know.*
*This house doesn't really feel like part of the village. It never did. It's too far away, sitting by itself near the forest, large and lonely.*
*Something about this place feels slightly 'off' now, though I'm not entirely sure what.*
*It's like... there's no warmth here. As though even the sun has abandoned this place.*
*And, in the garden...*
*There's a sign.*
*It's a sign that was never here before. It's not something I remember.*
*And the sign reads, quite plainly, in large characters: 'FOR SALE.'*
*This house is for sale? But why? Does that mean Noelle and her family are moving...?*
*I never heard anything about this. Amu didn't mention it in any of her letters, and she didn't tell me about it yesterday, either. Neither did Noelle. Nobody did.*
*Why did nobody tell me Noelle was moving...?*
*I walk forwards with trembling legs, down the front path, up to the front door.*
*When I reach the doorstep, I raise my right hand, form a fist, and knock.*
*I knock and wait.*
*I find myself staring up at the grandiose, slightly overbearing structure that is Noelle's home for the second time these last two days.*
*Just as before, the large sign that reads 'FOR SALE' is displayed in the front garden; a firm indication that what I saw yesterday wasn't some kind of delusion or dream.*
*Noelle's family really is moving away. That is the truth.*
*For some reason... that sign makes me feel anxious.*
*It's not like I'm superstitious or anything. Sometimes I flip through the daily newspaper to look at my horoscope, but that's about it. I don't take things like that too seriously; they're just a fun distraction.*
*However... it's almost as though that sign is some kind of omen. A portent of misfortune.*
*Although it's a fairly warm, sunny day, it seems oddly cold here.*
*Maybe that's because of the sheer size of Noelle's home. Perhaps it blocks out the sun. Or maybe the sun is too intimidated by the size of her home to shine near here.*
*Noelle's home is the biggest building in the whole village, and it's situated a little way apart from the rest of the houses, which all co-exist together in a cluster.*
*Noelle's home is cold and aloof; just far away enough from the rest of the village to make it feel like it exists in its own alternate reality.*
*Now that I think about it like that, I'm starting to feel creeped out. W-Was that really just the wind against the back of my neck, or... was it an invisible, ghostly hand?*
*... Ridiculous. I'm being stupid.*
*These thoughts are completely useless; worth even less than manure. You couldn't even fertilize a field with the contents of my head, so... there's no point pondering this any further.*
*Shaking my head in derision, I try to drive away the rest of my weird thoughts.*
*I stride forwards with a new sense of purpose; down the front path and right to the front door.*
*I stand on the doorstep and knock.*
*There's no reply.*
*I wait there a while, arms hanging at my sides. I'm standing so stiffly I must look like a scarecrow - which might be a useful talent, if there were any birds around here that needed scaring.*
*But there aren't. Noelle's home remains quiet, desolate. A wasteland.*
*Is anybody home...?*
*I raise my fist again, ready to knock - but this soon proves to be an unnecessary action.*
*Standing in the entrance is a woman.*
*She's tall to an almost intimidating degree, and the serious expression on her face doesn't help.*
*Her hair is long and blond, tied back in a ponytail so tight her forehead looks unnaturally taut.*
*She's wearing a pristine white blouse, ironed without a single crease, and a pair of tightly fitting black pants in equally perfect condition.*
*It's Noelle's mother, Sakata Lucy.*
Mrs. Sakata: "Here you go. One marshmallow tea."
*Mrs. Sakata places a willow-patterned cup of freshly brewed tea, complete with matching saucer, down on the kitchen table before me.*
*I bow my head in silent thanks, my face flushed pink.*
*Somehow, it feels wrong accepting tea brewed by the hands of this woman.*
*She seems so incredibly perfect, so completely above any other person I've met, that having her serve me tea makes me feel like I'm being waited on, hand and foot, by a real member of royalty.*
*It's not as though I asked for the tea, however. I didn't come here and start barking orders at her. If I had, I doubt she'd have listened to them.*
*Mrs. Sakata ushered me into the kitchen of her own accord, then asked me if I wanted anything to drink before I'd even had the chance to get my bearings together.*
*I thought it would be rude to reject her offer, especially as she'd already started rifling though the cupboards with army-like efficiency, so I weakly muttered the name of the first tea that came into my mind.*
*I can't bring myself to say anything. Instead, I just sip my tea in silence, watching as Mrs. Sakata pours herself her own cup.*
*It really is interesting to watch her. She doesn't waste a single movement, and does everything with poise and grace.*
*She makes even a simple task, like pouring water into a cup, look like a work of art.*
*This person... really is incredible...*
*She's incredible but, at the same time... frightening...*
*The kitchen doesn't help soothe my nerves, either.*
*The stark white walls, clinically clean surfaces and modern coffee maker sitting on the side makes me feel like I'm not even in the same village anymore.*
*Noelle's home feels like a completely different universe, separate from anything and everything else.*
*It's a strange world where every single thing is in its proper place, not a speck of dust in sight.*
*An odd, sterile environment which lacks any real warmth, infused with the smell of detergent.*
*It feels more like I'm in a hospital than in somebody's house. That, or a space ship.*
*The atmosphere is oppressive. My fingers tremble when I reach for my cup of tea. My eyes dart around uneasily, unsure where to rest.*
*Once Mrs. Sakata pours her own cup of tea, she takes a seat facing me at the spotless table in the center of the room.*
*The two of us sit together in silence, in her cold, impersonal kitchen.*
Mrs. Sakata: "So... I see you've come back."
Atcchan: "Y-Yes. I have."
*Not that I need to confirm it. That much should be obvious, given I'm sitting here right now.*
Mrs. Sakata: "Mm. That's good. I think Noelle missed you quite a bit."
Atcchan: "I-I... I'm sorry?"
Mrs. Sakata: "Oh, there's no need to apologize. You don't have to be so formal."
*Mrs. Sakata offers me a small smile. However, it gets lost in the cold atmosphere of this room, and none of its warmth reaches me.*
Mrs. Sakata: "How long are you going to be here?"
Atcchan: "Well, I have to go back home tomorrow..."
Mrs. Sakata: "Ah. So, not very long at all. I suppose you don't want this old woman keeping you, then."
*I flinch. I might have been thinking something along those lines, but...*
Atcchan: "A-Ah, um... I... I-I don't think you're old at all!"
Mrs. Sakata: "Ahaha. Well, thank you. That makes me feel a little bit better."
Atcchan: "A-Ahaha..."
*With a stilted laugh, I turn my attention back to my tea. I want to drain my cup as quickly as possible, just so I have an excuse to get out of here...*
Mrs. Sakata: "Still... I really can't thank you enough."
Atcchan: "Thank me? For what?"
Mrs. Sakata: "For being Noelle's friend. She doesn't have many of them."
Atcchan: "H-Huh?"
Mrs. Sakata: "I don't think Noelle has been feeling too well lately. She became even quieter than usual after you left."
Mrs. Sakata: "I'm worried that she hasn't been able to make friends with the other children in the village."
*Mrs. Sakata looks troubled.*
*I start to feel even guiltier for wanting to escape. Even though Mrs. Sakata is quite a serious person, she certainly isn't a bad one.*
*It's clear she really does care about Noelle.*
Mrs. Sakata: "Oh... I apologize if it's awkward to talk about such things. It might be a bit unfair."
Atcchan: "N-No, it's all right. I-I don't mind."
Mrs. Sakata: "It's just... I do worry about my daughter. She's always been so quiet. She's never been very good at talking to others and... I get concerned about it."
Atcchan: "O-Oh, um... It's all right... I'll be Noelle's friend...!"
Mrs. Sakata: "I know you will. You're already a good friend to her. A very good friend."
Atcchan: "Well, I don't know about that..."
Atcchan: "She is a little bit quiet, but that's no problem! I like being with her! And, because I like it, there's no reason to thank me."
Atcchan: "Since I enjoy being with her, I'm benefiting, too..."
*Although saying it like that makes it sound like a business merger. What do I mean, 'benefiting?'*
*I smile awkwardly, unsure whether I've worded it right. It's hard to get my point across.*
*I guess I just react badly to being complimented. It makes me anxious. If people compliment you it means there's a greater chance that you'll let them down in the future.*
*Compliments seem to weigh even more heavily when they come from a woman like Mrs. Sakata.*
*And why should she compliment me for spending time with her daughter? That makes it sound like a chore.*
*Being with Noelle wasn't a burden. It was fun.*
*Every day with her... was so much fun.*
Atcchan: "I really didn't do anything special."
Mrs. Sakata: "It might not seem like anything special to you, but I appreciate it all the same. On behalf of my daughter, I would like to thank you."
Atcchan: "A-Aah... W-Well, uh... I-If you're sure, but..."
*R-Really, being praised like this... I don't know if it's fair.*
*Can Mrs. Sakata truly, honestly say that I'm a good friend to Noelle?*
*How can I be a good friend when I betrayed her?*
*Mrs. Sakata stands by the sink, washing the used teacups. Her blond ponytail bobs with her every movement, not a tendril out of place.*
*The sound of running water fills the kitchen. It's comforting, though I'm not sure how. Maybe it's homey.*
*At least it makes this place feel less stagnant, less sterile, less detached from the rest of reality.*
Mrs. Sakata: "Thank you for humoring this old woman. I'm sure you didn't come here because you wanted to talk to me."
Atcchan: "Ahaha... I-I, um... I-I still don't think you're old, you know?"
Mrs. Sakata: "That may be true. But I am old enough to know better."
Atcchan: "Huh...?"
*Mrs. Sakata continues to clean the inside of the cups with a flannel cloth over and over again in a circular motion, but she looks distracted.*
Mrs. Sakata: "I shouldn't burden you with my troubles. You're just a little boy."
Atcchan: "Hey...! I'm not that little...!"
Mrs. Sakata: "You are compared to me. I know it isn't right for me to burden you with my worries. It's just..."
*Mrs. Sakata sighs again, her shoulders drooping.*
Mrs. Sakata: "I don't really know anybody in this village. It's such a tightly knit community, and I feel like I'm still considered a stranger - even after all these years."
Mrs. Sakata: "It's claustrophobic."
*I don't say anything. I don't really know what to say.*
*Mrs. Sakata finally turns off the faucet. The sound of running water fades away, enveloped by the silence that rushes to meet it. Once again, everything is deathly quiet.*
*This house really is in a secluded area, isn't it?*
*If a person feels isolated already... living in a place like this, where not even the sounds of the cicadas can reach you, must only serve to make you feel even more alone.*
*I can imagine why Mrs. Sakata feels unhappy living out here. Maybe that's one of the reasons why the family has decided to move.*
*I'm sympathetic towards this but, at the same time... I'm anxious.*
*What about Noelle? How will she cope if her family uproots and moves somewhere else?*
*I keep thinking back to the 'FOR SALE' sign in the garden. I can't shake this ominous feeling I have about it, no matter how hard I try.*
*The worried look on my face must be obvious because Mrs. Sakata frowns, clicking her tongue against the roof of her mouth.*
Mrs. Sakata: "Are you all right?"
Atcchan: "O-Oh... I, um... I'm fine..."
Mrs. Sakata: "Are you sure? You look a little bit pale. Would you like me to get you some medicine?"
Atcchan: "A-Ah... N-No, I don't think I need any. I'm good."
*Mrs. Sakata doesn't look fully convinced, but she relents anyway.*
Mrs. Sakata: "Well, if you're sure."
Atcchan: "I'm sure. There's no need to worry."
Mrs. Sakata: "Hm..."
*She purses her lips, arms folded. It's the same face Mom wears whenever I tell her I'm too sick to go to school. Unconvinced.*
Mrs. Sakata: "Noelle never tells me when she's feeling ill, either."
Atcchan: "A-Ahaha... W-Well, we are kind of alike."
Mrs. Sakata: "I suppose so. That must be why you get along so well. Maybe it's something I'm too old to understand."
*Mrs. Sakata sighs, turning her head away from me. For those few brief moments, she looks unusually unsure of herself.*
*She really is worried about Noelle. That much is obvious. But...*
*If that's the case... why is she leaving...?*
Atcchan: "Hey... I was wondering..."
Mrs. Sakata: "Yes? Do you want me to get you that medicine after all?"
Atcchan: "A-Ah... No, it isn't about that."
Mrs. Sakata: "Are you sure? It isn't any trouble."
*It seems that Mrs. Sakata is quite a doting parent after all.*
Atcchan: "No, I was just curious. Um... I hope you don't mind me asking, but..."
Mrs. Sakata: "I won't know if I'll mind you asking until you ask it."
Atcchan: "T-True. You can't argue with logic like that."
Mrs. Sakata: "No. I am very difficult to argue with. At least, that's what my husband says."
Atcchan: "I-I can imagine... Ahaha..."
Atcchan: "O-Oh, not that I'm trying to sound rude or anything! I-I wasn't trying to offend you!"
Mrs. Sakata: "No offense taken. I prefer it this way - being ever so slightly intimidating. It means people take you more seriously."
*Mrs. Sakata smiles. I wonder if she's joking or not. I can't tell. Even so, I can't help but smile back, my face flushed light pink.*
Atcchan: "It's just, um... I noticed that your house is up for sale and... I was wondering if you're planning to move anywhere?"
*A pause.*
Mrs. Sakata: "... Yes. That seems like a fair conclusion to take from that piece of evidence."
*Huh... That was an oddly roundabout way of confirming my statement.*
*The expression on Mrs. Sakata's face, too... All of a sudden, it's started to look strangely grim.*
*I should be careful with my words. I might upset her if I ask the wrong question...*
*Why are you moving?":
*Where are you moving?":
Mrs. Sakata: "Where are we moving?"
*Mrs. Sakata repeats the question slowly, looking a little taken aback. Maybe that isn't what she expected me to ask.*
Atcchan: "Yeah. I want to know. So I can still keep in touch with Noelle."
Mrs. Sakata: "Oh. I see. I understand."
*Mrs. Sakata makes her way over to the table. She takes a seat once more, facing opposite me.*
*I wonder if this action is meant to calm me down, since it's effectively putting us at the same level. However, it does the exact opposite.*
*My overactive imagination kicks in, making me panic.*
*Is this news so shocking that Mrs. Sakata wants to ensure I'm as calm as possible before she tells me it?*
*Why? They can't be moving anywhere that extreme, can they? It's not like they've started colonizing Mars yet, right?!*
Mrs. Sakata: "Well... It hasn't been completely finalized yet. There's still a lot of paperwork I need to fill in, and perhaps we'll change our minds later."
Mrs. Sakata: "Or, who knows? Maybe this house won't get sold. That would put an end to most of our plans. But..."
Mrs. Sakata: "If everything comes together, my husband and I were hoping to move somewhere quite far away."
Atcchan: "Q-Quite far away?"
*What does that mean? How far away is 'quite far?'*
*But Mrs. Sakata remains calm. She tells me the shocking news like it's the most natural thing in the world.*
Mrs. Sakata: "We want to move to England."
*I don't know how much time has passed. It's hard to take it in. I know my mouth is open wide, but I don't have enough energy to close it.*
*England...? Why England...?*
*That isn't Japan. It's not Japan at all! That's so far away it might as well be Mars...!*
*Mrs. Sakata looks at me sympathetically. It's the kind of expression a doctor might give a patient after breaking some very unfortunate news.*
Mrs. Sakata: "I'm sorry to tell you this so suddenly. It must be a shock to you."
Atcchan: "A-A... A shock... Y-Yeah, j-just a little..."
Mrs. Sakata: "But it isn't so bad. I know you're good friends with Noelle, but it's not the end of the world. You'll still be able to exchange letters."
Atcchan: "L-Letters...? Y-Yeah, I guess..."
*How long does it take for a letter posted from Japan to arrive in England? I don't know. I've never done it before.*
Atcchan: "B-But..."
Mrs. Sakata: "Besides, you yourself live so far away now. This is the first time you've come back in two years. I don't think it would make that much difference to your daily life whether Noelle was living in Japan or England."
*Mrs. Sakata is right, of course.*
*It must seem ridiculous to her that I'm making such a big deal about Noelle moving. I certaintly haven't made all that much of an effort to remain in contact with her.*
*But, even so... the fact she was still here, in Japan, was comforting. Although she was a seven hour train journey away, it wasn't impossible. I could still go and visit her if I wanted to.*
*But...*
Atcchan: "Why England?"
Mrs. Sakata: "My husband was offered a job there with his company. It's simple enough."
Atcchan: "B-But that's... T-That's so far away..."
Mrs. Sakata: "It might seem that way to you, but it isn't to me. I was born in England, after all."
*Of course she was. I should have known.*
*I've always known that 'Lucy' isn't a Japanese name. I've always known that Noelle's mother doesn't look anything like any of the other Japanese women I've met.*
*Noelle's mother is a tall, striking beauty. Her eyes are pale blue, her hair blond. She doesn't look Japanese at all.*
*I've always known that Noelle's mother isn't Japanese, but... because I've only ever interacted with her here, in this small village in Japan... I guess I never saw her as anything other than 'my friend's mother.'*
*I never really thought about her as a real human being.*
*Now I feel silly, like a small child.*
Mrs. Sakata: "Even though I've spent most of my life living in Japan, England is still the place where I spent my childhood. It's still my home."
*Mrs. Sakata looks off into the distance as she speaks, her eyes misty. In this brief moment, she looks uncannily like her daughter.*
Mrs. Sakata: "Although I have enjoyed living here... it has always been my dream to go back. Now that I finally have that chance, I don't want to pass it up."
Atcchan: "But... Noelle... Noelle doesn't speak any English..."
Mrs. Sakata: "I know. I realize that she might find it difficult, making such a large transition. It's something I have worried about. But..."
Mrs. Sakata: "It might sound selfish, but... I only moved here for Noelle's sake. If it weren't for her... I definitely wouldn't have come here."
Mrs. Sakata: "I don't like it here. I hate small, closed minded communities like this. People stare at me whenever I go out like I'm some kind of exotic animal."
Mrs. Sakata: "I've had enough of it. I really am sick of living in such a place, where I'll constantly be reminded that I don't belong. It gets... very tiring."
Atcchan: "..."
*I want to reply, but I have no idea what to say. There are no words.*
*How can I ever hope to relate to Mrs. Sakata and her problems when I've never faced anything like that before in my life...?*
*I wonder if I'm being too forward again, asking all kinds of impertinent things, but I still want to know.*
*I'm curious... and I'm worried about Noelle, too.*
*The reason behind their sudden decision to move... What could it be?*
Mrs. Sakata: "Oh, it isn't anything particularly interesting."
*Mrs. Sakata shrugs her shoulders, but her expression remains grim.*
Mrs. Sakata: "My husband was offered an opportunity to work elsewhere and he simply decided to take it. That's all."
Atcchan: "But... What about Noelle? I thought she liked it here?"
Mrs. Sakata: "Of course we factored Noelle's feelings into this as well. What kind of parents do you take us for?"
*Although Mrs. Sakata doesn't sound angry, exactly... she doesn't sound entirely calm, either. I think I might have offended her.*
*I wince, scooting back in my chair as far as I can go. I've never liked being scolded, especially not by people a lot older than me...*
*Hanging my head, I mutter some kind of apology, face flushed.*
*I'm beginning to feel like I've overstayed my welcome...*
*At least Mrs. Sakata takes note of my discomfort, because her expression instantly softens, as does the tone of her voice.*
*No longer sounding like a stern school teacher reprimanding a student for handing in a subpar essay, she instead takes on a gentler tone more fitting for a discussion with a friend around the tea table.*
Mrs. Sakata: "I'm sorry if I was a little terse. I've been on edge lately."
Atcchan: "U-Uh... N-No, um... It's okay... I-I was out of line..."
Mrs. Sakata: "No, that's fine. I know you only asked because you care about my daughter. It's admirable, really."
Atcchan: "I-I... I don't know..."
Mrs. Sakata: "I know. I know you're a nice boy. I didn't mean to snap at you. I'm just stressed about moving."
Atcchan: "Y-Yeah... My parents got stressed about it, too. There was a lot of stuff to sort out. Lots of paperwork, I think."
Mrs. Sakata: "It's true. It is a tiresome process. But it wasn't a decision made on a whim. I discussed it with my family at great length this last year."
Atcchan: "O-Of course... I-I wasn't doubting that."
Mrs. Sakata: "Even so, I'm still not sure if it's the right decision... But I've become so tired of living in this village."
Atcchan: "Tired?"
Mrs. Sakata: "Yes. There's so little to do here and everything is so far away. It feels like my brain is stagnating."
*Mrs. Sakata rubs her forehead, a complicated expression on her face.*
Mrs. Sakata: "Maybe this sounds selfish... but I only moved her because of Noelle. If it wasn't for her, I would never have come here at all."
Atcchan: "U-Um... I-I don't think it's selfish... The fact you sacrificed that much for your daughter is admirable... Um, I think...?"
Mrs. Sakata: "Really? I hope so."
*Mrs. Sakata sighs. She looks at me with tired eyes, underscored with lines. The markers of old age.*
Mrs. Sakata: "I think we need a change of scenery. A change of pace. I think it'll do Noelle some good. Maybe a sudden move will shake her up a little."
Mrs. Sakata: "And it'll do me some good, too. It's all I could think of doing..."
*Silence descends upon us. In this kitchen, in this house, in this isolated part of the village... it really is complete silence.*
Mrs. Sakata: "..."
Atcchan: "..."
*It is Mrs. Sakata who finally breaks it.*
Mrs. Sakata: "Still. Look at me, talking about myself so much. You must be bored. You want to know where Noelle is, don't you?"
Atcchan: "Um... Well... I-I suppose so..."
*That is the real reason why I came here, though it would seem rude just coming out and saying it. I think Mrs. Sakata knows this already, though.*
*She folds her arms, pondering.*
Mrs. Sakata: "Well, let's see... Noelle has been spending a lot of time outside lately. I think she went into the forest this morning with her sketchbook. She must have gone to do some drawings."
Atcchan: "In the forest... Right."
*This might seem like a fairly vague description, but I have a pretty good idea as to where Noelle will be.*
*She and I always used to go to one particular clearing, not far away from the main walking path, to draw. If her routine has remained the same, I don't doubt she'll be there somewhere.*
Mrs. Sakata: "I think she may have taken a picnic hamper with her, too. Maybe she's expecting company."
Atcchan: "C-Company?"
Mrs. Sakata: "That's right. So you should hurry along. If you're only staying here for a few days, you should make those days count."
Atcchan: "A-Ah... Y-Yes, Mrs. Sakata..."
Mrs. Sakata: "And you don't need to call me that. I get enough of that at work."
Atcchan: "Uh... W-Well then... Um..."
*I flounder around with my words, unsure of what to say. W-What other way is there to address a woman much older than you...?*
Mrs. Sakata: "Ehehe~"
*Seeing my distress, Mrs. Sakata starts to laugh.*
*She actually laughs.*
*It's the first time I've ever heard her sound so casual, so it takes me by surprise.*
*When Mrs. Sakata laughs like that... she seems like a different person altogether. A much younger one. Her blue eyes suddenly look a lot brighter, and her face seems to radiate youth.*
*The only way to really describe it is 'girlish.' Girlish and strangely sweet.*
Mrs. Sakata: "If you want, you can call me Lucy."
*I walk through the forest, sticking to the familiar, well-worn paths Noelle and I always used to take in the past.*
*Foliage and loose sticks shift and snap underneath my feet. I can hear the cicadas chirping in the distance, mixed with the noisy chatter of birds amongst the trees.*
*Around me, and everywhere I look, tall trees stand proudly: their trunks thick, boughs laden with leaves, large branches shielding me from the sun.*
*The sunlight that is able to filter through down to the forest floor is tinted green by the leaves.*
*The air smells damp and earthy: of soil and moss; browns and greens. The earthy scent fills me with each breath I take.*
*This must be why my grandparents still look so healthy despite their old age. It's because they live in a tranquil place like this.*
*Compared to the city with its dull grey buildings and constant strings of cars congesting the road, this is far more peaceful.*
*I really do think that humans were meant to live simply, like this, surrounded by nature.*
*Surely this is the best, for both the heart and the body.*
*Even if the convenience stores are a long way away, and it's not so easy to get hold of the jello that Noelle likes so much in the forest. Or any food at all, really...*
*I certainly wouldn't be able to have any ice cream.*
*And, if it started to rain, I don't imagine it would be so nice to live out here. It would get pretty damp and muddy.*
*And what if you happened to catch some kind of disease? Would you just keel over and die, right here in the open, with festering wounds and infected cuts, teeming with maggots...?*
*I-I guess I was being a little overly sentimental earlier, when I claimed that the forest was so much better than the city.*
*Medical treatment, access to food, and a roof over your head when weather is poor is essential if you want to live a comfortable life as a human, I think...*
*Still... This place really is pretty.*
*I walk deeper and deeper into the forest, the trees clustered around me like commuters on a train.*
*It's almost as though I'm sinking... Sinking to the bottom of a pale green sea...*
*Finally, I make my way to the small clearing where Noelle and I always used to go.*
*The ground is soft and mossy, the soil light brown and loosely compacted like sand. The trees in this area are especially dense, forming a circular shape with a small plot of ground nestled in the middle.*
*There, sitting at the base of a large tree trunk, weathered with age and almost completely covered in moss...*
*... is Noelle.*
*She's sitting there on a picnic blanket, spread out on the ground.*
*Just like yesterday when I saw her in the park, she's wearing that white dress with the long, billowing skirts. The lack of sleeves exposes her long, thin arms and sharp collarbone.*
*Her legs are crossed demurely, feet bare, toes twitching. She must've kicked her shoes off somewhere. Noelle never did like wearing them very much.*
*On her lap rests a sketchbook; in her right hand is grasped a pencil.*
*Her eyes are focused downwards. She only occasionally glances upwards to look at the subject of her drawing before returning to her sketchbook.*
*I don't think she's spotted me. She isn't paying me the slightest bit of attention.*
*This is so very like Noelle that I can't help but smile.*
*She's the sort of person who gets engrossed in tasks easily, to the point where she forgets about the outside world altogether.*
*I think it's an admirable skill. Because I'm always worrying about something or other, my brain never shuts up - but Noelle can immerse herself in her own fantasy worlds for hours.*
*She looks... exactly the same as I remember her, all those years ago.*
*Everything is the same, from the way she holds the pencil in her hand, to the way her hair falls over her shoulder.*
*She's even wearing the same ribbon in her hair.*
*It's almost as if she's been waiting for me... frozen in time, in this exact spot. Just like a princess from a fairy tale.*
*A-Ah... Au...*
*Wait... Wasn't that last line, maybe... just a little bit embarrassing?*
*Ah... Now I feel foolish.*
*I start to worry I must look like a stalker or something, standing here at a distance watching her.*
*I should go up to her. I need to let her know I'm here.*
*Watch her silently a little longer.":
*Go and tell her you're here.":
*Aah... I don't want to wait around here any longer. It feels too strange, dumbly watching Noelle from a distance. It's making me restless.*
*With this thought in mind, I decide to press on, not content to linger around pointlessly.*
*I need to act more like Amu. Moving forwards, regardless of the situation...! That's the best way to be!*
*... Right?*
*... Maybe not.*
*As I walk towards Noelle, I suddenly start to feel self-conscious. Why are my footsteps so loud?*
*The rustling, crunching, snapping symphony that accompanies my every moment is so ostentatious it's almost as though I'm being accompanied by a marching band.*
*By this point, Noelle has definitely noticed me.*
*She sets her sketchbook down to one side, her pale blue eyes fixed upon my stupid face.*
*Aah... Now I can't just turn around and leave. That would look even more bizarre.*
*But what kind of expression should I make? How should I give the best impression?*
*I feel like I did on my first day at my new school, when I had to introduce myself to my class. I tripped over almost every single word in my introduction, and wrote my name down wrong on the blackboard.*
*Well, since I hardly ever use my real name, maybe that's sort of acceptable... maybe?*
*Urgh... Just remembering it is making my face go red...*
Noelle: "Hello, Atcchan."
*Of course, Noelle is the one who greets me first. Calm, composed Noelle, who doesn't even blink at my noisy entrance.*
Atcchan: "U-Um... H-Hello, Noelle."
Noelle: "Your face has gone red. Did you get stung by something?"
*Do I look that bad?*
Atcchan: "N-No, um, I-I... I-I was just remembering something embarrassing... A-Ahaha..."
Noelle: "Do you mean the time when you saw a cockroach in school, and you were so surprised that you fell out of your chair?"
*My face turns even redder.*
Atcchan: "A-Ah... N-No, that wasn't what I was thinking of, actually... but that's a good pick..."
Noelle: "Yes, it is. You hit your head on the floor so hard you passed out."
Atcchan: "I remember that..."
Noelle: "And the whole class laughed at you. Even the youngest students."
Atcchan: "I remember that too..."
Noelle: "They called you Cockroach Kid for weeks."
Atcchan: "O-Okay, okay...! I-It's not like I've forgotten or anything! You don't need to remind me!"
Noelle: "I apologize. It just seems like such an embarrassing story I'm surprised that wasn't the one you were thinking about."
Noelle: "If I had done that, I would think about it a lot. At least three times a day."
Atcchan: "A lot of embarrassing things have happened to me. You don't need to list them all..."
*I take a seat next to Noelle, sinking down to the ground with a groan.*
*At least the cool shade cast by the trees is cooling my face down. Maybe it's helping to stem the embarrassment, too.*
*One can but hope.*
Atcchan: "So... What were you drawing?"
Noelle: "A picture."
*... That was a very unhelpful reply.*
Atcchan: "I realize that, but... what of? Flowers...? Trees?"
Noelle: "No. None of those. An animal."
Atcchan: "Like a bird?"
Noelle: "Not a bird."
Noelle: "I was drawing a rabbit."
Atcchan: "Oh? Can I see it?"
Noelle: "No."
Atcchan: "Why not?"
Noelle: "Because it isn't finished. You startled it, and the rabbit ran away."
Atcchan: "A-Ah... O-Oh..."
*I hang my head in shame. Even though Noelle didn't raise her voice, it still feels like I'm being scolded.*
*Maybe she has more in common with her mother than I thought.*
Noelle: "Don't worry. I'm not annoyed."
Atcchan: "Even though I ruined your drawing...?"
Noelle: "Even so. There are more important things."
Atcchan: "But... how long were you working on it?"
Noelle: "Long enough to realize it wasn't worth continuing. I couldn't make it look right. Don't worry about it."
*Noelle turns her head, offering me a small smile.*
*It's reasonably muted, much like the rest of Noelle's expressions... but even so, it's a comfort.*
*I'm glad she isn't upset.*
Noelle: "Even though rabbits are cute, and sketching them makes me happy... it isn't the same."
Atcchan: "It isn't the same as what? Having a real rabbit?"
Noelle: "I do want a real rabbit, but my parents won't let me."
Atcchan: "Why?"
Noelle: "... They think it will get fur around the house."
Atcchan: "Well, your house is pretty pristine. Your mother doesn't seem like the type of person who'd allow something like that."
Noelle: "She is quite strict. But I don't mind so much. She simply likes everything to be in its proper place. That wasn't what I meant, though."
Atcchan: "Oh...? What did you mean...?"
*Noelle draws her legs up under her chin, resting her chin on her knees.*
*Snaking her slender arms around her legs, she looks up at me from beneath her eyelashes.*
Noelle: "I mean... I'm happy. I'm happy that you came to see me. That's all."
Noelle: "That's more important than any drawing of any rabbit in all the world... I think."
*Although I feel distinctly awkward, hanging around here like an unwelcome intruder... I think Noelle is very focused on her sketching. I don't want to distract her.*
*I wait patiently, trying to tell myself that I'm not being creepy.*
*It's not like I'm stalking her. I'm just trying to be courteous. I'm not doing anything wrong, right...?*
*I wonder what she's drawing. Her expression looks pretty intense, even more so than usual.*
*I've seen Noelle draw still life pictures before, and even though she does take that quite seriously, her posture is never usually this rigid, or her eyes so focused.*
*Then, probably... she isn't drawing a still life at all. Instead, it must be something alive. Something that can move around - and so, something that requires a greater amount of concentration to draw.*
*I begin to look about out of curiosity, searching for the subject of Noelle's latest piece.*
*It's a white rabbit, slightly obscured by foliage, sitting in the grass. Its eyes are alert, its head moving this way and that as it surveys its surroundings.*
*I wonder how long it's been here for, and how long Noelle has been sketching it.*
*It's pretty impressive that she's able to remain so still and silent, so as not to frighten it away. I wouldn't be able to do it.*
*A few moments pass. I don't know how many.*
*Noelle keeps on sketching, her pencil skirting across the open page of her sketchbook as she glances up and down.*
*However... this small moment of tranquility can't last forever. These moments never can.*
*The rabbit suddenly raises its head, ears alert. Maybe it's heard something. Something I can't hear but it can. There must be a reason for those long ears.*
*Finally, the rabbit bounds away, disappearing off into the foliage.*
*It blends in with its surroundings completely... and, in a matter of seconds, vanishes. Almost as though it was never there at all.*
*I take this as my cue to make my presence known.*
Atcchan: "Ah... H-Hey there..."
*Noelle doesn't seem surprised at my sudden appearance at all. Instead, she lifts her head, giving me a wave.*
*The contrast between this Noelle and the one from before, focusing intently on her drawing, is so vast they almost seem like two different people.*
Noelle: "Hello, Atcchan."
Atcchan: "Y-Yeah, h-hello... Um..."
*I pause, trying to think of something clever to say.*
Atcchan: "So, uh... Were you drawing...?"
*Wait. That wasn't clever of all!*
*Of course I knew she was drawing - I saw her do it. That's such a pointless question. It's like asking if the sky is blue...*
*At least Noelle doesn't seem to mind.*
Noelle: "Yes. I was drawing."
Atcchan: "The rabbit?"
*Noelle nods.*
Noelle: "It was a very cute rabbit."
Atcchan: "Y-Yeah, it was. Not that I know so much about rabbits. They all look cute to me."
Noelle: "This one was particularly cute. She had nice eyes."
Atcchan: "You could tell it had nice eyes from that distance?"
*And she could also tell the rabbit was a 'she?'*
*This girl really is something.*
Noelle: "Yes. They were very intelligent eyes."
*Noelle takes hold of her sketchbook in both hands, turning it over this way and that, shifting it around at different angles. At the same time, she tilts her head.*
*What's she looking for? Maybe she's hoping, if she stares at her picture in a certain way, she'll discover something that wasn't there before - like one of those magic eye images.*
Noelle: "..."
Noelle: "It's no good."
*But I guess Noelle can't find what she wants in her picture after all.*
*With a sigh, she closes her sketchbook and sets it down by her side.*
Atcchan: "You don't like it...?"
*Another sigh.*
Atcchan: "Did you make a mistake?"
Noelle: "Not really. It's just beyond my abilities, I suppose. I wanted to capture something special."
Atcchan: "Can I take a look?"
Noelle: "Well, it isn't finished. I don't know..."
Atcchan: "I'm sure it'll be fine."
Noelle: "If you're sure, then. It's not very good, though, so don't expect too much."
*I take a seat next to Noelle and cross my legs. Then, I reach out for the discarded sketchbook.*
Atcchan: "Ah..."
*When I flip it open... my eyes widen in surprise.*
*I always knew Noelle was good at drawing... but I never knew she was this good. She must have improved during these last two years.*
*The rabbit looks almost identical to the one I saw sitting by the tree. Everything, from its twitchy little nose to its alert eyes, are exactly the same.*
*Noelle's lines are bold and strong in stark contrast to her personality. It's clear a lot of dedication and passion went into creating this picture.*
*This really is amazing, and yet...*
*Noelle said she didn't like it?*
*Frowning, I set the sketchbook down on my lap.*
Atcchan: "Why don't you like it? It's really good."
Noelle: "You might think that, but I don't. Art is subjective."
Atcchan: "B-But... this is, objectively, a good picture, isn't it?"
Noelle: "I don't think so."
*A pause.*
Noelle: "I don't know. I don't like the eyes. They look too lifeless."
Atcchan: "Well, it is a drawing."
Noelle: "I know. But... I wanted it to be more than that, somehow. Maybe."
*And yet, despite Noelle's critical evaluation of her work, my curiosity has been piqued. I want to see the rest.*
Atcchan: "Hey, um... Can I take a look at your other pictures?"
Noelle: "... If you want. But I still haven't reached it yet. I don't know how to draw what I want."
Atcchan: "I'm sure they'll look good anyways."
*Noelle bites her lower lip. She looks troubled.*
Noelle: "Maybe to you... but that's only because you don't understand my vision. You don't know what I want to communicate. But I do."
Atcchan: "Well... I'll have to take a look and see, I guess."
*With Noelle's consent, I begin to flip through the sketchbook.*
*Each page is covered with drawings; either quick sketches or more developed pieces with firmer, more defined lines.*
*All of these drawings are amazing. They're better than anything I could ever do.*
*But the amount of craftsmanship isn't the only common theme amongst these pieces...*
*It doesn't take me long before I realize it. It stands out almost immediately.*
*Every single drawing in this book... and, there must be one hundred or so... whether they include background details or not; trees, flowers or moss...*
*... has the same subject matter.*
Atcchan: "Rabbits...?"
Noelle: "Mm."
*Noelle nods, picking at a loose thread at the hem of her sundress.*
Noelle: "I've been liking them a lot lately. They're cute."
Atcchan: "I-I agree, rabbits are cute, but... don't you ever want to draw anything else?"
*Noelle blinks, tipping her head to one side.*
Noelle: "Why?"
Atcchan: "W-Well, uh... I don't know. Doesn't it get boring, doing the same thing over and over?"
Noelle: "But it isn't the same thing. It changes all the time."
Atcchan: "It does?"
Noelle: "Mm."
Noelle: "There are different rabbits. They make different poses. There are different locations. Different times of the day."
Noelle: "And how I feel when I draw them, too. It all changes. Always. Each picture is different from the last. No two drawings are the same."
Atcchan: "I-I guess that's true, but... Aren't there other things you want to do?"
Noelle: "Maybe. Sometimes. But I have to. This is what I need to do, I think."
Atcchan: "Why?"
*Noelle looks at me for a few moments.*
*I can almost imagine little gears turning inside of her brain, moving slowly as they try to generate the answer she thinks is the most correct.*
*Noelle doesn't say careless things without thinking. She never says anything she doesn't mean. And so, all of her words...*
*... they weigh heavily, each with equal importance.*
Noelle: "If I don't draw the rabbits... then who else will...?"
Atcchan: "Huh...?"
*It's a strange, enigmatic answer, and one I don't really understand.*
Noelle: "..."
Noelle: "But... If that's too complicated..."
Noelle: "I just think they're cute. That's all. And I like cute things. They make me happy."
*Noelle and I sit together, cross-legged, on a tartan picnic blanket spread out underneath the old, moss covered tree.*
*We're both silent, sketching. Noelle procured another sketchbook from the large picnic hamper she brought with her and handed it to me, asking if I'd keep her company. Of course, I obliged.*
*Somehow, this situation with both of us sitting down demurely like two little kids, neither making a sound... reminds me of being back in school.*
*My pencil, also borrowed from Noelle, moves across the page slowly, falteringly.*
*My drawing style is very different from Noelle's - the polar opposite of her firm, confident lines. Noelle's sketches rest upon the page with a certain kind of authority, as though even the drawing itself is sure of its placement in the world.*
*Mine, however...*
*To put it bluntly, they look awful.*
*It's true that I've drawn together with Noelle underneath this tree before, but I've never had much artistic talent.*
*I overthink things and start to panic. I focus too much on the objects I'm trying to draw, and then feel guilty if I'm unable to replicate them accurately - as though my subpar skills are doing nature a great disservice.*
*If I get this anxious drawing flowers and trees that can't talk or offer any kind of criticism... I wonder just how worked up I'd get if I actually had to draw a real human being.*
*I'd probably get so scared that my amateurish strokes would offend them that I'd have some kind of breakdown. I'm not very good at dealing with pressure.*
*Noelle and I sit like this for a while without talking. The sounds of our pencils tracing across pages in our sketchbooks, mingle with the rush of the wind, the rustling grass, and the birds in the trees.*
*It feels a lot like it did back then. A long, lazy day that stretches out forever; almost endless. It feels as though this moment might last forever.*
*I wish it could.*
*I'm worried I'll ruin it if I talk. With my clumsy voice and awkward syntax I'd break something irreplaceable; shattering this delicate, dainty moment between my teeth.*
*So I keep silent. There isn't anything pressing I really want to say, anyway... And if there is, I can keep it at the back of my mind.*
*If I wasn't starting to feel hungry, maybe I could stay like this with Noelle - frozen in silence, together.*
*But of course, I do get hungry. If you have a human body, it's inevitable. Humans need food to survive, after all.*
*And so the silence is broken by a loud rumbling from my stomach.*
Atcchan: "Aah... I-I'm sorry..."
*Noelle smiles, setting down her sketchbook.*
Noelle: "Hungry?"
Atcchan: "Y-Yeah, I guess. It's been a while since breakfast."
Noelle: "I never have breakfast. It slows me down."
Atcchan: "Really? But don't you ever get hungry?"
Noelle: "You can get used to anything after a while."
Atcchan: "I don't know if that's good for your body. Maybe that's why you're so skinny..."
Noelle: "Hm? Do I really look skinny?"
Atcchan: "J-Just a little..."
*More than a 'little', actually.*
*Noelle's always looked somewhat ethereal, but now... I worry that a single gust of wind could blow her away.*
Noelle: "That's just how I am. I have fragile bones."
Atcchan: "E-Even if the bones are fragile, you can at least put some meat on them!"
*Noelle frowns.*
Noelle: "My mother always tells me to eat more too. It's tiresome."
Atcchan: "She's only saying that because she's concerned about you. And I'm a little worried as well! Breakfast is the most important meal of the day!"
Noelle: "Aah... But eating it is a pain. It takes up time and makes my stomach feel heavy. It doesn't make me feel happy."
*I can't help but smile at this, even if I am trying to remain stern. Noelle sounds unusually defiant.*
*If I'm acting like Noelle's mother, then she's acting just like a child who's being scolded.*
Atcchan: "Well... It's your own life, and you're free to choose what you want to do, but... I still think you should eat more."
Atcchan: "I get worried about you, you know?"
Noelle: "Hm... Well, okay... If that's what you think, I'll try to remember. But..."
Atcchan: "But what? Don't tell me if you eat food at a certain time of the day you'll multiply by two, or turn into a pumpkin."
Noelle: "It's not that - although that would be interesting. It's just..."
Noelle: "It's already after breakfast. I suppose that means I'll have to work on that tomorrow."
*Aaah... Why does she look so proud for realizing it? Does she think she's thwarted me or something...?*
*O-Of course I already knew that! I'm not stupid!*
Noelle: "I will try to remember, but sometimes I forget things. Like my socks. I always forget to wear socks."
Atcchan: "Don't your feet get cold?"
Noelle: "It isn't winter, so it's fine."
*Noelle wiggles her toes, all ten of them, as though confirming their status.*
Noelle: "Anyway. If you're hungry, I made food. I made it all myself last night. Do you want to look?"
*I examine the picnic basket that's lying by Noelle's side.*
Atcchan: "Woah... That's huge. It looks like there's enough food for twelve people in there!"
Noelle: "Mm. Maybe I made too much..."
Atcchan: "W-Well, my grandparents keep telling me to eat more. I'm sure they'll approve."
Noelle: "Why do they want you to eat more?"
Atcchan: "Because they think I'm too skinny."
Noelle: "Even though you eat breakfast every day?"
Atcchan: "Yeah. It doesn't seem to make a difference, I - H-Hey!"
Noelle: "I got you~ "
Atcchan: "G-Gah... I-It was a complete defeat... A flawless victory..."
Noelle: "Thank you very much. Ehehe~"
*Noelle is a lot craftier than I give her credit for.*
Atcchan: "B-But anyway..."
Atcchan: "Can I take a look inside?"
Noelle: "By all means, please do. And try some if you want. Unlike art, food isn't made merely to be looked at."
*With Noelle's permission, I open up the picnic hamper and dig through the contents.*
*Just as I thought... there really is a lot.*
*There are sandwiches of many different flavors - cheese, ham, even strawberry and kiwi.*
*In carefully prepared lunch boxes I see mounds of fluffy white rice, egg omelet cooked to perfection, pickled vegetables, boiled eggs... It's almost endless.*
*There are even little octopi made of sausage pierced on sticks, and apple slices cut into the shape of rabbits.*
*Aah... I forgot how good at cooking Noelle is...*
*I was always surprised at her cooking skills given she looks so daydreamy, lost in her own little world.*
*I thought that for sure she'd be the type of person to leave pots on the boil for too long or accidentally use too much hot sauce in her curry, but she's far better at cooking than I am.*
*Maybe it's because cooking is like art. It's about the presentation.*
Atcchan: "It's impressive that you were able to make so much."
Noelle: "It's not so impressive. I just felt like it. That's all."
Atcchan: "B-But... You didn't even know if I was coming. I never confirmed it with you. What would you have done if I didn't show up?"
*There is a small pause.*
*Noelle lifts her head to look at me. Her pale blue eyes stare directly into mine.*
*Somehow... it feels as though she's looking right through me. I feel about as transparent as a jellyfish.*
Noelle: "... I just had a feeling that you would come. That's all."
*She says it simply, as though it's a fact... just as one would state that summer comes after spring. A logical statement that everybody knows that doesn't need to be supported by evidence. The objective truth.*
*I-Is that how much Noelle trusts me?*
*How can she trust me to that extent when I'm so indecisive and weak-willed?*
*I-I feel like, maybe... with that serious, light blue stare... she's expecting just a little too much of me.*
*It makes me feel uneasy, somehow... as though a cold wind is blowing down my back.*
Noelle: "Well then..."
*Noelle smiles, offering me a piece of fried chicken pinched between her chopsticks (when did she pick those up, anyway?).*
*Her smile is so unusually vibrant, stars seem to be twinkling around her face.*
Noelle: "Do you want to try it?"
*I feel my face flushing. My cheeks feel hot.*
Atcchan: "Huh...? You... you want to feed me...?"
Noelle: "Why not? Aren't we friends?"
Atcchan: "I-Is that what friends do?"
Noelle: "I don't know... But I read somewhere that food tastes more delicious if somebody feeds it to you."
Atcchan: "Wa... W-Where did you read something like that...?"
*This book that Noelle has somehow gotten her hands on... sounds kind of dangerous.*
*Dangerous for my heart.*
Noelle: "I found it in a girl's comic that belonged to Amu."
Atcchan: "Y-You went looking though Amu's things? Isn't that illegal?"
Noelle: "It fell out of her bag during class. I found it on the floor."
Noelle: "I know I should have returned it as soon as possible, but I was interested... so I looked through it, just a little."
Noelle: "Was that bad of me...?"
*Waah...*
*Now Noelle's giving me those puppy dog eyes... I-I can't resist, can I?*
*Was this another technique Noelle learned from that book? And why was Amu reading something like that to begin with? It clashes with her character.*
Atcchan: "O-Okay, fine... T-Thanks for the food..."
Noelle: "Ehehe~ Yay~"
*And so, my face still flushed, I let Noelle feed me; nibbling at the pieces of food she offers me between her chopsticks.*
*S-Somehow... T-This kind of thing seems a little too intimate...*
*My heart is pounding so fast I can hardly focus on how the food tastes.*
Atcchan: "Aah... I'm starting to feel tired..."
Noelle: "But walking is the best way to work off a meal, Atcchan~"
Atcchan: "I know, but I'm getting a pain in my side..."
Noelle: "That's no good at all. If you never exercise, it's no good for your body. Even if it doesn't make you happy, you should still do it."
Atcchan: "Coming from you, that stings a little..."
Noelle: "Ehehe~ And now you know how I felt."
*I breath in heavily, doubled over by a tree. My ankles sting. I think I must've walked into a patch of nettles by mistake.*
*That's probably why our 'relaxing walk' ended up being such a burden to me.*
*I hope my skin isn't hasn't gone red and blotchy.*
*Well, even if my ankles aren't red, my face probably is.*
Noelle: "If you want to rest a while, I don't mind. I like it here."
Atcchan: "W-Wawawa... T-Thank you..."
*I'm so grateful for these simple words I'm almost in tears. I feel like getting to my knees and kissing Noelle's toes in gratitude - even if her feet are still bare, caked with soil and mud.*
*... Actually, I might pass on the toe-worshipping. Just for now.*
*How is Noelle able to navigate these woods with such ease when I - even wearing my shoes - still managed to get stung?*
*It isn't fair.*
Noelle: "If you feel agitated, you can listen to the river. It's soothing, isn't it?"
Atcchan: "A-Ah... Yeah, it is. Soothing, I mean."
Noelle: "I like to come down here. It's good for thinking."
Atcchan: "You do much thinking?"
Noelle: "Of course. I am a human. My brain is working all the time. I feel it works best here."
*Noelle takes a seat on the ground by the side of the river.*
*I follow suit, first pausing to wipe away any stray clods of dirt that could stain my pants.*
*We sit together in relative silence, listening to the sound of the river.*
*I can see small insects hovering over the water, suspended in the air. A dragonfly flutters past, caught on the gentle breeze.*
*The indistinct, murky shapes of fish move along through the river, carried by the current.*
*I wish I had some bread with me so I could feed them. Noelle and I always came here to feed the fish when we were younger.*
*Trees surround us on all sides, forming a protective barrier between us and the outside world.*
*Right here, right now... it feels as though I'm lost inside my own little universe, detached from the rest of reality.*
*Here, it's just Noelle and I, together; existing in a small fragment splintered off from all other life.*
Noelle: "Atcchan..."
*Noelle's voice is soft. She looks pensive, curious; dipping her toes in the water as she speaks, swirling them around.*
Atcchan: "What is it?"
Noelle: "..."
Noelle: "Is there anywhere like this in the city?"
Atcchan: "What do you mean?"
Noelle: "Somewhere... quiet. And peaceful."
Atcchan: "Maybe a public library. It's the only place where people aren't allowed to talk, after all."
Noelle: "Oh... I see..."
Atcchan: "There's nowhere as wide or as green as this, though. There are too many people."
Noelle: "Not even the parks?"
*I wrinkle my nose.*
Atcchan: "Too crowded. There are always mothers with children there, or people with dogs, or gossiping students..."
Atcchan: "Everywhere you go, there's some kind of noise. It's impossible to avoid it."
Noelle: "... Oh. That's sad."
*Noelle sighs, staring down at her reflection in the river.*
*When she swirls her feet around in the clear, cool water, her reflection distorts, looking strange and inhuman; ripples forming across her features and dispersing it outwards like running watercolors.*
Noelle: "I don't like people very much..."
Atcchan: "But you're talking to me. I'm a person, aren't I?"
Noelle: "Yes. You are a person. But you are not 'people.'"
Noelle: "One person, I think I can manage. Any more than that is just... a hassle."
Atcchan: "Sitting here together, though... you and I are both 'people.' We make a plural together, don't we?"
Noelle: "I suppose..."
*Noelle accepts this piece of logic begrudgingly, frowning.*
Noelle: "..."
Noelle: "People are no good."
Noelle: "When there are too many people... it gets so noisy, and it isn't pretty at all. I don't like it."
Noelle: "I would never want to live in a place with lots of people. Not again."
*She sounds despondent, listless; as though all her energy has drained away. I wonder what triggered it.*
*Maybe nothing did. Maybe these resentments are ones she's been turning around in her head for a while.*
*I don't know.*
*Even though I'm Noelle's best friend, it's always been hard for me to understand what she's thinking.*
*Honestly, I... I don't know very much about her at all.*
*Not about her old life. Not about her old school. Not about her old friends.*
*Not even about her current feelings, right here and now.*
*I can't... understand it at all.*
*All I can do is nod my head.*
Atcchan: "Well... I kind of agree with you there."
Noelle: "You do?"
Atcchan: "Mm. I find large groups of people overwhelming as well. It's too noisy and crowded..."
Noelle: "And yet... you still had to move to a place like that."
Atcchan: "I did."
Noelle: "Wasn't that sad?"
Atcchan: "It was a little sad to begin with. I was kind of nervous. But..."
Atcchan: "After I met Saki, Miho, and Yuuna, everything seemed to work out."
Noelle: "Who?"
Atcchan: "People at my new school."
Noelle: "You mean, your new friends...?"
Atcchan: "Hey. You're still my friend too, you know?"
Noelle: "I know..."
Atcchan: "Besides... I had to make new friends. I had no choice. It was the only way to fit in."
Noelle: "The only way, is it...?"
*Noelle sighs, shoulders slumping.*
*She begins to tear at clumps of grass with her fingers, yanking the green tendrils up out of the soil with unexpected strength.*
*Although her voice remains quiet as ever, she's clearly agitated. She doesn't tell me that, though - not straight out. She isn't that kind of person.*
Noelle: "I know how that feels... Not having a choice."
Atcchan: "You do...?"
Noelle: "Yes. I know it. And I don't like it."
*Noelle's fingers continue to work at the grass, tearing out clumps. I can see small bald patches opening up in the riverbank, brown spots of exposed soil amongst the grass. Somehow, it looks kind of sad.*
*I wonder, if the grass could talk, whether it would scream or not. Noelle's rough treatment of it looks quite painful.*
Noelle: "In this world... The only person I can control is myself. The only person I can rely on is myself. Everybody else..."
Noelle: "They do things I can't understand... and I have no way of stopping them."
*I watch Noelle silently. She sounds bitter. Her words are cold.*
*I wonder if this has anything to do with the fact she'll be moving.*
*In a scenario like that, it's understandable that Noelle would feel trapped, unable to say what she truly wants. I know. I've been there myself. But...*
Atcchan: "Hey. I-It'll be okay."
Noelle: "But how do you know?"
Atcchan: "I... Well, I don't, but..."
Noelle: "But?"
Atcchan: "..."
Atcchan: "Sometimes, you need to tell yourself that, so you can get through the hard times."
Noelle: "How pragmatic."
*Noelle turns to look at me. She's holding a small clump of grass torn roughly from the ground and tipped with dirt in her right hand, squeezing it tight so her palms turn green.*
*I wonder how long Noelle has been suffering for. How long has she been worrying in silence, with nobody to turn to?*
*I...*
*I have to try and help her. Even though I was a bad friend in the past... right now, I'm here for her. I have to be here for her.*
*Maybe... this is the only meaningful way I can apologize for leaving her.*
*I'm going to do my best.*
Atcchan: "I think, maybe... P-Probably... well, uh... You're worried about moving, right?"
*Noelle flinches. Her grip on the grass in her right hand tightens, her fingers flexing.*
*She doesn't reply, not with words, but her reaction is all the answer I need.*
Atcchan: "Well, I, um... I, too... didn't want to leave. I was worried about it... and argued with my parents a lot."
Atcchan: "My mother got a little mad at me, actually. A-Ahaha..."
Atcchan: "B-But... R-Really, it... It wasn't nearly as bad as I expected, you know...?"
Noelle: "Really...?"
Atcchan: "Yeah...! I mean, um... It's a little crowded and noisy, and there are a lot of people... and it took me a while to get used to the public transportation..."
Atcchan: "I may have gotten lost once or twice... or maybe even a few more times than that... Ahahaha..."
*My face flushes as I remember. Those are embarrassing memories... but still.*
*I hope by sharing them it will bring a smile to Noelle's face. That's all I want.*
*My pride is worth nothing when it comes to Noelle's smile. That's like comparing coal to a diamond.*
Atcchan: "But there isn't too much to worry about. It's still in Japan, after all. It's not like you're moving to a different country, right?"
*Noelle surveys me silently, blinking slowly. Once. Twice.*
Noelle: "..."
Atcchan: "..."
Noelle: "..."
*Silence.*
*And then...*
Noelle: "Yes. That is true. It should... be fine."
*Although she says it slowly, hesitantly, as though she doesn't quite believe it... I like to think maybe, just maybe, I was able to get through to her.*
Atcchan: "T-That's right! And we can still see each other. Maybe not a lot, but we can write letters."
Noelle: "Letters... I think I might like that."
Atcchan: "Mmhmm! And not to mention, all of those convenience stores! You can buy as much jello as you want!"
Noelle: "Yes... But..."
*Noelle looks at me... and a very small smile crosses her face.*
Noelle: "Not too much jello. Then it wouldn't be special anymore."
*I wonder if it has anything to do with what Mrs. Sakata said earlier. Maybe it's about her family's plan to move.*
*It's still hard for me to take in, even now.*
*England... They're going to move to England.*
*In a situation like that, of course Noelle would feel trapped.*
*It's not as though she can just ignore her parents. What her parents say goes; she's too young to disobey.*
*This is something I know too well myself, after arguing with my mother about moving.*
*Still... England.*
*That's so far away.*
*If I were in Noelle's position, it would all feel so hopeless. It would feel hopeless... and I would be scared.*
*I wonder if Noelle is scared... or angry.*
*Is that why she's tearing handfuls of grass out of the ground so forcefully, until the tips of her fingers and the palms of her hands get stained with green pigmentation and brown soil?*
*Is it an act of defiance? A symbolic stand against her parents... which will amount to nothing, given they can't see it?*
*I don't know - but I don't want to ask.*
*Since Noelle hasn't mentioned herself that she's moving to England, it's clear that she doesn't want to talk about it. Maybe she isn't ready to.*
*She probably doesn't want me to know about it.*
*It would better if I let her tell me in her own time... whenever she feels ready to confide.*
*If I said anything careless, I might just make her feel worse - and I don't want to make her cry. I'd feel too guilty.*
*I think it's best to remain silent.*
*I'll remain silent and try to support her without words, by staying at her side.*
*All I can do now is keep being her friend.*
*As evening descends, the forest air starts to smell even crisper than before.*
*I don't know long Noelle and I were walking for, but it must have been a while.*
*Traversing around the forest aimlessly, moving from one place to another... even though it wasn't a particularly exciting experience, it was still fun.*
*Simply being with Noelle was more than enough to make this experience special.*
*Although we didn't talk so much, Noelle did get uncharacteristically excited about some things.*
*I remember with a shudder the large cluster of mushrooms she found growing against the bark of an old, dead tree.*
*Even though she claimed, her eyes sparkling:*
Noelle: "These mushrooms are really cute! And they're good for you! They have medicinal properties and can cure aches and pains!"
Noelle: "I think you should try one~  Hm, hm, hm~"
*I couldn't quite bring myself to.*
*I don't know why. It's not like I didn't trust Noelle's judgment. I'm sure, when it comes to the various flora and fauna of the forest, she has a far greater understanding of it than I do.*
*However...*
*There's something about fungi that's inherently creepy - just like spiders and small, scuttling insects. That they make a living leeching off of other living beings has always seemed sinister and suspect to me.*
*With the oncoming evening, the two of us have eventually returned to our original starting point. The small clearing with the large, moss covered tree.*
*Noelle's picnic blanket and wicker basket are still laid out there, in the exact same places they were before - just like exhibits in a museum. Timeless.*
*Seeing them again feels almost nostalgic. That tartan blanket and that wicker basket... they're like objects from the past, hazy memories lingering on the edge of my mind.*
*Even though Noelle and I couldn't have spent more than a few hours walking together... it feels as though we've been together in the forest for days.*
Noelle: "Atcchan..."
*Noelle's voice, soft as falling snow, interrupts my musings.*
*She sounds constrained, a little quieter than usual. Her voice trails off hesitantly into nothing, falling into an empty void.*
*I turn to look at her. In her white dress, arms exposed, she looks very small - even though, in actuality, she's an inch or two taller than I am.*
*Everybody's taller than I am.*
Noelle: "Atcchan... Thank you."
Atcchan: "H-Huh? Why are you thanking me all of a sudden?"
Noelle: "For spending time with me. I had a fun day."
Atcchan: "W-Well, of course I wanted to spend time with you. I like you."
Noelle: "Really...?"
*Noelle's expression darkens. Storm clouds gather across her countenance. Her pale blue eyes look oddly cold.*
Atcchan: "O-Of course. You're my good friend. Why wouldn't I like you?"
Noelle: "Oh... I don't know. I was just wondering..."
Atcchan: "Wondering what...?"
*There is a long pause. It takes Noelle a while to articulate her thoughts.*
Noelle: "... It's about Amu."
Atcchan: "Amu...?"
*I didn't expect Noelle to talk about Amu, so the sudden mention of her name catches me off guard.*
*It isn't just the subject matter that makes me double-take, however. It's the tone of Noelle's voice.*
*Even though it sounds just as quiet and calm as ever, there's something different to it. Something I can't quite put my finger on.*
*If I had to try and define this mystery quality in just one word... maybe I would say...*
*Foreboding.*
*Her voice is oddly harsh... and completely devoid of warmth - like the cold hearth of an unlit fire.*
Noelle: "I know that you're close to Amu. After all, she is your best friend. You've been friends with her longer than you have with me."
Atcchan: "W-Well... Yes, that's true, but... That doesn't change the fact you're one of my best friends too."
Noelle: "So you say... But..."
*Noelle looks down at the ground. Her silver hair obscures her eyes so I can't see them. I don't know what kind of expression she's making.*
*Her long, white fingers begin to pick at a loose thread at the hem of her dress. Pick, pick, pick.*
*All of a sudden, those long fingers look a lot like the legs of a spider...*
Noelle: "If you wanted to spend time with Amu, I would understand."
*It's cold.*
*Why is it so cold?*
*Even though evening is approaching, and the wind running through the woods is a little chillier than before... I don't think that's the reason.*
*It's not the wind.*
*It's Noelle.*
*The sound of her voice, and her choice of words... are making me feel cold.*
Atcchan: "I don't get it... Why are you talking about Amu? I decided to spend time with you, didn't I?"
Noelle: "That is true. But..."
*She sighs. It's a soft exhale of air; a very slight movement from her chest, pushing inwards.*
