Noelle: "Amu's company must be far more enjoyable than mine. That's what all our classmates seem to think."
Noelle: "Amu's desk is always surrounded by friends, and everybody likes talking to her. I've never seen her alone before."
Atcchan: "That's because she's a sociable person. She likes talking to people. But there's nothing wrong with being quiet, either."
Noelle: "People do say that... but I wonder. Maybe it's just a nicety. Something people say, but nobody believes."
Atcchan: "N-Noelle... T-There's nothing wrong with you. There's nothing wrong with being quiet."
Noelle: "I don't know. I don't know what's best... and I don't know what's right. Sometimes, I worry."
Atcchan: "W-What is it... that you've been worrying about...?"
*My voice is barely a whisper. It's hard to get the words out.*
*I'm afraid to hear the answer, but... at the same time, I want to know.*
*Humans always want to know. We're nosy creatures.*
*But even if I knew... would I be able to understand?*
Noelle: "Atcchan."
*Noelle stares me down intently. Her expression is piercing. Those light blue eyes don't look so dreamy anymore.*
Noelle: "Did you come back here because you wanted to see me or Amu?"
Atcchan: "Ah..."
*In that instant... my body freezes. It feels as though my blood has turned to ice.*
*Isn't that... an unfair question?*
*I came here because I wanted to see both of them. Noelle and Amu. What's wrong with that? Isn't that good enough?*
Atcchan: "Y-You're both precious friends to me...!"
Noelle: "But that isn't the answer to the question I asked. Try again, Atcchan."
*Noelle's eyes...*
*There's something strange about them. They don't look normal.*
*They're dark and hard, like stones or buttons. There's no compassion in them at all.*
Noelle: "Atcchan. Who do you like the most? Me or Amu?"
*She asks this question pointedly, her gaze focused. I can't look away from her. It's as though I've been pinned in place.*
*She wants me to reply. I feel like I have to reply.*
*But to a question like this... what on earth can I say...?*
*I like you both the same.":
*I like you more than Amu.":
*It's clear that Noelle is expecting a certain answer from me, but I can't give it. How could I?*
*How could I tell her that I like her more than Amu when they're both my dear friends? They both mean so much to me, I couldn't possibly choose.*
*But Noelle doesn't seem to like my reasoning.*
*Although the expression on her face doesn't flicker, it's abundantly obvious she's unhappy. I can tell that much by the tone of her voice.*
Noelle: "Both the same?"
Atcchan: "Y-Yes."
Noelle: "But why?"
Atcchan: "B-Because... B-Because you both mean a lot to me and... A-And I can't choose. I-It's too cruel... to make me choose..."
*My legs are shaking. My voice is, too.*
*The girl standing before me in that white dress... is Noelle, isn't it?*
*I don't know.*
*Even though Noelle is one of my best friends, and I've known her for seven years... right now, she looks more like a stranger.*
Noelle: "That's hypocritical. You're contradicting yourself."
Atcchan: "I-I am...?"
Noelle: "Yes. If it really was impossible to choose between us, then you wouldn't have been able to do it so easily yourself."
Atcchan: "I-I... I..."
*My voice falters; breaking away like the side of an eroded cliff.*
*I can't reply. I can't say anything, do anything. I have no way to defend myself.*
*How can you argue against the truth?*
*She's right. I did choose between them. Even though I didn't want to, I did.*
*When I moved away, Amu was the one I confided in. Amu was the one I told.*
*I never said a thing to Noelle, reasoning that it would hurt her if she knew - but I was just fooling myself. I was being a coward.*
*I didn't want to move... and I didn't want to face the reality that I was moving. I created an illusion in which everything was fine and nothing would change... hoping to live out my last days in this village as peacefully as possible.*
*Looking at it like that... I really was selfish. Inexcusably so.*
Noelle: "You're a liar."
*Her words are cold and unforgiving, striking my body like stones. Each and every single one leaves a wound.*
*I don't have the heart to try and deflect these blows. I don't even know if I deserve to.*
Atcchan: "Y-Yes. I know."
Noelle: "And you really did upset me. Do you know that, too?"
Atcchan: "I... I do..."
*I look at the ground, red-faced.*
Atcchan: "I know I hurt you, and I really am sorry..."
Noelle: "Atcchan."
Atcchan: "Y-Yes...?"
Noelle: "... I don't like people who tell lies."
*Yes...*
*That is... the only answer I can give, isn't it? Even though I feel guilty for simply thinking about it...*
*It's the only answer Noelle wants to hear. I can tell, judging by that cold, hard look on her face.*
*In these oppressive surroundings, trees pressing in on me from all sides, Noelle affixing me with that lifeless stare that reflects no light...*
*I don't know what else I can do.*
*There's nothing I can do.*
*I only hope, if Amu ever finds out, she'll forgive me.*
*I'm sorry. I know I'm a coward.*
*I just don't know what else to say.*
Atcchan: "I... I like you more than Amu, Noelle..."
*Noelle accepts this response with a slight nod of her head, but she still doesn't turn away. Her eyes bore into mine, with an intensity that makes me shiver.*
Noelle: "Is that true?"
Atcchan: "Y-Yes. It's true..."
*She surveys me coolly, unblinking. Her lips are pursed slightly, eyebrows furrowed.*
*In the silence that seeps around us, the cicadas chirp. They continue to chirp this evening, just as they have done every evening for as long as I can remember.*
*But, even though this is a comforting familiarity... it isn't enough to lift the feeling of unease coiled in the pit of my stomach.*
*Why does it feel so cold?*
Noelle: "I don't know if I believe you, Atcchan."
*I flinch. Given how badly I've treated her in the past, it's understandable.*
*If I was in Noelle's situation I wouldn't believe in me, either.*
Noelle: "But. I know you are not a bad person and you do not like to tell lies. I will give you the benefit of the doubt. This time."
Atcchan: "I-I... I-I understand... I-I'm sorry..."
Noelle: "It is fine. But..."
*Ah...*
*Noelle's eyes are still cold, but they don't look as blank as before. At least I can see some kind of compassion in them, some vestiges of reason and emotion, even if they are only faint.*
Noelle: "I will keep your response in mind. And at some point... I might test you on it."
Atcchan: "A test...?"
*Noelle nods.*
Noelle: "Yes. A test. But don't worry..."
*Slowly but surely... a smile creeps its way onto her face.*
*An unpleasant, poisonous smile... that I've never seen her wear before.*
Noelle: "I'm sure you'll pass it. I believe in you."
Noelle: "Oh... No... It's nothing..."
*Noelle looks down at the ground, her voice tailing away into thin air.*
Atcchan: "Nothing?"
Noelle: "Yes. Nothing. I was just thinking out loud."
*I tilt my head to one side, regarding Noelle with concern.*
*She isn't the sort of person who wastes words. Usually, she's very frugal with them.*
*Because she took the time and effort to articulate something... most likely, this means that she did have something to say. It must have been something important, too, judging by the look on her face.*
*But now...*
*Now, it seems as though I'll never know.*
*Noelle turns her back to me, refusing to elaborate further. Instead, she tries to change the subject, gesturing towards the picnic hamper that's lying innocuously under the tree.*
Noelle: "It's getting dark. We should pack this up and return home."
Atcchan: "H-Home...? A-Ah, yes. Of course..."
*But, even as I start helping Noelle clean up, my mind remains elsewhere.*
*What was she going to say? What did she want to tell me?*
*A few moments ago, the expression on her face was so sad. So distant and alone.*
*Maybe she was reaching out for me. Maybe she wanted some help.*
*But at the very last second... for some reason, she reconsidered, and she drew her hand away.*
*Now it feels as though I'll never know what those unarticulated words were. Perhaps she'll never tell me what she meant.*
*Is it because she doesn't trust me?*
*I wouldn't blame her if she doesn't. I don't know if I deserve her trust.*
*As I pad through the hallway of my grandparents' home, my hair dripping wet with hot water, my eyes are drawn towards the phone sitting on the side.*
*Inevitably, I start to think about Saki. I wonder how she's doing, taking care of her younger siblings. Hopefully, she hasn't snapped and torn them all limb from limb yet...*
*I wonder if I should call her, just to see how she is...*
*Call Saki.":
*Don't call Saki.":
Saki: "Ah... Hello, Atcchan."
Atcchan: "Hey there, Saki."
*In what is fast becoming a routine, I find myself sitting on the hard, wooden floorboards in the hallway; knees tucked up my chin, bulky telephone propped up against my ear by my shoulder.*
*My hair is dripping slowly, droplets of water sluicing down from my disordered bangs and onto my forehead, my cheeks, my nose.*
Saki: "Did you spend more time with Noelle today?"
Atcchan: "Yeah, actually. I went to go and see her. It was nice."
Saki: "Good. I'm glad. Do you feel more comfortable around her now?"
Atcchan: "It's not like I felt uncomfortable before, I just... I just thought she was hiding something."
Saki: "And how do you feel about it now?"
Atcchan: "Well, um... I went to see her mother, actually."
Saki: "Her mother?"
Saki: "Goodness. You are an awfully fast mover. Are you trying to pursue the mother and the daughter at the same time?"
Atcchan: "W-What? I-I, um... N-No, of course not...!"
*My face starts to flush bright red. T-This sounds more like something Amu would say, not Saki. Is she trying to embarrass me?*
Saki: "What a pity. I thought that sounded interesting. Like something from an 18th century drama."
Atcchan: "N-Now look here..."
*I'm trembling - not just my body, but my voice, too. I must look so silly, sitting here on the floor, folded in on myself, my face red as a beet.*
*I hope my grandparents don't find me like this. They'd never let me live it down.*
*Hopefully, they've both already gone to bed by now...*
Atcchan: "I'm not some kind of corrupt feudal lord. I-I wouldn't try to go after Noelle and her mother! T-That... T-That's just wrong."
Saki: "But how can it be wrong when it feels so right?"
*Saki says something that ought to be scandalous (and, indeed, it is), but her voice is completely deadpan.*
*I guess that's a crucial difference between Amu and Saki.*
*Whenever Amu teases me, she does so with obvious glee, a wide smirk splitting across her face.*
*Saki, however, does so only occasionally, and very wryly, in a tone that makes me wonder why she even bothers, since I don't know if she gets all that much enjoyment out of it.*
*Maybe she just likes saying shocking things.*
*This is the girl who, when asked what she'd like to be when she grew by her 2nd grade teacher in elementary school, responded with 'The Great Vampire Carmilla, Lady of the Night'.*
*That's what Miho told me, anyway.*
Atcchan: "It... It wouldn't be right! I-It wouldn't be right at all! Noelle's mother is much older than me, a-and anyway, she's already married!"
Saki: "Married, huh? Until death does she part?"
Atcchan: "I-I suppose so..."
Saki: "Marriage vows are rather morbid, aren't they? Haven't you ever thought that?"
Atcchan: "I... I-I guess...?"
Saki: "And they're so easy to circumnavigate, too - if you're willing to think outside the box a little."
Atcchan: "W-What are you suggesting exactly?"
Saki: "Oh, nothing. Only... there's a surprisingly large number of things you can do with a dead body, Atcchan."
*All color drains from my face.*
*At least it makes a change from being red.*
Atcchan: "That's disgusting! A-And how do you know about that kind of thing, anyway?"
Saki: "There are books."
*I shudder. I wonder what kind of books Saki's been checking out of the school library.*
*Why would they even have books like that in there in the first place? Couldn't it warp the minds of any impressionable young students?*
*... Then again, during my own ventures into the school library, I did manage to unearth a battered old copy of De Sade's Justine.*
*Maybe the library staff don't care all that much about what we students read in our spare time...*
Saki: "Haa..."
*I hear Saki sigh on the other end of the line. She sounds tired. I wonder if it's because of her siblings. It seems as good a guess as any.*
Saki: "I apologize for being confrontational. Playing the role of Mary Poppins for so long really has taken a toll on me, it seems."
Saki: "I'm tired of all the wax crayon drawings and trips to the park and reruns of Heidi."
Atcchan: "So they're back to Heidi, are they?"
Saki: "Mmhmm. Tyltyl and Mytyl never got the chance to find their bluebird - the brats got bored of that show before they could reach the conclusion."
Saki: "Children can be so fickle."
Atcchan: "Heh. If I didn't know any better, I'd say you were a little disappointed you didn't get to watch all of it?"
Saki: "No, I'm not disappointed. Not really. I didn't get that invested..."
*I'm so sure.*
*I smile, shaking my head. I can't help but be amused.*
*Saki always speaks what's on her mind - except in the rare circumstances when she's overcome with unusual amounts of sentimentality.*
*Even though she loves horror movies I'll bet, deep down, she still has a soft spot for those old animated shows of her youth somewhere.*
Saki: "Anyway. You were talking about Noelle's mother?"
Atcchan: "Y-Yes, that's right. Mrs. Sakata. Or, um..."
*My face flushes.*
Atcchan: "She told me to call her Lucy."
Saki: "Lucy? You two really did get cozy, didn't you?"
Atcchan: "I-It wasn't like that! She was just trying to be friendly!"
Saki: "I know, I know. I'm in a bad mood, so I'm just teasing."
*Well, at least she's honest about that. I'd already figured that much out for myself, though.*
Saki: "Lucy is a rather nice name. It's pretty."
Atcchan: "You would like it. You're obsessed with Western culture."
Saki: "I'm not obsessed. Not really. One of the main characters in Dracula is called Lucy, that's all. Did you know that?"
Atcchan: "No, I didn't know. I've never read Dracula before."
Saki: "You should. It's good."
*I hear a click on the other end of the line, a slight shuffle. Is Saki trying to get comfortable, too?*
Saki: "Anyway. Back to your Lucy."
Atcchan: "She isn't 'my' Lucy!"
*But Saki presses on, ignoring my concerns.*
Saki: "What did she have to tell you?"
Atcchan: "Well..."
*I frown, biting on my lower lip.*
Atcchan: "I asked her about them moving, and..."
Saki: "And?"
Atcchan: "Well, she... S-She said something... A little unbelievable, actually."
Saki: "They're not going to Mars, are they?"
Atcchan: "No, they're not - but they might as well be. You see, they... She..."
*I frown, coiling the plastic wire from the telephone round one finger. Even though I've had several hours to process this new piece of knowledge, I can still hardly bring myself to believe it. It doesn't feel real.*
*Maybe I need somebody to pinch my cheek for me. Would that wake me up?*
*How could something like this happen, and so suddenly? I have no idea.*
Atcchan: "She said they were moving to England."
Saki: "England?"
*A pause.*
*Was Saki stunned into silence?*
*I wonder. Knowing Saki, she's probably jealous.*
*I know Saki's always wanted to go to Europe, to see the countries she's only ever read about in her books - England and France and Germany. She thinks they're romantic, exciting.*
*I don't really see what the big deal is myself. What's wrong with Japan?*
Saki: "My, my. That is quite a shocking piece of news."
Atcchan: "Isn't it just? I still can't get my head around it."
Saki: "Well then... If that really is true - and I see no reason why Noelle's mother would lie to you - then... Perhaps it is no wonder Noelle did not want to tell you that she was moving."
Atcchan: "What do you mean...?"
Saki: "Think about it logically. Although I have always wanted to go to England, and wouldn't see such a move as a burden in the slightest, for somebody who likes their homeland and doesn't want to leave... it must be incredibly upsetting."
Saki: "This news must have shocked Noelle more than it shocked you - for it is her life it will directly affect, not yours."
Atcchan: "You... Y-You're right. That's true."
*I suddenly feel selfish. I was trying to make Noelle's moving all about me - but it isn't really, is it? I'm not the one who will suffer from it. Noelle is.*
*Noelle must be feeling upset or anxious right now... and so she doesn't want to talk about it. She doesn't want to tell me.*
*Is she trying to avoid the issue? Is she trying to avoid it because it hurts - like eating on the right side of the mouth when you get an ulcer on the left?*
*If that really is the case, then... I can understand it. I didn't want to tell Noelle that I was moving, either. It was too painful for me - and my situation wasn't nearly as difficult as Noelle's is.*
*At least I didn't have to move country; get acclimatized to a whole new culture.*
Atcchan: "I... I'll try to be sensitive if I ask Noelle about it. I don't want to upset her any more than I may already have done."
Saki: "I think that's a sensible thing to do. Even if she doesn't tell you, she might want a friend to rely on right now. Make sure you're there for her, okay?"
Atcchan: "I... I-I'll do my best...!"
Saki: "That's the spirit."
*I hear Saki laugh dryly (as always) from the other end of the line.*
*Somehow, her laughter always helps put me at ease - even though my thoughts are still jumbled and disordered from the bombshell that was dropped on me earlier.*
*Is that because Saki, my one link back to my new life, represents calm and stability? It could be.*
*I've been feeling conflicted a lot throughout these past two days, constantly torn between Amu and Noelle, unsure of which one to see.*
*Although I have enjoyed being back at home, this constant guilt that comes with picking one over the other has been marring the experience somewhat - and the news of Noelle's sudden move hasn't helped matters, either.*
*When I'm with Saki, however, I don't have to feel like that. Despite her love of the gothic, she's a fairly well-balanced person - easy to talk to, and dependable to boot.*
*I... I think I might miss her. Even though it's only been two days, I... I'm already starting to feel a little lost without her here to guide me.*
*If she were in my situation, Saki would know what to do. Saki always knows what to do. And because Saki is so cool, so strong, so mature... I inevitably started to look up to her.*
*I rely on her.*
*I think a sensible person like that, who always knows what to do and say in every situation, is good for me.*
*I need a person in my life like that.*
Atcchan: "Well... To be honest, she got kind of mad at me."
Saki: "Did she snap at you?"
Atcchan: "A little. I think she thought I was being impudent. Maybe I didn't ask the right kind of question, or maybe it's a sensitive issue..."
*I frown.*
Atcchan: "You think it's serious?"
Saki: "It must be, if neither Noelle nor her mother wants to talk about it."
Atcchan: "Aah... Geez."
*I sigh, running one hand through my damp locks. As my hair is still wet, it keeps its shape even after I let my hand fall to my lap; remaining, stuck up, in strange spikes.*
*I probably look like a cartoon character that's just stuck their hand into an electrical outlet - but I don't suppose that matters too much. It's not like anyone can see me.*
Atcchan: "It's making me feel anxious. The less I know, the more serious everything seems..."
Saki: "That's always is the case. The human imagination is the most powerful poison there is - yours especially."
Atcchan: "You think there's something wrong with me?"
Saki: "No. I just think you worry too much."
*Ahaha. It's true. I can't deny that.*
*Especially not to Saki.*
*She's seen how I am days before important exams; strange and pale, twitching, keyed up with anxious energy and unable to concentrate.*
*I never really had 'exams' at my old school, in this small village - or, no, that isn't true. Miss Tachibana did need to assess our abilities, and she did follow a set curriculum, but...*
*Because the village school was small, and there weren't many students, Miss Tachibana was fairly lax. Examinations very felt particularly stressful; not with Amu's bright pink head bobbing in front of me.*
*It was a horrible shock, upon moving to the city, to suddenly have to sit in a classroom filled with forty students my own age, most of whom were far further advanced in their studies than me.*
*If Saki hadn't let me borrow her notes so I could catch up, I might have been left behind for good.*
*I hadn't realized quite how easy I had it at my old school until I came to the city. In the city school, with its shiny floors and bright light fixtures and brand new tables and chairs, everything was far less lax.*
*Although my grades are fairly average now, neither good nor bad, I still hate doing exams and taking tests. The teachers are always so serious about it, the atmosphere so silent and staid, and it makes my nerves flare up.*
*I still haven't gotten used to it. Maybe I never will.*
Saki: "I'm sure, if you give it time, Noelle will open up to you eventually."
Atcchan: "Really? You think?"
Saki: "If your friendship is as close as you have told me, then yes."
*Huh... I wonder.*
*Just how close are we, anyway? We did have a fun time together today, and I'm grateful that we were able to catch up, but... can a couple of days really undo the amount of damage the last two years have done?*
*If Noelle never trusts me again, I wouldn't be too surprised - even though merely thinking about that possibility hurts.*
*Why... Why is thinking about Noelle so painful?*
*Since we're friends... shouldn't I be glad that I'm going to see her again? But, instead, when I turn over the events of today in my mind's eye... My heart is beset by a strange kind of pain, sharp and stabbing.*
*Am I reading too much into it? Am I being melodramatic? Probably. Being melodramatic is one my one strong point.*
*Sometimes, I think I should write the scripts for those sappy TV dramas. I'd probably do a good job at it.*
Saki: "She probably wants to talk to you, too. Maybe she doesn't know how yet."
Atcchan: "I... I hope that's the case. If I can be of any help to her, any at all, then... I-I really want to be!"
Saki: "Heh. You say that, but... is that really true?"
Atcchan: "W-What do you mean?"
Saki: "I mean... Do you want her to confide in you so you can help her, or... do you want her to confide in you so you can feel good about yourself?"
Atcchan: "I... Well..."
*I wince, biting my lower lip. Even though Saki is miles and miles away, more than seven hours down a long, unbroken expanse of train tracks, she can still see right through me.*
*How does she do it? Maybe she really does have magical, witch-like powers. I wouldn't put it past her.*
Atcchan: "M-Maybe it's a little bit of both..."
*I finally reply, cowed.*
*Saki's response is breezy, light. I can picture her running a hand through her hair as she says it.*
Saki: "Well, there's nothing wrong with that. A little bit of selfishness can be rather helpful, in fact."
Saki: "Most people perform altruistic deeds for the self-satisfaction, whether they admit to it or not - and I don't think that's a bad thing. Not so long as it achieves a positive result."
Atcchan: "That's so cynical, though..."
Saki: "It's called being a realist. You need to look facts square on someday."
Atcchan: "Even though you love vampire stories so much?"
Saki: "That's different. I love them because I know they're not real. People are always intrigued in the strange, the unknown, the impossible."
Atcchan: "And not by reruns of Heidi?"
*I bet Saki's shuddering. I can hear the shudder in her words, though she doesn't stutter. Saki doesn't stutter often.*
Saki: "No. God no. If I have to watch one more episode of that blithe, rosy-cheeked little girl skipping through the alps I might disembowel myself. Right in front of my siblings, too. That'll show them."
Atcchan: "You'd scar them for life!"
Saki: "I'd scar myself for life, too - though I think it might be worth it."
Atcchan: "You can be so maudlin sometimes."
Saki: "Why thank you. It's part of my charm. Hahaha."
*The sound of Saki's laughter, wry and subdued as always, filters through the receiver, into my ear. Somehow, even though the topic of our conversation has turned incredibly ghoulish, it cheers me up.*
*A small smile spreads across my lips despite myself.*
*Why does talking to Saki always put me at my ease? Maybe it's because she's reliable, dependable. I know where I stand with Saki. Even though she can be caustic, cutting, sarcastic, at least she does it with comforting regularity.*
*That's more than can be said for my situation right now.*
*Torn between Amu and Noelle, I feel conflicted. I don't like picking what to buy for lunch, let alone which childhood friend I should hang out with over the other, and it's making me feel guilty.*
*Talking to Noelle can be so challenging, too - almost as though every single string of short syllables that comes from between her lips is a new puzzle to be pondered. Unfortunately, I'm too dimwitted to put everything together.*
*If Saki were here with me, I bet she'd know what to do. Saki always knows what to do. She's smart like that. Always gets the highest scores in biology. And, because Saki is so cool, so strong, so mature... I inevitably started to look up to her.*
*I rely on her.*
*I... I miss her.*
*I think a sensible person like that, who always knows what to do and say in every situation, is good for me.*
*I think I need a person like that in my life.*
*Eventually, I decide against it. I know Saki won't appreciate this sudden silence, but I feel exhausted after having so many busy days in quick succession. Right now, all I want to do is curl up in my futon and go to sleep.*
*I feel a little guilty, but I hope she'll understand. I am going to go back home tomorrow, after all, so it's not like we'll be apart for all that long.*
*Thinking this, I give the phone a small bow of apology (I'm not sure why - it's not like Saki's going to see it) and vacate the hallway; returning to my temporary bedroom.*
*I'm sorry, Saki. I hope you can hang in there for just another day! Do your best!*
*I lie in my futon, staring up at the ceiling.*
*Since I spent a lot of time walking around in the forest, I feel exhausted and my muscles are aching. My legs feel strangely dead, like the stumps of two felled trees; lying uselessly on the ground, thick and heavy.*
*Aaah... I can't even feel my toes anymore...*
*I really have overexerted myself...*
*It's amazing, really, how quickly Noelle can walk through the forest - especially given she's not that athletic and she doesn't often wear shoes. She really does set a fast pace.*
*I, on the other hand, lagged along behind her pathetically, out of breath like an old man. But no, not even that description holds true, because my grandfather is a lot more spry than he looks. He might be even healthier than I am.*

*And the pain coursing dully throughout my body isn't the only problem here. There is another issue; one I've been turning around in my mind for a while.*
*It's about Noelle.*
*It's clear that something's wrong, but I have no idea what. I don't know because she won't tell me.*
*Noelle's always been secretive like that. She doesn't open up easily... and when she does, it's often only about silly, inconsequential things.*
*I know that she likes fruit jello from the convenience store, and I know that she has a fondness for rabbits. I know she enjoys sketching, and I know she doesn't like crowded places.*
*But other than that... I don't know very much about her at all.*
*I don't know anything about her life before she moved here, and I don't know why she moved either.*
*I don't know why her family has decided to move this time, and I don't know how Noelle feels about it.*
*If she told me, maybe I could help, but... if she won't talk, there's very little I can do - and I don't want to pressure her, either.*
*This really does seem like an impossible situation.*
Atcchan: "Aaaah... What should I do?"
*I groan and turn over in my futon, trying to get comfy. It's hard to trick my body into feeling sleepy when my mind is so crammed full with thoughts.*
*I wonder... what am I going to do tomorrow?*
*Amu phoned my grandparents' home at around 8:00 p.m. and invited me out tomorrow. She said we could go hunting for cicadas in the forest, like when we were kids.*
*She didn't mention anything about Noelle, though.*
*I wonder... Should I invite Noelle anyway...?*
*Spending more time with her would be nice. Maybe, if I keep at it, I could find out just why she seems so gloomy lately. There's no sense in just giving up - that never achieves anything.*
*But if I did that... maybe Amu wouldn't like it. I know the two of them don't get along very well.*
*Aaah... Decisions, decisions...*
*I don't know what to do.*
*Then again, that isn't anything new. I never do.*
*Then... she finally speaks.*
Noelle: "..."
Noelle: "It's about Amu."
*When Noelle says Amu's name... it sounds cold. There's no trace of warmth in her tone at all.*

Atcchan: "A-Amu? What about Amu?"
Noelle: "I know that you're close to her. You are best friends, after all. If you wanted to spend time with her instead of me... it would be understandable."

Noelle: "You and Amu... You've been friends ever since you were children. Isn't that right?"
Atcchan: "W-Well, that is right..."
Noelle: "And Amu has so many good qualities. She's so bright and cheerful... always smiling. Always talking. People say she's a fun person to be with. She has a lot of friends."

Atcchan: "N-Noelle..."
Noelle: "If I was more like Amu, I think even my parents would be happier. They don't like that I'm so quiet. They worry about me."
Atcchan: "But... Your parents don't love Amu. They love you."
*Noelle nods.*
Noelle: "They do. But it's painful for them."
Atcchan: "Painful...?"
Noelle: "Because I am deficient as a person."
*It's a cruel thing to say, but she says it so simply - almost as though stating that the sky is blue and the grass is green. There's no room for argument in her tone.*
Noelle: "I am a difficult person. I don't speak very often. Sometimes I tell lies, even though I hate liars. And I don't make friends easily."

Noelle: "But you stopped talking to me. The past two years, you didn't send me any letters. Even though you sent them to Amu."

*I think I might have forgotten how to breathe.*
*Noelle is right. I did abandon her. For the last two years, I ignored her completely. But...*
*But that wasn't her fault. It wasn't because of anything she did - and it certainly wasn't because I was sick of her...!*
*But feebly protesting that inside my own head is no good. The words won't reach anybody in there.*

Noelle: "You are very kind, Atcchan. At least, that's what I think."
Atcchan: "N-No, I... I-I wasn't... tired..."
Noelle: "And then I thought... maybe you were glad that you were moving. You were glad to get away from me. So I wasn't being a burden anymore."

Noelle: "And I think that might be... inexcusable."
Noelle: "I'm an inexcusably selfish girl."
*I can hear the sounds of the cicadas. This forest is filled with chirping.*
*All around us, there are insects, hidden from sight... listening to us. Listening to this sad, painful monologue, coming from a person far more self-conscious, far more self-loathing, then I ever imagined.*
*Even though I always worry about the worst possible scenario... maybe I don't have that much of an imagination after all. I certainly never expected this.*
*It's true Noelle has always been a quiet person with few friends, but... I thought she didn't mind. I thought she liked it that way.*
*... Maybe I was wrong.*
*Nobody likes to be alone.*
*She wants to be a brighter, more confident person, just like Amu - not necessarily for her own sake, but for the sake of others. So she won't have to worry about burdening them.*
*I... I didn't know... I had no idea she felt that way.*
*There are so many things about Noelle that I don't know. So many things that she hasn't told me...*
*I wonder...*
*Is it lonely, being that trapped inside your own head... feeling as though you can't share your real thoughts with anyone?*
*I bet it was lonely. Lonelier than I can imagine.*
*I'm sorry if I hurt you...":
*Say nothing and just hug her.":
Atcchan: "A-Ah... Noelle..."
*I stumble, stuttering. I've never been very good with words. When I need them the most, they inevitably slip away, falling between the cracks of my fingers like water.*
*But I can't give up now. I won't allow it.*
*I need to tell her.*
*I need to tell her how I feel - and then I need to apologize.*
Atcchan: "I'm sorry..."
Noelle: "N-No, it's all right... You don't need to say that."
Noelle: "If I'm irritating then it's my fault. You probably couldn't help it... being irritated by me..."
Atcchan: "N-No, that... that isn't right. I wasn't annoyed at you! You could never annoy me - not even for a second!"
Noelle: "Hn...? What do you mean? I don't understand."
*Noelle looks at me in confusion. Those pale blue eyes... they look so lonely.*
*She's so convinced I was trying to avoid her that she can't see it any other way. Even when I try to explain it, it doesn't work.*
*She probably thinks I'm lying. I haven't set a good track record for that in the past.*
Atcchan: "Noelle... The reason I left without telling you... it wasn't your fault. It was mine. I..."
Atcchan: "I was worried I would hurt you if I left, since we've always been so close... and I didn't want to see that. I didn't want you to get upset."
Atcchan: "Seeing you get upset... would make me feel too guilty... So..."
*I have to pause, composing myself, before I can continue.*
Atcchan: "S-So... I did something thoughtless. I was a coward, and I just never told you. I never told you so I wouldn't have to deal with the reality. For just a bit longer, I..."
Atcchan: "I really wanted to live in a fantasy world with you, where we could always be together, no matter what...!"
*Noelle's eyes widen. She stares at me.*
Noelle: "A-Ah... Atcchan..."
*Her voice is soft. The words break up in her mouth. I can hear her, just barely, over the dull hum of the cicadas.*
*The cicadas, the spectators of this melodrama. Our audience. And, if this was a play, I'm sure I'd be the villain. A foolish, bumbling one, but a villain nonetheless.*
Noelle: "I-If... If that's true... Why didn't you ever write to me? You could have explained your feelings in a letter, at least."
Atcchan: "I know... I just... I didn't have the heart."
Noelle: "The heart? What does that mean?"
Atcchan: "I..."
Noelle: "You wrote Amu letters. Why did you write them to her, but not me?"
*I look at Noelle in surprise. I-I didn't know she'd heard about that.*
*I felt guilty enough as it was, sending Amu those letters discretely, but... I thought, since Noelle would never find out, it wouldn't hurt her.*
*I was just being thoughtless again.*
*Noelle found out. She knew. She always knew.*
*How... must that have felt...?*
Atcchan: "H-How do you know about that?"
Noelle: "Amu brought them into school and read them to the class. They were all excited. They wanted to know how you were. What it was like living in the city."
Atcchan: "A-Ah..."
*I wince.*
*I know Amu, and I know she's not a malicious person. I'm sure she didn't bring those letters into school to hurt Noelle on purpose.*
*It's more likely that she thought the rest of the class might be interested, and maybe she could show off a little about still being in contact with somebody who lives all the way out in the big city.*
*That must've been why she did it.*
*But to Noelle...*
*Knowing that I was sending Amu letters, but not her... must have been painful. Especially when she didn't know the reason why.*
Atcchan: "It's true that I wrote Amu letters... but they weren't anything special. They were just silly."
Noelle: "But that's still better than nothing."
Noelle: "You say it was only silly, but... I-It wouldn't have been like that to me. I-I still would have liked a letter too."
Noelle: "After all... I am... also your friend. R-Right...?"
Atcchan: "R-Right. That's right. I just... I felt too guilty..."
Noelle: "Why should you feel guilty?"
Atcchan: "Because I left you. I left you without saying goodbye, even though I told everyone else. And I..."
Atcchan: "I-I'm sorry, Noelle. I-I just got scared you would hate me for treating you so poorly... And I was afraid..."
Atcchan: "I was scared, and I was anxious... so I just tried to forget it. All of it. Like a true coward."
Noelle: "Scared...?"
Atcchan: "Y-Yes. I know it sounds stupid, but... I really was."
Noelle: "Atcchan... You know..."
*Noelle looks down at the ground. Her hair flutters around her shoulders in the light breeze. She shivers, wrapping her arms around herself.*
Noelle: "Every day, I waited... I waited for you to send me a letter. I wanted some proof that you hadn't forgotten me... That we were still friends."

Noelle: "But the days went by... and then the weeks. Months. And still, I got no letter."
Noelle: "I got no explanation for why you left and no information about how you were, and... I started to get worried."
Noelle: "At first, I thought that maybe you did send a letter. Maybe you did, but it got lost in the post. And I thought, if I kept waiting, you'd realize I hadn't sent a reply, and send me another... That's what I hoped for."
Noelle: "And then a whole year passed, and I'd still heard nothing. But Amu had. Amu brought in many letters. But I had none."
Noelle: "And that's when I started to think... Maybe you didn't like me after all. Maybe, this whole time... it was Amu you liked... and you just stayed with me out of pity."

Noelle: "All this time... I was the one who was scared! I was so scared that my best friend, my only friend... had never even liked me...!"
*Noelle's voice breaks, collapsing in on itself, and is soon replaced by another, distinctive sound.*
*It isn't the sound of speech.*
*Neither is it the sound of the cicadas, still chirping monotonously in the undergrowth.*
*This sound is much more despairing... and much more heartbreaking.*
*Noelle's eyes are filled with tears.*
*She's crying.*

*Under normal circumstances I would feel embarrassed for being so forward. I've never really hugged a girl like this before.*
*It is true that I hugged Amu a few times when we were kids... but those interactions may more accurately be described as a hyperactive Amu pouncing on me, rather than a mutual hug.*
*I was never the one who initiated those embraces, and Amu grew out of it when she got older.*
*This kind of embrace feels completely different. It's not something I'm used to. And yet...*
*Even though my heart is beating just a little too fast and my face has gone a light shade of pink... I don't care.*
*How I feel right now... shouldn't matter.*
*It doesn't matter.*
*I want to show Noelle just how much she means to me - and this is the only way I can think of doing it.*
*It's the only way I know how to apologize without the message being misunderstood.*
*Noelle and I don't talk that much anyway. We're not natural conversationalists. I think I can get along with others a little better than she can, owing to the fact I've been friends with Amu for so long... but, at heart, I get nervous when I have to interact with other humans.*
*I'm always worrying. Will I look foolish? Can I get my point across properly? Am I even representing the truth of what really happened? And, worst of all, am I just being a bore?*
*Because using language is difficult, and different people will take away different meanings from the exact same accounts... I can't rely on it at all.*
*If I want to show Noelle how much I care about her... I think that this is the only way.*
*Between awkward people like us who don't like to talk, maybe it's the only way.*
*S-So, even though it feels kind of strange... I-It's not awkward or embarrassing.*
*If it's between us... I think it's completely natural.*
Noelle: "Aah... A-Atcchan..."
*Noelle sniffles a little, her voice breaking.*
*I continue to hold her, my cheeks flushed.*
*Owing to the slight height difference between us, my nose is pressed against her forehead. I can't rest my chin on the top of her head, like a scene in a romantic girls' manga. I'm not tall enough.*
*But at least I can do this. And 'this', whatever 'this' is, might just be enough.*
Noelle: "Atcchan... Y-You don't dislike me?"
Atcchan: "N-No... I never disliked you. N-Not ever. I-I couldn't. I..."
Atcchan: "I was just awkward and... I didn't want to hurt you."

Noelle: "Before I knew it, a whole year had passed. A whole year, and I'd still heard nothing..."

Noelle: "I've always been alone."
Noelle: "I-I was so alone, and nobody tried to talk to me. Not even you..."

Noelle: "She always smiles. S-She has so many friends..."
Noelle: "S-So, obviously... If you had to pick between her and me... I thought you'd choose her. I thought that for sure."

Noelle: "And I thought our whole relationship was a lie...!"
*Noelle's voice breaks. It falters, fading away into nothingness... and soon, is replaced by a more heartbreaking sound.*
*The sound of sobbing.*
Atcchan: "Noelle..."
*I draw her even more tightly to my chest, as though this simple hug can take all her pain away.*
*I know it can't. I know that's just wishful thinking. But I still want to try.*
*I want her to know... just how much she means to me.*

*I hope it's enough.*
*Ah...*
*My shirt's starting to get damp. She buries her head against my chest, her fingers clutching at the fabric of my jacket.*
*I rest my chin on top of her head.*
*It's funny...*
*In this gentle, caring embrace... I can't hear anything else. Just the sound of my heartbeat, Noelle's tears.*
*Nothing else matters anymore. Not even the low, mournful cries of the cicadas.*
*I lie in my futon, staring up at the ceiling.*
*Even though my body is tired, exhausted after that long walk in the forest with Noelle, my brain doesn't feel sleepy at all. I just can't switch it off.*
*Even when I close my eyes I can still see it; replaying over and over again inside my head.*
*That expression on Noelle's face...*
*That frightening, sinister expression that I've never seen before.*
*Her eyes, usually so light and dreamy, looked almost completely dead. Devoid of human emotion.*
*In all the years I've known her, I've never seen her make a face like that.*
*I wonder...*
*Just how well do I know her, anyway?*
*Underneath her gently smiling face and those sleepy, half-lidded eyes... maybe something sinister was always hidden underneath.*
*Just thinking about it is enough to make me shudder. It's almost as though invisible insects are crawling across my body, making every inch of my skin prickle.*
*I need to stop worrying. I need to calm down. I need to go to sleep.*
*But... But...*
*How can I go to sleep after what just happened?*
*I toss and turn in my futon, trying to get comfortable, but it's a pointless effort. Every few minutes my body becomes consumed with nervous energy, and I have to move.*
*This room is far too hot, far too stuffy. My brain is overheating inside the cramped confines of my skull.*
*As the minutes move by slowly, the pressure continues to build. I can feel it pressing against the inside of my head, making my eyes ache.*
*All that anxiety, all that guilt, all that worry... it comes together in a rush; animating my body with nervous energy, left with nowhere else to go.*
*By now, even the restless shuffling of my body fails to diffuse it.*
Atcchan: "Aaaaah...!"
*I moan, pressing my face into my pillow to muffle it.*
Atcchan: "I've had enough of this... I can't take it anymore...!"
*And, the moment I say that... almost as though orchestrated by fate...*
*I hear a noise.*
*It's the sound of knocking.*
*At this late hour of the night, when the moon is up and the streets are dark... somebody is knocking on the door.*
*My heart seizes up inside my chest. A cold sweat begins to bead on my forehead.*

*Even while turning these questions over in my mind, I think I know the answer.*
*It could only be one person, couldn't it?*
Atcchan: "Noelle..."

*Or else... will it be the new girl I met earlier; the cold, harsh, almost inhuman person I still can't believe is really Noelle?*

*Of course, such a delusion doesn't work for me anymore. I'm too old to believe that pretending to be a superhero will genuinely save me from any adversity.*
*Even as I do this, wasting time, the sound of the knocking continues.*
*It doesn't get louder and it doesn't get faster. It keeps going at the same slow, unhurried pace.*
*I'm sure, even if I ignore it, it won't go away. Noelle can be quite stubborn at times.*
*Even though she looks frail, she has a strong constitution. She was willing to walk almost a two hour round journey to the nearby town just to pick up some of that jello she likes so much, after all.*

*To make matters even worse, I have no idea what 'this mood' actually entails.*

*I don't want to upset her. I've done that far too much already.*
*If this is some kind of test, I need to face it. I can't just try and ignore it, hoping it will go away, like I do with the rest of my problems.*
*If I keep behaving like that then I won't make any progress.*
*I'm like a creature in a swamp, trapped in primordial ooze. The only way I can evolve into a real human being is to take that first step outside of the swamp, up onto dry land.*
*I need to go forward.*
*I've been avoiding this... for far too long.*
*I slip out from my futon and pick up my discarded clothes, folded neatly on the floor. I pull my jacket on over my pajama shirt, my hands trembling.*
*The whole while, I can still hear it.*
*The dull drone of that continuous knocking - almost in synch with my own heart, beating fast against the inside of my ribcage.*
*I stand on the doorstep of your house, waiting.*
*I've been waiting for a while already, but... what is a few minutes compared to a couple of years?*
*I'm a patient person. If it's just this much, I can bear it. I won't give in.*
*I'll never give in.*
*It's cold outside, especially since I'm wearing this old dress, but I don't mind it all that much. I've learned to get used to it.*
*People can get used to anything, really.*
*With my right hand curled into a fist, I knock on your door. Over and over again, I knock.*
*It's not polite to be too noisy and I don't want to wake up your grandparents. They're nice people.*
*With this bit of common courtesy in mind, I try to make my knocking as indiscreet as possible.*
*But I still want you to hear me.*
*Until you come to answer me, I won't stop. I won't give up.*
*I can't give up.*
*I need to keep knocking.*
*Even if the skin peels away from my bones... Even if blisters begin to form between my fingers... Even if my knuckles turn bright red...*
*Even if my hand freezes up from the cold and the pain and I can't move it anymore, I still won't stop knocking. I'll just force myself to keep going.*
*I told myself this and I'm going to stay true to it. I don't want to betray my own principles.*
*People are no good in this world. You can't trust people.*
*They move around in herds just like animals. They go with the majority and agree without thinking, nodding their heads in unison.*
*This isn't a bad thing if you're part of the crowd, but...*
*If people exclude you because of how you look or act... it will cost you.*
*Everybody will turn against you. Nobody will stand by your side. That's because nobody wants to stand out. If they go against the majority they'll end up suffering, too.*
*That's just how the world works.*
*It's not as though I don't understand that point of view. I understand it perfectly. I even sympathize with it.*
*Nobody wants to be hurt. Nobody wants to be excluded. Nobody wants to be alone.*
*So people continue to act based on their own self interest... and, in doing so, they trample on the feelings of others.*
*It can't be helped. If you don't want to be hurt, you hurt others.*
*It makes sense. I understand it. If I could do that too... I'm sure I would.*
*Everybody tells lies. Everybody will betray you.*
*Even if that person is your best friend... if they had to kill you to save their own life, they would. They definitely would.*

*The people who can't admit to that are just deluding themselves.*
*I'm not going to betray myself again... and I'm not going to be betrayed again.*

*I thought we were friends.*

*I can't help but worry about you, just a little. Are you feeling sick? Is it my fault?*
Atcchan: "N-Noelle...?"
*Sharply observed.*
Noelle: "Yes. It's me."
Atcchan: "A-Ah... Ahaha..."
*You laugh nervously and ruffle your hair with one hand. That's one of your habits, isn't it? You've done it ever since I can remember.*
*It might explain why your hair always looks so messy.*

Noelle: "You always do that when you're anxious."
Atcchan: "H-Huh? D-Do I...?"
Noelle: "Yes. Are you anxious right now?"
Atcchan: "J-Just a little... I-I mean, I... I-I was wondering..."
Noelle: "What?"

Noelle: "..."
Noelle: "I apologize for intruding. There was something I needed to talk about. That's all."
Atcchan: "C-Couldn't it wait until tomorrow...?"
*I shake my head.*

Amu: "Kukuku~"
*Amu giggles. She sounds a little out of breath.*
Atcchan: "I think you made some fans out there. The other guys seemed pretty impressed."
Amu: "Ehehe~ Well, it's not like I dislike the attention. Being respected is waaay more fun than being made fun of and taken for granted."
*At these words, a dark cloud passes over Amu's face.*
Atcchan: "Are you still hung up about your job?"
Amu: "Of course I am. That's why I started coming here more often. It helps work off the stress. I just imagine each ball I hit is a human head, you see."
Atcchan: "W-Well, as long as you don't actually hit any human heads at work, it's fine...!"
Amu: "Heh. I do my best."
*I feel like I should say something to her. Something to comfort her, or congratulate her, maybe. But what?*
*I think you're really amazing.":
*It sounds tough. Hang in there!":
Amu: "H-Huh...?"
*Amu stares at me in shock. Even though her face is already flushed from all that exercise, I think it looks even pinker now...*
*Well, if Amu's face is pink... that's nothing compared to how flustered I'm feeling.*
Atcchan: "I-I mean, um... I'm sorry if that was too forward o-or anything... I just think it's admirable..."
Amu: "Admirable? Me?"
*And now Amu doesn't look confused and flustered but incredulous. I might as well have exploded, or revealed myself as the second coming of Christ, given how wide her eyes are.*
Amu: "Atcchan, are you feeling okay...? Is your helmet on a little too tight or something?"
Atcchan: "N-No, I don't think so. I-I feel fine...!"
Amu: "Really...? Are you sure it's not cutting off the circulation to your brain?"
Atcchan: "N-No...! At least, I don't think so..."
Amu: "Are you sure? It's not like you to compliment me so much."
Atcchan: "I-I know... maybe it seems a little unexpected, but... really..."
Atcchan: "I was just thinking... that you're quite admirable..."
Amu: "Hoh...? I-I don't know about that. I'm nothing special..."
*It's funny. Before, Amu was so jubilant at her batting victory, making all sorts of claims about how amazing she was. But now I'm actually agreeing with her, she looks unsure and embarrassed.*
*For a straightforward, no-nonsense kind of gal like Amu, isn't this a bit too contrary?*
Atcchan: "I just mean... I think you're a very determined person. When you want to do stuff, you really go for it. I wish I could be more like you."
Amu: "O-Oh... It's nothing special. It's just a silly task I set myself for fun."
Atcchan: "But even if it is silly, you still did it."
Amu: "Well, I'm flattered, Atcchan - but there's no sense in just looking up to me!"
Atcchan: "Huh...? What do you mean...?"
Amu: "I mean, if you wanna do something, you've just gotta get along and do it!"
Amu: "There's no sense in idolizing somebody from afar and thinking 'Oh, that's so amazing, but I can never be like that.' Before you can do anything on your own, you've got to have more faith in yourself!"
*These words perk me up. It's almost like she's coaching me.*
*She seems to realize this herself, because she starts to laugh.*
Amu: "Hehehe... Look at me, talking like a self help book... That was so uncool."
Atcchan: "I-I... I don't think so..."
*An uncomfortable feeling slowly starts to build up in the pit of my stomach, but I try to push past it. Ignore it.*
*Isn't that what Amu just told me? I need to make active changes in my life, or else everything will remain the same.*
*I thought that was what I wanted. I thought I was afraid of change. But...*
*The world doesn't work like that. The world won't stop turning just for me.*
*I need to start taking some steps of my own.*
Atcchan: "I... I think you're really cool, Amu. And... I really am grateful... that you became my friend."
Atcchan: "You're one of the best friends I've ever had."
*I look at Amu from underneath my bangs shyly. My cheeks feel hot and my hands are trembling, but I don't back down.*
*I don't apologize or stutter excuses, or even hang my head. Instead, I decide to stand by my word. I try to be brave.*
*...*
*......*
*.........*
*A silence stretches out between us.*
*I can hear the sounds of other people batting, bats striking baseballs as they fly through the air, but that all seems very far away. Almost on a different planet altogether.*
*It's Amu who speaks first.*
Amu: "A-Ahahaha... Thank you, A-Atcchan. I-I really appreciate it! Even if it was over the top and a little too sappy for this rotten girl's tastes... A-Ahaha...!"
Atcchan: "I-I know. Maybe I am a little too sappy, but... it's what I really feel!"
Amu: "E-Ehehe... W-Well, that's good to know! I'm glad we've been able to become so close again, even though it's been so long."
Amu: "E-Even though you might not have realized it, I was a little worried..."
Atcchan: "Even you get worried?"
Amu: "O-Of course...! But I continue to push on ahead 'cause that's all I can do! A-Ahaha!"
Amu: "But anyway, Atcchan!"
Atcchan: "Y-Yes...? What is it...?"
*Amu leans forwards. She seems a little calmer now. Her smile is devilish, challenging. It's an expression that makes my heart flutter.*
Amu: "You said you wanted to do your best?"
Atcchan: "Y-Yes...! I-I want to do my best...!"
Amu: "You really want to do your best?"
Atcchan: "Y-Yes...! I really, really do...!"
Amu: "Well then... Kukuku...~"
*She laughs her patented creepy laugh, perfect for Halloween.*
*Amu gets to her feet dramatically...*
*... and jabs her baseball bat into my face; stopping it short just inches away from the tip of my nose.*
Amu: "Then get out there and hit some home runs, all right?! Let's go!"
Amu: "Yeah..."
Amu: "It's just kind of depressing working a job like that. It made me realize something I haven't really thought about before."
Atcchan: "Huh? What's that?"
Amu: "If you take on a role where you have to act subservient to others... people stop seeing you as a real human being, and use it as an excuse to treat you like shit."
Atcchan: "Ah, um... N-Not everybody is like that, though?"
Amu: "No, not everyone. Most people are polite. But that doesn't make up for the people who aren't."
Atcchan: "O-Of course not. I'm sorry."
*Amu waves one hand.*
Amu: "You don't need to apologize. You've never worked as a waiter, so you probably don't know, but..."
Amu: "Some people out there are just so stupid. They come into the café and ask for things we don't even have on the menu, then get pissed when we don't have it."
Amu: "If somebody's kids start screaming, somehow it's my fault and I need to sort it out!"
Amu: "Some guy drops a fork on the floor and makes me pick it up and gets mad if I'm not there quick enough; somebody orders a hot chocolate and then complains because it's hot."
Amu: "And some guys catcall me and say really creepy things! It's so gross!"
*I guess taking on that kind of meek role, where the customer is always right and the server has no room to complain, is completely opposed of Amu's character.*
*I should've known that much, really, but Amu never mentioned this in her letters to me. Instead, she focused on things that seemed trivial, like how much she hated the café's name.*
*I thought she was just joking this whole time, but I think her feelings are more serious than that.*
*Why didn't I realize before? Is it because I'm unobservant? Partially, perhaps, but...*
*There's a limit to how much information you can convey in a letter, and letters aren't nearly as personal as talking face to face.*
*It's only by being at Amu's side, sitting this close together, looking at the subtle shifts of her expression and the changes in her tone of voice that I've been able to discover just how much she really dislikes her work.*
Amu: "I just feel like I'm losing my faith in people, day by day... and it's kind of depressing."
*Amu leans back in her seat and stares up at the ceiling. Her hands rest in her lap, clenching and unclenching into fists.*
*Her sudden confession comes as a surprise. I don't know what to say. Amu always seemed so confident, so sure of herself, but...*
*The stress that comes with her part-time job is really wearing her down.*
Atcchan: "Hey..."
*I pat her on the shoulder awkwardly.*
Atcchan: "It's okay. Even if those people are irritating... I can always try not to be?"
Amu: "Yeah. Am I ever glad of that. If everybody was as awful as the customers I've had to deal with, I wouldn't even want to live in this world anymore."
Atcchan: "Well, don't let them get you down...! They probably can't hit one hundred home runs in a row, unlike you!"
Amu: "..."
Amu: "..."
Amu: "Kukuku~ Yeah, you're right! It was the culmination of several months of practice, but it paid off!"
Atcchan: "You've been coming here for that long?"
Amu: "Mmhmm. I set myself a target, to hit one hundred home runs, and I was working up to it little by little!"
Amu: "And finally, I reached it! My goal!"
*Amu grins, giving me a victory sign. Even though her face is still flushed, and she looks tired, her smile is filled with pride.*
*Amu achieved something she can be proud of. Although it's an achievement that won't matter to anybody else... I'm sure she'll be able to treasure this memory all the same.*
*I wonder, if I follow Amu's example... maybe, one day, I can accomplish my dreams too?*
Amu: "Ehehe. Thank you for humoring me, Atcchan~"
Atcchan: "It's all right. I had fun too."
Amu: "Even though you only hit about three balls?"
Atcchan: "T-Three is still better than nothing! It was probably an improvement over the last time I went there with you..."
Amu: "Heheh. Well, at least I can admire your tenacity! Even though it all seemed so hopeless, you stuck it out until the very end! And I thought you'd break down crying, beat the floor with your fists and shout 'This is all useless...!'"
Atcchan: "H-Hey! I-I've never done that once in my life...!"
Amu: "Well, you know. There's a first time for everything~"
Atcchan: "Bleh!"
*The two of us bicker companionably as we make our way back home.*
*After we played around in the batting center, we ended up doing some window shopping (more like, Amu dragged me around from shop to shop until my feet felt like they were going to fall off) and then we got something to eat, so it's pretty late now.*
*It's getting pretty late, and the wind is colder than it was earlier.*
*We could've gotten a ride back with Amu's dad, which would've spared us the need to walk, but Amu flatly refused.*
*She said she didn't want to go back with her dad, since he would just take the opportunity to lecture her about her 'unacceptable work ethic.'*
Amu: "Seriously... Dad's always drilling it into me about how important the café is to him, and how I need to get my act together... At some point, you just get tired of hearing the same thing over and over, you know?"
*I do know that Amu's dad only has her best interests at heart, but I also know he is a very loud man who loves the sound of his own voice, and arguing with him is often impossible.*
Atcchan: "Yeah. It must be a pain."
Amu: "It really, really is! No matter what he says, I'm not going to run the business for him when he retires. I absolutely refuse to live a life already planned out for me!"
Atcchan: "Does he want you to take it over from him?"
Amu: "Yeah, but I don't wanna. It doesn't sound like much fun."
Atcchan: "What do you want to do instead, then?"
*Amu has to think for a few seconds before she comes up with an answer.*
Amu: "... Professional baseball player?"
Atcchan: "I think you can do it! You've definitely got the skills."
Amu: "Ahaha~ Who knows? Maybe a kindly passing talent scout will come here someday and save me from my life of drudgery."

Amu: "Exactly! Only with more baseball."
Amu: "Of course, Dad wouldn't be too happy about that."
Atcchan: "I didn't know you cared all that much about what your parents thought."

*Amu shrugs her shoulders, a slightly bitter smile on her face.*
Amu: "Of course I care about them, and I wanna make them proud. I'm glad for everything they've done for me. But at the same time..."
Amu: "What they want for me and my future, and what I want for my future, are totally different things."
Atcchan: "You mean... You don't want to stay in this village?"

Atcchan: "But don't you like it here...? The scenery, the familiarity, the quiet..."

Amu: "Heheh... Well, of course memories are important. I had a lot of fun together with you, too! But, you know..."
Amu: "I've been thinking... maybe this place only seemed like fun when we were little because we didn't know any better."
Atcchan: "What do you mean...?"
Amu: "Well... It's kind of hard to explain, and I'm not so good at explaining difficult things, but..."
Amu: "I think, when you're a kid... everything is a lot bigger and a lot more exciting because you don't know very much about the world."
Amu: "Simple things, like playing in the forest or climbing trees, seemed like really big adventures back then."
Amu: "And then, when you get older, you realize that the tiny bit of land you live on isn't the entirety of the world... and you start wanting to see more of it."

Amu: "Hehehe~ I remember that. I think I got a little annoyed. It was something I really, reaaaally wanted to do, and you didn't seem to appreciate your chance at all!"
Atcchan: "Well, I would've swapped with you if I could. My mother always wanted a girl."

Atcchan: "I-I... I'm not girly..."
Amu: "Yeah, you are. You're far cuter than me."
Atcchan: "I-I... I-I am not cute...!"
Amu: "You are so cute. So cute it's unbelievable."
Amu: "I've never seen anybody as little and delicate before! You could totally be some kind of teen idol! I bet you'd have so many fans!"

Amu: "You are! You're humble and shy! And you have such a cute little baby face!"

Amu: "I want to go to somewhere with lots of people, where I can discover all kinds of new things!"
Amu: "I wanna be able to wear the new fashions I see in magazines; I wanna try all these interesting foods I've never had before; I wanna go and have some fun and exciting experiences!"
Amu: "I've never been ice skating, or to a theme park, or seen any of the bands I like live! I've never even had any exciting encounters with guys, like I read about in those advice columns in girls' magazines..."
Amu: "I've never had the chance..."
*When Amu finally reaches the end of her tirade, she looks exhausted. She sighs.*
*I wonder how long she's been holding these thoughts inside - these lingering resentments held against her hometown that just keep growing and growing as the days go by...*
*Standing in the middle of a dusty, rarely used road, which only serves to illustrate her point about how isolated this village is... with her hands clasped into fists at her sides... Amu lets her head hang.*
*Her figure casts a long, gloomy shadow out over the road.*
Amu: "I want to go out into the world and have some fun. It's so stifling here, and everything always looks the same, day after day... I feel like I'm running out of things to do to keep me distracted."

Amu: "If it keeps me busy... Then sure, I guess..."
*Amu sighs.*
Amu: "But, really... Even though all this stuff upsets me a little, it didn't used to be so bad. I could deal with it."
*Why is she talking in the past tense...?*
Atcchan: "What do you mean, you 'could' deal with it?"
Amu: "I mean... Ehehe... This is gonna sound kind of corny, but..."
*Amu smiles sheepishly and hooks her hands together at her front, rocking back and forth on her heels.*
Amu: "Well... I wasn't alone. You lived here, too."
Atcchan: "Hey... Is that Tiger?"
Amu: "Huh? Oh yes! Yes, it is!"

Amu: "I bet Dad'd do that to me, too, if I let him. He loves feeding people. It's like he's obsessed."
*I start to smile stupidly despite myself as Tiger - Amu's cat - nuzzles herself against my side.*
*It's been two years since I last visited Amu's home... and yet, despite that, her cat still seems to remember me, even though the cat itself (or herself, should I say?) looks totally different.*

*Tiger's sleek, ginger fur, marked here and there with white stripes, remains as distinctive as always; an indication of how she got her name.*
Atcchan: "A-Aah..."

Amu: "Sleepy?"
Atcchan: "J-Just a little. It was a tiring day..."
Amu: "Whaaa~aaat? Really?"

Amu: "How can you be sleepy at this hour? You're not in elementary school anymore!"
Atcchan: "Well, I'm not, but you are."
Amu: "Eeeh?! And what do you mean by that?"

Atcchan: "I-Indeed..."

Amu: "Heh. You've gotta be strong. You're so polite, Atcchan, you'd probably thank somebody if they started tearing out your fingernails!"
Atcchan: "P-Probably..."

*And I feel like we've had this conversation before...*
Amu: "Ehehe~ Don't worry, Atcchan, don't worry. When you get kidnapped by any evil forces, I'll come to save you every time! You can rely on me! "
Atcchan: "W-Waah! Don't go deciding these things for yourself like that!"
*I-It isn't fair...*
*How is it that Amu can say such corny lines but still sound cool... yet, if I tried to do the same, I'd just sound ridiculous...?*
*It must be some kind of natural, innate talent. I can't imagine there are any self-help books or schools that will teach you those techniques.*
Amu: "Ooh... By the way, Atcchan..."
*I eye Amu dubiously.*
Atcchan: "Yes? What is it?"
*From my extensive knowledge gleaned from being this girl's friend, I'm willing to bet 500 yen she's going to ask me to do something embarrassing or demeaning.*
*However... When I look at Amu's face...*
*There's something strange about her expression. Something I never expected to see.*
*Amu is... blushing.*
*She's actually blushing.*

Amu: "Well, um... Lately, I was just... doing a bit of practicing, and... you know I said I was learning to play the guitar, right?"
Atcchan: "Oh...? I do remember that, kinda."
Amu: "Yeah, um... I've been learning for, maybe five or six months now... um... and, even though I'm not that good, I... I wanted to show you...!"

Amu: "You wouldn't mind...? Would that be okay?"
*Waah...*
*Amu sounds so unusually serious, for once, and yet so unsure of her own abilities...*
*It makes my heart melt, just like Valentine's Day chocolates left on top of a heater (I think Amu would hit me if she heard that simile, though. 'What kind of cold person would do something like that?!' is what she'd probably say).*

Atcchan: "U-Um... O-Of course you can play something...! I-I'd love to hear it...!"

*I-It's not like I mind, but... M-Maybe my heart does, a little...*
*Since I'm stupid, like a heroine from a Victorian romance, it flutters at the slightest of provocations.*

Amu: "If you make fun of my playing, I'll get so pissed off I'll probably smack you in the head with my guitar!!!"

*I should've known she'd say something violent and un-cute like that. That's just part of her personality, after all.*
*Still... It's not like it's a bad thing.*
*I don't think Amu would be Amu if she wasn't just a little bit imposing.*

*What she's doing right now... is it called 'tuning?'*
*Although I don't know much about guitars (the only instrument I've ever played is the recorder in music class, back when I was a kid) I can tell that it's old. It looks chipped in some places, and has a few marks running across it.*
*When Amu sees me looking, she offers an explanation.*
Amu: "My parents wouldn't buy a guitar for me, even though I asked and asked. I had to buy it with my own money, from working at the café."
Amu: "Since they're expensive, I couldn't afford a brand new one..."
*Does that make the sound quality worse, or anything?":
*Did you give it a name?":
Amu: "Hm? Of course she has a name, Atcchan! What kind of cruel parent would I be if I didn't even give my baby a name?"
Atcchan: "B-Baby?"
Amu: "I mean, you wouldn't call your child 'Humanoid Creature A'... and, likewise, you wouldn't just call your guitar 'Guitar!' That implies a lack of passion! Commitment! Feeling! Fervor!"
Atcchan: "O-Okay, okay. I-I think I understand what you're trying to say."

Amu: "But if you live in the country, you need to get pumped up about the small things, because there aren't enough big things to keep you busy."

Amu: "Ohoh, but... Just to make sure you actually put in 110%%, and don't try to sneakily slack off..."

*The color drains from my face.*
*A 'punishment game'... Really? At our age?*
*Oh no...*
Noelle: "Punishment game? What's that...?"
*Noelle asks innocently, her eyes wide.*
*Poor child. She doesn't know what the dreaded words 'punishment game' entail, since she's never been on the receiving end of one.*
*Ah... Noelle is still so pure, so sweet...*
*If Amu ropes her into this demented game, what will happen to her innocence?! That gentle light in her blue, blue eyes may be snuffed out for all eternity!*

*Noelle frowns.*

*Amu smirks. It's a smirk lifted straight from the bowels of Hell, promising a world of pain.*
*My legs start to tremble. I feel faint.*
*Can I get out of this by claiming I've suddenly been struck down with a bad case of smallpox?*
*Has that been eradicated yet or not? I don't remember.*
*Why don't I pay more attention in biology class...?*
*... Probably because learning about various diseases from all over the world, and just how much damage they can do to the human body, makes me feel ill.*

*Why am I so uncreative? I read enough books in my spare time, you'd think I'd be able to come up with something. I even read that translation of De Sade's Justine I found in the school library a year ago - though what it was doing in the school library, I have no idea.*
Atcchan: "Um... Well, um..."
Noelle: "I have a suggestion."

Atcchan: "W-What is it...?"

*I want to reply with self-righteous indignation, but I can't. I know Amu's right.*
*Why does she have to be right all the time...?*
Amu: "What do you suggest?"
*Noelle looks at Amu with a small, shy smile.*
Noelle: "I think the person who captures the most interesting bug, which inspires my creativity, should be the winner."
*Out of the corner of my eyes, I spot it.*
*A large stag beetle with a hard, shiny black shell, sitting on the trunk of a tree.*
*Stag beetles are interesting insects, aren't they? I'm sure Noelle would like it. It's definitely more unusual than a cicada or a butterfly, with its black shell and strange tusks.*
*This is it. This is my big break.*
*After numerous false starts and foolish mistakes, tripping over tree roots and scaring away my potential prey... I finally have it.*
*With a specimen like this, I'll win that competition for sure!*
*I stare at the stag beetle intently, wiping beads of sweat from my forehead.*
*Although the thick leaves overhead stop the heat from becoming too oppressive, it's still a warm day, and I have been wandering around for a while.*
*Since I got overly picky about what bugs I should catch, then fumbled over the ones I did intend to take, I haven't caught a single thing yet. The clear jar Amu gave me to contain my spoils is completely empty.*
*This beetle is my last, and only, hope! It's the single thin, fine thread that separates total humiliation from complete victory...!*
*What should I do...?*
*I reach out with the net, aiming at the beetle.*
*It's because I rush that I end up making mistakes. If I do it slow and steady, I'm sure I'll succeed.*
*I'm sure of it.*
*I can do it. I believe in me!*
*I...*
*I...*
Atcchan: "W-What...?!"
*The beetle... where did it go...?*
*Did I take too long? Did it slip away while I was trying to psych myself up? W-What happened...?!*
*That was my last hope... and I let it escape.*
*I let it escape... and I didn't even see it go!*
*Waaaaah... There's no hope for me - none at all!*
*I really am stupid...*
Atcchan: "Why must life be so unfair?"
Amu: "Wahahaha! Atchaa~aan, you look so cute!"
Atcchan: "S-Stop it...! Stop staring at me like that!"
Amu: "No way, no way~ You're so adorable I could eat you up like an ice cream sundae!"

*I have feelings too, you know?*
Atcchan: "I-If I really was that cute you wouldn't be laughing at me..."
Amu: "Hm? What's that~?"
*Amu grins. I don't like that expression. I don't like it at all.*

*Noelle speaks up suddenly, her head peeking out from over the top of her sketchbook.*
*Noelle sits alongside Amu and me, at the side of the river. Her hair flutters gently in the breeze, her skirts shifting about her legs.*
*Her shoes have been kicked off somewhere, I don't know where, and she's pressing her bare feet against the earth, grinding up the soil between her exposed toes.*
*Before her sits the clear jar containing Amu's winning bug: an interestingly colored, fluffy caterpillar.*

*An accordion in a dress.*
*How charming.*

Atcchan: "Well, I... Um..."

Amu: "Well, it doesn't matter if you know or not~ The fact is, you didn't win so you can't test it out! It's the perfect devil's proof! "
*What a pragmatist...*
Atcchan: "Grrrrr..."
*I grit my teeth together.*
*It's annoying, but Amu is right.*
*Even though I'm sure her words are a massive lie, I can't disprove them. Because I've never beaten her at anything before, not once in my whole life, I have no way of knowing how she reacts to failure...*
Amu: "Ehehe~ But never mind, never mind. I am a gracious winner!"

*After an hour or so, Noelle finally sets down her sketchbook.*
*Her expression is inscrutable as always. I'm not sure what it means.*
*I wonder if she's happy with her picture?*

*Noelle's voice is soft and judicious; her head peeking out from over the top of her sketchbook.*
*She's sitting, cross-legged, barefoot, her shoes kicked off somewhere unknown. Before her sits the jar that contains my winning stag beetle, and on her lap is her sketchbook.*
*Slowly, methodically, Noelle sketches out a picture of that beetle; her pencil held tightly in her pale hand.*
*Tipping her head this way and that, pale hair falling over one shoulder, she ponders; biting her lower lip in thought.*

Noelle: "Ah... That's enough for now."

*I open my mouth, ready to ask Noelle a question (though I'm not entirely sure what), when-*
Amu: "That's stupid."
*Her voice is curt, sharp; almost as pointed as the end of a knitting needle. I jump in alarm, as though I've been jabbed in the side by one - and Noelle does, too.*
*Why does she sound so irate?*
Atcchan: "Amu? Are you okay...?"

*I thought, up until a few minutes ago, we were playing around, having a good time. Why did her mood suddenly change like that?*
*I don't understand Amu sometimes. Maybe it's because I'm a guy...?*
*She's always saying I'm too dimwitted. That I can't understand her 'maidenly heart.' Perhaps it's true.*
*But...*
*No. That's no good. I don't like it. I won't accept something like that.*
*Saying things like 'Oh, I can't relate to your worries because you're not like me' is pretty cheap. It's a get out clause used by lazy people to give them the leeway to stop thinking. To stop trying.*
*To discard the problems of others as something irrelevant, completely unrelated to them.*
*I don't want to do that. Since Amu's my friend, I can't dismiss her feelings that easily.*
Noelle: "I, um... I..."
Noelle: "I-I'm sorry... D-Did I did something wrong...?"
*Amu sighs.*
Amu: "No, you didn't do anything wrong. I just don't like what you said."
Noelle: "W-What I said?"
Amu: "That's right. I don't like it when people say things are 'impossible.' Nothing's impossible."

Atcchan: "Amu, I think you're being too mean."

Noelle: "I'm fine, really. Amu has a point."
*Noelle smiles, though her expression is weak; like orange squash mixed with too much water. Her fingers, gripping the sides of her sketchbook, are trembling.*
Noelle: "I... I need to try harder."
*I guess that means you try hard.":
*Doesn't that mean you're lonely?":
Noelle: "Hm? Ah..."
Noelle: "I don't know. Because I like drawing, it doesn't seem like a difficult task."
Noelle: "You know... I think it's strange, praising people for doing something they love. The act of doing it in the first place is enough of a reward."
Amu: "Huh... Maybe I understand."
Amu: "Like... if you enjoy the art, then you don't need to be complimented?"
Noelle: "Mm. I think it's something like that."
Noelle: "Although I don't dislike compliments, they don't feel very necessary. That's not why I draw."
Amu: "Aah! No, I've got it! I really think I've got it!"
*I look at Amu dubiously. Is that really true?*
*Maybe I should test her.*
Atcchan: "What have you 'got', Amu?"
Amu: "Kukuku~ Weeell... I enjoy teasing you,  Atcchan - and it comes easily to me!"

Amu: "I enjoy teasing you! That's what I said, right~?"

Amu: "It has everything to do with everything!"
Amu: "You might not agree, but...  Personally, I think annoying you is also a form of art!"
Atcchan: "Huh? That's stupid! That isn't what 'art' is, is it, Noelle?"
*I look at Noelle, searching for support.*

Amu: "Yes, yes~ Thank you, thank you! But I don't need to be praised for my art, because I love doing it so much!"
*At this, Noelle gives Amu a small round of applause, clapping her hands together politely.*
*The soft pitter-patter fills the forest, mingling with the sounds of the running river.*
*Aaaah... Amu looks so pleased with herself...*
*I-It's almost as though she exists simply to embarrass me...*
*That isn't how art really works, is it? That's ridiculous!*
Noelle: "Hm... Lonely...?"
Atcchan: "Y-Yeah... Maybe a little."
Noelle: "Why do you think I'm lonely, Atcchan...? Why?"
Atcchan: "Aah, well, um... It's just the impression I got from hearing you talk..."

Amu: "No, you're really not. You were always terrible in art class!"
Atcchan: "I know..."
Amu: "Remember when we were making papier-mâché sculptures, and you'd been biting the skin around your nails, and then you got all that glue into your cuts and it made you cry?"
Atcchan: "Y-Yes, I know that...! It hurt a lot, so I wouldn't forget it in a hurry! You don't need to remind me!"

Atcchan: "Y-Yes, it did... It happened before you transferred here."
*I pout, my face turning pale.*
Atcchan: "It wasn't very much fun..."
*After that incident, I always dreaded going to art class.*
Amu: "I thought it was funny~"
Atcchan: "That's because you're a horrible person."
*I have so many painful childhood memories, if I sold each one for 50 yen I'd probably end up rolling in money.*
*However... my tragic history wasn't meant to be the centerpiece of this conversation, was it?*
*I thought we were meant to be talking about Noelle.*

*I want to try and understand her.*
Atcchan: "I still think it sounds sad."

Atcchan: "Because... The idea that, maybe, you draw to communicate with others... but you still can't get your ideas across..."
