Amu: "Huh. That's so gloomy. Thinking like that wouldn't be fun at all."
Noelle: "No, it isn't."
Amu: "Then just don't think like that!"
Noelle: "What...?"
Amu: "Just don't do it! If thinking something makes you unhappy, then don't think it!"
Noelle: "But... I don't know if that's possible for me..."
Amu: "Of course it is! You just need a little training!"
*Amu grins. Waving one finger in the air, as though she's a teacher giving a lecture on philosophy, she continues her spiel.*
Amu: "If you have a bad attitude, then the way you view life will be gloomy and grey."
Amu: "If you think things like 'Nobody can understand me so I can never get close to anyone.', then you'll never be able to make friends!"
Amu: "You can't have a defeatist attitude in life. You've gotta keep going forwards, no matter how many times you get knocked back, and keep trying to reach out to people!"
Amu: "Push through the bad times and get rid of the bad thoughts! Pretty soon, you'll find out the world isn't as gloomy as you think... and there are lots of interesting colors, instead of just grey."

Amu: "That's right~!"
Noelle: "Ah..."

*She directs her gaze downwards, staring down at her drawing in her sketchbook.*

Noelle: "I don't know... It's confusing..."

Amu: "With me, it's more like... I have to think like that."
Amu: "Otherwise, I'd get so tired living in this little village in the middle of nowhere I'd start tearing my own hair out - and I like my hair. I don't wanna ruin it over something so silly."
Amu: "Ehehehe..."
Noelle: "No, it... It's interesting..."
*And with this, Noelle offers Amu a small, hesitant smile.*
*It may not seem like much, but... coming from a reserved girl like Noelle, a tiny smile like this is worth more than any diamond.*
Noelle: "Thank you... I will try."

Amu: "Yes, of course! Why wouldn't it be?"

Amu: "So, I really haven't done anything wrong! I'm just taking advantage of somebody else's mistake!"

Amu: "Hey. You can hardly talk, Atcchan. You're just as complicit in this crime as I am."
*Darn it... She's right. Since I'm an accessory to the crime, it's impossible for me to counter her.*
*Amu and I are standing around in our classroom (Noelle having already wandered off somewhere earlier).*
*This is the only classroom in the whole school, actually. The only one that actually gets used, I mean.*
*There are a few other classrooms; a reminder of when the school was first built and this village was bigger. Now, however, there are so few students they can all be taught in one room, together.*
*The other classrooms are always locked. I've never been inside them.*
*As such, they've inspired a lot of ghost stories...*
*I don't really know why Amu decided to come here. Maybe she doesn't, either. I think she was just acting on the spur of the moment.*
*All I know is, one moment we were all sitting together by the river... and the next, Amu was up on her feet, trying to chivvy us along.*
Amu: "Come on, come on! I just had a really great idea!"
Atcchan: "Is it as good as your mastermind plan to combine green tea with Pocari Sweat?"
Amu: "Sadly, it isn't quite as good as that. That really was a stroke of genius, if I do say so myself!"
Atcchan: "You'll have to say it yourself. Nobody else will."
Amu: "Huh? What are you talking about? Green tea is amazing, so it's only natural that everything will taste better with it!"

Amu: "Then it's decided! Let's do it! Right now!"
Atcchan: "O-Okay, but... I just thought. Won't it be locked?"
Amu: "Kukuku~ You underestimate me, Atcchan. We'll find a way around that somehow!"

*Amu, being the devious person that she is, somehow knew about a window that hadn't been locked. By carefully entering in through that window we were able to get inside.*
*And... That's about the gist of it, really.*

Amu: "Nonsense! We're students. They should be glad we're coming in to school more than we have to!"

Amu: "Yes! It shows that we have a good work ethic!"
Atcchan: "I don't know if that's true, but..."
*I look around my settings, taking in the familiar sights once more.*
*I move through the classroom, a little dusty from disuse over the holiday, and sit down at my old desk.*
*It's been so long since I was last here, but... the time really did fly by.*
*I didn't want to move to the city at all. I was sure I would hate it.*
*The first few weeks were pretty hard, trying to acclimatize to my new environment. I got lost so many times, and it was hard for me to make new friends. However...*
*After some initial bumps, I was eventually able to settle in.*
*After a month, I'd already fallen into the comfortable monotony of routine. No longer was riding the train to school intimidating; finding my classroom confusing; my new classmates strangers.*
*I got used to it and I accepted my new position. I started to take it for granted.*
*After that, the time began to move by more quickly. Before I knew it, two years had gone by, just like that... and I started to forget.*
*I started to forget what my old life used to be like.*
*Somehow, without even intending to, my memories of this building and its comforting, sawdusty smell, faded away.*

*It's strange how that happens.*
*I guess people can adapt to anything, no matter how daunting it may seem to begin with.*
Amu: "So, Atcchan..."
*Amu walks over to me, her hands behind her back. She stops to rest by my desk, looking down at me with a smile.*
*Light filters in through the open windows. I can see individual particles of dust dancing in the air, strangely ethereal.*
Amu: "Have you been having a good time with Noelle?"
*Amu's voice is fairly light, and yet...*
*It feels like a trick question - like asking what a whole string of numbers multiplied together are, and sneakily slipping in a zero without the other person noticing.*
*Of course, the answer to that would be zero - but you'd only know that if you were paying close attention.*
*Is Amu going to play some kind of prank on me?*
Atcchan: "Ah, um... Y-Yeah, I... I've been having a good time..."
Amu: "Oh. That's nice. I'm happy for you."
Amu: "I bet you really missed her. She is your best friend, after all - isn't she?"
Atcchan: "I-I, um... S-She's very important to me, but-"
Amu: "More important than me?"
Atcchan: "I... I-I..."
*My words catch in my throat.*
*Amu isn't smiling anymore.*
*There's no way... you could call that unpleasant expression a smile...*
Atcchan: "A-Amu..."
*Amu takes a step towards me. Then she takes another. And another. Slowly. Very slowly.*
*Her footsteps echo throughout the otherwise empty classroom, the floorboards creaking in protest. It's the only noise I can hear, other than the beating of my own heart.*

Amu: "Atcchan... I really did try, you know?"
Amu: "I tried to be a good friend. I tried my best. I really, really did... But..."

Amu: "But, even though it's been two years... Even after all this time, I..."

*I... I had no idea...*

*They always do whenever I really need them.*

Atcchan: "I... I-It's not like I like her more, i-it's just-"

*I...*
*I don't know what to say.*
*Amu's right.*
*This whole time, I... was only ever thinking about Noelle.*
*That's because Amu's strong. She's always been the best at climbing trees; at skipping stones; at jumping rivers; at catching bugs; at playing sports.*
*For the duration of our friendship I've always been two, three, four steps behind her, trailing behind in the dust.*
*When I fell over and scuffed my knee, Amu gave me a piggyback home. When I got scared of some wild dogs when we went for a walk, Amu chased them away with a stick. When I couldn't climb up a tree, Amu offered me her hand.*
*During the summer festival, when we were only kids... Amu scooped up all those goldfish for me when I couldn't catch a single one... and she gave me that cute, fluffy teddy bear that she won from a stall.*

*Like the other gestures of kindness Amu has shown me over the years... I gradually forgot about it.*
*This whole time... I've only been thinking about Noelle.*

*Is that... really it?*

*I remember one time when I was little, my dad shouted at me.*

Mrs. Jougasaki: "Don't be mad, Amu, dear. It's not his fault. His ears just get clogged up easily."

Amu: "I said, I don't care."

Mrs. Jougasaki: "Dear, it's all right. If Amu is sick then-"

Amu: "It doesn't matter. I don't care!"
Amu: "Shut up, Dad! You're stupid! You don't understand! You don't know how I feel, so you should just shut up!!! I hate you!!!"

Mrs. Jougasaki: "Dear. Please calm down."
*Mom rests a hand on Dad's shoulder. Her gentle voice seems to bring him back to his senses. It definitely brings his behind back down to his chair.*
Mrs. Jougasaki: "Now then."

Mrs. Jougasaki: "What do you mean, honey? Did something bad happen at school?"

Amu: "..."
Mr. Jougasaki: "..."
Amu: "..."
*Did I... do something wrong...?*
*Why isn't he giving me a hug? Patting me on the head? Trying to comfort me?*

Amu: "Don't call me a liar when I'm not! You're all lying, saying I'm a liar!!!"

*I don't get it. It doesn't make any sense...!*
Mr. Jougasaki: "Amu."

*At other times, that would probably make me laugh. But right now, I can't.*
*...*
*...*
*...*
*The silence... is very heavy.*
*I tremble.*
*My dad opens his mouth...*
*... and then, he shouts. He shouts at me.*

Amu: "D-Daddy, I-"

Mr. Jougasaki: "Amu..."

Mr. Jougasaki: "I'm sorry I shouted at you, honey, but some things need to be made clear so you can understand. So you can become a proper adult."

Mr. Jougasaki: "I was always messin' around - and it worked out all right for me."
Mr. Jougasaki: "But Amu..."

Amu: "D-Daddy..."

Amu: "Ow..."

*Even though he's trying to comfort me, it hurts. He's way too strong.*

*At least... I think I do.*
Mr. Jougasaki: "If you don't like it, then you'll just need to try harder next time!"
*I failed that test because I didn't try. And yet, even though it was all my fault... I still got upset and angry - but I had no right to.*
*If I wanted to do well on the test, I should have tried harder.*

*It's something I've always tried to do... even when it got difficult. Even when it hurt.*

Amu: "D-Don't talk to me."
Atcchan: "But Amu, I-"

Atcchan: "But, I- I really am so-"
Amu: "Shut up! Go away! Just disappear!"
Atcchan: "I..."

*But, with love... it doesn't matter how hard you try. Your efforts may never be rewarded.*
*If somebody doesn't like you... what can you do? Brute force can never make somebody fall in love with you. It only turns people away.*

Amu: "Did you miss this place?"

Atcchan: "I thought, since I spent so much time here, I wouldn't forget, but... even though it's just the minor details, I... I don't remember as much as I thought I would..."

Amu: "I was just thinking... Even though the time we spent together is still so important to me, maybe... maybe it isn't the same for you."
Amu: "Since you're going to a new school in the big ol' city now, and you're all caught up in your shiny, exciting new life... I got kind of... scared..."

Amu: "Hehe. You flatter me. They were just dumb mutts. I ain't afraid of dogs!"

Amu: "I don't think I'm explaining it right, but..."
Amu: "I just thought... maybe you'd start to forget about the small things in this village... like the sound of the cicadas, or how the air smells, or where you used to sit in class..."
Amu: "And then, after that, you'd start to forget bigger and bigger things, and then..."
Amu: "I thought, maybe... you might even start to forget me."
Atcchan: "I-I... I wouldn't forget. My memory isn't that bad."
Amu: "I know, but... It's not simply a case of bad memory. Over time, people grow up. They see new things, and they start to forget old stuff."
Amu: "It happens slowly - so slowly you might not even realize it."
Amu: "But is that really okay?! It's scary! If you don't realize that you've started to forget, how can you make yourself remember!?"
*I... I understand what she's saying.*
*Even though I wasn't trying to forget the details of my life here, and was so convinced I never would... inevitably, I did.*
*I was so busy getting accustomed to my new life I didn't have much time to think about my old one.*
*By the time I'd finally settled in, I was too caught up in my new routine to keep living in the past.*
*And so, although it wasn't intentional... I started to forget. The rot of time had already set in, eating into my memories one by one.*
Atcchan: "I guess you're right... Even though I didn't mean to, I... I really did forget..."
Amu: "Yeah. And I don't like it."
Amu: "I don't want to be stuck here in this crappy little village while you go off and forget about me. I don't think I could stand that."
Amu: "I don't want you to forget, or it'll start to seem like our time together wasn't even real!"

*For the last two years, I ignored Noelle steadfastly. I didn't call her and I didn't write to her. I didn't try at all.*

*And so, here I am... back at the dilapidated old train station with the single, lonely looking wooden bench.*

*She bites her lower lip.*
Amu: "I carried you back to the village."
Atcchan: "H-Huh? You carried me?"
Amu: "Ah... Y-Yeah, well..."
*Amu looks down at her knees, refusing to meet my eyes. She looks embarrassed.*
Amu: "You're small so it wasn't very hard. I-It wasn't a problem for me or anything."
Amu: "Even though it makes me look an Amazon... Haha..."
*So, I guess... Amu saved me...?*
*Like a knight in shining armor, she came to my aid... and even carried me, the fainted damsel, back to safety.*
*Hau...*
*Amu really is cool.*
Amu: "A-And then, uh... I guess, I phoned the police. And told them what happened. Um, and I called an ambulance, too... Since, when I found Noelle, I kind of, um..."
Amu: "... Reacted instinctively, and hit her over the head with that glass jar..."
Amu: "I hit her pretty hard, actually. Harder than I meant to."
Atcchan: "Y-Yeah... You've always been bad at judging your own strength."
*Whenever we played baseball at school, and Amu was the batter, she hit the ball so hard it was impossible for anybody to best her. She made the younger kids cry in frustration more than once.*
*To counter this, Miss Tachibana eventually decided Amu could never be the batter in P.E. class. It was just too unfair.*
Amu: "But, um... Noelle's all right. She's going to be okay."
Amu: "S-She's still unconscious and... she's more badly injured than you are. She might have to stay in the hospital for a few weeks."
Amu: "But... I think she'll be fine."
Atcchan: "Aah..."
*I sigh, leaning back against my pillow. It requires too much energy to keep myself upright, and I already feel exhausted as it is.*
Amu: "Atcchan? Are you sleepy? Do you want me to go?"
Atcchan: "No. I... I'm all right. I'm just..."
Atcchan: "I can't believe this really happened."
Amu: "... Neither can I. It was like something from a movie."
Amu: "I... really had no idea Noelle was so... unwell..."
Atcchan: "Yeah. Me neither."
*I should have known.*
*I should have known just how unhappy she was.*
*Since I was her best friend... her only friend... I should have known better than anyone else.*
*I should have tried to support her.*
*If I had been a better friend... maybe this wouldn't have happened. Maybe this could have been avoided.*
*But there's no use saying 'What if?' There's no use saying 'Maybe.'*
*As Noelle might say... averting your eyes from the facts is useless. That doesn't change reality.*
*It doesn't change a thing.*
*Noelle...*
*I'm sorry I betrayed you.*
Noelle: "Atcchan?"
Atcchan: "Y-Yeah...?"
Noelle: "You know, I... I've never... had a friend before..."
Atcchan: "R-Really? Not a single one...?"
Noelle: "No. So, um..."
Noelle: "You... Y-You mean a lot to me..."
Noelle: "C-Can you promise we... W-We'll be friends forever...?"
Atcchan: "Ah..."
Atcchan: "Of course I can. Friends forever. Until the end."
Atcchan: "I promise."
Noelle: "Hn..."
Noelle: "It is true I am upset by that, but... That isn't it. That isn't it at all."
Noelle: "You don't really understand, do you? You don't understand a thing."
Atcchan: "A-Ah... I... I..."
*My eyes dart around in their sockets, as though searching for an escape - but it's useless. It's all useless...*
*I can't budge an inch.*
Noelle: "For abandoning me... For ignoring me... I could forgive you for that."
Noelle: "If you hated me, I would understand. I can be difficult. I can be annoying. So, if you never liked me... that's fine. I'm used to it."
Noelle: "Nobody has ever liked me. So that makes sense. I understand. I'm not mad."
Noelle: "It..."
Noelle: "It's the lying that I can't stand."
Noelle: "Please don't tell me you're my friend... when you've hurt me so much. Friends aren't meant to hurt each other like that."
Atcchan: "B-But we... we are friends, aren't we?"
Noelle: "I don't think so."
*Noelle's voice is cool, cutting through my words without mercy.*
*She's right. I can't counter her.*
*If I was Noelle... I wouldn't trust me either.*
Noelle: "Just tell me you hate me. Say you never liked me. That... would be fine..."
Noelle: "But don't pretend to be my friend. Not when you've hurt me so much."
Noelle: "That gives me false hope. It makes me think, maybe you do like me..."
*Noelle's body trembles.*
Noelle: "But I don't want to think like that anymore."
Noelle: "It's because I had that vague hope... that, for the past two years, I've been suffering."
Noelle: "I don't want to like you anymore. If I could stop liking you... I would stop hoping. So please..."
Noelle: "Don't let me hope anymore."
Noelle: "I know I'm a sick person who doesn't deserve to have any friends...! So, please, don't pity me...!"
*Noelle's voice is quiet but frantic. Her words trip over one another in a desperate bid to escape her mouth.*
*I've never heard her talk so much before. It's a little intimidating.*
*What happened to her? She used to be my best friend, didn't she?*
*How did she end up like this...?*
*If I had been a better friend, maybe I would know. But I don't. I don't... know anything...*
Atcchan: "S-So, why... W-Why are you doing this, Noelle...? I-I thought we were friends..."
Noelle: "Oh. Are we friends? Are we?"
Atcchan: "W-We've been friends for almost seven years, d-dummy..."
Noelle: "Maybe there was something like that once. But..."
*Noelle wipes her eyes with the back of her arm, brushing aside the tears easily, as though they're inconsequential - mere drops of rain.*
Noelle: "Surely we're not friends anymore? If we ever were to begin with."
Atcchan: "H-Huh...? W-What do you mean...? O-Of course we're friends...!"
Noelle: "So you say, but..."
Noelle: "If we really were friends... why did you abandon me? Why?"
Atcchan: "Ah..."
*I open my mouth, but my words catch in my throat.*
*I can't counter her.*
*It's true.*
*What she's saying... is all true.*
Noelle: "I like you, Atcchan. I do. I really do. But..."
Noelle: "Don't tell me that we're 'friends.' Don't lie to me like that. Because, if it was true..."
Noelle: "If it was true... you wouldn't have left me without saying goodbye. And you would have written letters."
Noelle: "You would have tried to stay in touch. And... A-And..."
*Her voice breaks. Her eyes well up with fresh tears. She doesn't wipe them away this time.*
*Instead, they course freely down her cheeks, trickling hotly, in a slow stream.*
Noelle: "Y-You... You would have wanted to see me... O-On your final day here, in this village... Y-You would have invited me along, too."
Noelle: "I-If I was your friend... I-If you really, truly cared... you wouldn't ignore me like this!"
Noelle: "A real friend... D-Doesn't make their friend feel so awful...! They wouldn't do it...! A-And so... A-And so..."
Noelle: "You are not my friend!"
Noelle: "I like you, Atcchan... but, you're a liar. And I hate liars."
*Noelle kneels down before me, the box cutter held in her right hand.*
*She presses it against my neck. The blade is cool and sharp.*
*I shiver. It nicks my skin. It stings, making me wince. A sharp burst of pain.*
*From the shallow cut on my skin... I can see small, round beads of blood, red as rubies, bubble up to the surface.*
*My breath catches in my throat.*
*I can't move. I can't struggle. I can't fight back.*
*I can only stare at Noelle... watching, waiting, in silent horror, as my entire field of vision is swallowed up. Engulfed by those large, light blue eyes.*
Noelle: "Atcchan..."
Atcchan: "N-Noelle..."
Noelle: "I'm sorry. I don't want to hurt you. I just want to teach you."
Noelle: "The world is a painful place. I know that better than anyone..."
Noelle: "And now... I'm going to teach you, too."
Noelle: "Maybe, this way... we can understand one another. Right...?"
*And with that, the blade sinks down, deep, into my throat.*
*The two of us, Amu and I, sit together on the mossy bank of a small river.*
*I stretch, grimacing. My feet ache and my ankles sting. I think I must've stepped in a patch of nettles.*
*That's what I get for foolishly venturing into the deeper parts of the forest. I should've known it would end up like this.*
*Naturally, Amu caught all the bugs, whereas I tripped over my own feet continuously and made a fool out of myself. In the end, I couldn't catch a single thing.*
*Maybe it was out of sympathy for me, but - at long last - Amu most judiciously decided we could take a break.*
*Aah...*
*Even though my body is covered in scratches, and my ankles are starting to go red and blotchy... it really is pretty here. Not even my own physical discomfort can detract from that fact.*
*The pale green light, filtering down through the trees, makes the surface of the water shimmer.*
*The sunlight, intercepted from above by the leaves of the trees, is mild and pleasant; not too hot nor too cold.*
*The sounds of the forest... the gentle running of the river... the smell of the earth...*
*It feels as though this moment could last forever.*
*I want to stay like this, with Amu... forever.*
Amu: "Hey, Atcchan! Think fast!"
Atcchan: "H-Huh? W-Wha-"
*But I don't get a chance to finish my sentence.*
*That's because I'm cut off, rather rudely, by a sudden spray of muddy river water - right in my open mouth.*
Atcchan: "Aaugh... Urgh...!"
*I cough and splutter, trying to rid my mouth of that unpleasant taste.*
*I wipe my face, rubbing my eyes with the backs of my arms. But it's all useless. It's not just my face that got wet - it's my hair and my clothes, too...*
*A-Aah... I-I must look ridiculous!*
Amu: "Kukuku! You look ridiculous~!"
*Of course I do. At least Amu was kind enough to reaffirm that for me - as if I had any doubts.*
*Amu stands in the river, smiling proudly. At some point, she must have kicked off her shoes and socks, leaving them lying amongst the grass.*
*The river seems fairly shallow, coming up to about halfway on her shins. The current is slow and gentle, too. I don't think there'll be much danger of her getting swept away.*
*Amu's bare legs shimmer with droplets of water. Her pink ponytail looks disheveled; even messier than usual.*
Atcchan: "A-Amuu! W-Why'd you do something like that?!"
*Amu shrugs, grinning.*
Amu: "I don't know! I thought it would be funny - and it was!"
Atcchan: "W-Waah...! Do you ever even think before you do stuff like that?!"
*There is a small pause. A semi-reflective expression crosses Amu's face...*
Amu: "..."
*And then...*
Amu: "Nah! If you think too much, you'll just get a headache! Thinking isn't fun at all!"
Atcchan: "I-I don't think splashing river water in somebody's face is fun!"
Amu: "I beg to differ. Why don't you go on ahead and try it? Try it, try it!"
Atcchan: "Huh? You mean you want me to splash water at you?"
Amu: "Mm... Not really. My parents will get mad if I come home all soggy."
*... I'm failing to see the logic behind this.*
Atcchan: "T-Then why?"
Amu: "Because it's fun, Atcchan! Because I wanna play! Is there anything wrong with that?!"
Atcchan: "Your parents will get mad. You just said so yourself."
Amu: "Hey, come on! Don't be so boring! We're young and carefree and we have our whole lives ahead of us! Let's go, let's go!"
*I eye the river dubiously, still sluicing river water out of my hair.*
Atcchan: "W-Well... I don't know. I don't want to take a seven hour train journey in wet clothes..."
Amu: "Then you can borrow mine! It'll be fine!"
Atcchan: "I-I'm hardly going to wear a skirt, am I?!"
Amu: "Oh, come on Atcchan, pleeeeeease? Pleeeease?"
*Aah...*
*I-I get the feeling, even if I flatly refuse and say 'no', Amu won't accept that. She can be a very stubborn person.*
*And besides... maybe it'll be fun...*
*Paddling in the river, splashing water at each other... It'd be just like the old times.*
*Instantly sensing my weakness, Amu strikes.*
Amu: "Yes! Come on, Atcchan, come on! The water will do you a world of good!"
Amu: "Since there are so many shrines in this forest, it might even have healing properties!"
*I think this claim sounds quite dubious, but still...*
*This will... probably be the last time I get to see Amu in quite some time.*
*If I leave now, without getting my revenge... that would be far too frustrating!*
*For the sake of my pride, I can't let this wicked deed go unpunished!*
*That's it! I can do it! I'm going to get her!*
Atcchan: "All right! You're gonna get what's coming to you, Amu! I won't show any mercy!"
*Amu and I lie together on the grassy bank of the river, both soaked to the bone. Our shoes and socks, kicked away somewhere, are the only articles of clothing we have that are still dry.*
*My breathing is labored from all that running. My chest rises and falls, my lungs heaving.*
*My face is light pink from exertion, while the rest of me is completely damp. But still...*
*Despite that, I'm happy.*
Amu: "Haah... Haah... You're a pretty tough opponent, Atcchan."
*Amu pants her appraisal; strands of light-pink hair stuck to her cheeks and forehead, whether from sweat or water, I don't know. Probably both.*
Atcchan: "Haah... Haah... Y-Yeah, you too."
Amu: "You fought with skill and determination. It was an honor being able to face off against you."
Atcchan: "Yeah... We really stuck it out until the very end, didn't we?"
Amu: "Ehehe..."
*Amu giggles softly, her green eyes directed upwards towards the light blue sky.*
Amu: "Heh. Who do you think won?"
Atcchan: "I think... I'd say it's a draw. We both did our best, and that's all that counts."
Amu: "Ehehe~ I guess. It feels kind of dull if there's no winner, though."
Atcchan: "Well, I'm the one who'll have to get on the train like this... So if the goal was to make the other person look as ridiculous as possible, you've probably won."
Amu: "Kukuku~ But Atcchan, there's far less of you than there is of me! You're so tiny!"
Atcchan: "Yeah, so...?"
Amu: "So, you must've splashed a wider surface area than I have. Does that make this your victory...?"
Atcchan: "That's pretty generous of you..."
*Even though I don't like her reasoning behind it.*
*I know I'm short. Does she really need to point it out?*
Amu: "I'm a pretty generous person~ Ehehe~"
*I lie there in silence, listening to the sounds of the forest; the running river and the chirping birds.*
*After a pause, I finally say it... a small smile on my face.*
Atcchan: "... Thank you, Amu."
Amu: "Huh? What for?"
Atcchan: "For... for always being here for me, and for making our time together so much fun."
Atcchan: "It really... wouldn't be the same without you, and... I really am going to miss you."
Amu: "Heh~ Don't talk like that, silly."
*I blink in surprise.*
Atcchan: "Like what?"
Amu: "Like this is some sad, final farewell, and you're never going to see me again."
Atcchan: "O-Oh, sorry... I guess I was being a little too sentimental..."
Amu: "Mmhmm! There's no need for 'thank you's! No matter where we go or what we do, we'll always be friends, right?"
Atcchan: "Y-Yes... Always... W-We're always going to be friends."
Amu: "Then there's no need to say goodbye."
*The two of us continue to lie on the bank, both dripping wet - but, more importantly... both smiling.*
*I wish this moment could last forever.*
Amu: "Ehehe... Atcchan..."
*Amu's voice is soft, barely more than a whisper.*
*It seems even she, as lively and loud as she usually is, doesn't want to spoil the peace of this moment.*
Atcchan: "Hm? What is it?"
*Amu smiles... and with a single, soft motion... rests her head on my shoulder.*
Amu: "I'm glad I was able to tell you..."
Amu: "Getting to confess my feelings to you... meant a lot to me."
Atcchan: "Ah... Au..."
*I feel my face getting red at this unexpected display of sentimentality.*
*D-Did Amu always used to talk like this...?*
Amu: "Ehehe~ It might sound weird, but... I think I might have liked you for a long, long time."
Atcchan: "E-Even though you always tease me?"
Amu: "Even so! It's because you get so flustered that I started to like you so much!"
Atcchan: "Y-You mean you like teasing me more than you like me as a person?"
Amu: "Kukuku~ Well, maybe~ There's never a dull moment with you!"
*I pout, my face red.*
Atcchan: "H-Hey... T-That's mean..."
Amu: "Sorry, sorry~ That's part of my personality. Even if we start going out, I won't stop being mean to you~ You'd better get used to it!"
Atcchan: "G-Going out...?"
Amu: "Well. We are, aren't we? We did kiss, after all."
Atcchan: "I-I know, but, but... S-Somehow, saying it like that seems... R-Really forward..."
Amu: "Ehehe~ You haven't had a girlfriend before, have you, Atcchan?"
Atcchan: "Y-You haven't had a boyfriend, either! Neither of us has that much experience."
Amu: "Yes, but I have read a decent amount of girls' manga. I know how it's supposed to go~"
Atcchan: "You read that kind of thing?"
Amu: "Huh? Of course I do. Why wouldn't I?"
Atcchan: "I-It doesn't seem to suit you..."
Amu: "Yeah... well, it was the closest to real romance I thought I was ever going to get to, living all the way out here."
Amu: "I wanted as much experience as possible. Even though I'm not cute like any of those heroines."
Atcchan: "I don't know about that. I think you're cute."
Amu: "H-Heh heh... E-Ehehe..."
*Amu laughs, but it doesn't sound her usual, easygoing giggle. Instead, it's a little stilted, slightly awkward.*
*Even though she often acts more mature than me, I know Amu's knowledge on romance is just as patchy as my own.*
*It's a comfort. It's nice to know I'm not the only one who's new at this.*
Amu: "You know... It's probably going to sound cliché, but..."
Amu: "I didn't realize just how much I liked you until you left."
Amu: "I guess I got so used to you being around me all the time that I started to take you for granted."
Amu: "But, as soon as you were gone, I realized. Everything was a lot more fun with you around. Nobody else reacts in quite the same way when I make fun of them."
Atcchan: "I-Is that supposed to be a compliment?"
Amu: "It is! It just means you look cute when you go all red!"
Atcchan: "Hau..."
Amu: "Yes, yes! Just like that~! "
*A-Amu really is the best at making me blush. Nobody else can come close.*
Atcchan: "U-Um, well... Me, too. I also missed you. I've never met anybody quite, um... quite like you..."
Amu: "Ehehe~ I'm glad. I thought, for sure, you'd have met up with some cool and cosmopolitan city girls who'd sweep you off your feet!"
Atcchan: "N-No way. I'm not that popular with girls - and anyway, I don't love those girls. I love you."
*Amu points at herself, her eyes wide.*
Amu: "You really love this country bumpkin? Seriously?"
Atcchan: "Yeah, I do. Seriously. You don't need to be jealous of any 'city girls.' We're both country bumpkins, you know?"
Amu: "I guess... Country bumpkins forever, huh?"
Atcchan: "Y-Yeah. Country bumpkins forever."
*I close my eyes and lie down by the gently flowing river, my fingers intertwined with Amu's.*
*Her hands... they feel so warm... so reassuring...*
*This really is perfect.*
*I wish we could stay like this forever.*
*As I lie there on the warm grass, I start to feel sleepy.*
*It's been a busy few days and I need to gather my energy for the train journey back.*
*It's not like I'll miss the train or anything, so... If I have a small nap right now... that won't matter, right...?*
*Slowly, slowly... I feel my consciousness slipping away.*
*Even if I died right now... I don't think I'd mind.*
*I've never been so happy before.*
*I can see you.*
*While I remain in hiding, like a fugitive, lost amongst the trees and shrouded in darkness... you lie by the river bank, bathed in the sunlight.*
*Unlike me, you're not alone. You've never been alone though, have you?*
*I used to think that was all right. The whole time, I told myself it was fine. I wasn't lonely. After all... I had you.*
*But not anymore.*
*Why...?*
*Why did you ignore me? I thought we were friends. You said were friends.*
*You told me that, and I believed you. I trusted you. Even though I swore I would never trust anybody else again, I tried my hardest. I really did try.*
*But... it seems I was wrong.*
*If you open your heart up to any human, they'll hurt it. Inevitably, they'll hurt it. They leave marks and scars that don't go away.*
*How long has my heart been like this?*
*When was the last time... that it didn't hurt?*
*I'm sure you didn't mean to hurt me. You're not a cruel person. I know you're not a cruel person. But even so...*
*Carelessness can do just as much damage as outright cruelty.*
*Even those who don't bully others cause damage, simply by doing nothing. It doesn't sound fair to say it like that, almost as though I'm accusing innocent people, but it's true.*
*I know that firsthand.*
*Even though you didn't do anything malicious... you still inflicted damage by ignoring me.*
*By abandoning me.*
*By never writing me a single letter - even though you promised we would always be friends. You promised.*
*All this time, I thought you were my friend. I told myself you were my friend. That our relationship was real. But...*
*That was... a lie...*
*Whenever you said you cared about me... it was a lie...*
*And I don't like liars.*
*I like you, but I don't like liars.*
*I like you, but you still hurt me.*
*I like you, but... that doesn't mean anything.*
*I already know you don't like me. I already know... you've abandoned me.*
*I can't keep hoping anymore. I need to put a stop to it right now.*
*It's because I still have hope... that it hurts.*
*It's because my hopes will never be realized... that it hurts.*
*My grip tightens around the box cutter in my hand. Although it looks cheap, the blade is sharp. I know that well.*
*So did the poor rabbit that I tested this on earlier. She knew.*
*I was following you this whole time, waiting. Waiting for you to let your guard down.*
*Now... I finally have my chance.*
*I walk towards you slowly, silently, ensuring my footsteps make no noise. You don't move. You don't stir.*
*You're both sound asleep, together by the riverside.*
*I'll make sure it stays like this forever.*
*I stand over you, my shadow dark against your pale skin.*
*You make a small sound, some kind of mumbling in your sleep, and turn over, shifting in the grass.*
*Your neck, pale white, is completely exposed. I can see the light blue veins criss-crossing underneath the surface of the skin.*
*Humans really are breakable, aren't they? Just like china dolls. How foolish, for your body to display the best spot for me to drive in my blade...*
*It's almost as though your body has given up. As though it wants you to die.*
*Maybe, on a subconscious level, you realize all the wrong you've done to me. You realize the hurt you've caused. And you're desperate to make amends.*
*Those light blue veins, standing out underneath your skin, are saying it. No, they're not just saying it. They're screaming it. My ears ring with the sound.*
*They're begging for forgiveness.*
*Ah...*
*It's all right, Atcchan. Don't worry. I don't want to hurt you.*
*I'll do it so quickly you won't even feel it. I'll do it so quickly you won't even have a chance to scream.*
*Gently, lovingly... I press the blade against your throat.*
*You wince a little, but you don't open your eyes. You don't wake up.*
Noelle: "I'm sorry..."
Noelle: "I really do like you, you know...?"
Noelle: "I like you... more than anyone else in the whole world."
*I mutter it softly, under my breath.*
*Then, I clench my fingers around the base of the blade...*
*And sink it deep into your neck.*
*I try to suppress my shivers as I walk along the darkened street.*
*My jacket doesn't do any good. Even when I jam my trembling hands deep down into my pockets as far as they can go, I don't feel any warmer.*
*How I can I ever hope to defeat this cold when most of it exists inside my own head?*
*I'm not trembling because of the weather. I'm trembling because I'm afraid.*
*This would be so much easier if Noelle were at home. Then I wouldn't have to walk as far.*
*However, when I called her house earlier, using my grandparents' ancient telephone, it was her mother who replied.*
*Noelle's mother, Sakata Lucy, has always frightened me a little. She always looks so serious - especially with her neatly ironed clothes and that pristine blond hair, tied up in a ponytail so tight it stretches the skin of her forehead.*
*Although I couldn't see Mrs. Sakata's face over the phone, her voice was enough to make me recall my fear of her from childhood. It rooted me to the spot, rendering me almost incapable of speech.*
*Added to this, it was quite late, so Mrs. Sakata sounded tired. She certainly wasn't in the mood for my stammering and stuttering; not when she plainly wanted to hang up as soon as possible.*
*As such, our conversation ended up being quite uncomfortable.*
*At least I was able to figure out where Noelle might be.*
*Mrs. Sakata didn't give me any real hints on where Noelle might be, but I think I already know.*
*She'll probably be at the same place she was yesterday.*
*The old park located by the school.*
*I need to hurry.*
*I feel tired when I finally arrive at the park. I think I walked here too quickly.*
*However, the minor aches and pains in my legs soon fade away from the forefront of my mind.*
*I have more important things to worry about.*
*I was right. She really is here - just like last night.*
*Noelle...*
*She's sitting on the swing, moving back and forth through the chilly night air.*
*Just as before, she's wearing that white dress. Her skirts billow around her legs like the petals of a lily.*
*Her pale fingers are coiled tightly around the metallic chains of the swingswet, white against silver. I'm taken aback by just how pale her skin is.*
*Her long hair drifts around her like a shroud, fluttering in the breeze.*
*She really does look like a ghost.*
*A spectral figure haunting the playground by night.*
*The slow, constant creaking of the old swing set only adds to the eerie atmosphere.*
*I watch her silently, eyes wide, frozen in place.*
*What can I do? What can I say?*
*It's been two years since I last spoke to her. Two years since I betrayed her.*
*I need to apologize. I need to tell her how I feel, but...*
*I can't.*
*My body... won't move...*
*It's while I'm standing here, deliberating, lost in my own thoughts... I hear it.*
*Or, rather... I don't hear it.*
*There's no sound to be heard.*
*The swing has stopped creaking.*
*Noelle turns to look at me, hands behind her back, head tilted to one side.*
*She's noticed me.*
*Before I can say a word, she starts to walk towards me.*
*Her expression is impassive. It shows no emotion. One wouldn't think it had been two years since we last saw each other.*
*One wouldn't think we'd ever even been friends at all.*
*I can't quite put my finger on it, but... her face...*
*There's something cold about it. She's wearing a strange, impersonal kind of expression that I've never seen before - almost like a mask.*
*Her light blue eyes seem hard... just like marbles.*
Noelle: "Hello."
Atcchan: "N-Noelle..."
*In my startled state, it's all I can manage to say.*
*Noelle surveys me coolly, her eyes narrowed.*
Noelle: "Yes. That is my name. I'm surprised you could remember."
Atcchan: "H-Huh...? W-What do you mean...?"

Amu: "So whaddaya say, Atcchan? D'you wanna come, do you, do you? It'll be really fun, I promise - just like old times!"

Grandpa: "You better do what Chiyo wants, lad. She can be scary sometimes..."

*It's so rare for Amu to do anything by half measures that her meek, shy appearance takes me by surprise.*
Atcchan: "A-Ah, um... Amu..."
Amu: "Y-Yes?"
Atcchan: "Why were you following us?"
Amu: "U-Um, well... Ehehe..."
*Amu stares down at the floor, her head hanging like a withered flower.*
Amu: "I-I was just in the general area, you know... A-And then I saw you two, and... Well..."
Amu: "I-It's just a coincidence, you know? T-That's all it is really! There's nothing strange about it!"
*But her forcefully specific denial makes everything seem even stranger. That, coupled with her guilty expression, only serves to deepen my suspicions.*
Atcchan: "Were you following us...?"
Amu: "Ahahaha... M-Me? Follow you? Of course not! Why would I do something like that?!"
Atcchan: "I don't know. You're the one who started it."
Amu: "I-I didn't start anything! I-I'm not so bored that I would devote my spare time to stalking you! L-Like I said, I was just in the area and, um-"
Atcchan: "You just so happened to be in the same area as Noelle and I... for about three hours?"
Amu: "Ahaha, yeah! I-It's funny how this stuff can happen, isn't it!"
Atcchan: "Amu..."
Amu: "H-Hey, don't look at me like that! Y-You're making it sound like I did something bad..."
Atcchan: "Following people around like that is bad!"
Amu: "Even if it's a cute girl like me?"
Atcchan: "That doesn't change a thing! I thought you were gonna abduct me or something!"
Amu: "Oh my... Ehehe~"
Amu: "Did I scare you, Atcchan~?"
Atcchan: "N-No, of course not! I-I wasn't scared! I-I'm just annoyed...!"
Amu: "Kukuku~ So you were scared after all?"
*I wish my face wasn't so red. Then my attempts at denial might sound more believable.*
Atcchan: "No I wasn't! I said I wasn't!"
Atcchan: "A-Anyway, don't try to change the subject! Being paranoid isn't a crime, but stalking somebody is!"
Atcchan: "You're the one who did something wrong, not me!"
Amu: "A-Ah, well... Um..."
*Amu quails under my accusation, tugging at the hem of her skirt. She looks like a child who's just been scolded.*
*Good. She deserves to feel guilty. Why was she following me, anyway?*
*Was it because she wanted to spy on my 'date' with Noelle? Maybe she was planning to play some kind of prank on us. That sounds like something Amu would do... but, even for her, this is a little too much.*
Amu: "Well, I... I..."
*And yet... even though I told myself I was going to be mad at her, and even though I have every right to be mad... I can't quite bring myself to be.*
*Looking at Amu's anxious expression, her eyes darting around as though seeking some kind of escape, her face unusually flustered... makes me feel bad.*
*I don't want to upset her, not really. She is one of my best friends.*
Atcchan: "Amu..."
Amu: "Y-Yes?!"
Atcchan: "Are you all right? You don't look so good."
Amu: "O-Oh. Are you worried about me Atcchan? Ehehe..."
*Amu giggles, but it lacks her usual energy. It falls flat in the most depressing way, like a small child tripping over on stage during a school play.*
Atcchan: "Yeah. I'm worried. I can't help but worry."
*Huh... Those words register in my brain with a heavy weight, making me blink. I'm sure I've said something like that before.*
*It's because I can't help being worried.*
*Isn't that what friendship is about?*
Atcchan: "But I still want to know. Why were you following me?"
Amu: "Ah, um... There was no real reason really, I just... Um..."
*Amu scratches her cheek with one finger, her gaze fixed at an indeterminate point just over my shoulder.*
*So she can't look me in the eye, huh? How suspicious...*
Amu: "I just... I have something I want to tell you, and... I got worried I wouldn't have the time."
Amu: "I got scared that I wouldn't be able to tell you... That I'd never be able to tell you. Ehehe..."
Atcchan: "Scared?"
*I can't imagine it. Not from Amu.*
Amu: "Y-Yeah... Just a little. I-It's... something I've wanted to say for a while, I guess..."
Atcchan: "Is it something important?"
Amu: "K-Kind of. I think it is, at least. But I, um... I don't want to say here it here, so... If it's not too much trouble, can we go somewhere else...?"
Atcchan: "A-Ah, well... I-If it's important, then..."
*I look at Noelle.*
*She's been hiding behind my back throughout my conversation with Amu, completely silent.*
*It's kind of odd that she was more comfortable with the idea of being followed by an (as-of-then) unknown stranger than being in the company of somebody she's known for seven years, but that's just Noelle.*
*She can be a strange person sometimes.*
*I feel a little bad cutting our time together short, especially as I know Noelle wanted to be alone with me, but...*
*I know I would feel even worse ignoring Amu during this time of need. I don't think I've ever seen her look so troubled before.*
Atcchan: "Noelle. I-Is it okay if I talk to Amu?"
Noelle: "Um... Well, I... I-I suppose, but..."
Noelle: "I thought... we were going on a date..."
*I wince. A sudden pang of guilt makes my chest ache.*
*'A date', huh...? Did we ever really clarify that?*
*Of all the places I thought Amu might take me, I certainly didn't expect it to be here. This place is so unlike Amu, so completely at odds with her character, that I can't help but feel surprised.*
*It's a reasonably large gardening store, popular with horticultural enthusiasts. My mother used to go here a lot.*
*In the front of the store they sell various bits and pieces gardening equipment, like shovels and trowels.*
*The back of the store is enclosed in a large greenhouse, where a wide variety of flowers, plants and herbs are kept in pots, ready to be bought and sold.*
*The air is warm and muggy, made even more oppressive by the large amount of plants that surround us.*
*Flies and mosquitoes hover about, droning and buzzing. I try to slap a few mosquitoes away from my arm, but my reflexes are too slow, and this act of self defense only results in several red, hand-shaped marks on my arm.*
*This place is kind of relaxing, though. There are so many flowers and plants it's kind of like being inside an artificial forest. The air is thick with the smell of vegetation, earth, and something that might be basil, I'm not sure.*
*Amu and I find a secluded place by a display of lilies and primroses, far away from the other customers, to talk.*
*Noelle decided to stay at the front of the store, examining some of the ceramic tanukis with mild interest.*
*Although Noelle doesn't get along with strangers, a soft-looking woman with strikingly dark skin approached her, noticing her interest in the tanukis, and engaged her in conversation. Oddly enough, Noelle seemed more than happy to reply to the woman.*
*I think Noelle thought the tanukis were cute, and she was happy somebody seemed to share her opinion.*
*I will never understand Noelle's notions of 'cute.' I shudder to think what the end result would be if she was ever asked to design a home.*
*How can somebody so good at drawing have such strange sensibilities?*
Atcchan: "So, um..."
Atcchan: "This is an unusual place to have a discussion, isn't it?"
Amu: "I suppose."
*Amu smiles faintly, but it doesn't look very convincing.*
*Silence reigns. This conversation is off to a good start.*
Atcchan: "I, um... I didn't know you liked flowers, Amu."
Amu: "I like them as much as anybody else, I guess. They're pretty."
*I try to joke around a little.*
Atcchan: "Even you like pretty things?"
Amu: "Heh. Of course.  I think everybody does, to a certain degree. Pretty things are relaxing."
Atcchan: "Yeah, that's true..."
*...*
*More silence. However, just before it gets awkward again, Amu starts to talk.*
Amu: "And anyway... it's kind of quiet back here. Not many people around. Which is good."
Atcchan: "I thought you liked people?"
Amu: "I do, but... there are some things people don't need to hear. Like, it... it would be embarrassing..."
Atcchan: "Embarrassing?"
*Amu smiles and shakes her head.*
Amu: "Even I can get embarrassed sometimes, you know? I'm only human."
Atcchan: "A-Aah, well... I-I know that, i-it's just-"
Amu: "Maybe it's easy to forget. Since I'm always doing my best. Like, badan, you know? Ehehe..."
Atcchan: "Hey... I know you're just a human. I think it's impressive that you try so hard, really."
Amu: "You do...?"
Atcchan: "Yeah. I think you're really amazing, Amu!"
Amu: "A-Au..."
*Amu's face turns light pink.*
*Flustered, she turns her head away, her fingers reaching up into her hair.*
*She coils a strand of her fluffy pink ponytail around one finger, winding it tighter and tighter.*
Amu: "But... You shouldn't say something like that."
Atcchan: "W-Why not? It's true. I-I really do think you're amazing!"
Amu: "No, I don't know. I don't live inside your head. I don't know how you think."
Atcchan: "B-But I'm telling the truth...!"
Amu: "I don't doubt that you're telling the truth, but... you have to be careful."
Amu: "Something like that... can get interpreted in a lot of different ways."
Atcchan: "What do you mean?"
*Uncoiling her hair from her finger, Amu lifts her head to look at me.*
*The light pink blush is still visible on her cheeks, but it's starting to fade away now, like make-up that's been worn for too long.*
Amu: "Geez. Y-You really are dense, aren't you?"
*Although she's still stammering, she sounds more composed than before. More self-assured.*
*More serious.*
Amu: "Atcchan... if you're not serious about your feelings, then you shouldn't compliment me too much. It's mean."
Atcchan: "Mean...? I-I wasn't trying to be mean..."
Atcchan: "You looked sad so I wanted to cheer you up. You haven't been acting like your usual self and-"
Amu: "I know. I know you're not a bad person, but..."
*Amu sighs.*
Amu: "You're not a bad person, but being with you makes me feel bad, okay? i-it upsets me, and I don't like being upset!"
Amu: "I'm supposed to keep smiling all the time, but when I'm with you that becomes a lot, lot harder!"
*I wince, taking a step backwards. I don't mean to. The intensity of Amu's words makes my feet move of my own accord.*
*My back hits a table behind me, making me wince. The display of primroses, pretty little flowers arranged neatly in rows, shakes from this sudden disturbance, their pots clinking together.*
Atcchan: "You don't like me...?"
Amu: "That isn't the problem! I do like you! I like you a lot! You're my best friend! I-It's just, it... I..."
*Amu's shoulders start to shake. Her eyes look suspiciously wet... like light green puddles.*
*Are those... tears...?*
Atcchan: "A-Amu! Amu, are you-"
*I reach forwards, meaning to pat her on the shoulder, offer her a tissue, give her a hug - do something, anything, I don't know.*
*Anything to stop her from crying.*
*But...*
Amu: "D-Don't touch me! Please don't touch me...!"
*Amu's voice makes me halt in my tracks, rooting me to the spot.*
*Even though the distance between us could be crossed by a single footstep... I've never felt so far away from her before.*
*How did this happen?  How did I hurt Amu so badly? I thought we were friends. We were childhood friends. I thought our bond would never be broken, no matter what.*
*Is this... all my fault...?*
Amu: "A-Atcchan, I... I-I really like you, you know...? I like you a lot."
Amu: "F-For such a long time now, I don't know how long... I've liked you so much. But... B-But..."
*A sniff, a shudder. Amu's eyes are rimmed with red.*
*Even though she's trying to hold back tears through sheer stubbornness, it isn't working.*
*They pool in her eyes and then spill over, dripping down her cheeks; hot and wet.*
Amu: "I like you, but you don't pay any attention to me at all! Y-You don't... You don't even seem to think about my feelings..."
Amu: "Maybe you don't even realize I have feelings."
Amu: "E-Even though I was so happy to see you again..."
Amu: "E-Even though I was so excited I couldn't sleep at all the night before you came here, so I ended up reading silly romance manga all night long..."
Amu: "Even though I felt like that, you didn't notice it at all! You didn't notice, and... A-And..."
Amu: "You spent the whole time... with her. T-Talking to her."
Amu: "Even when we were together... she was the only thing you could focus on! It's always ever, only, been about her!"
*Amu sniffs, wiping her eyes with the sleeve of blue sweater.*
*Her eyes are red and puffy. They must be sore. I wonder if wiping them was painful.*
*Maybe that's why she's wincing.*
*I...*
*I don't want to hurt her. I don't want to cause her pain. But... But...*
Atcchan: "I... I can't make myself feel the same way, you know...? I can't... make myself love you..."
*Amu sniffs, her head hanging like a broken puppet.*
Amu: "I... I know that. I'm not a child. I know I can't get what I want all the time by crying and stamping my feet. But..."
Amu: "It... I-It's so unfair..."
Atcchan: "I-I know. I'm sorry, but-"
Amu: "Y-You don't have to be sorry, silly. It isn't your fault. There isn't anything you can do about it."
Atcchan: "A-Amu, I-"
Amu: "If you don't like me, you don't like me. That's all there is to it."
Amu: "I-It's not something you can force... so you don't need to apologize. Not for how you feel."
Amu: "T-That... T-That would just be stupid."
Amu: "Although I can act quite childish, I'm not that immature, you know?"
Atcchan: "I... I'm aware of that. I wasn't trying to call you immature."
Amu: "Ehehe. It's good to know you have some faith in me, even though I was such a pain when I was little. But I've grown up since then."
Atcchan: "N-No, I-I didn't think you were a pain! Every day was a lot of fun!"
Amu: "It really was fun. I... had a good time being with you. So I'm a little sad..."
*I frown, my lower lip wobbling. Why is Amu making this sound so final?*
*We're best friends, right? Even though this is a little awkward, it... shouldn't ruin our friendship, should it?*
Atcchan: "Amu... You're making it sound like you won't see me again."
Amu: "Well, I... I do want to see you. Of course I do. But..."
Atcchan: "B-But...?"
*That small 'but', spoken softly, sets me on edge. Naturally, I start to worry.*
*Even though I always carry tissues around with me in my pocket, a habit that started solely so I had something on hand to clean up the various cuts Amu kept getting when she was younger...*
*I don't think they'll do much good now.*
*Although I was always hiding behind Amu's back as she protected me... in a way, I tried to protect her, too. But now...*
*What can I do?*
Amu: "I can't see you in the same way again. No matter how hard I try. I can't change how I feel, just like you can't change how you feel."
Atcchan: "Amu..."
Amu: "But... I don't think it's a bad thing."
Amu: "Although this may sound strange... I'm actually glad you told me how you feel, straight-out."
Amu: "It means I can stop hoping for something impossible. So I can stop trying."
Amu: "I think the most difficult thing in the world... is trying so, so hard to achieve something... that will never come true, no matter what you do."
Amu: "Ehehe..."
*Amu giggles. A small, tentative smile curves the corners of her lips upwards. Although it isn't as bright as her usual grins, it seems... there's something very warm and gentle about it.*
Atcchan: "Amu... You're all right...?"
Amu: "I'm all right. Really."
*Amu smiles at me, eyes wet, cheeks damp, her body trembling.*
*She looks almost like a young child, lost and confused... not at all like the strong, confident person I know so well, who always cheered me up when I was sad.*
*Who protected me from wild dogs when we went out for walks. Who won me that cute teddy bear at a local festival, with a wide smile on her face...*
*What was the bear's name again? Knowing Amu, it was something overly literal... Something like Ted, or... Teddy...?*
*I used to keep that bear in my room, on a shelf by my bed. It was a dear possession of mine. But, when I moved to the city, I lost it. I don't know where. I can't remember.*
*Amu is right. She's only human. Even the strongest person can be upset. Can despair. Can cry.*
*I wonder how many times she's been sad or scared or lonely... and never told me. How many times she's hidden her true feelings behind a wide smile.*
*She is a strong person... even now, with her red eyes and wet cheeks.*
*No, that isn't it. She isn't strong despite her sadness. She's stronger now because of it.*
*That she was able to tell me how she feels, even though it made her cry... shows just how courageous she really is.*
*Although her smile is small, it sparkles like a precious jewel.*
*Amu always shone... and I could only watch her in awe, wishing I could do the same. Wishing I could be like her.*
*Maybe that's why I can't bring myself to return her feelings. It's because I look up to her far too much... and so a wide gulf has opened up between us, formed from my own childhood insecurities.*
*I could never see myself as her equal. I always thought I was inferior. And so I decided... that I had no right to love her.*
*Even now, the distance between us... feels far too big...*
Amu: "Atcchan... Thank you..."
*With a small smile, Amu walks forwards...*
Atcchan: "A-Au..."
*-and gently, very gently...*
*... presses her lips against mine.*
*A goodbye kiss...?*
*I can hear my heart pounding. It feels so loud, so insistent, I'm surprised it hasn't burst out of my chest already.*
*I... I've never... been kissed before...*
*E-Even though I don't feel that way about Amu... Even though she's just a friend... Even though I was supposed to be going out with Noelle... This is still...*
*My first kiss...*
*I-Is that... really okay? Is it?*
*I don't know. I can't think.*
*Slowly, my eyelids fall shut. Everything goes black. All I can feel is the sensation of Amu's lips against mine.*
*It's soft and gentle and sweet, and it makes me feel lightheaded.*
*Amu...*
*Silently, inside my mind, I say the words I wish I could say out loud, but don't know how to.*
*I hope, even if she can't hear it... she can still understand.*
*I'm sorry. I didn't want to hurt you. I never wanted to hurt you. I'm sorry I'm such a idiot.*
*But... even though I don't love you... I would like it if we can still be friends. I always want to be your friend.*
*In a way, maybe it makes sense that my first kiss should be with Amu. So many of my first experiences have been with her, after all.*
*Amu is the first friend I ever made at school. She's the first friend I had a sleepover with. The first friend I went to a festival with.*
*She's also, embarrassingly enough... the first girl who gave me chocolates on Valentine's Day - though she told me, very sternly, it was only obligation chocolate. She even mixed one deadly chocolate in there, filled with chili powder.*
*Since she was five, Amu has given me chocolate every single Valentine's Day - though she remains firm in her assertions that it isn't because she likes me.*
*Now, I have to wonder...*
*Doesn't it make sense that she's the person I should have my first kiss with, too? It feels only natural. After all... she is my childhood friend.*
*She really does mean... so much to me... I...*
*I wish I had never hurt her so much. If only I had realized how much pain she was in earlier.*
*Then, maybe I could have made a difference. Maybe this could have been avoided.*
*But there's no sense in thinking 'what if?'*
*The two of us, Noelle and I, sit together on a park bench. It's the same park I went to with Amu a couple of days ago.*
*It's a nice place, secluded from the rest of the town by a thick row of trees.*
*There aren't many people, so it's fairly relaxing. I can hear birds twittering in the trees overhead and the very distant hum of cars.*
*The sky overhead is a warm, bright blue, like something from a watercolor painting.*
*It's a nice change from the dull, dreary, dark brown interior of that weird antiques store.*
*Being able to inhale large lungfuls of air without choking on dust mites feels like nothing short of a blessing.*
*If I wanted to be melodramatic about it, I could say I feel as though I've been born again!*
*The doll Noelle admired earlier is perched on her lap, enjoying the warm sunshine of this golden afternoon.*
*The doll's light blond hair shimmers under the sunlight. I think even that small frown on her face looks just a little more hopeful.*
*I wonder if the doll is relieved to have escaped, too?*
*Noelle seems preoccupied with rearranging the doll's bonnet.*
*She unties it, then sets to work tying it again, manipulating the small strip of yellow ribbon expertly with her slender fingers.*
*Watching her attend to this unnecessarily fiddly task, with such a look of intense concentration on her face, is soothing.*
Noelle: "Atcchan..."
Atcchan: "Hm?"
Noelle: "..."
Noelle: "Thank you for buying her for me."
Atcchan: "A-Ahaha... It's nothing, really."
*I say that chivalrously, even though it's a lie. That doll wasn't 'nothing.' It was the complete opposite of 'nothing.'*
*My poor wallet is so empty I wouldn't be surprised if its stomach started rumbling. Or whatever it is that wallets have in lieu of stomachs.*
*Pointing that out would be rude, though - and it's not like I mind too much.*
*So long as this gift makes Noelle happy, it's fine. It's not like there I was anything I wanted to buy for myself.*
Noelle: "I... appreciate it. And I..."
Noelle: "I think she is happy, too. She looks a lot more cheerful."
Atcchan: "I'm glad. Maybe she got depressed, being stuck inside for so long?"
Noelle: "Maybe. Perhaps I should ask her."
Atcchan: "Do you think you'd get a reply?"
Noelle: "Perhaps. If I'm very polite."
*However, the beautiful weather is marred by my own gloomy mood.*
*Tsuzumi's foul temper really was something else.*
*Although she told me such a ridiculous price when I inquired about the doll... the moment Noelle asked about it, Tsuzumi became a lot more cooperative.*
*She even knocked a couple of zeros off the end of the price tag so Noelle could buy it with her own money.*
*This proves it. I must have done something to upset Tsuzumi - although I can't think what that might be. I hardly even know her.*
*Why does she dislike me so much? Is it just because I'm a man? Or is there some other reason...?*
*I want to know, and yet... at the same time, I don't. It's kind of scary...*
*That woman at the store... she really was something else...*
*Even though she told me such a ridiculous price when I asked about that doll... when Noelle asked if she could buy it, she instantly relented.*
*She even dropped a couple of zeroes off the end of the price tag as if it were nothing, smiling the whole time.*
*And so Noelle bought that doll for herself, with her own money.*
*It was egotistical to think Noelle was relying on me.*
*Why would she, anyway? It's not like I'm a particularly 'princely' or dependable figure. I've never read a single fairy tale or romance novel that features a male protagonist quite like me, with lots of freckles and no height.*
*I'm not cut out for the life of a valiant knight at all. If anything, I'm the one who needs to be protected and taken care of by Noelle.*
*Noelle looks at me with concern, her hair falling over her shoulders.*
Noelle: "I hope the woman at the shop didn't upset you too much, Atcchan."
Atcchan: "Ah, no... It's okay. I'll get by."
Noelle: "That's good. It looked like you were in tears earlier, so I'm relieved."
Atcchan: "I-I... I-I wasn't in tears...! I just had something in my eye."
Noelle: "If you say so. I was worried that maybe you were feeling bad because you were unable to purchase the doll yourself, even though you said you would."
Noelle: "I thought you might be embarrassed."
Atcchan: "G-Gyaah..."
Noelle: "But maybe I was imagining it."
*Haaa... Noelle really is sharp. Despite the daydreamy look that often steals across her countenance, she's often spot-on with observations like that.*
Atcchan: "Ah... Maybe, just a little. I didn't want to let you down."
Noelle: "It's all right. I was able to get what I wanted in the end, so there's no harm done."
Noelle: "Your performance earlier was funny, too~ I think it really cheered my new friend up. Right?"
*Noelle gestures towards her doll, a soft smile on her face.*
*Her delicacy in handling my wounded ego... isn't something to be scoffed at.*
*Noelle... R-Really is a nice person, i-isn't she?*
*Sometimes I feel like I'm not worthy of her...*
Atcchan: "E-Ehehe... Yeah, I guess. I'm glad you were able to rescue her."
Noelle: "Me, too."
Atcchan: "Have you thought of giving her a name...?"
Noelle: "Hm..."
*Noelle stops, pausing for thought.*
*One would've thought I'd asked her a complicated mathematical quandary, judging by her expression.*
*Is it really that difficult to answer?*
Noelle: "No. Not yet. Names are special things. They create meanings, after all."
Atcchan: "I suppose so. Since nobody ever calls me by my real name, it makes me feel kind of insignificant sometimes. Like nobody cares."
Noelle: "I think Atcchan is a cute name. It suits you."
Atcchan: "But it's not my real name. It's a diminutive."
Noelle: "Ehehe."
Noelle: "You're a diminutive sort of person, Atcchan."
Atcchan: "Somehow, I don't feel like that's a compliment..."
Noelle: "..."
Noelle: "Names really are important, though. They change how people perceive the world. Not just names, but words."
Atcchan: "Huh? What do you mean?"
Noelle: "I mean... For instance..."
Noelle: "Is this doll an antique, or is she old?"
Atcchan: "I don't know. Both are probably true. Aren't antiques meant to be old?"
*I have my doubts about just how much this doll is actually worth, though.*
Noelle: "That's right. They are both true. But they both exist at the same time."
Noelle: "How people perceive the worth of this doll will change depending on which word is used, but both words are true."
Atcchan: "So... Words shape reality?"
Noelle: "Something like that. It's complicated."
Noelle: "That's why names are not to be taken lightly. Names give meaning. They contain the wishes of the parents."
Atcchan: "You mean, how parents want their children to be viewed... or what they want their children to become?"
*Noelle nods her head.*
Atcchan: "I see... I think I get it."
Atcchan: "I remember, back when I was younger... at school, we were set a homework question. We had to ask our parents about the meanings behind our names, and why they chose them."
Noelle: "I was given a similar task at my old school, too."
Atcchan: "My parents said my name means 'hard-working.'"
Noelle: "Mine means 'Christmas' in French."
Atcchan: "Really...? I didn't know that."
Noelle: "I don't know how many people do."
Atcchan: "You were born near Christmas as well, weren't you?"
Noelle: "Mm. On December 17th."
*Noelle frowns. She looks pensive.*
Noelle: "... You have to be careful with names. If you give your child an unfortunate name... you may, inadvertently, give them an unfortunate life."
Atcchan: "Huh...? Is that how it is...?"
*She nods her head.*
Atcchan: "That sounds kind of bleak..."
Noelle: "The world is bleak. People judge others based on appearances and first impressions. If you have an unusual name, then..."
*Noelle's voice trails off.*
*Her hands, holding her doll on her lap, are trembling.*
Atcchan: "Hey... Are you okay?"
Noelle: "..."
*Noelle opens her mouth but no words come out.*
*She looks frustrated. Maybe it's because she can't find the words. I don't know.*
*Noelle soon gives up on the idea of verbal communication. Instead, she settles for something simpler. She shakes her head.*
*Even I can understand that.*
Atcchan: "Do you want to talk about it?"

Atcchan: "I had... no idea... people could be so cruel..."
