Atcchan: "Maybe it was. It made me smile, at least."
Noelle: "See?! You are laughing at me!"
Atcchan: "Not at you, exactly..."
Noelle: "You are. You are laughing at me. Meanie."
*Noelle gives me a sour glance... before, with a soft 'hmph', she turns her head away, her hair hitting me in the face as she does so.*
*And yet, despite this...*
*I think she's smiling. Maybe. Just a little.*
*But a little is good enough for me.*
*Right now... it's more than enough.*
Noelle: "Ooh... Jello..."
*Noelle stares at the shelf before her with sparkly eyes, her face flushed with happiness.*
*These jello snacks have an odd effect on Noelle.*
*Simply seeing them in their plastic packaging, stacked neatly on the shelves of a convenience store, can reduce her to this strangely excitable, child-like state.*
*That's the power of our consumerist society.*
*Um, maybe...?*
Atcchan: "Sure. I'll buy you some if you want. That's why we're here, after all."
Noelle: "Ooh... Really, really?"
Atcchan: "Yes. I can even buy you more than one."
*Noelle suddenly straightens up, clasping her doll to her chest even tighter. She has a serious expression on her face, her mouth drawn into a line.*
Noelle: "No, no, Atcchan, that's no good. If you buy me too much jello, it will make the experience seem less special."
Atcchan: "Is that how it works?"
Noelle: "Indeed. I believe I've already told you about this."
Noelle: "Food of this caliber is something to be savored, eaten slowly over a long period of time. You need to let it linger on your tongue."
Atcchan: "I... see..."
Noelle: "Moreover, if I were to try several different kinds of jello, I would need to have something to drink in between to refresh my palate."
Atcchan: "Is that how it is...?"
*Noelle nods her head.*
Noelle: "Yes, it is. Each flavor of jello is important. Very important. They need to be treated with respect."
Atcchan: "I could buy you some bottled water as well, if you want. Is that cleansing enough?"
Noelle: "No, no, no. That's just no good. Are you even using your head?"
Atcchan: "I... I'm sorry...?"
*All of a sudden, I feel like a novice chef on a cookery program, being scolded by an angry senior...*
Noelle: "Bottled water is not worthy of being consumed alongside this jello. It's cheap water."
*I eye the cooling cabinet which contains the drinks. The spring water sure doesn't look cheap, judging by that price tag...*
*It's fine that Noelle loves jello so much - really, it is. But her love is blinding her to the truth...!*
Atcchan: "But that water is even more expensive than the jello itself..."
*Noelle waves her hand in a dismissive motion.*
Noelle: "That doesn't mean anything. The water still can't compare. This only proves how ignorant the masses are when it comes to the worth of this jello."
*It must be nice being this enthusiastic about something.*
*Even if it is only jello.*
*If I said that, though... Noelle might kick me.*
Atcchan: "A-Ahaha... Okay, I get it. The jello really is amazing."
Noelle: "Yes, it is."
Atcchan: "I'll buy you one, then. Just one."
Noelle: "That is for the best. If I ate too many delicious things, I might die."
Atcchan: "Y-You won't die, will you?"
Noelle: "It's always a possibility."
Atcchan: "T-Then I'll try to treat the jello with the respect it deserves..."
*Noelle turns back to the display of jello, a small smile on her face. It's an expression of pure bliss.*
*Her eyes scan the various pots of jello. Sometimes she picks one up and reads the back of the pot... but, with a heavy sigh, she returns it back to the shelf.*
*As I watch her repeat this routine once, twice, many, many times, my eyes naturally start drifting towards the clock hanging at the back of the store.*
*A minute passes. Then five. Then ten.*
*We're probably going to be here for a while.*
*Noelle and I walk back home companionably under the darkening evening sky.*
*The air is cooler than it was this morning; much more crisp. The wind feels a little stronger, too.*
*I can hear the sounds of the cicadas chirping in the surrounding trees. They're all around us, yet I can't see them - hidden from sight.*
*It makes me feel exposed, somehow... as though a vast, invisible audience is watching me.*
Noelle: "Atcchan... thank you."
Atcchan: "Ahaha... Hey, now... what are you thanking me for?"
Noelle: "...... For buying me the jello. It was truly delicious."
Atcchan: "It was really that good?"
Noelle: "Yes, it was. I haven't had jello that good in a while."
Atcchan: "Was it any different from usual?"
Noelle: "A little."
Atcchan: "Did they change the recipe?"
Noelle: "No. The recipe was the same as ever. I looked at the list of ingredients."
Atcchan: "Why did it taste so good, then?"
Noelle: "I don't know. Maybe it is because..."
Atcchan: "Because...?"
Noelle: "I am not entirely sure."
*I feign surprise, taking a step back in supposed alarm.*
Atcchan: "Even the great jello connoisseur herself doesn't know? Truly mysterious!"
*Noelle, however, doesn't react. Instead, she simply nods her head, lost in her own thoughts.*
Noelle: "It is indeed."
Atcchan: "Do you think we should call Sherlock Holmes?"
Noelle: "No. Don't be foolish. He's a fictional character."
Atcchan: "A-Ah... I... I know that..."
Noelle: "Then why did you suggest it?"
*My shoulders sag under the weight of Noelle's serious stare.*
*Even though she says such strange things herself, her logic is as sound as ever.*
*Talking to Noelle sometimes feels like playing a board game. A board game with illogical rules that haven't been explained beforehand, where every single throw of the dice is loaded.*
*If it's with her, I really can't win.*
*Then again... Relationships aren't about winning or losing, are they? That's a skewed way of looking at things.*
*I think it's about having fun - and being with Noelle always makes me smile.*
Atcchan: "I-I wasn't being serious. I was just joking..."
Noelle: "... Oh."
*...*
*...*
Noelle: "I think... maybe..."
*Noelle looks up at me from beneath her eyelashes. I wonder whether it's my imagination or not, but...*
*It looks almost like she's blushing... ever so slightly.*
Noelle: "Maybe it tasted better... because I was with you."
Atcchan: "U-Uu... W-Well, I um..."
Atcchan: "T-Thank you..."
Noelle: "It's no problem."
*We walk together for a while in silence, our fingers brushing, shoulders bumping.*
*The sounds from our separate footsteps mingle together. Our shadows stretching out across the road seem to merge.*
*The thought is almost comforting.*
*Even though I have to return home soon... I would like to believe, at least for a short while... I was able to understand Noelle.*
*The sky above us is steely blue. The sun, which was so bright earlier, has sunk underneath a cover of dark clouds, making our surroundings muted and grey.*
*It's a little sad. It seems like fairly depressing weather, given I'm going to say farewell soon.*
*It would've been nice to remember my final day here with more sunshine...*
*Ah...*
*The second pair of footsteps. They've stopped.*
*Is there something wrong with Noelle?*
*I come to a halt, turning my head to look behind me.*
*Noelle is standing at the side of the road, unmoving, gripping her doll tightly to her chest.*
*Her light blue eyes are staring, distant. They look almost as murky as the afternoon sky.*
*Doubling back on myself, I make my way towards her.*
Atcchan: "Noelle? Are you all right?"
Noelle: "I'm all right. Just thinking."
Atcchan: "About what?"
Noelle: "I'm not sure."
Atcchan: "You don't know what you're thinking?"
Noelle: "Well, I do, but... it's complicated. Maybe it doesn't mean very much. I just had a fancy. Or a whim. Maybe."
*She's making her thought process sound incredibly airy and insubstantial, like chiffon cake.*
*I'm sure it's something far heavier, though. Otherwise, her expression wouldn't look so unsure.*
*After a brief pause, Noelle eventually elaborates.*
Noelle: "Let's make a detour. I want to take a more scenic route."
*She speaks in the imperative, most unlike her. She isn't usually so straightforward.*
*Perhaps it is this out of character assertiveness that makes me nod my head in agreement, without question.*
*Noelle leads me to a large field, located just on the outskirts of our village.*
*I see a vast array of tall, yellow flowers spread out before me; their large circular heads repeating over and over, as far as the eye can see, in endless rows.*
*I know a lot of people think sunflowers look pretty, but I've always found them strangely eerie - especially when clustered together like this.*
*En masse, they look like a large display of vast, unblinking eyes, staring right through me.*
*The colors, too, are unsettling. I think the bright yellow is too garish, far too bright to be becoming. It feels forced, unnatural... almost ugly.*
*These flowers disturbed me so much when I was younger that I tried to avoid coming here at all costs.*
*I shudder, eyeing the flowers with unease.*
*Even though I'm older now, and more sensible (hopefully), it still feels like they're staring at me.*
Atcchan: "Why sunflowers...?"
Noelle: "I think they're inspiring."
Atcchan: "Inspiring...?"
*Noelle nods.*
Noelle: "Even though they're only flowers... they're able to grow so tall."
*I don't feel much like complimenting the sunflowers, since I find them so unpleasant. But still... despite my stubbornness, I have to concede on that point.*
Atcchan: "I suppose that is impressive. I don't like them very much, though."
Noelle: "No?"
Atcchan: "No."
*A small smile rises to Noelle's face.*
Noelle: "That's just because you're jealous."
Atcchan: "J-Jealous...? W-What do you mean...?"
Noelle: "That they're taller than you."
Atcchan: "W-What...?"
*My face goes light pink. I fold my arms, scowling, wanting to prove Noelle wrong.*
Atcchan: "T-That isn't the reason. They're not taller than me, anyway!"
Noelle: "Maybe not yet. Give them time."
Atcchan: "I-I'm really not jealous, you know? I just think they look creepy."
Noelle: "Creepy how?"
Atcchan: "I... I don't know. It's just like... like they're too big and too yellow, or something. Like... they're trying too hard."
Noelle: "Is it wrong to try?"
Atcchan: "I... I don't think so. But these flowers... They look kind of unnatural somehow..."
Noelle: "Maybe."
*Noelle gives a small nod, a slight inclination of her head.*
*It takes her a few moments before she replies.*
Noelle: "I thought... if I could see these flowers that try so hard... it would give me some courage."
Atcchan: "Courage...?"
Noelle: "... Yes. I need more. Lots, lots more."
Atcchan: "I think you're already pretty courageous."
Noelle: "No, I'm not."
*Noelle looks out towards the sunflowers as she speaks.*
*In stark contrast to the grandeur of these large flowers, swaying back and forth in the wind... Noelle's voice sounds incredibly soft. Almost as though it could fade away altogether.*
*These sunflowers are different.*
*They seem so permanent in their gaudy bright yellow, their roots planted deep down into the soil with the strength of iron.*
*Together, they form a united front, an army. A whole squadron of sunflowers, casting long shadows under the setting sun.*
*I think I understand what Noelle means.*
*These sunflowers possess a certain kind of strength which I've never appreciated before.*
*I wonder... is that why people like them?*
Noelle: "I... am a weak person. I find it hard to speak my mind. The words I want to communicate get lost... and nothing comes out."
Noelle: "I don't know how to express myself and... I don't want to burden others with pointless words, so... I don't say anything."
Noelle: "I try to keep everything inside, but... over time, it just builds and builds and builds, like snow - or trash, maybe."
Noelle: "A large pile of trash. And I have no way to shift it."
*A sigh.*
Noelle: "It's because I don't trust others. I don't... let them in. I don't let them help. And so... I'm weak..."
Atcchan: "Noelle..."
Noelle: "But... Today I decided. I won't give up. Even if it is difficult, I... will keep trying. I will do my best."
Noelle: "Like the sunflowers. I must grow upwards, not inwards."
*Noelle looks at me resolutely, her eyes narrowed with determination.*
Noelle: "I want to tell you everything."
*The wind blows through the sunflowers and makes them rustle, as though with suppressed excitement.*
*Are they listening? Can they hear?*
*They can certainly see us.*
*An audience of disembodied eyes framed with yellow petals.*
Noelle: "I am going to be moving soon. Moving to England."
*I stare at Noelle, my mouth wide open in shock.*
*England?*
*W-What's this about England...?*
*I knew she was moving, but... I had no idea it would be so far away.*
*I had assumed, naïvely, that she'd be moving somewhere close by; to a large city, maybe, but definitely one still in Japan.*
*I hadn't even considered the possibility that she might be relocating anywhere as strange, as alien, as completely incomprehensible and unknown as England.*
*She might as well have said she was flying to Mars. We'd have about the same likelihood of seeing each other again in that scenario.*
*Noelle watches me passively, holding her doll tightly to her chest.*
*Her voice is calm when she next speaks, but... I can see her fingers are shaking, just slightly.*
*Even so... She stands firm.*
*Perhaps she's trying to draw some strength from those sunflowers.*
Noelle: "You look surprised."
Atcchan: "Ah... I-I... Um..."
*I can't reply. I can only respond in random syllables, mixed bits of sound.*
Atcchan: "I-I... England...? Really?"
Noelle: "Yes. England. Really."
Noelle: "Rain. Strawberry jam and scones. Earl grey tea. England."
Atcchan: "That England...?"
Noelle: "Is there any other England?"
*It's a fair question, I guess.*
Atcchan: "But I... I had no idea..."
Noelle: "I know. I'm sorry I didn't tell you."
Atcchan: "A-Ah, no, it... It's okay..."
*By this point, I'm starting to regain my composure. My mind has recovered, slightly, from this revelation.*
*It still doesn't feel real, though. It's hard for me to warp my head around it.*
*I don't know anything about England. I hardly even know any English, apart from a few stock phrases; 'Hello.' and 'How are you?' and 'I can't speak English.'*
*It doesn't make sense.*
*How could Noelle, my dearest friend, be moving somewhere so far away?*
*England is a completely uncharted land in my mind, just like the bottom of the sea.*
*But... even though it's shocking, I can understand it.*
*I can understand why she wouldn't want to tell me... and I can hardly fault Noelle for it.*
Atcchan: "I didn't tell you that I was moving, either... So it's only fair... that you didn't want to tell me."
*However... my reaction is not one of abject surprise, as Noelle might have been expecting.*
*I nod my head in resignation.*
*So it's true.*
*I'd already heard from Noelle's mother, but... at the time, it hadn't really felt real.*
*It's only now, hearing those words from Noelle herself, that I'm able to recognize it as the truth.*
Noelle: "You don't look very shocked, Atcchan."
Atcchan: "A-Ah... I'm sorry. Is my face all wrong?"
Noelle: "It's all right. No matter what expression you pull, I like your face."
Atcchan: "E-Ehehe... Thanks..."
Atcchan: "But... I think acting more surprised would be a lie. You see... I already knew."
Noelle: "You did? I'm impressed. What kind of detective work did you have to carry out?"
Atcchan: "It was nothing as underhanded as that. I wasn't investigating you behind your back or anything. I just asked your mother."
Noelle: "Is that so?"
Atcchan: "Yeah. I went over to see you. You weren't there, but your mother was. She gave me a cup of tea and told me."
Noelle: "I see."
Noelle: "I'm sorry I didn't tell you myself, until now."
Atcchan: "N-No, it's all right. You don't need to apologize. I didn't want to tell you that I was moving, after all. It's understandable..."
Noelle: "..."
Noelle: "I didn't want to talk about it. Not with you. It's all my family has been able to talk about for the past few months."
Atcchan: "It sounds stressful."
Noelle: "It is. All this endless talk about moving companies and property hunting and selling our home..."
Atcchan: "My parents were like that when we were moving, too. They argued a lot at that time."
Noelle: "There are so many forms, so much paperwork. A lot of official documents piled up on my mother's desk. The pile gets higher and higher every day."
Noelle: "And so she becomes more and more stressed."
*Thinking back on it, Mrs. Sakata did seem rather tired when I saw her yesterday.*
*Although she'd been attired as primly as usual, her hair tied back with not a strand out of place, her eyes were half-lidded and carved with dark, grey bags.*
Noelle: "That isn't the only scary thing, though."
*Noelle pauses.*
*Standing against a backdrop of bright yellow sunflowers, under the gently dying sunlight... Noelle looks strangely ghostly.*
*Her dress, once pure white, now dirty grey, flutters around her legs.*
*Behind her, the sunflowers continue their dance, caught in the breeze.*
*It sounds as though they're mumbling amongst themselves, having a private discussion nobody else can understand.*
Noelle: "Moving to England... really is frightening."
*I can imagine.*
Noelle: "I can't speak English. I don't understand the language. And I'll stand out. I look... strange..."
Atcchan: "I don't think you look strange."
Noelle: "Because you're used to me. But other people won't be."
Noelle: "When I think about communicating with strangers in a completely unfamiliar country, far away from home..."
Noelle: "I don't know what to do..."
Noelle: "I-I've been having bad dreams about it... Nightmares. Lots of them."
*Noelle bites her lower lip. Her body is trembling from tip to toe.*
*She looks as though she's standing in the middle of a Siberian winter, not before a vast field of sunflowers, butter yellow, under a darkening sky.*
*When she trembles like that... she looks so frail, so fragile...*
*She seems even more delicate than the doll in her arms.*
*She doesn't often talk for such long periods of time. Yesterday, in the woods, was an exception. And today, too...*
*During the short amount of time I've spent back home... I've seen many different sides of Noelle.*
*Many sides I didn't even realize existed.*
*It's like looking at a painting from a different angle and noticing the little details you never saw the first time around.*
*Or, maybe... it's like digging for buried treasure and uncovering the dusty bones of dinosaurs, bit by bit, with a fine-bristled brush?*
*But, in actuality... it's something far more precious and important than all of that.*
*It's about spending time with an old friend... and beginning to understand how deep and complex their mind really is.*
*It's about becoming closer to somebody... and learning more and more about them.*
*It's about human relationships... and deepening your bonds.*
*And I don't think there's anything more worthwhile in this world than that.*
Noelle: "And yet... I am going to try..."
*Noelle's words are softly spoken but quietly hopeful. She sounds optimistic, unusually so - different from the Noelle I saw yesterday with tears dripping down her cheeks.*
Noelle: "I have become tired. Tired of being worried. It doesn't get me anywhere and it doesn't change anything."
Noelle: "Even though this is something I can't change... I can, at least, try to make the best of it."
Noelle: "I don't want to be scared. It's painful and... it hurts my chest. So I want to stop that. I want to stop being scared."
*Like a sunflower, Noelle stands tall and proud. Although she isn't painted the same yellow color... her words hold that kind of quality.*
*That self-confidence - unsure, yes, but still stubbornly unfaltering - is, surely, the same color as those sunflowers.*
*A bright, glorious yellow.*
Atcchan: "But... is that really okay?"
Noelle: "What do you mean?"
Atcchan: "Is it really so easy to just stop being scared? Maybe it's something you can't help."
Noelle: "Maybe. Of course, there will be times when I want to give up. Times when it feels like it's all too much. But..."
Noelle: "Because I have you by my side... Because you continued to care for me, all of this time... I realized something important."
*I look at my feet, my face light red.*
Atcchan: "I... I don't deserve that kind of praise. I mean, I did abandon you for the last two years..."
Noelle: "I know. And it hurt. But... I was able to survive. It did not kill me."
Noelle: "I'll be fine on my own. "
*A small smile.*
Noelle: "And now I know... This whole time... you were still worried about me. You still considered me a friend. And that... is more than enough."
Noelle: "Knowing that there are people like you in this world comforts me."
Noelle: "Even though you still make mistakes, and even though you're not perfect... I don't mind. No person is."
Noelle: "The fact that you exist... gives me enough strength to go on, I think. Even if that sounds silly... I don't know. I think it's a little silly."
*Noelle laughs softly.*
Noelle: "But... I have decided... Like these sunflowers, I want to try my best. Although I am small... I will keep on growing."
*And when she smiles... her whole face glows... just like a sunflower.*
*That single smile is so beautiful it almost takes my breath away.*
Amu: "Atcchaa~aan! Welcome home!"
Atcchan: "K-Kyaaa!"
*A pair of arms suddenly clamp around my middle, hard, making me gasp for breath.*
*Of course, it's Amu.*
Atcchan: "A-Amu... I can't breathe..."
Amu: "Oops~ Ehehe~ Sorry~ "
*Her voice light and lilting, cheerfully sing-song - a sharp contrast to her iron grip - Amu draws away from me, grinning.*
Atcchan: "Why are you here, anyway? This isn't your house."
Amu: "I know. I just got bored waiting for you to come back. So I came here~ Your grandmother is a really good cook, by the way!"
Grandma: "Hello, dear~"
*My grandmother is kneeling at the table in the dining room. She greets me with a wave.*
*There's an empty bowl on the table, a set of chopsticks discarded hurriedly alongside.*
*When I turn to inspect Amu, I note there are a few stray grains of rice stuck to her cheeks.*
Atcchan: "Have you been helping yourself to my grandmother's food?"
Amu: "Who, me? No! No no no no! It was offered to me. I didn't steal it or demand it!"
Grandma: "It's true. I like to see a young girl with a healthy appetite. It makes me feel glad, as though my hard work has been appreciated~ Hohohoh~"
Amu: "That's right. I can't stand brats who don't eat every single morsel of a meal. It's such a waste."
Grandma: "I know, I know. It is distressing for an old woman like me, too. Children today don't understand the worth of a simple, square meal."
*And so the two of them start to complain, just like old women.*
*... Well, I guess my grandmother really is an old woman, but Amu sure isn't. Why does she sound so passionate, anyway?*
*And does she really have the right to gripe about 'the youth of today' when she's one of those 'youths' herself?*
*I wince, shifting uncomfortably on the spot.*
*Although my grandmother sounds content enough... it feels like these barbed comments are being aimed at me.*
*Is she holding a grudge...? Or am I just being paranoid?*
*Noelle stands by my side, shielding her body behind my back.*
*Is she trying to hide from Amu...?*
*Nevertheless... Noelle made that resolution, didn't she? She said it herself. She was going to grow just like a sunflower, lifting her head towards the sky.*
*And that's just what she does.*
*Taking a deep breath, trying to steady the shaking of her body... she peeps her head out from behind me, and mutters a small hello.*
Noelle: "I-It... I-It's nice to see you again, A-Amu..."
Amu: "Hoh?"
*Amu looks a little surprised, her eyes widening.*
*I guess she didn't expect to be addressed by Noelle - not when Noelle often goes to such great lengths to avoid conversation with others.*
*I don't know if she's ever spoken a full sentence to Amu before.*
*It doesn't take Amu long to adjust to this unexpected occasion, though.*
Amu: "Yeah! It's nice to see you, too. How have you been?"
Noelle: "I-I... um... I am all right... Thank you for asking."
Amu: "That's good! Atcchan said you were feeling kind of down, maybe, so I was worried."
Noelle: "Ah... Y-You were... worried about me...?"
Amu: "Of course! Any friend of Atcchan's is a friend of mine!"
*Amu says it so naturally, with such a good-natured smile, it's almost impossible not to be taken in by her charms.*
*I have to admire her. Her boundless energy really is inspiring.*
Noelle: "B-But I... W-We haven't really spoken, so..."
Amu: "Then we'll have to make sure we talk more! It's no problem! And, speaking of which..."
*Amu looks down at the doll in Noelle's arms.*
Amu: "Who's this? She's cute!"
Noelle: "S-She's, um... I... I decided to name her... Himawari..."
Amu: "Himawari? Like, 'sunflower?'"
Noelle: "Y-Yes... That's right."
*Amu grins.*
Amu: "Ooh, I see. Because of her golden hair? How cute~"
Noelle: "B-But, um... Is this... really okay...?"
Amu: "Huh? Is what okay?"
Noelle: "Y-You... talking to me...?"
Amu: "Why wouldn't it be? I'm talking to you because I want to talk to you, aren't I?"
Noelle: "I-I, well... um... I thought, maybe..."
Noelle: "..."
Noelle: "I thought, maybe... you did not like me."
Amu: "And why shouldn't I like you? I don't have any reason not to."
Noelle: "Well..."
Amu: "I may seem like a strange person, but even I have some common sense! Why should I dislike somebody as cute as you?"
Noelle: "C-Cute...? I... Well, um, I..."
*Noelle looks flustered. It takes her a short while to regain her composure.*
Noelle: "I-It's just, I... I haven't spoken to you very much in the past, and... maybe it looked rude...?"
Noelle: "Maybe you thought I was bad... because I don't talk. Or aloof. I was worried about it..."
Amu: "Hey. You don't need to worry. I know I can be a difficult person sometimes. Atcchan tells me that aaa~ll the time."
Atcchan: "Because it's true."
Amu: "Kukuku~ You jerk, go die. "
Atcchan: "H-Hey! Don't say something that awful with a smile!"
Amu: "Sorry Atcchan, that's one of my charm points~"
Atcchan: "T-That isn't a 'charm point!' It's the exact opposite of a 'charm point!'"
Grandma: "I think Amu is very charming."
Amu: "That's right. Do you hear that, Atcchan? I'm charming!"
*I give my grandmother a half-lidded glare. She merely smiles in response, like a benevolent old tortoise, as though nothing at all is amiss.*
*I feel like I've been betrayed. Betrayed by my own grandmother. All because I didn't eat enough of her food.*
*This is, indeed, a cruel world.*
Amu: "So, so, Atcchan!"
*As Amu says this, she pats (more like slaps) my back, hard.*
Atcchan: "O-Ow..."
*Amu doesn't need to eat any more of my grandmother's 'rejuvenating' homemade food... She has enough boar-like strength as it is!*
Amu: "I'm curious, I'm curious~ How was your date?"
*D-Date...? I-Is Amu still calling it that...?*
Atcchan: "I-I... A-Ah, um, well... It wasn't really, um..."
*I open and close my mouth, but I'm only able to come out with garbled noises and half-formed syllables.*
*I don't even have a chance to elaborate further because my grandmother cuts me off.*
Grandma: "Ah, yes. I am also curious about my cute grandson's love life. How was it, dear? Did you remember to wear clean underwear?"
*And what does that have to do with anything...?!*
Grandpa: "A date?!"
*Now this is just getting ridiculous. Where did he come from, anyway...?!*
Grandma: "Our grandson went out on a date, dear. His nice friend, Amu, told me."
Amu: "That's right, I did~ It's the truth, 100%%~ That's why they call me 'Reliable Amu!'"
Atcchan: "N-Nobody calls you that...!"
Amu: "They do~ I just called myself it~ "
Atcchan: "That doesn't count!"
Amu: "Why not? I'm allowed to have an opinion, too!"
*This girl... She really is impossible...*

*I stand on the platform underneath the evening sky.*
*Everything looks dark, dull, and murky. My surroundings have lost their color. Even Amu's hair looks strangely grey; less pink than usual.*

Atcchan: "H-Hey, I... I..."

*But there's one more thing I need to say before I go. Just one...*
Atcchan: "Noelle..."
Noelle: "Yes?"
*Noelle looks up at me, eyes wide, staring. She's holding Himawari to her chest, clutching her tightly.*
*Noelle will be fine. I'm sure she'll be fine, no matter where life takes her or what happens in the future.*

*Even if we're not together, we'll always be friends.*

Atcchan: "I'm going to eat a lot of breakfast every morning, and I'm going to drink a glass of milk after every meal, and I'll ride my bike a whole lot!"
