Atcchan: "U-Um... I... I-I wonder... Why is the new girl boring...?"
Amu: "Because she is! Really, really boring!"
Atcchan: "Au... Maybe that's a little mean..."
Amu: "It isn't mean if it's true!"
Atcchan: "It's just your opinion..."
Amu: "My opinion is the truth, then!"
Atcchan: "W-Well, I... I don't know..."
Amu: "I do."
Amu: "I was so excited about having a new classmate, but... this is a total disappointment!"
Amu: "It's like we haven't got a new classmate at all. She's so quiet you wouldn't even know she's here!"
Amu: "I wanted to ask her lots of stuff about the city. About the big buildings and the fast cars and the large stores and the food and the people and... everything!"
Amu: "I wanna know everything! But she won't tell me anything."
Amu: "She doesn't act like a person from the city should. Not at all!"
Atcchan: "I... I don't think the new girl is so bad. She hasn't done anything wrong..."
Amu: "But she keeps ignoring me! No matter how hard I try, and no matter what I do, she won't even look me in the eye!"
*Amu's grip on the swing set grows even tighter. She kicks her legs back and forth, hard, the motions becoming more powerful, more violent.*
*The creaking of the swing swells, growing louder and louder. It sounds menacing.*
*Amu's words... are menacing.*
*It's not like I can't understand how she feels. I think it might be annoying if you keep reaching out to somebody, only to be shot down constantly.*
*It might make you feel sad. Maybe it would make you mad. Maybe it would make you feel... like the other person doesn't like you.*
*Like they're looking down on you.*
*But... I don't think Noelle is like that.*
Atcchan: "She's probably just shy..."
Amu: "Shy? How can she be shy? I've been trying so, so, soooo hard to make her feel welcome! I say 'hello' every morning, you know?!"
Amu: "I even brought in some of the dorayaki my mom made!"
Amu: "I gave her one so she could have something yummy to eat, and so she'd realize I wanna be her friend, but she didn't even touch it!"
Amu: "I left it on her desk, but she didn't eat any of it! Even though Japanese sweets are the best! Even though my mom's cooking is delicious!"
Amu: "It's not fair! I'm mad!"
Atcchan: "Well, um... I don't know. Maybe she just needs some time to adjust?"
Amu: "Tea only takes a few minutes to prepare and it's still tasty. Why should this girl be more special than that?"
Amu: "Does she think she's better than me???"
Atcchan: "I don't think it's on purpose..."
Amu: "Aaah! It's stupid, useless! I don't care anymore! I don't wanna be friends with a person like that if she won't even try!"
*And with that, Amu propels herself forwards on the swing.*
*The swing set jerks forwards, arching through the air. I watch, immobile, as Amu's form moves up, and up, and up... seeming, almost, to become one with the summer sky.*
*Then, with a sudden, swift movement, Amu jumps.*
*Amu jumps from the swing at its highest point in its arc... and goes flying.*
*She looks just like a bird. A bird soaring in the sky, unbound by the laws of physics.*
*I'd never be able to make a daring jump like that. I'm far too small, far too shy... far too scared.*
*But something like that is easy for Amu. It's nothing. She didn't even have to think about it.*
*That's because she's a strong person.*
*She isn't like me.*
*She isn't like Noelle.*
*Then, could it be... maybe...*
*I am like Noelle...?*
*Amu's sneakers - old and off-white, worn from play - hit the ground with a loud thud, her arms held out at either side like a tightrope walker.*
*Somehow... Amu's back seems so far away.*
*It happens about a month or so after Noelle joins our school.*
*We're going on a class field trip to the zoo. It's three hours away, so we have to set off early - at 6:00 a.m.*
*My classmates, accompanied by Miss Tachibana, are gathered outside the school building in the early hours of the morning, waiting for the bus.*
*The sun is just starting to rise, peeking out over the top of the school building. *
*It's a little chilly. I shiver into my coat, pressing my hands deep inside my pockets. Nevertheless, I'm excited. I've never been to a zoo before.*
*I heard there are lots of animals there, like elephants and giraffes and tigers, and maybe even some strange ones I don't know about!*
*Even though seeing lots of big animals sounds kind of scary, they'll all be inside cages so they won't be able to hurt me. At least, that's what my mother told me...*
*Amu, standing by side, is also excited; even more so than I am. She shakes my arm, her whole face shining.*
Amu: "Atcchan, Atcchan! I wanna see a polar bear!"
Atcchan: "Do they have polar bears? Wouldn't it be too warm for them...?"
Amu: "They have special cages for them, silly!"
Atcchan: "I see... I hope they don't get sick. That would be sad..."
Amu: "Don't worry, don't worry! They'll be fine, just fine! You're too anxious, Atcchan~"
Atcchan: "Au... M-Maybe... I just hope none of the animals got hurt."
Amu: "They're fine! You're getting hung up on the wrong thing here!"
Amu: "What about the cool animals? And the ice cream stalls? And the gift shops?! That's way, waaay more exciting!"
Atcchan: "I should buy my parents a gift. I wonder what I should get them..."
*Amu sighs.*
Amu: "No. You're still focusing on the wrong thing..."
*At long last, the bus pulls up outside the school. There is a collective cry, a cheer of voices, and a surge forwards.*
*Amu grabs hold of my arm and pulls me along behind her, dragging us up to the front of the queue.*
Amu: "I'm gonna get on first - me, me, me!"
Miss Tachibana: "Calm down, Amu. We wouldn't want an accident before we've even set off."
Amu: "B-But, but... That's not fair! I want to be first!!!"
Miss Tachibana: "I know that, but you're not the only person going on this trip. You should show some more consideration to your fellow classmates."
Amu: "Consideration is a boring word."
Miss Tachibana: "That may be, but you must be careful. Please, think about the others a bit more."
Miss Tachibana: "... Hm."
*Miss Tachibana's voice trails off.*
*She lifts her gaze, looking over the top of Amu's light pink head. I follow her eyes, intrigued.*
*There, standing at the back of the crowd, a foot or so away from everybody else... is Noelle.*
*She's standing there by herself, all alone.*
*From tip to toe, her whole body is trembling - and I don't think it's because of the cold.*
*Everyone else is already paired up in a couple or part of a group. Noelle is the only one all alone.*
*Miss Tachibana frowns.*
Miss Tachibana: "Amu, you stay there. I'm not finished talking to you. I'm going to speak to Noelle for a few moments, all right?"
*Amu kicks her shoe against the ground mutinously, scowling.*
Amu: "That isn't fair. I don't wanna wait! Waiting is boring! This is discrimination!"
Miss Tachibana: "I know, I know. Just hold tight. If you can stand there patiently for five minutes, I'll give you a reward."
Amu: "Oooh, a reward..."
*The bribery seems to do the trick. Amu instantly silences, pressing a finger against her own lips, a look of intense concentration on her face.*
*Is not talking really that hard for her?*
Miss Tachibana: "Good girl."
*Miss Tachibana nods her head in approval before turning her full attention towards Noelle.*
*Noelle takes a step backwards as soon as she sees Miss Tachibana approaching, her eyes wide.*
*I watch their exchange curiously while Amu continues to hold her finger against her lips, her cheeks puffed out from the exertion of not speaking.*
*Miss Tachibana kneels down so she's at eye level with Noelle, talking so softly I can't hear her.*
*Noelle looks frightened but, little by little, this apprehension begins to wear away.*
*Her anxiety is still present in her too-wide eyes and her trembling fingertips, but she looks more at ease now.*
*Finally, Miss Tachibana straightens up and returns to Amu and I.*
*Amu, tiring of the game of not talking, takes her finger from her mouth and lets out the deluge of words that, no doubt, was building up inside her for the last five minutes.*
Amu: "Teacher, teacher, I did it! I was really good and really quiet so do I get a treat now, I want a treat, I hope it's edible, I'm hungry!"
Amu: "I had breakfast this morning but it wasn't enough but Mom wouldn't make me anymore because she said I might be sick since we're going on a long bus journey but that's stupid because I don't get travel sick-"
Amu: "-and anyway, I want something to eat! I want some snacks! Do you have any food? I'm hungry!"
*Miss Tachibana laughs.*
Miss Tachibana: "Now, now, calm down. I'll give you the treat when we get on the bus."
Amu: "Uu... But I can't wait that long..."
Miss Tachibana: "You can't wait for a minute?"
Amu: "No! I want it now!"
Miss Tachibana: "Easy there, Amu. Don't worry, you'll get your treat. I promise."
Amu: "Well, if you promise..."
Miss Tachibana: "Now. I am faced with something of a dilemma."
*Miss Tachibana looks between Amu and I, her arms folded. Even though she's smiling, the tone of her voice is serious.*
Atcchan: "D-Did I... do something wrong...?"
Miss Tachibana: "Hm? No, of course you didn't. I'm not going to punish you, silly."
Atcchan: "Au... O... O-Okay..."
Miss Tachibana: "Rather... I'm worried about Noelle."
Atcchan: "About Noelle?"
Miss Tachibana: "Yes. Unlike everybody else, she has no partner for this trip."
Miss Tachibana: "I don't want her looking around the zoo on her own, it wouldn't be safe. I would prefer it if she had somebody to go with her."
*Amu pulls a face.*
Amu: "Hey! I don't wanna pair up with her! She never talks to me, so why should I talk to her?! That isn't fair!"
*Amu's being too loud. Noelle can hear her.*
*Noelle flinches. I feel sorry for her.*
*Even so... I'm a little impressed.*
*If somebody said those kinds of things about me, I don't think I'd be able to keep my composure. I'd have run away by now, in tears.*
*Maybe Noelle is stronger than she looks.*
*Miss Tachibana sighs, giving Amu a slight rap on the head with her knuckles.*
Miss Tachibana: "Amu. You're being rude."
Amu: "No, I'm not. I'm just telling the truth."
Miss Tachibana: "You mean, your opinion."
Amu: "My opinion is the truth!"
*Miss Tachibana shakes her head.*
Miss Tachibana: "Not now it isn't. I can't allow you to say something like that. It isn't fair."
Miss Tachibana: "Now then. I would like you to join the group with Eri and Tsuzumi, Amu."
Amu: "Huh? What?!"
*Amu's eyes widen. She looks indignant.*
*Clinging to my arm tightly, so tightly I worry she might yank it straight from the socket, she gives Miss Tachibana a challenging glare.*
Amu: "No! No way! I wanna partner with Atcchan! I already decided that I'm with Atcchan!"
Miss Tachibana: "Amu, please. I want you to go with Eri. Atcchan should be with Noelle."
Amu: "But, but, but Atcchan is my friend - mine! He isn't Noelle's, he isn't!"
Miss Tachibana: "Amu..."
*But Amu isn't listening. I think she's having a temper tantrum.*
*Amu is scary when she gets angry. I don't like disagreeing with her. That's why I wish, every single Tanabata, that I never get on her bad side. But...*
*I look back at Noelle. She's standing there, all alone, looking so small and afraid. She really doesn't have any friends, does she?*
*Even though she's been at our school for a month... she hasn't been able to talk to anyone.*
*It's sad.*
*I don't want Noelle to be alone. Especially not on a day out like this. I want us to see the zoo together.*
*And so, even though I'm afraid... and even though I don't want to upset Amu... I lift my head... and meet Miss Tachibana's gaze.*
*My voice is hesitant and weak, but at least it's audible. Better than nothing.*
Atcchan: "I... I'll do it..."
Atcchan: "I want to be with Noelle."
*Noelle and I sit together on the bus, neither saying a word.*
*Everybody else is being so noisy. I guess they're excited. But it doesn't help bring Noelle out of her shell.*
*She seems even quieter than usual, if that's possible. Is it nerves?*
*I can see Amu sitting a few seats in front of me. She's sitting with Eri, a girl about our age.*
*Even though Amu protested so fiercely about being with Eri, she looks just fine now.*
*I think she's talking about some cute magical girl TV series with Eri. It sounds like they're arguing.*
*Their discussion sounds pretty heated, but I think Amu's having fun. She likes arguing. It's one of the things she excels at.*
*I turn away, staring out of the window.*
*We've been travelling for about half an hour.*
*We're out into the main road now, though it isn't very busy, given it's still so early in the morning. In another half hour, I'm sure there'll be lots more traffic. Trucks and vans and cars of every single color.*
*It's kind of scary, but also exciting.*
*I can't imagine this is anything special for Noelle, though. She used to live in the city, after all.*
*I wonder what it was like. Was it busier than this? By how much? How was she able to cope?*
*But I don't ask her. She's sitting by my side, head bent, sketchbook on her lap, drawing.*
*She looks completely immersed. Her pencil doesn't falter against the page, not even when the bus goes over bumps in the road. The line remains just as smooth, as straight, as sharp as always.*
*That's so cool. She really is talented...*
*I watch her from the corner of my eyes, trying to be discreet.*
*What an interesting person.*
*It's around 9:00 a.m. when we reach the zoo. The sun has finally risen, shining boldly, brightly, in a light blue sky.*
*Amu fell asleep at some point during the journey here, her head resting against Eri's shoulder. Even though she was acting so hyperactive and energetic, I bet she was so excited for today's trip she didn't get any sleep at all last night.*
*Now, however, she looks as wide awake as it's possible to be; hands planted on her hips, a wide smile on her face. I think she's arguing with Eri again, but I don't know what about.*
*Noelle was quiet for the whole drive here, drawing. She didn't put down her pencil once. Neither did she seem to get travel sick, even though the bus was pretty jerky.*
*She's so cool. I wouldn't be able to draw on the bus without feeling ill. She must have a lot of skills!*
*I consider telling her that, but I eventually decide not to. It might sound weird and she might get embarrassed. I wouldn't want that.*
*Miss Tachibana gives us a list of instructions. She tells us to split up in our groups and look around the zoo together.*
*We're not meant to split up from our group or go off on our own, especially not the very youngest students. The younger students are grouped together with the oldest kids.*
*We're meant to meet up at the entrance at 4:30 p.m. for the drive back home.*
*We all stand at the entrance of the zoo, waiting for her talk to be over. Amu keeps tapping her foot against the floor, and a few other students glance towards the zoo restlessly, not even looking Miss Tachibana in the eye.*
*Once the instructions are over, everybody rushes off like a swarm of bees, desperate to see absolutely everything as quickly as possible.*
*Even Miss Tachibana is dragged along by the entourage of young kindergarten students she's supervising, aged from three to five. They take hold of her hands and drag her away, en masse - some of them shouting about feeding her to the lions.*
*In the wake of this stampede, Noelle and I are the only ones left; both silent, neither saying a word.*
*I know, if I was with Amu, I would've been dragged off at breakneck speed by now. She wouldn't give me a single second to rest. But with Noelle... it's different.*
*With Noelle, I can savor the feeling of the sunlight against my skin, the wind through my hair, and the sounds and the smells of this new, unfamiliar place.*
*Taking everything in slowly, bit by bit, makes it all seem even more special, somehow.*
*I look around at my surroundings, blinking.*
*There's a big group of school children that look about my age crowded around by one of the barriers.*
*They're wearing a neat uniform with white shirts, black blazers, and black pants for the boys, red and white check skirts for the girls.*
*They're being herded along by several older people, presumably teachers, who are trying to calm them down.*
*They must be from another school, having a trip on the same day we are. Their school looks an awful lot bigger than ours.*
*There are so many students it's impossible for me to tell just how many there are. It's like trying to count the number of sweets crammed together inside a large jar.*
Atcchan: "Wow... Is that what schools in the city are like...?"
*I'm so in awe I say it out loud without really intending to. I don't expect an answer. That's why I'm caught off guard when, out of the blue, I receive one.*
*And from the most unlikely source, too.*
Noelle: "My school was even bigger."
*I look at Noelle in surprise. I don't think I've ever heard her talk before.*
*Noelle peeps up at me from underneath her bangs. Her cheeks are flushed a very, very pale pink.*
Atcchan: "Wow... That does sound very big. Wasn't it noisy?"
*Noelle nods her head.*
Noelle: "Very."
Atcchan: "I... I don't think I'd like something like that. It sounds kind of scary..."
Noelle: "It was, a little."
*Why does she sound so gloomy...? Since we're on a school trip, I feel obliged to cheer her up.*
Atcchan: "Well, y-you don't have to be scared anymore! You're here now."
Noelle: "I... I'm here now..."
Atcchan: "Yeah. So don't worry. If you want, I'll be your friend."
*The two of us both prove to be as indecisive as the other.*
*Even after inspecting a map of the zoo, we still can't make our minds up about what to see first. Neither of us really mind, so we can't come to a decision.*
*As a result, we end up walking around aimlessly - but that's fun, too.*
*After around an hour or so, we found ourselves sitting on a bench outside a cage filled with monkeys. It's a fairly secluded area of the zoo with few people to disturb us.*
*Maybe the crowds are more interested in the bigger, more exciting animals, like the elephants or giraffes?*
*The monkeys might be less impressive to look at, but I still like them.*
*They're so sneaky; clambering along the bars of the cage and swinging from their perches. They make funny noises, too, which makes me giggle.*
Atcchan: "They're cute, aren't they?"
Noelle: "..."
Noelle: "T-They... They are cute, I think..."
Atcchan: "Ehehe~ They're so fluffy."
Noelle: "Yes. I... like fluffy things..."
Atcchan: "What kind of fluffy things?"
Noelle: "... Rabbits, mostly."
Atcchan: "I like rabbits too. They have floppy ears and twitchy noses."
*Noelle nods.*
Noelle: "Rabbits are fun to draw. I do... lots of drawings..."
Atcchan: "Is that what you were drawing on the bus?"
Noelle: "I, um..."
*Noelle turns her head away, hiding behind her hair.*
Noelle: "I-I... didn't know... you were watching..."
*Ah...*
*Maybe I shouldn't have said anything.*
*I don't like it when Amu looks over my shoulder when I'm reading.*
*It's embarrassing, and it makes me feel ashamed of my reading choices, especially when she rolls her eyes and says 'That's boring! Let's go and play!'*
*I hope I didn't make Noelle feel embarrassed like that...*
Atcchan: "Oh, um, I... I'm sorry, I... I didn't know you didn't like it. I was just being nosy, I-I guess. I didn't mean to upset you."
Noelle: "Um, no... It's all right, I... don't mind, so much... I just didn't expect it."
Atcchan: "Maybe I should have told you I was looking? I just didn't want to be a bother..."
Atcchan: "I worried, if I told you, you'd get distracted."
Noelle: "T-That is... very thoughtful of you. T-Thank you..."
*Noelle offers me a small, hesitant smile. I don't know if it's entirely convincing, but at least she makes the effort.*
Noelle: "I wasn't drawing anything in particular on the bus. It was just a doodle."
*I'm not sure if she's being modest or not. It's hard for me to tell. But I'm still impressed.*
Atcchan: "Really? But it looked like you were paying so much attention - and the bits I could see looked really good...!"
Noelle: "W-Well, I... I'm all right, I suppose...?"
*I don't think these compliments are making her feel better. It's obvious she doesn't like being at the center of attention.*
*Noelle starts picking at a loose thread in the hem of her skirt. Pick, pick, pick.*
*If my mother were here, I'm positive she'd tell Noelle to cut that out.  I don't know anything about clothes, but even I can tell her skirt looks pretty expensive.*
*All of Noelle's clothes look expensive, come to think of it. Maybe her family is rich?*
*I know they're the people who moved into that large, modern house on the outskirts of the village. They'd have to be rich to build a house like that, wouldn't they?*
*I wonder but I don't ask. It might seem rude, like I'm prying into her private life. If she doesn't want to tell me, she doesn't have to. She's not obliged.*
*Instead, I turn my attention back to the cage, to the antics of the scampering monkeys.*
*When our stomachs start to rumble we realize that it's time for lunch.*
*Taking the homemade lunches out of our bags, prepared by our parents, we start to eat.*
*Noelle bows her head, her eyes closed.*
Noelle: "Thank you for the food."
*Her manners really are impeccable...*
*Then she takes her disposable chopsticks and tries to snap them apart.*
Noelle: "Haa..."
Noelle: "Nn..."
Noelle: "Auu..."
*But it is not to be.*
*No matter how much effort she puts in, or how frustrated her expression becomes... she's unable to tear the two chopsticks apart.*
*I ponder reaching out to help her, but-*
Noelle: "A-Aah...!"
*The sound of snapping wood fills the air, alongside a small cry of disappointment.*
*Noelle was finally able to separate the chopsticks... but their bond was too great to be torn apart so easily.*
*The chopsticks have not been broken cleanly. They're still joined together at the very base, leaving Noelle with one chopstick too short and one too chunky.*
*Noelle's face falls. She looks crestfallen.*
Noelle: "Au..."
*She sounds so defeated I can't help but laugh.*
Noelle: "I'm going to have bad luck now..."
Atcchan: "What do you mean?"
Noelle: "If you don't break your chopsticks cleanly... you'll get bad luck..."
Atcchan: "I don't know about that. I think it's just a rumor."
Noelle: "Are you sure...?"
Atcchan: "Yeah, I'm sure. Amu can never split her chopsticks right, but she's always smiling."
Noelle: "I suppose that is true, but..."
Noelle: "The last time this happened... a bird..."
Atcchan: "A bird...?"
Noelle: "..."
Noelle: "A bird... did something dirty... on my head......"
*She confesses this with red cheeks, her head hanging, fingers gripping the fabric of her skirt tightly.*
*It looks like she's trying to fold her body up like a towel, right out of existence.*
*Her story is pretty funny, but... she looks so embarrassed I'd feel guilty laughing.*
Atcchan: "D-Don't worry! You can borrow my chopsticks if you want."
Noelle: "Ah... um... R-Really...?"
Atcchan: "Sure, I don't mind. Here."
*And, feeling just a little bit cool, like a chivalrous knight, I hand Noelle my own disposable chopsticks; cleanly snapped into two distinctly separate pieces, unlike hers.*
Noelle: "Oh, no... I-I couldn't possibly..."
*Is what Noelle says - but she still reaches out to take them.*
*After we finish swapping our chopsticks, I turn my attention back to my lunch.*
Atcchan: "Thanks for the food."
*I bow my head and begin to eat.*
*Noelle's chopsticks are a little awkward to hold, but I don't mind. I think it was worth it.*
*Even if a bird does do something dirty on my head later on.*
*The two of us look around the zoo together.*
*We were given a worksheet by Miss Tachibana, with a list of activities we're supposed to do.*
*They're supposed to be educational tasks which will enrich our minds, letting us get the most out of our experience. The main reason we go on field trips is to learn things, after all.*
*At least, that's what it says on paper. The reality is quite different.*
*I can't imagine many people will actually bother to fill these forms in. They'll be too busy running around having fun, eating ice cream and shouting.*
*Noelle and I make a small effort to fill out some of the questions, but we don't exert too much energy. We're too busy enjoying the weather; the gentle breeze and the warm sunshine.*
*Mostly, we try to avoid areas where lots of people will be. As such, we don't get to see any of the really, really big animals. We still see a quite a lot, though.*
*The bush babies, with their big eyes, are creepy. The lemurs, with their black and white ringed tails, are very lithe. And the sloths, which lie on the branches of trees, unmoving, make me feel calm and relaxed.*
*At some point, we run into Amu, Eri, and Eri's big sister. Amu is eating a snow cone. A bit of it has melted on the tip of her nose.*
Amu: "Atcchan, Atcchan! Did you see it, did you see it?!"
Atcchan: "See what? I-I don't know what you mean..."
Amu: "The giraffes, of course, the giraffes! They have such long, long necks  it makes me want to tie a knot in one! That's my dream! Kukukuku~"
Atcchan: "U-Um, well... I don't know if they'd like that. That might hurt them..."
Amu: "But that's my dream! Sacrifices must be made! For the greater good!"
Atcchan: "U-Um... Did you know you have some snow cone on your nose...?"
Amu: "Silly Atcchan! As if I have the time to worry about that! I have many things to do, places to see, new lands to explore!!!"
Atcchan: "And animals to torture?"
Amu: "Maybe that too! I'll see you later, Atcchan!"
Atcchan: "See you. Have fun...!"
Amu: "I will~! I'll go at it with all I've got - like BADAN!!!"
*Noelle jumps at the sudden noise and hides behind my back, trembling like a baby bird.*
*I think being around Amu might have adverse affects on Noelle's health. She really doesn't get along with noisy people, does she...?*
Amu: "Okay! Let's go, my minions! To the future!!!"
*I watch as Amu runs off, Eri and Eri's big sister trailing behind.*
*When they finally leave, Noelle peeks out from behind my back, still trembling.*
Noelle: "H-Have they gone...?"
Atcchan: "They've gone. Don't worry."
Noelle: "Au... O-Okay..."
*I smile at her, trying to reassure her. I want to stop her shaking.*
Atcchan: "You don't need to be afraid of Amu. She's a nice person really."
Noelle: "R-Really...?"
*Noelle looks unsure. I guess I can understand why, given Amu was so rude to her only this morning.*
*I know Amu didn't really mean anything by it, though. She's just thoughtless sometimes. She always says exactly what she wants, never thinking about the feelings of others.*
*It can be upsetting, but I don't know if it's always a bad thing. I admire her.*
Atcchan: "Yes. She is nice - very nice. Just loud. At least she isn't as loud as her Dad."
Noelle: "T-There is somebody even louder...?"
Atcchan: "Yeah. Her dad's scary... He's really big, too..."
*Noelle shivers.*
Noelle: "T-That sounds frightening... I-I feel sorry for Amu..."
Atcchan: "I think Amu feels sorry for Amu, too. I don't know if she likes him very much."
*Our day at the zoo seems to end almost as quickly as it began. The time goes by in a flash, making me doubt whether it even happened at all.*
*Noelle and I wait by the entrance while Miss Tachibana does a quick head count, checking to make sure nobody is missing.*
*She does this a couple of times, reaffirming the accuracy of her first count, before straightening up.*
Miss Tachibana: "All right everyone. It's time to get back on the bus."
*A chorus of 'aaaw's ripple through the crowd. Everybody looks upset.*
*I'm upset too.*
*On this trip, I feel I finally got to know Noelle a little bit more.*
*She's a shy girl who has a hard time talking to others. She's bad at snapping chopsticks but very good at drawing.*
*She doesn't like large crowds and she thinks rabbits and monkeys are cute. And, maybe, if she doesn't mind...*
*She could be my new friend.*
*I really hope we can stay friends. I want it more than I've wanted anything before.*
*I just want her to be happy forever.*
Eri: "You're late! Off with your head!"
Atcchan: "Haah... Haah..."
*Breathing heavily, I lean forwards, pressing the palms of my hands against my knees.*
*Even though I ran here as fast as I could after finishing breakfast... it still wasn't good enough. Not for Eri.*
Atcchan: "You're not really... going to execute me, are you?"
Eri: "Not right this second. I would get blood on my dress."
Atcchan: "So... I'm spared, then...?"
*Eri turns her nose up in the air, arms folded.*
Eri: "Hmph. Just this once, all right?"
Eri: "I decided to go a little easy on you, but don't get the wrong idea. It'd be too much of an effort to chastise you properly, that's all."
Eri: "It's not like I like you or anything, moooo~ron."
*Of course not. As if I could ever make that mistake.*
*The sunflowers look even brighter than ever in the early morning. They're like a vast sea of orange and yellow spots against a canvas of mint green and light blue.*
*The gentle breeze makes them sway, petals fluttering, leaves rustling, without a care in the world.*
*I can understand why some people think they're pretty. Looking at this blanket of sunflowers is somewhat relaxing... Especially with the soft 'zaaa' of the wind as it goes passing by.*
*However... I can't quite shake my lingering paranoia that the sunflowers look like eyes. A large cluster of eyes. A whole audience, filling each and every seat in an auditorium, staring unblinkingly at the action taking place on stage...*
*I shudder.*
Atcchan: "I'm sorry if I'm a little late."
Eri: "Five minutes! Five minutes!"
Eri: "That's more than a 'little.' That's a whole 300 seconds! It doesn't sound like 'a little' when I put it like that, does it?"
Atcchan: "I-I really am sorry. my grandmother kept putting more and more food on my plate at breakfast, and I felt too guilty to just get up and leave..."
Eri: "Hmph."
*Eri makes her 'that's-not-good-enough' snort and snaps her pocket watch shut, placing it back in her pocket.*
Atcchan: "So... We're looking for Shiro today too?"
Eri: "Yes, that's right. And we haven't a moment to lose."
Atcchan: "Did anybody phone you about him?"
Eri: "As a matter of fact, my parents called me this morning, at Tsuzumi's."
Atcchan: "Oh? And what did they say...?"
Eri: "They said an old woman called. She said she'd seen our posters in town and..."
Eri: "She said she'd seen a white rabbit on her walk in the forest yesterday, and she thought it was peculiar since white rabbits aren't very common around here. Or something."
Atcchan: "That sounds like as good a lead as any."
Eri: "Exactly! We should get going as soon as possible. Otherwise the trail might go cold!"
*I give Eri a small smile, though I refrain from doing anything overly familiar, such as patting her on the shoulder. If I did that, she might break my fingers. Or cut them off.*
Atcchan: "Anything you say, Holmes. You lead the way."
Eri: "Does that make you Watson?"
Atcchan: "Ah... I guess so...?"
Eri: "Heh. You would be the incompetent, bumbling one, wouldn't you? Just don't get in my way."
Atcchan: "I-I'll do my best..."
*The two of us walk into the forest together, both silent. Eri seems too concerned about Shiro to say anything, and I'm caught up in thoughts of my own.*
*I forgot just how peaceful this place was. I used to come here all the time with Noelle, didn't I?*
*We went for long walks together down these old, earthen paths, skipping stones in the river, having picnics under the tall trees, and searching for birds and animals amongst the undergrowth...*
*Aah...*
*When I think about all the lighthearted, lazy days I've spent down here, it makes me feel just a little nostalgic.*
*Everything I see brings old memories to the forefront of my mind.*
*The smell of the plant life and vegetation, mixed with the richness of the damp earth, fills my nostrils. I inhale this clean, pure air almost greedily.*
*The sunlight filtering down through the leaves above is a soft green when it reaches the forest floor, dotted about in a mosaic of light.*
*Crunching, rustling noises fill the air as leaves and twigs shifting underneath us. The very landscape of the forest alters as we venture deeper and deeper.*
*I forgot just how pretty this place was, how soothing.*
*I thought I'd never forget. I willed myself not to forget. And, yet...*
*Despite that, the memories still slipped from my mind, day by day - just like sand through an hourglass.*
*Inevitably, the finer details of my life in this village began to fade away, completely overtaken with the hustle and bustle of the city.*
*I feel as though, for the first time... I really am back home where I belong.*
*The city has some good aspects, too, I won't deny it. It is nice being able to go buy snacks whenever you want, and not having to walk for an hour to get to the book store, but... the city doesn't have anything like this.*
*The neatly trimmed parks in the city, with bright green grass and carefully arranged flowers, don't compare at all. They're not as vast or expansive, wide and sprawling, as the forest - and they don't have the same kind of quiet, tranquil majesty.*
*But the wide and sprawling nature of the forest seems to be troubling Eri right now...*
Eri: "Aaah... This is stupid..."
*Eri turns about, scowling, and kicks the base of a tree with a loud thud.*
*A few birds sitting in the boughs squawk in alarm, flying away in a flurry of feathers.*
Eri: "Haah... Haah..."
*Red-faced, she leans forwards, panting. Her hair looks disheveled, as does her dress.*
Atcchan: "What's wrong...? Are you okay?"
Eri: "Do I look like I'm okay, you moron?"
*I thought she'd stopped calling me that. Evidently not.*
Eri: "This forest... It's just so big, I..."
*Eri holds a hand to her brow, shielding her eyes from the sun.*
Eri: "I have no idea how we'll find Shiro in here. There are so many places he could be hiding, and he's such a small rabbit..."
Atcchan: "Ah... But you... You've tried so hard! You can't give up now...!"
Eri: "I know.  If I gave up now, I'd never forgive myself. I can't leave Shiro. That'd be the worst - the complete and utter worst. But..."
*She sighs.*
Eri: "I didn't realize how big this place was. I had no idea."
Atcchan: "You've never been in the forest before...?"
*I try to keep the incredulity out of my voice, but it's difficult.*
*I've been coming here ever since I could walk - at first chaperoned by my parents, then side by side with Amu, and now, more frequently, with Noelle.*
*We used to go for small, impromptu school trips here a great deal, too; searching for interestingly shaped leaves and trying to identify the different trees.*
*Eri must have been on those as well, mustn't she?*
Eri: "W-Well... Obviously I've been in the forest before! I'm not that sheltered! I had to, to do all those 'fun fun fun' exercises in class, remember?"
Eri: "I-It's, just... um... I haven't been here so recently and... I forgot how big it was, o-okay...?"
Atcchan: "But it's so pretty. If I still lived nearby, I'd want to take walks in the forest all the time."
Eri: "What's your point?"
Atcchan: "I don't know. It just seems like a waste, that's all."
Eri: "Hmph. Different people enjoy different things, you know."
Atcchan: "Well, that is true..."
*Like Noelle and her passion for drawing, and Amu with her baseball. Neither of my best friends have interests entirely parallel with mine, now that I think about it.*
Eri: "Besides... It's dangerous here."
Atcchan: "Dangerous? You mean you might get lost?"
Eri: "No, of course not! I'm not stupid! As if I would ever get lost!"
Atcchan: "Or stung by nettles?"
Eri: "I'm far too cautious for such a thing!"
Atcchan: "Or bitten by mosquitoes?"
Eri: "Certainly, my high-class scent might attract disgusting bugs, but they wouldn't bother me."
*Eri stands, drawing herself up to her full height.*
Eri: "Rather... You know... There might be bears. Or wolves."
Atcchan: "There aren't any wolves in Japan, they've been extinct for years. And I don't think there are many bears here, either."
Eri: "W-Well then, M-Maybe not, but... But... I-It's all dirty in here and I could ruin my clothes!"
Eri: "Scrambling through the mud for fun isn't very ladylike. It's the pursuit of a commoner! It has nothing to do with me!"
Eri: "It's not as though I wanted to play out here! The fact that Big Sis didn't like it has nothing to do with it!"
*And with this, Eri turns her nose up in the air, arms folded.*
*She looks restless and exhausted at the same time. Her fingers clench and unclench at her sides, her face far too pale.*
*I feel like I should make a suggestion...*
Atcchan: "Well... I've been here quite a lot, so I think I'm fairly familiar with this forest. I can help lead you around, if you want?"
Eri: "Huh? You, lead me? What am I, a faithful pet?"
Atcchan: "A-Ah, no, t-that isn't what I-"
Eri: "Are you gonna put a collar on me and start calling me 'Hachiko?' Is that your idea?"
Atcchan: "N-No way, I-I'd never do that...!"
*Now I feel like I've done something wrong...*
Eri: "H-Hmph... I-Idiot..."
Eri: "I-If you know a place to look then... you could have suggested it earlier. Stupid."
Atcchan: "H-Huh...? You don't mind?"
Eri: "Not really."
Atcchan: "B-But I thought you didn't like the idea of following me...?"
Eri: "I don't. Not at all. But..."
Eri: "If it will help me find Shiro, then... it's all right, I suppose. I'll relent."
Eri: "I'm not completely unreasonable, you know?"
*Well, as long as she isn't completely. Now we might be able to get somewhere.*
*There's one girl I know who spends more time in this forest than anybody else. If anyone will know where Shiro is, she will.*
*I need to go and find her.*
*After ten or fifteen minutes of walking, we finally make it to our destination.*
*It's a large, old tree, standing proudly in the middle of a small clearing. Its branches jut upwards into the sky, its trunk covered in splotches of deep green moss.*
*When Noelle and I used to go for walks in the forest this tree was always our designated resting spot. It's a landmark in my mind, just as iconic as the Tokyo Tower.*
*Noelle and I spent countless hours together under this tree - her sketching, and me reading a book.*
*We sometimes brought food with us, and we would have picnics beneath the comforting shade of this tall tree, sipping tea from a thermos and eating sandwiches.*
*And, just as I predicted... she's there right now.*
*Sitting under that tree, her silver hair fluttering in the breeze, her sketchbook on her lap and a pencil poised in one hand, is Noelle.*
*I don't think she's noticed us, despite the rustling of leaves and crackling of twigs that herald our arrival. She seems completely engrossed in her drawing.*
*Her light blue eyes flicker up to meet some indeterminate point in the forest, then settle back down to her sketchbook. Her gaze continues to move up and down, up and down, her grip on the pencil never faltering.*
*That level of concentration really is something. She's so focused, her gaze so intense, I feel it sucking me in.*
Eri: "Hey. Why did you bring us here, you cretin?"
Atcchan: "O-Ow..."
*But I don't have enough time to stand around, gawping. I'm not at an art museum, and there's certainly no rule against raised voices here.*
*That's something Eri starts to demonstrate amply, to the best of her ability.*
Eri: "We need to find Shiro, remember?  We don't have enough time to stand around!"
Atcchan: "Aaah... T-That's right. I-I haven't forgotten..."
Eri: "You're such a pain. Why do I even put up with you?"
Atcchan: "B-Because you don't have to pay me for my services...?"
Eri: "Hmph. As if you even deserve to be paid for your 'services.' What cheek."
Atcchan: "I-I apologize, Milady..."
*Our small scuffle is enough to break Noelle's concentration. She lifts her head to look at us, blinking in surprise.*
*She looks as though she's just surfaced up from a large body of water... or else woken up from a beautiful dream.*
Noelle: "Atcchan...? And...... Eri?"
*When Noelle sees Eri, standing a little way behind me, her eyes suddenly widen. She looks nervous, just like a deer in headlights.*
Noelle: "W-What are you doing here...?"
*I instantly start to feel guilty.*
*I've never liked interrupting Noelle while she's drawing.*
*She goes through life with such a hazy, distant look on her face, as though she's completely disconnected from her surroundings, but... when she draws, a certain kind of light begins to spark in her eyes.*
*It's only when she draws that she comes to life.*
*I feel that kind of thing... isn't something that should be interrupted. Like waking a sleepwalker, I worry it could be dangerous.*
*When she draws... it seems to be the only time Noelle is ever truly awake.*
Atcchan: "Ah, um, well... A-Actually, I... um, 'we', rather. We came here to ask a favor."
Eri: "Huh? We did?"
Atcchan: "Y-Yes, we did..."
*Eri looks at me dubiously.*
Eri: "But why should Noelle be of any use? We've hardly ever spoken to one another."
*At the phrase 'of any use', Noelle flinches. Her head hangs so low it looks as though it might slip off her neck and fall to the ground.*
Noelle: "Yes. S-She's right. W-We... we haven't really spoken..."
Eri: "Exactly. So she won't know anything. This has been a complete waste of time. Honestly."
*Eri sighs, flipping one blond curl behind her shoulder.*
Eri: "You really are a fool. And I thought, for a few seconds, I could trust your judgment."
Atcchan: "A-Ah, no - you see, Noelle has a talent!"
Eri: "A talent?"
Noelle: "I-I do...?"
Atcchan: "Y-Yeah, that's right...!"
Noelle: "But... I can't do any party tricks. I wouldn't even be able to pull a rabbit out of a hat..."
*What a strange thing to get hung up about...*
*Well. She might not be able to produce a rabbit out of thin air, but she might be able to help us track an existing one down.*
Atcchan: "No, that isn't what I meant. Maybe 'talent' isn't the right word, then. It's just..."
Atcchan: "Noelle is better acquainted with this forest than anybody! Isn't that right?"
Eri: "Is that true?"
Noelle: "U-Um, well..."
Noelle: "I-I do go here for walks quite often. I am fairly well acquainted with the forest, um... I think...? Not that I would want to boast or anything..."
Noelle: "I don't know if it's something worth boasting about..."
Atcchan: "T-That's right! So, if Shiro is in this forest, Noelle is the person most likely to have seen him!"
Noelle: "Shiro...?"
Eri: "My rabbit. A very cute rabbit, with a white body and a fluffy tail and floppy ears. He... He went missing two days ago."
Noelle: "Oh, T-That's too bad. I like rabbits a lot, too..."
Eri: "You do?"
Noelle: "Yes. They're very cute. I want one of my own, but my parents won't let me..."
Eri: "Hmph. That's a weak way of looking at things."
Noelle: "W-Weak...?"
Eri: "Yes. If you really, really want something, you shouldn't let anybody stand in your way! That shows a weak will!"
Atcchan: "H-Hey... I think that might be quite a dangerous way to live."
*Eri glares.*
Eri: "It's the only way to live."
Eri: "But anyway. Ignoring the goody two shoes over here..."
Atcchan: "T-There's nothing wrong with being sensible!"
Eri: "Rabbits are cute, but Shiro is the cutest. You'd definitely know him if you'd seen him. He's not at all like the wild rabbits that overrun this forest, copulating like nymphomaniacs then eating their babies."
*I stare at Eri in horror, my mouth falling open.*
Atcchan: "Do rabbits eat their babies?"
Noelle: "Sometimes, yes."
Atcchan: "B-But why...?"
Eri: "It's a cruel world out there. You need to take what you want, and try to avoid being taken yourself."
Atcchan: "I... I see."
*I whimper. I thought rabbits were just cute and nice, like living balls of cotton wool - but if even Noelle is nodding along with Eri, then it must be true.*
*Why must the world be so disturbing and corrupt...?*
Eri: "Anyway, Shiro isn't a peasant. He's of noble descent. After all, he's a member of the great Onodera family!"
Noelle: "Oh...? Is your family noble...? Is it...?"
Eri: "W-Well, um... In a sense...!"
Noelle: "Is that so...? I thought your parents ran the general store in the village..."
*Eri's face flushes.*
Eri: "A-Aaah... W-Well, t-there are different levels of nobility, you know? N-Not all the people in Versailles were particularly wealthy!"
Noelle: "Oh... Um, I... I don't know much about that, but I suppose it's true..."
Noelle: "I did read in a book one time that Madame DuBarry achieved her position in the palace by sleeping with the king, even though she was of a fairly lowly birth."
Noelle: "I suppose the message is... A-As long as people try hard, they can achieve anything, regardless of their wealth?"
Eri: "T-That's exactly right! There are different levels and -"
Eri: "Hey! W-What are you trying to imply?!"
Noelle: "I-Imply...? I-I... I wasn't implying anything... I-I was just trying to join in with the conversation..."
Eri: "Hmph."
Eri: "Atcchan, your friend is just as dense as you. You'd make a good couple."
*Our replies are simultaneous.*
Atcchan: "A couple?!"
Noelle: "'Atcchan?!'"
*Eri shrugs her shoulders.*
Eri: "I'm just saying it like it is. Birds of a feather flock together. And my feathers are far too ornate to be associated with either of you."
Noelle: "But you... Y-You're calling Atcchan 'Atcchan'...? I, um..."
*Noelle looks down at the ground, her eyes obscured behind her bangs.*
*I can't tell what kind of expression she's wearing, but judging by her tone of her voice, she sounds more than a little gloomy.*
Noelle: "I, um... didn't realize you called him that..."
Eri: "Well, 'Atcchan' is Atcchan, just like cows are cows. What's the problem?"
Eri: "I-It's not weird to call somebody by a nickname, i-is it...? Especially not a classmate."
Noelle: "N-No, I suppose not... It's just, I... I didn't know you were such good friends."
*We're not good friends.":
*I suppose we are friends...":
*Ah...*
*Knowing Eri, I don't think she'd be too pleased with Noelle's assessment of our 'relationship.'*
*Actually, I think she'd try to deny we have a 'relationship' at all.*
*If I agreed with Noelle and said we were friends... what would happen? Maybe Eri would get annoyed, chide me for being overly presumptuous, and then hit me...*
*It's a bleak line of reasoning all right.*
*Naturally, I want to avoid getting hit at all costs. I think most people do.*
Atcchan: "U-Um, well... we're not really good friends. We don't know each other that well."
Eri: "T-That... T-That's right!!!"
*Eri nods her head firmly, her curls bouncing all the more.*
Eri: "As if I, Onodera Eri, would became friends with a half-wit like this. It would be a blemish upon my reputation!"
Atcchan: "W-Well, I... I don't know if I'm a 'half-wit', but-"
Eri: "You are a half-wit. Maybe even worse than that."
Atcchan: "There's worse?!"
Eri: "Of course. Like being a third-wit, or a quarter-wit. Or a third-rate third-wit."
*Wah... All of these fractions are making me feel dizzy...*
Eri: "The fact you don't realize your own half-wittedness is further proof that you are one."
Atcchan: "R-Really...? It's proof?"
Eri: "Unshakable. Mathematical."
*Well, if it's mathematical, how can I argue against that?*
*I wish Saki was here. Saki was always fairly good with math. After biology, it was one of her best subjects.*
*It's funny. Given she loves European literature so much, I'd always assumed she'd be good at English class, but...*
*Most of the English phrases she actually knows are strange, specialist terms like 'I'm going to suck your blood.' and 'Let's sacrifice the virgins.', neither of which are particularly useful on assessed speaking tests.*
Atcchan: "Au... W-Well, if that's the way it is..."
Noelle: "Yes. Sometimes Atcchan can be dense."
Atcchan: "H-Huh...?"
*I stare at Noelle in horror.*
*I didn't think she would agree with Eri! I thought Noelle was meant to be my friend...!*
*Waaa... Wawawa...*
*M-Maybe everybody thinks I'm an idiot, and the only people honest enough to state that are Amu and Eri...*
*And Noelle now, as well?!*
*That's simply too cruel...*
Noelle: "But I think that is part of his charm. It... is endearing."
*So I'm an endearing half-wit, am I...? Doesn't that just make me a court jester?*
*At least Noelle looks more cheerful than she did before.*
Atcchan: "Well, um, I... I-I suppose we are... friends. Kind of...?"
*As I say this, my face flushing pink, both Eri and Noelle give me incredulous looks.*
Noelle: "Y-You are?"
Eri: "We are? Since when?!"
Atcchan: "A-Ah, well, um... I-I mean, we don't know each other that well, but, um... I-I think, maybe..."
Atcchan: "Since I've been helping you... maybe you could say we're friends...?"
Eri: "H-Hmph...! Don't be so presumptuous, you half-wit!"
*For some reason, I knew she'd say that.*
Eri: "I-I don't become friends with every single ruffian who stumbles in my direction! I'm a real lady, of true class and breeding!"
Eri: "Refined people such as myself don't have - nay, don't need - any 'friends.'"
Atcchan: "You don't?"
Eri: "N-No, not at all! If you have noble blood, 'friends' become obsolete!"
Eri: "'Friends' are something commoners need, to stuff the gaps created by their own lack of elegance!"
Eri: "Friends are mere distractions from the truth - a way to make oneself feel better!"
Eri: "Naturally, I am above such nonsense...! H-Hohohoh..."
*She laughs her patented princess-style laugh, but for some reason, it sounds weak.*
*It might just be my imagination, but... Eri's adamant rebuttal of the mere idea I might, quite possibly, be her friend... seems a little sad.*
Eri: "So. About Shiro."
*Eri turns back to Noelle, hands on hips, expression serious.*
Eri: "Can you help or not? Have you seen him?"
Noelle: "..."
*Noelle blinks slowly. She seems to be thinking something over, although I'm not entirely sure what.*
*It takes her a very long time before she finally replies.*
Eri: "What a waste..."
*Eri sighs, arms folded. She gazes out over the heads of hundreds upon hundreds of sunflowers, rocking gently by the breeze.*
*After doing a search around the whole forest... we ended up back here. Right where we first met.*
*And, just like last time, there's no sign of Shiro.*
*Although we asked Noelle, her answer wasn't the one we wanted to hear. Instead, she shook her head sadly, a frown on her face.*
*No, she hadn't seen any white rabbit in the forest. If she had, she would have remembered. White rabbits are very distinctive, so if she had seen one, she would have remembered, but she didn't.*
*And so, like a trickle at the bottom of a well in the middle of summer, our last lead dried up.*
Atcchan: "I... I-I'm sorry..."
*I approach Eri hesitantly, unsure of how to phrase my condolences without them sounding insincere.*
*However, to my surprise... Eri doesn't react with anger. She doesn't get mad.*
*The expression on her face... can only be described as 'listless.'*
*Has she given up?*
Eri: "It's all right. You don't need to apologize. It wasn't your fault."
Atcchan: "I-I... I know, but... I-I wanted to help..."
Eri: "It's fine. I already said it's not your fault."
Eri: "I'm the real fool here. I'm the one... who got my hopes up too much."
Eri: "I'm not so unreasonable... that I would blame you for that."
Atcchan: "Eri..."
Eri: "I guess I was right. If you have hope, things really do start to fall apart."
Eri: "Life isn't kind enough to nurture such naïve dreams. It stands to reason that, if you hold onto your hopes, you'll just get disappointed."
*I guess that makes sense, but... it sounds so lonely.*
*As she stares out at the sunflower field, the setting sun swallowing her in shadows... she looks small and lonely.*
Atcchan: "B-But..."
Eri: "But?"
Atcchan: "If you refuse to hope, i-isn't that the same as denying your future happiness?"
Eri: "No. I don't think so."
Eri: "Maybe I did once. I dreamt about lots of things. Stupid things. But it didn't work out. All it did was hurt me."
Eri: "After that painful lesson, I realized something. Something important. I think it's part of becoming an adult."
Eri: "Dreams are nice distractions, but they're not the same as reality. They're not always things you can achieve."
Eri: "If you pine after these dreams for too long... you might up chasing after something that doesn't even exist."
Atcchan: "B-But that... T-That isn't true...! Shiro does exist. You know that...! S-So it's not like you have to stop searching!"
Eri: "Maybe. That is true. But..."
Eri: "Trying to find a single rabbit in a whole forest? Isn't that ridiculous?"
Eri: "It's not like I'm Alice or anything. This isn't a children's story. I'm not so stupid that I believe in things like that, even if you are."
Atcchan: "A-Aah..."
*Even though she's insulting me, it still makes me smile.*
*That sounds more like the Eri I've grown to know over the last three days.*
Atcchan: "Maybe I am stupid."
*I sigh.*
Atcchan: "You're right. Some things do change, even if you try to stop them. That's just part of life."
*Like when I had to move to live in the city.*
*I didn't want to do it but I didn't have a choice. It was something I couldn't control.*
*When I tried to hide the truth from Noelle, it didn't stop it from happening. All it did was hurt her.*
*I really was... stupid.*
Eri: "Yeah. It's true. And it's sad. It's frustrating. It's upsetting. Having so little control over my own life makes me wanna punch the wall or smash things sometimes."
Atcchan: "Do you ever do that...?"
Eri: "From time to time. When I go see Big Sis. Her place is messed up enough as it is, so it doesn't make any difference."
Atcchan: "Is that why everything in her store looks so chipped and broken?"
Eri: "Heh. No, that'd be because of her bad taste. Big Sis herself is warped and weird, so she likes warped and weird things."
Eri: "I think a person like her, with a twisted heart, is most at home in a room full of junk, don't you?"
Atcchan: "A-Ah... T-That's a little harsh..."
Eri: "But it's totally true. Big Sis is such a creep. You don't even know the half of it."
Eri: "But anyway..."
*Eri sighs heavily, exhaling so hard it sounds almost painful.*
Eri: "It might be a waste of time. It's been too long. I don't know if Shiro will ever turn up now."
Atcchan: "But you searched so hard..."
Eri: "Yeah. I did. I tried my best. But it still wasn't good enough."
Eri: "Sometimes, no matter how hard you try... things just don't go your way."
Atcchan: "You're going to give up? Just like that?"
Eri: "It isn't giving up. That's a callous way to put it. As expected of a peasant like you. Hmph."
Eri: "I simply know when to stop hoping for the impossible."
Eri: "Even if you don't want to admit it... Even if you try to trick yourself, or think of something else to make yourself feel better..."
Eri: "What you want won't always happen, and things always change. The world is unpredictable like that."
Eri: "And..."
Eri: "There isn't anything I can do about it."
*I sit cross-legged on my bed, flipping through my sketchbook.*
*Pages upon pages of sketches greet me; most of them half-formed, unfinished. Deformed. Ugly.*
*I don't like them. I don't like them at all.*

*I... I don't know...*

*Nothing that makes them special.*

*This time I'll create something meaningful. This time, people will understand.*
*And yet, despite these innocent hopes... it never really works out. A miracle does not occur. And everything remains the same.*
*Then I get scared. I get scared of finishing my drawings... because I know, when I do... I'll just be disappointed.*
*I try to draw the process out, adding more and more minute details, drawing the same things over and over again.*
*People praise that. They mistake it for dedication. They don't know what it really is.*
*They don't know that I'm afraid.*
*I continue to flip through my sketchbook, hardly paying attention to all the unfinished sketches that flash by my eyes.*
*They're all failures. Just like me.*
*I should probably feel some kind of kinship with these pictures, given they're so much like me, but... all I can summon up is mild distaste.*
*Why... am I so tired?*
*My fingers finally stop. I look down at a particular page in my sketchbook and stare.*
*Gripping my sketchbook tightly with both hands, my knuckles slowly begin to turn white.*

*A beautiful white rabbit.*
*I wanted to capture at least some of that beauty, but my picture doesn't look quite right. The eyes are wrong. They're too dull, too empty, too blank and staring.*
*Why does everything I draw... end up like this...?*
*Why...?*
*Maybe it's because... I'm a bad person... and I have a rotten heart...*
*Maybe it's because I'm a liar.*

*Although Amu can be... boisterous at times, her smile can work wonders - just like herbal tea or lemon balm. It's a soothing medicine which can cure any kind of lingering malignancy.*
*But she isn't here.*

Atcchan: "A-Aah..."

Eri: "Are you sure...?"
Atcchan: "Of course I'm sure. Why wouldn't I be?"

Atcchan: "Hahaha~ And I didn't think Princess Eri cared about the feelings of lowly commoners such as myself."

Eri: "A-Ah...! T-That is, um..."

Noelle: "She will forgive you... definitely."
Noelle: "T-That is what I think."
*Eri shifts a little, averting her eyes.*
Eri: "A-Ah... Well, maybe... Maybe that's true, but I..."
Atcchan: "Are you scared?"
Eri: "W-Who, me? O-Onodera Eri, scared? D-Don't be stupid! I'm not scared of anything!"
Eri: "I'm not scared of ghosts or monsters, or even of eating spicy bell peppers whole! H-Hohohoh!"

Atcchan: "Well... Everybody knows me by an asinine nickname too. I thought it was only fair."
Eri: "H-Hmph... W-Why you... Of all the impudent things, I..."
Eri: "..."
*Eri's voice breaks off. She turns her head, blond curls bouncing. She seems to be deep in thought.*
*Seems to be. For a few moments. Until...*
Eri: "..."
*Eri's voice breaks off. She turns her head, blond curls bouncing. She seems to be deep in thought.*
*Seems to be. For a few moments. Until...*
Eri: "M-My gosh...!"
*Eri's eyes widen. Her mouth falls open. And, with a sudden shriek...*
Eri: "K-Kyaa!!!"
*She rises to her feet, skirts fluttering, blond curls bouncing with renewed vigor.*
*There, sitting by the river bank, head tilted to one side... is a small, white rabbit.*
*Shiro...?*
Noelle: "Ah... That is..."
Atcchan: "W-What is it, Noelle?"
Noelle: "The rabbit. The rabbit I sketched this morning."
Atcchan: "R-Really?"
Noelle: "Yes. Truly. So she was here all along?"

*Eri runs towards the small rabbit, her curls fluttering.*
*The rabbit doesn't run away. Instead, she continues to sit there, looking up at Eri, her nose twitching. Waiting.*
*Waiting to be reunited with her friend.*
*Eri scoops Shiro up into her arms and holds her close, pressing her to her chest, though not too hard.*
*She holds onto Shiro dearly, as though she's something precious; a sparkling jewel. And, to Eri... I suppose she is.*
*They've finally found one another. The reason for Eri's quest, through towns and woodlands and treacherous environs, has finally come to an end.*
*I wonder... how long was Shiro sitting here, anyway?*
*Was she waiting here, just out of sight... until Eri found her?*
*Maybe she was afraid she would interrupt our conversation if she came forwards too early... and so, politely, as though at a train station... she waited.*
*She waited for Eri to notice her. She waited for Eri to find her. And she did it all without making any noise.*
*Those two... are true friends, aren't they?*
*As I watch them, Eri holding Shiro to her chest tightly, a wide smile on her face... I can't help but feel moved.*
Noelle: "Atcchan..."
*Noelle tugs my sleeve. I turn my head to look at her.*
Atcchan: "Yes...? What is it...?"
Noelle: "I'm happy, Atcchan. I glad she was able to find her friend."
*I smile.*
Atcchan: "Me, too. I'm glad as well."
Amu: "Atcchan! I'll miss you!"
Atcchan: "A-Ah... I-I'll miss you, too..."
Amu: "I mean, without you around, who else do I have to make fun of? It'll be so boring!"
Atcchan: "H-Hey...! T-That can't be the only reason, can it?"
Amu: "Mm... No, there are others."
*Amu giggles, winking playfully.*
Amu: "You sometimes buy me things as well. That also counts for something~!"
Atcchan: "W-Waaah...! So mean!"
Amu: "Ehehe~ Just kidding, just kidding~"
*Amu smiles, petting me on the head as though I'm some kind of household pet (but not a goldfish, of course. Nobody pats them on the head. Do goldfish even have heads?)*
*I pout and pull a face, but I don't try to pull away. I don't think there would be much point.*
*I'm meant to be going back home today. This will be one of the last times I get to see Amu, won't it?*
*While I'm here with her... I might as well let her muss up my hair, if it makes her happy. It's always messy, anyway.*
*Since it's already getting dark and this village exists in such a secluded spot... I can't imagine there'll be that many people on the train, either. Most likely, it'll be completely empty.*
*It's not like anybody will be there to judge my hair - so, why does it matter? I know Noelle and Amu don't care. And Eri...*
*I'm sure, if Eri were here, she would. She would tut and sigh and fold her arms and tell me, in no uncertain terms, that I look like a mess.*
*That being seen in public with an unfashionable person like me is incredibly embarrassing - bad for her image. And then she'd flick my forehead.*
*But Eri isn't here.*
*Even though I stayed by her side these last couple of days and helped her find Shiro, together with Noelle... she didn't turn up. She didn't come to say goodbye.*
*It must be because of Amu.*
*I thought, maybe, those two girls might be able to rekindle their friendship, if only they made a little bit of effort. If Eri had come to the station with me to meet Amu... I'm sure they could have worked something out.*
*They used to be such close friends. It is true they always argued, but it looked like a lot of fun. I thought they suited one another.*
*But, even though I suggested the idea to her... Eri didn't even consider it. Not for a second.*
Eri: "Y-You want me to spend time with Amu? No way..."
Atcchan: "But it'll be a chance for you to see her again. To make up. Don't you want that?"

Atcchan: "But you two... I thought you were friends?"
Eri: "'Were' being the correct choice of word. And I never liked her that much to begin with, anyway."
Eri: "She's rowdy person who talks too loudly and too inelegantly, and she doesn't mind her manners. She's not the type of person I wish to be associated with. Simply suggesting it is an insult."
*Or so she says. And yet, I can't help but notice...*
*Her hands, holding Shiro tightly against her chest... are trembling.*
*Eri looks down at the ground and sighs, expelling the air from her lungs in a rather melancholy manner.*
*Sensing her discomfort, Shiro began to nuzzle against Eri's face. Eri accepts this display of affection with a small frown.*
Eri: "Besides... She doesn't like me. I know she doesn't. It would be pointless going to see her when I already know what the outcome will be."
Noelle: "Like the story about the hedgehog...?"
Eri: "Exactly. If you know it'll hurt when you touch the prickles of the hedgehog... then why should you reach out to begin with?"
Atcchan: "But, um..."
Atcchan: "M-Maybe I interpreted it wrong... and I'm not the most intelligent person, but-"
Eri: "Well, that's a given."
Atcchan: "Y-Yes, well... Um..."
Atcchan: "T-This is just my opinion, but... I always thought the story about the hedgehog... meant something like... Um..."
Atcchan: "It's inevitable, if you form relationships with others, that you'll get hurt. Because people aren't perfect and they all make mistakes."
Atcchan: "But, even if being hurt is inevitable, you have to keep trying. You can't give up. And, even if the prickles are painful... sometimes, the close company can be worth it?"
*Eri sighs.*
Eri: "I didn't know you were such an optimist. You always seem so jumpy and scared of everything. I thought you, of all people, would be pretty anti-people."
Atcchan: "W-Well I, um... E-Even if I am a little shy, i-it... I-It's not like that's anybody else's fault. I-It's something I need to deal with myself."
Eri: "Yes. That's true enough. And..."
Eri: "Being hurt is something I need to do deal with by myself."
Eri: "If you reach out to the hedgehog with bare fingers, even though you see the prickles... when you get hurt, you can only blame yourself. You got hurt because you were stupid."
Eri: "But I'm different. I'm not stupid. I don't want to be stupid."
Atcchan: "You mean... you don't want to hope?"
Eri: "It amounts to the same thing. People who hope and people who dream..."
Eri: "They're all going to be let down eventually. At some point, you have to accept things the way they are and move on."
Atcchan: "And so... You've already moved on?"
Eri: "Yes. I already did. I don't want to get hurt again."
*Eri cuddles Shiro tightly, embracing her in a loving hug.*
Eri: "And if I did show up to the train station... it would be selfish."
Atcchan: "Selfish...?"
Eri: "Yes. Amu is your friend, not mine. Not anymore.  And this is your chance to say goodbye to her."
Eri: "If I was there I'd just get in the way. It would make her hate me even more than she already does."
Eri: "Amu likes you a lot, you know?"
*Eri looks at me intently... and my face turns red.*
Atcchan: "W-Well I, um... I-I don't k-know about that, I... Au..."
*I turn my head and look away, staring down at the grassy bank of the riverside.*
*Eri is a stubborn person. Since she'd already made up her mind, I couldn't do anything to change it. And... I couldn't get her to go and see Amu.*
*I wanted to berate her for that defeatist mode of thinking, but... that would be hypocritical.*
*I never told Noelle that I was moving. I kept putting it off, too afraid to admit the truth. After I left, I couldn't even bring myself to phone her, too afraid she'd be mad at me.*
*And I couldn't stand the thought of her being mad at me.*
*There's nobody who's more of a defeatist than I am.*
*Eri and I... maybe we're not so dissimilar after all.*
*I sit on the train, leaning my head against the window. My head vibrates against the windowpane, but I ignore it.*
*A slow, dense pain begins to spread through one side of my skull, like rot setting into a tooth. In my state of mind, however, I can't bring myself to care.*
*I'm too busy thinking. Thinking about her. And, for once, that 'her' isn't Noelle.*
*It's Eri.*
*Eri standing in the sunflower field that evening when I nearly hit her with my bike, a scowl on her face.*
*I remember... she looked as though she was trying to freeze me in place merely by the power of her self-righteous anger.*
*But that isn't the only image of Eri embedded in my mind.*
*There's also the smiling, cheerful Eri, standing by the riverside with Shiro in her arms.*
*She looked so happy then. So overjoyed. I've never seen her make such an expression before.*
*I wish... she could always be that happy. But maybe that isn't possible now...*
*I wonder...*
*If I had pressed her a little more... maybe I could have learned something about her relationship with Amu. And... maybe I could have helped resolve it.*
*But that never happened. It was impossible.*
*It's like a mathematical problem. If you don't know the question, you can't work out the answer.*
*What could I have done to help repair that relationship? What questions should I have asked, and how should I have acted?*
*I don't know.*
*It's probably... too late for that now.*
*I stare out the window. Beyond the thick glass, separating me from the rest of the world, I see a strip of hills and mountains speeding by... marred by the tinted windows, and obscured by dirt and dust.*
*My surroundings look dim and murky under the darkening sky. It makes me feel as though I'm staring out at a strange, underwater scene - gawping at a tank in an aquarium.*
*I wouldn't be surprised if, at any moment, I saw a school of sardines, or a small shark, swim by amongst the clouds, lost in the evening sky.*
*If only I had said or done something, anything, maybe I could have made a difference. But the moment for that has already gone. And, with every passing second, I get further and further away from both of them. Amu and Eri.*
*At least I helped Eri find Shiro. That's something. But what if...?*
*I sigh.*
*The question fills my mind. It repeats on a loop, over and over again. What if, what if, what if...?*
*But I know it's pointless. There's nothing I can do to find that out. And there's nobody I can ask.*
*Other than me, the train is completely empty... as it makes its slow, steady journey through the murky green mountains, back towards civilization.*
Eri: "Hey, um... A-Amu..."
Amu: "Eri..."
*The two of them stand there, backs unnaturally straight, dutifully looking in any direction other than each other.*
*In the darkened train station, evening slowly approaching... Noelle and I stand there, side by side, watching them. Waiting.*
Noelle: "Hey, Atcchan..."
*Noelle whispers under her breath. I lean in closer to her and she bends down, placing her mouth nearer to my ear.*
*Uuu...*
*Again, I'm reminded of just how small I am. I really am the shortest person here, aren't I...?*
*I need to watch out. If I'm not careful, somebody might step on me, and my tiny little life will be extinguished faster than blinking.*
*I wonder if this is how Gulliver felt when he went to Brobdingnag...*
Atcchan: "Yes? What is it, Noelle?"

*I guess those two girls will be stubborn until the very end.*
*Even though I brought them together so Eri could apologize, the hallowed words 'I'm sorry.' have yet to pass between her lips.*
*Maybe she's too prideful to admit she was wrong, especially in front of somebody she's been incorrectly accusing for two years. Suddenly having to admit you were mistaken all that time must be pretty painful.*
Eri: "I... I... au..."
Eri: "Au..."

Atcchan: "But?"
*...*

*At least neither of them has grown so infuriated that they've walked away.*

Noelle: "Um..."
Noelle: "..."
Noelle: "Please accept my apology!"

Noelle: "I'm sorry! I was the one who destroyed that letter... and I am the reason that your friendship with Eri fell apart!"
*...*
*...*
*...*

*And then, her face bright red...*

*I swear I can almost see tears beading in the corners of her eyes.*

*Then she tilts her head to one side.*

Eri: "Urgh..."

Eri: "I thought... everything was already messed up beyond repair... so I shouldn't get my hopes up. So I should push you away, as much as possible..."

Amu: "I don't know. Maybe I got tired of being angry. It's not very much fun. And it's exhausting."

*Eri's face contorts. She looks like she's in pain.*
Eri: "I'm sorry for doubting you all this time, Amu. I should have known you weren't lying. I should have... believed you..."
*It's like pulling teeth. This girl really is bad at admitting her own mistakes, isn't she?*
Amu: "Ah, well, um... E-Ehehe... I-It's fine, it's fine. I-I forgive you. I don't like being mad that much, either..."
*And this girl is bad at accepting sincere compliments.*
*What a funny pair they make. Kind of like a stand up comedy duo.*
*Maybe, if I spoke to a TV station, I could get them their own show. I'm sure it'd be popular.*
Eri: "Au... Um..."
