Eri: "Thank you, Amu... Thank you for forgiving me..."
*Although my opinion might not be worth much, being an outsider... I think the atmosphere between these two has become far more gentle.*
*I think, in the last minute or so... something fundamental about their relationship has changed.*
*That must be why they both look so at peace.*
*I wish that they could always be friends. They compliment each other well.*
*They clearly like one another a lot, so... it would be sad if they ever fell out again. Especially over a misunderstanding like this.*
Eri: "But I-I'm only going to say that once, you know?! S-Since I don't make a habit of prostrating myself before commoners!"
*Amu giggles.*
Amu: "It's all right. You don't need to say anything else. Knowing you and your big mouth, you'd just ruin the mood."
Eri: "E-Eh...?! W-What do you mean? H-How could I, Onodera Eri, ruin anything?! You should be glad I'm imparting even more of my wisdom on you, stupid Amu!"
Amu: "Kukuku~ As if I would be glad about an annoying, faux-bourgeois gangster like you talking to me. You're the one who should know your place."
Eri: "Gangster...? W-Why you, you jerk! I'm nothing of the sort! I-I'm a refined lady!"
Amu: "Kukuku~ Your true colors are showing right now, Eriri~ You're so unrefined, it's just a little bit adorable~"
Eri: "A-Adorable? N-No way...! S-Shut up or I'll smash your teeth in!"
*And then, since it's these two idiots...*
*That calm, peaceful atmosphere is destroyed in approximately thirty seconds.*
Noelle: "Hey, Atcchan..."
*Noelle walks towards me, a small frown on her face.*
Atcchan: "Yeah? What is it?"
Noelle: "I'm troubled."
Atcchan: "Why?"
Noelle: "I think... this is all wrong, somehow."
Atcchan: "Wrong?"
Noelle: "Yes. I did something bad. So I am a bad person. So..."
*Noelle frowns.*
Noelle: "Why aren't they angry with me?"
Noelle: "It's natural for people to be angry if somebody does something bad... but they're arguing with each other instead. I don't understand."
Atcchan: "Ah... Well..."
Atcchan: "Don't worry about it. Maybe they like fighting with each other more than they like fighting with anybody else?"
Noelle: "Oh. Is that so?"
Atcchan: "I suppose...?"
*This, too... might just be another way of showing love.*
Eri: "W-Why don't you just die in a fire, stupid Amu?!"
Amu: "Yes, yes~ You could use my ashes as a new type of concealer, then maybe your skin won't look so wrinkled~"
Eri: "M-My... My skin is not wrinkled, you hag...! Why don't you go look in a mirror?!"
Eri: "Oh, I'm sorry~ I forgot, you can't! Because your face is so hideous, it would make any mirror break! Hohohoh!"
*Albeit, a very twisted one...*
Amu: "Hello, Sir, and welcome to Amu Café!"
Atcchan: "Ah... H-Hey there, Amu."
Amu: "Heehee~ "
*Amu grins at me, hands on her hips.*
Amu: "Is there anywhere in particular you would like to sit? Will you be dining alone today? Or..."
*Her smile widens. There's something sneaky, almost simian, about it. It reminds me of the monkeys I saw on that school trip to the zoo all those years ago.*
Amu: "Did you, perchance, come here to gawp and stare at our very cute new waitress? Kukuku~ "
*Indeed, standing by Amu's side, her hair neatly curled and her face flushed, is another waitress. A new employee who only started working here a couple of weeks ago.*
*Her blond hair falls around her shoulders in curly waves like a golden waterfall. Her eyes are indigo, a penetrating shade of purple.*
*She's wearing a light brown maid outfit, complete with puffed sleeves and an apron. The frilly skirts shift around her legs with each movement, with a certain kind of grace.*
*In this café, where fancy outfits aren't required, she stands out like a sore thumb. This place isn't - as Amu has impressed upon me many times before - a maid café, after all.*
*Even though she's trying to hide behind Amu, her face lightly flushed, I can tell who it is at once.*
*She always did stand out, didn't she?*
Atcchan: "Ah... H-Hey there, Eri..."
Eri: "H-Hmph...!"
*She turns her head away, blond hair fluttering. It's such an Eri-ish reaction I can't help but smile.*
Eri: "W-Why are you conversing with me in such a familiar manner? I-Isn't that a little bit too forward...?"
Atcchan: "Ah, um... I'm sorry... I-I thought, since we were writing letters, that-"
Eri: "T-That doesn't mean anything, you moron! Letters aren't the same as face-to-face interaction! I-It's completely different...!"
Eri: "The rules are all different! Everything is different! A girl's heart is a delicate thing!"
Eri: "Y-You should try to have more tact for once...! H-Honestly...!"
Atcchan: "All right. I'll try..."
Eri: "A-And you can stop smiling, too! I-It's not like I'm glad to see you or anything, i-idiot...!"
*Aah...*
*Even though she looks a little different, the abrasive way she speaks hasn't changed at all.*
*I don't know why, but I find it comforting. I think that style of speech suits her.*
*It's not just Eri who looks different, either. Amu does, too.*
*Instead of wearing those soft sweaters she often favored, she's now wearing a pale green dress freckled with white spots. Her hair is a little longer, too, and tied up with a ribbon.*
*I-It... I...*
*Even though I'm not used to looking at Amu in such a way, I... think it's kind of cute...*
Amu: "Kukuku~ Where are you looking, Atcchan~?"
Atcchan: "A-Ah...! No, I, um..."
*My face turns red. I start to wave my hands before my face, lost for words. I-I didn't think she'd notice me looking...*
*I must've forgotten. Amu's eyes are sharp, like a hawk's. Nothing can get past her - especially not if that 'something' could be used as material to embarrass me...*
Atcchan: "I-I was just thinking, um... Y-You look different... A-Ahaha..."
Amu: "Ehehe~ Have you finally been bowled over by my good looks and charm? Have you, have you~?"
Atcchan: "Ah...! No, I just... I-I just-"
Eri: "Hmph. I-If you think she looks good, y-you should be thanking me..."
Atcchan: "Huh...?"
*I look at Eri.*
*Still staring down at the floor, her face flushed, she grips her hands against the hem of her skirt, eyes narrowed.*
Eri: "I was the one who chose that dress. I picked it out when we went shopping. It was all my idea."
Atcchan: "A-Ah... Is that so...?"
Eri: "Yes. Amu's no good at all with fashion. She'd probably wear potato sacks or garbage bags if I let her."
Amu: "Ehehe..."
*Amu giggles sheepishly, sticking out her tongue.*
Amu: "Well, I've never been so good at that kind of thing. It seems like a waste if you live out in the country. It's not like there's anybody I want to impress around here..."
Eri: "So you say, but..."
*Eri smirks.*
Eri: "Since you started dressing like that you've been getting a lo~ot more tips during work, haven't you?"
Amu: "I guess so... Even though I haven't really changed at all."
Amu: "People sure are stupid."
Eri: "It's true. People are stupid. They often judge others based on appearances, nothing more. But there's nothing wrong with taking advantage of that."
Amu: "Still, dressing up like this... It feels a strange. Like I'm wearing a disguise."
*Amu frowns, tugging at the hem of her dress.*
*I must admit, that dress looks strange to me too, given I'm not used to it. But it's not like it doesn't suit her. In actual fact... I think she looks quite nice.*
*I-It's too embarrassing to say something like that, though. N-Not to Amu. She is my childhood friend, after all.*
*Amu notices my flushed face and giggles.*
Amu: "Well~ It seems Atcchan likes it, anyway! "
*W-Waah...! Caught out again...!*
*I need to learn to stop staring when I get surprised. It must make me look so stupid...*
*I don't think an open-mouthed goldfish expression looks particularly becoming on anyone.*
Atcchan: "A-Au... W-Well, I, um, I... au..."
Eri: "Che."
*Eri clicks her tongue against the roof of her mouth.*
Eri: "What a typical response for a commoner like you. I'm not surprised at all."
Atcchan: "A-Ah, um... I-I'm sorry... I-I think you look pretty, too!"
Eri: "Huh? Y-You do?"
Atcchan: "Y-Yeah, um... That outfit... it really suits you!"
Eri: "Really...?"
Eri: "I-Isn't it a little too much? Since none of the other waitresses dress like this, I wasn't sure."
Atcchan: "W-Well, um... I-It does look a little unusual, but I think it suits you...!"
Eri: "Ehehe... Thanks."
Eri: "It wasn't my choice to wear this though, you know? It was Big Sis."
Atcchan: "It sounds like something she'd do."
Eri: "Yeah. When she heard I was gonna be working at a café she went nuts. She said any girl working at a café needs to look the part, especially if that girl is her cute little sister, and... well..."
Eri: "It kind of escalated from there."
Eri: "She ordered this before I could stop her, and... well..."
Eri: "I'd feel bad not wearing it, since it cost so much money, but..."
Eri: "It's still kind of embarrassing. I like pretty clothes, but this sort of outfit draws too much attention."
Eri: "Big Sis is such a blockhead."
Atcchan: "A-Ah, well, um... E-Even if the outfit is unusual, it does look good on you...! R-Really!"
Eri: "You think so?"
Atcchan: "Yeah, I do. I-I really do. I, u-um, I-"
Amu: "Kukuku..."
*But my failed attempts at flattery are cut short. They're cut short by that devilish giggle that I know so well.*
Amu: "Hohoooh? And what's this? Aren't you two getting along surprisingly well?"
Eri: "Kya!"
Eri: "A-Ah, no, I was just... Um, ah..."
Eri: "I-It's nothing, okay, stupid Amu? Nothing at all! I was just looking for some moral support!!!"
Amu: "Moral support? Are you suuure that's all it is?"
Eri: "O-Of course! I-Is it really so strange I'd want some comforting after spending so much time with a brute like you?!"
Eri: "I-It's not like I'm glad to see him again, s-so don't get the wrong idea...!"
*Amu's grin widens. She looks like a shark when she smirks like that...*
Amu: "I can't believe you're still so bad at being honest, Eriri - even after all this time~"
Amu: "I tried to work on my appearance to make you happy, buuuut... You haven't taken any of the lessons I gave you to heart at all, have you~? Kukuku~"
Eri: "A-Ah, well, um..."
Eri: "I-I don't need your advice, you moron! I-I already told you, I don't like Atcchan!"
Amu: "Really? Not one bit?"
Eri: "Not at all!"
Amu: "Even though you wrote him all those letters?"
Eri: "T-That doesn't mean anything! W-We're just friends!"
Amu: "'Just friends?' Is that what they're calling it now?"
Eri: "J-Just... J-Just shut up, okay?! This isn't any of your business!"
Amu: "My, my. Even though you're so young, you act like a crotchety old lady~"
Eri: "I, I... I-I do not act like an old lady! I'm simply being refined! Stupid Amu!"
Amu: "Old lady Eri!"
Eri: "Uneducated fool!"
Amu: "Wannabe gangster!"
Eri: "Sea slug brain!"
Atcchan: "E-Ehehe..."
*I watch as the two bicker back and forth. A customer coughs, trying to get their attention, but they ignore him.*
*Have they forgotten they're supposed to be working...?*
*This is so like them I can't help but smile.*
*They still squabble like young children, getting heated over the most pointless of things. And yet, despite that... although it may look like they hate each other...*
*I swear I can see them smiling.*
*The time goes by so quickly it almost feels as though it's being carried by wings. Without me even realizing it, the days slip past in a blur; the regular routine of my life in the city reestablished.*
*I wake up at 7:00 a.m. every morning, shrugging off my blankets and wiping the sleep dust from the corners of my eyes, then go to the bathroom to splash cold water on my face.*
*I get changed and go downstairs to eat breakfast with my parents - usually toast with jam, (my parents don't go in for making the large, hearty meals my grandparents do), with a glass of milk on the side.*
*That milk still hasn't made me any taller, and my bones don't feel particularly stronger, despite the advertising spiel, but it doesn't hurt to have hope. If I gave up on my height now, that would be like giving in; embracing my sad destiny with both arms wide open...*
*I brush my teeth, comb my hair, and fretfully examine my face in the bathroom mirror for while (those freckles are still there, just as visible as ever), before cutting my losses with a small sigh.*
*I pick up my schoolbag, sling it over one shoulder, bid goodbye to my parents, then leave; making my way to the train station.*
*Typically, I arrive at school at 8:00 a.m., and spend a while sitting in class, chatting to my friends, before the teacher arrives to start the school day.*
*After school, I hang around with Saki, Miho, and Yuuna - usually shopping, sometimes going to see a movie, and occasionally getting something light to eat in a nearby café.*
*After a few hours, I return home, finish my homework, eat dinner, watch overly sentimental TV dramas with my mother since we have very similiar tastes (my dad just sighs and rolls his eyes when we commandeer the big TV in the living room, but its two against one so he never wins), then go to sleep.*
*Rinse and repeat, over and over again - excepting weekends, of course.*
*It's a nice routine. Comfortable. Not exactly the most exciting, but how many people in this world can claim to do something uniquely interesting every single day?*
*If somebody had told me, just before I moved to the city, that I would soon fall into such a comfortable rut... I wouldn't have believed them. My nerves were shot by the mere prospect of moving, and thinking about it was enough to keep me up all night, gnawing at my fingernails.*
*I thought I'd never be able to adjust to such a busy, hectic lifestyle - but, truth be told, living here isn't all that different from my old life. I still have to go to school, I still have a small circle of friends, and I still watch TV dramas with my mother.*
*Although the city is far, far bigger than my old village, that isn't really relevant. I'm more than adept at tuning all the background noise out - existing solely inside this little sphere I've carved out for myself.*
*And so time goes on, the days, then weeks, then months, slipping into one another like drifts of snow...*
*Sometimes I exchange letters with Noelle and Amu. I call them on the phone, too. Amu's still working at her parents' café, complaining bitterly every step of the way - especially in the run-up to Christmas.*
*According to Amu, listening to the looping Christmas music over and over again while she waits tables and greets customers is nothing short of excruciating; a cruel and unusual kind of torture that makes her want to sew her own ears shut.*
*Noelle's family, meanwhile, have already gone on ahead with their plans to move. I think they left Japan in late July, when the weather was at its hottest and most overwhelming.*
*I wonder what England's like. Noelle's told me about it in her letters, and she says she isn't as bad as she thought it would be. I'm glad that she seems to be doing all right.*
*It must be a strange experience. I've never been outside of Japan before, so I can't help being curious. What is there to do in England, anyway? I've only ever seen it represented in movies as some dim, dismal place filled with rolling fog and old, stone buildings snaked with ivy.*
*It sounds like the kind of place Saki would like. In fact, I think she's jealous of Noelle. That girl would probably give her right arm, and a sizable chunk of her left leg, to go to England for a two week holiday - let alone live there.*
Saki: "The snow really is piling up out there..."
*Saki stares out of her bedroom window, back facing me, arms folded. I can see her face reflected in the window, just dimly.*
Saki: "Hey, Atcchan."
*Saki turns about, her hair fluttering around her shoulders. Her skin is pale, almost deathly so. Her skin is naturally pallid, but it becomes even more so in the winter - rendered ashen grey through lack of sunlight.*
*That pale skin is offset by the dark, black bags underneath her eyes, which make her eyes seem deep-set, slightly droopy.*
*I once asked her if she naturally had such large bags underneath her eyes, so black they look like bruises. She told me some of it was make-up, just to 'enhance the look.'*
*I'm not really sure why anybody would want to look like they haven't slept in five years, but this is Saki we're talking about, and I don't always understand her taste in aesthetics.*
Saki: "Are you cold? Do you want something to drink?"
Atcchan: "I, um... I'm fine. You don't need to worry about me."
Saki: "But of course I'll worry about you. You're one of my dear friends. And you're so little, too. I feel a single gust of wind could blow you away."
Atcchan: "A-Ahaha. I'll try to be careful."
Saki: "We have some cocoa powder in the kitchen. Or, at least, we should - if the brats haven't gotten to it first. Do you want a hot chocolate?"
*I raise my eyebrows, surprised.*
Atcchan: "Hot chocolate? I didn't know you liked things like that."
Saki: "I'm not the biggest fan. It is slightly too childish for my tastes. That's why I was offering it to you."
Atcchan: "But what are you going to have?"
Saki: "..."
Saki: "Warm human blood, of course - drawn freshly from a still-pulsing jugular."
Atcchan: "W-Waah...!"
*I whimper, throwing one hand against my neck in self defense.*
Atcchan: "D-Don't look at me when you say that! I'm not a blood bank! I-I could never give blood - I'm too afraid of needles!"
*I don't even like having injections when I go to see the doctor. I know it's silly, getting so worked up and anxious over something so small - something that only lasts a few seconds - but I still can't help it.*
*My face goes pale, my hands start to shake, and I can't relax, which only makes the sensation of the needle plunging into my skin even more acutely painful...*
Atcchan: "B-Besides, my blood wouldn't taste good! I eat sweets and chocolate all the time! It'd be far too sweet - and I know you don't eat a lot of sweet things, Saki."
Saki: "Hm... Well, that is a shame."
Saki: "Oh well. I will content myself with a hot tomato juice, then."
Atcchan: "You can drink hot tomato juice?"
Saki: "Of course. You just need to mix in lemon juice, pepper, and Tabasco sauce."
*I wince. I can feel my stomach churning simply at that description...*
*It sounds like the kind of thing Amu would mix into my cooking in home ec. class as a joke.*
Atcchan: "T-That... T-That sure sounds like something, all right."
Saki: "I'm sure a human like you could not understand. To walk the path of the vampire, shrouded in eternal darkness, is something mere mortals like you can never hope to accomplish."
Atcchan: "Ahaha... If being a human means I get to enjoy nice things, like hot chocolate, then I'm not sure I really want to be vampire."
*The two of us sit together on Saki's bed, our drinks resting on the small table to one side.*
*Saki's... concoction... sure looks interesting. Her glass is filled to the brim with a thick, deep red fluid that looks uncannily like blood...*
*I am a little curious about how it tastes, but... I've always been suspicious about garishly colored foods. Red just isn't a normal color for a drink, is it? Especially not a fierce, fiery red like that.*
*It practically screams 'don't drink me' - just like those poisonous frogs in the Amazon with the bright orange and acid green bodies.*
Saki: "Hm... Hm, hm, hm~ "
*Humming tunelessly under her breath, Saki shuffles her pack of tarot cards. I watch her, frowning.*
Atcchan: "So... Why do you want to tell my fortune all of a sudden?"
Saki: "Because it's nearly New Year's Eve; a time for new beginnings."
Saki: "In these times of tumult, is there any more perfect a moment to attempt to divine the future?"
Atcchan: "Like the slips you get at the shrine on New Year's, you mean?"
Saki: "No. It's far, far more precise than that. Those slips at New Year's are only worth anything to the most neurotic and superstitious."
*And tarot cards aren't?*
Saki: "Ah... This should be enough."
*With this declaration, Saki finishes her shuffling.*
*She places the first three cards in her deck face down on the bedspread, as though setting up a game of solitaire, then sets the rest of the pack down to one side.*
Saki: "Now then..."
*An eerie smile slowly spreads across her face.*
Saki: "Are you ready to see what the cards have in store for you? Do you think you can face it? Fufufu..."
*Her laughter trails away eerily, lost in the sound of the snow outside, drumming gently against the windowpanes.*
*I gulp.*
*I'm not usually a superstitious person, but... since Saki's taking it so seriously, it's hard not to get sucked in...*
*I look at the cards anxiously, my heart drumming inside my chest. Just what cards are there in a standard tarot deck, anyway? If I knew, maybe I'd be able to mentally prepare myself.*
Saki: "All right. Let's see what we have here..."
*Saki reaches forwards with one hand, white and ghostly, her black nail polish standing out like squid ink on snow.*
Saki: "The first card represents your past - things that have already been. And, in your past, we have..."
*She flips over the first card with a well-practiced motion.*
*I've seen her use these cards with various people at school before. In fact, it's almost become like a business.*
*Saki spends most of her lunch break sitting in class, reading tarot cards for girls and guys interested in their fortunes - usually those pertaining to love or money.*
*I don't know how many people really believe in her fortunes, but Saki is very good at making them sound realistic. I think it's something about the tone of her voice - low and mysterious, deadly serious.*
Saki: "Aah... I see. Interesting."
*Saki draws in a breath as she flips over the first card. It's an image of an old tower, so intricately detailed it almost seems to crumble while I stare at it.*
*I blink in confusion, looking between Saki and the card.*
*What does that mean?*
Atcchan: "Is it something about... a poorly constructed building? Should I be on the look out for rogue architects?"
Saki: "No, it doesn't mean either of those things. It's the lightning struck tower."
Atcchan: "Lightning?"
*I don't know if I like the sound of that.*
Saki: "Mm. It represents sudden change. Can you think of a moment in your past that this might relate to?"
Atcchan: "Ah..."
*My breath catches in my throat. It doesn't take long for me to think of a fitting memory.*
*When I had to move from my old village. When my parents brought me here. That would definitely count as a 'sudden change', wouldn't it...?*
*I start to tremble, even though it's not particularly cold in Saki's room, and the hot chocolate has helped to warm me up.*
*That really is uncanny. Is it just a coincidence, or... is there something more?*
Saki: "Fufu... I see, I see. The cards really do know everything. You shouldn't try to doubt them, Atcchan."
Atcchan: "H-How did you know?"
Saki: "I could tell by the look on your face. But, if you doubt the cards... they might become displeased."
Atcchan: "D-Displeased?"
Saki: "Yes. And then the fortune you receive... may be rather unpleasant. Rather unpleasant indeed..."
Atcchan: "Eep..."
Saki: "And, for the second card... Your present..."
*Saki extends her hand once more, reaching towards the middle card laid on the bed.*
Saki: "Aha. I see, I see. Now, that is interesting..."
Atcchan: "W-What is?"
Saki: "This card..."
*Saki taps the newly unveiled card with one finger.*
Saki: "... is the chariot. It represents assertiveness, progress. The ability to overcome trials - to develop as a human being. A positive card."
Atcchan: "Ah... Thank goodness..."
*I breathe a sigh of relief.*
*I'm not entirely sure how accurate this card is, though. Was I really able to overcome a trial?*
*Maybe I did manage to overcome some kind of test, and I didn't even realize I was taking it.*
Saki: "And now... the final card..."
*Saki reaches forwards, letting her fingers play over the card for a few moments; skirting close to it, but not picking it up.*
*I wince. Is she toying with me? Why doesn't she just pick up the card already?*
*A tense silence fills the room, broken by the slow, repetitive drumming of snow against the window... or maybe that sound isn't snow. Perhaps it's an echo of the erratic beating of my own heart.*
*Could it be...?*
*W-Will this card... show me something incredible, something amazing; a future I could only dream about? Or else...*
*I think back to the first card: the image of the ruined tower, struck by lightning. Desolation and despair.*
*Death.*
*Isn't that one of the tarot cards? The only one I really know about - whose meaning seems obvious, even to a complete novice like me.*
*I don't want Saki to draw that card for my future. W-Who wants their future to be spelled out with the image of a grinning skull? T-That would be far too much of a bad omen...!*
*If the card lying on the bed, facedown, is revealed to be something that depressing... I don't know if I'll be able to stand it...!*
*Aah... What could it be, what could it be? I want to know and yet, at the same time, I don't...!*
Saki: "The final card... The card that represents your future..."
*I inhale, hard, hardly daring to breathe.*
*She picks it up between her fingers, slowly, ready to turn it over, when...*
Honoka: "Big Sis, Big Sis! Come and play with me!"
Ruka: "Yeah! Let's play, let's play!"
Kei: "Let's watch Heidi! I wanna watch Heidi!"
Saki: "K-Kyaaa...!"
*Saki's body is, all of a sudden, buried by a deluge of children - a downpour of sharp elbows and kicking legs and flailing limbs.*
*Three of Saki's younger siblings are piled on top of her, all bundled up in thick, white coats and scarves and mittens so they look like snowmen.*
Saki: "H-Hey... You guys..."
*Saki tries to claw her way out from underneath her screaming, shrieking siblings, pushing herself upright once more with a great deal of determination.*
*Her siblings, giggling, are thrown off her lap; falling to the floor with three dull thuds.*
*Even though Saki looks so slender, so waifish, so pale, she must have some serious energy reserves stored somewhere. I'm impressed.*
Saki: "Weren't you out shopping with Mom and Dad?"
Honoka: "We were, we were!"
Kei: "We just came back just now!"
Ruka: "I got a new pair of mittens, look!"
Kei: "I wanted a new pair too!"
Ruka: "But mine had a hole in them and yours didn't!"
Honoka: "It was snowing!"
Kei: "We had a snowball fight!"
Ruka: "I won, I won!"
Kei: "No you didn't, I did!"
Honoka: "Want to play with Big Sis!"
Ruka: "Let's play in the snow!"
Kei: "Snowball fight, snowball fight!"
Ruka: "I'll beat you this time!"
*Even though only three of Saki's siblings are crowded into her room, the fourth conspicuously absent, one might be forgiven for thinking there are at least fifteen young children running around, screaming, judging by how energetic they are.*
*Saki's bedroom, much like the rest of her home, is rather small, and packing so many young children into such a cramped space can only end in disaster.*
*Saki senses this, too, because she gets to her feet, all fortune telling pretensions cut short for the time being, as she steps into the role of the reliable big sister.*
Saki: "All right, you guys. I'll go and play with you once. Just once. I'll join you in a few minutes. But you have to promise to get out of my room, okay? I don't want you breaking anything."
Saki's siblings: "Okaaay..."
*Her siblings chorus in unison, wide smiles on their pink faces, as they shuffle out of her room; contented for now.*
Saki: "Geez... What a handful..."
*Upon their exit, Saki sighs, sinking down against her bed with a dull flump.*
Saki: "You see what I have to put up with, Atcchan? It's a nightmare."
Atcchan: "I thought you handled it rather well."
Saki: "I have to handle it well. If I lose my temper, they'll just start to cry."
*She groans, stretching her arms above her head; clicking her joints at both her elbows, then her wrists for good measure.*
Saki: "I'm sorry I didn't get to finish, Atcchan. You must have wanted to know your future."
Atcchan: "Ah, no, it's fine. I'm sure I'll be able to get over it!"
*Besides, I'd be lying if I said I wasn't just a little bit relieved at the sudden distraction posed by Saki's siblings. Noisy as they are, they have their uses.*
Saki: "You sure you're sure? You don't want me to do it again, do you?"
Atcchan: "No, it's fine, really! In fact, I think I prefer it this way."
Saki: "Hm? What do you mean?"
Atcchan: "I mean, um... Not knowing the future... I think that's more exciting than having it told to you. Things are always the most fun when you don't know, precisely, what's going to happen... right?"
Saki: "Hm. Maybe so. Maybe the unpredictability of life... is part of its charm."
*Saki smiles sardonically.*
Saki: "Of course, it's easy to say that if one doesn't have so many young siblings."
Saki: "Being jumped on and shouted at all the time isn't particularly pleasant. I think, for the sake of my health, I would like some kind of advanced warning beforehand."
Atcchan: "Ahaha. I guess I didn't think of that..."
Saki: "It's all right. Maybe we have different ways of looking at the world."
Atcchan: "Maybe we do. But, um..."
Saki: "'Um?' What do you mean, 'um?'"
Atcchan: "Well, I..."
Atcchan: "Even if we are a little different, I... I like you all the same, Saki."
Saki: "Heh. You charmer, you."
Atcchan: "I-I wasn't trying to be...! I was just telling you how I feel!"
Saki: "I know, I know - but please, forgive me. I am not one for such open displays of sentimentality. However..."
*She smiles softly, playing about with a strand of her hair.*
Saki: "I suppose it would not kill me if I told you... I like you an awful lot, too."
Atcchan: "Y-You mean... you want to stay my friend?"
Saki: "Of course I do. I can think of nothing I would like more."
Atcchan: "Nothing?"
Saki: "Well... Almost nothing."
*Saki grins, rising to her feet; the joints in her knees clicking this time.*
Saki: "Right now, what I want to do, more than anything in the world... is show those annoying little siblings of mine what happens when they cross the great Saki, Eternal Queen of the Night."
Atcchan: "Is the Eternal Queen of the Night well-versed in snowball fights?"
Saki: "She's more than well-versed in them. She's the best - and she's going to make them rue the day that they were ever born."
Saki: "If she has some help from her faithful assistant, of course."
Atcchan: "Of course. I'd be more than happy to help you. That's what friends are for, after all!"
Atcchan: "Um... I was wondering..."
Tsuzumi: "Yes? What is it, little boy?"
*Tsuzumi smirks, arms folded, leaning forwards against the counter. Instinctively, I back away, just as one would do when confronted with a venomous viper.*
*And Tsuzumi might be even more dangerous than that.*
Atcchan: "Um, well, I..."
Atcchan: "I don't want to sound rude or intrusive but, um..."
Tsuzumi: "You are going to do so anyway - simply to satisfy your own selfish curiosity? Is that right?"
*Well, I suppose that is right, but... why did she have to frame it like that? She just wants to make me feel as guilty as possible, doesn't she?*
*And the worst thing is, it's working.*
*I gulp. Although the interior of this store is fairly cold, the windows shut and blinds drawn, my face feels hot.*
Atcchan: "I, um... I just... I-I was wondering... what you've been drawing..."
Tsuzumi: "Hm? You were peeking at my work, were you?"
Atcchan: "I-It's work?"
*Like college work? Is she a part-time student? But wouldn't that just eat up more money? Money I don't understand how she earns, given how few customers she seems to get?*
*Maybe it isn't academic. Maybe it's something more suspicious...*
*But what?*
Tsuzumi: "Yes, work. The thing that people do to make money. An occupation, you know?"
Atcchan: "B-But I thought you worked at this store?"
*Tsuzumi waves one hand carelessly.*
Tsuzumi: "That's more of a hobby than an actual 'job.' I took over this store because it's what Grandpa would have wanted, but working in retail is such a pain."
Tsuzumi: "There are always so many people coming in trying to interrupt me, asking me all these questions, like it's my duty to give a damn..."
*A long-suffering sigh.*
Tsuzumi: "It's all so boring. Life's too short to spend time talking to people. Especially people who want to know if I sell any Meiji period vases, or if I can put their purchases in a carrier bag, or whatever."
*But when you work at a shop, shouldn't you expect people to talk to you? I wonder if Tsuzumi's grandfather would really be happy if he knew his granddaughter was deliberately sabotaging the future of his beloved store like this...*
*And I wouldn't exactly call the amount of customers this place gets 'so many.' If anything, I'd term it 'virtually nonexistent.'*
Atcchan: "J-Just what is your definition of 'too many' people?"
Tsuzumi: "More than zero."
*Her response is so curt, too!*
Tsuzumi: "After my continued efforts, I've been able to drive most of my clientele away. When I'm really lucky, I'll go a whole week without anybody coming in here at all. But there's always one or two who never quite get the message..."
*She glares at me. I whimper.*
*Does she want me to go away that badly?*
Tsuzumi: "Drawing is my real job, my true passion. I write manga."
Atcchan: "H-Huh?"
*I stare at Tsuzumi, my mouth falling open like that of a hooked fish.*
*She's... a manga artist? Really?*
*So that's how she's able to keep this store running, despite the complete absence of customers?*
*I wonder what kind of manga she draws. Is it romance, action, horror? Does she publish it under a pen name? And how did she get to be a manga artist, anyway? Isn't it really hard to get into that industry?*
*I'm impressed. I certainly didn't expect that.*
*For a while there, I was convinced she kept this store running through other, illegal means...*
Tsuzumi: "Fufu~ You look as though you've found a chicken fetus in your boiled egg~ "
*W-What a horrible simile...*
Atcchan: "I-I was a little surprised, that's all. I-I didn't expect... I mean... I-I've never met anybody who draws manga before. T-That's kind of cool..."
Tsuzumi: "It is cool, isn't it? I really am the best. Fufu~"
*At least my compliments seem to be having some kind of effect. She looks more cheery than she did a few minutes ago.*
*However...*
Tsuzumi: "..."
*Her face darkens.*
*With a frown, she taps one finger against her lower lip. Her dark nail polish applied to her long, sharp talons, flashes dangerously under the dim lighting.*
Tsuzumi: "I seem to be having writer's block lately. I'm all out of ideas."
Atcchan: "Even manga artists can have writer's block?"
Tsuzumi: "Of course. Although it involves more drawing than writing, I still need to create a solid story and some good characters. But..."
*Tsuzumi glances down at the sheets of paper spread across the counter dispassionately.*
*With a sigh, she sweeps it all to one side, off onto the floor, crumpling the paper as she does so.*
Tsuzumi: "It's hopeless. I can't think of anything. I have no good ideas. I can't even think of what to call my characters, or how they should look."
Tsuzumi: "I should probably go people watching at some point to get some inspiration... but that's no good either. I hate people."
*I can imagine that designing characters might be kind of difficult if you don't like talking to people. It must be hard coming up with individual, unique characters if you never deign to associate with others.*
Tsuzumi: "And my team quit on me, too. Said something about 'artistic differences'-"
*Here she makes quotey marks with her fingers, her face distinctly unimpressed.*
Tsuzumi: "-and how I'm 'too strict' - that I 'expect too much' from them. But is there anything so wrong with expecting perfection?!"
*Tsuzumi jabs a finger at me, her sharp fingernail stopping just a few inches away from my eyes.*
Tsuzumi: "What's the point of creating something if you don't aim for perfection?! If you try with anything less than 110%%, you might as well not bother at all! Don't you think so?!"
*She's really getting fired up about this...*
*I worry, if I say no, she might just gouge one of my eyes out. And I wouldn't like that.*
*If I didn't have any eyes, how would I be able to watch the season finale of that soap opera I was watching with my mother?*
*I'd never even get to find out if the two leads got together or not - and Emiko was trying so hard, too...!*
Atcchan: "Um, I... I-I agree! Y-You really have to try your best, don't you?"
Tsuzumi: "..."
*Tsuzumi stares at me for a while with those dark purple eyes, deep and murky like pools of black tea.*
*It's impossible for me to tell what she's thinking - and I'm not entirely sure if I want to know, either.*
Tsuzumi: "..."
*Finally, after a long pause, she replies.*
Tsuzumi: "... That's right. You're right. For once."
*Was that 'for once' necessary?*
Tsuzumi: "There's no point trying if you don't give it your all, so I don't need people like that on my creative team. They can get out and go die for all I care. But..."
Tsuzumi: "I only have four months left. If I can't come up with an idea soon, I won't have enough time to meet the deadline... and I wouldn't want to let down my fans."
Tsuzumi: "What should I do? What should I do?"
*A long pause.*
*Is this my cue to leave?*
Atcchan: "A-All right, well... I-It was nice to talk to you. I-I need to find a present for my friend, so-"
Tsuzumi: "Wait! Hold it right there, mister! Did I say that you could leave?!"
Atcchan: "Aaah...! I'm sorry...!"
*I jump, my body tensing. What does she want?*
*Tsuzumi frowns, still tapping that sharp fingernail against her lower lip. I'm transfixed by it. I can't budge an inch.*
*You could kill a man with fingernails like that. You could slice through his chest like a knife through butter and tear all the internal organs to ribbons.*
*Against an enraged Tsuzumi... I wouldn't stand a chance. I'd have more luck fighting against a bear.*
Tsuzumi: "Normally, I would never ask for a favor from a person like you. In fact, simply contemplating it makes me feel as though I'm going to throw up in my mouth. However..."
Tsuzumi: "Desperate times call for desperate measures. I need a few people to bounce ideas off of, or else I'll never be able to come up with a solid story."
Tsuzumi: "And so... out of the benevolence of my heart, I will give you an opportunity to impress me. You've got the job! Welcome to the team, you little rat!"
*I stare at Tsuzumi, blinking once.*
*Twice.*
*Thrice.*
*No matter how many times I blink, the scene before me doesn't shift. It remains the same - stubbornly so.*
*I pinch my arm.*
Atcchan: "O-Ow..."
*It hurts.*
*It hurts because this isn't a dream. This really is... real...*
*All I wanted to do was buy a present for Saki - but somehow, I stumbled into a job interview instead... and I had no idea until it was too late!*
Atcchan: "I... I-I'm sorry, but... I don't know anything about publishing manga."
Tsuzumi: "That's fine. You read it, don't you?"
Atcchan: "A little...?"
Tsuzumi: "Then you can still help. Even a complete idiot will have one or two good ideas in their lifetime - even if the strain of thinking it up destroys their tiny brain. But we must keep going for the greater good."
*S-So she doesn't care if I die?!*
Atcchan: "But, but... why would you ask me for help? You hardly even know me."
*Tsuzumi shrugs.*
Tsuzumi: "That's completely irrelevant. I know you're a weak-willed, spineless person who'll go along with what I want and not disobey me - which is more than enough for now."
Atcchan: "I-I can still say 'no', you know!"
Tsuzumi: "But you're not going to."
Atcchan: "H-How do you know?"
Tsuzumi: "Because you're too afraid."
Tsuzumi: "I don't know if you've realized it, but you're trembling. Fufu~"
Atcchan: "Wah..."
*The worst thing is... she's right. I'm not going to oppose her. I wouldn't be able to.*
*I feel my cheeks heating up. I clench my hands into fists, trying to stem the shaking, but it doesn't work.*
*Why is she so sharp?*
Atcchan: "B-But I... I-I wanted to buy Saki a present..."
Tsuzumi: "Saki?"
*Tsuzumi raises an eyebrow.*
Tsuzumi: "Who cares about Saki? My career is far, far more important than any girlfriend you might have back in the city."
Atcchan: "S-Saki isn't my girlfriend...!"
Tsuzumi: "I don't care if she's the Princess of Monaco. She's not important. Delete her from your mind. From now on, you will be working for me, and I will tolerate no distractions!"
Atcchan: "Ah, um... Y-Yes..."
Tsuzumi: "Yes what?"
Atcchan: "Y-Yes, Miss...?"
Tsuzumi: "Good boy. You keep that behavior up and maybe you'll get a treat."
Atcchan: "T-Thank you, Miss..."
*I hang my head, my face flushed. I feel like a trained dog. I half-expect Tsuzumi to throw me a tennis ball, or order me to play dead...*
Tsuzumi: "And bring in your friend waiting outside. The girl with the pink hair and the awful fashion sense. I want her on board, too."
Atcchan: "Y-You knew Amu was here all along?"
Tsuzumi: "Of course I knew. I'm not blind - and I'm not stupid, either."
Atcchan: "W-Well... A-All right then. I can ask her, but I don't know if she'll like the idea..."
Tsuzumi: "You think I care what she wants?"
Atcchan: "No. Probably not."
*Not based on how she's been treating me, anyway.*
*I don't think Tsuzumi cares about anybody other than Tsuzumi.*
Amu: "Um... H-Hello, Tsuzumi."
Tsuzumi: "The same to you, Amu. It has been a long time since we last spoke, hasn't it?"
Amu: "Yes... And I was hoping to keep it that way."
Tsuzumi: "Fufu~ How cold. Your words wound me. Not as much as they wounded my little sister, however."
Amu: "Can we leave Eri out of this? She isn't even here!"
Tsuzumi: "Even if Eri isn't here in person, she's always here in spirit, inside my heart! We sisters are linked by a bond stronger than blood - a tie that can never be severed, no matter what!"
Amu: "Eriri was right. You really are a creep."
Tsuzumi: "D-Don't call my beloved little sister 'Eriri' like that! It's uncouth!"
Amu: "It is?"
Tsuzumi: "That's right! You're not her friend anymore so you lost the right to act all familiar with her! Only I can call her Eriri!"
Amu: "Ha. What a desperate woman. The face you're pulling right now is kind of gross, you know?"
Tsuzumi: "Oh, Amu - poor, short-sighted Amu. How I pity you."
Amu: "You pity me?"
Tsuzumi: "Indeed. Finding the beautiful love shared between two blood-related sisters gross... It's enough to make my heart wither."
Tsuzumi: "My feelings for Eri aren't 'gross', they're touching and heartfelt - pure enough to bring a swan to tears!"
Tsuzumi: "Truly, you must be a brute to look past such an expression of pure love! You are a tainted woman, and you should douse yourself in water and pray for forgiveness!"
Amu: "Tainted? Me?"
Tsuzumi: "Yes. Tainted. You."
Amu: "Now look here... The only 'tainted' one I can see is you and your weird obsession for Eriri!"
Tsuzumi: "My love for my little sister is not weird, it's perfectly natural! As her big sister, it's normal that I should want to look out for her! You just can't understand that level of devotion, you harpy!"
Amu: "Harpy? That's funny, coming from a worthless, washed-up siscon like you."
Atcchan: "Um, hey... You guys..."
*I sit there meekly, looking between Amu and Tsuzumi.*
*The two women are glaring at one another, their eyes narrowed into slits. Amu's right hand is curled up into a fist, and Tsuzumi is grinding her teeth so hard I worry she might sand them down.*
*Whenever I think they're going to run out of insults, they manage to dredge up a new round of ammunition, and the fight continues just like before.*
*I have to admire their tenacity, if nothing else... but now I'm starting to get worried.*
*What if one of them loses their temper and tries to physically attack the other? Would it be my duty to get between them?*
*But, when faced with the prospect of being rent asunder by Tsuzumi's claws, my whole body starts to shake.*
*What should I do...?*
Tsuzumi: "Listen, Amu. I'm going to be perfectly honest with you."
*Tsuzumi surveys Amu with a disdain even more pointed than the one she showed me, her words dripping with venom more profuse than a snake's bite.*
Tsuzumi: "I don't like you. You were mean to my little sister and that's a crime that can never be forgiven. However..."
Tsuzumi: "I need some help. Did you know I write manga?"
Amu: "Manga?"
*Amu blinks slowly. She looks just as taken aback as I was. I guess she doesn't know about Tsuzumi's lucrative side-job either.*
Amu: "You really write manga?"
Tsuzumi: "That's right~"
Amu: "And it's proper manga?"
Tsuzumi: "Mmhmm~"
Amu: "And you have fans?"
Tsuzumi: "Of course~ Quite a lot of them, actually~ "
Amu: "Ooh... That's kind of cool..."
*Amu looks impressed in spite of herself.*
Amu: "No, wait a minute..."
*She shakes her head, hard, her pink ponytail bobbing.*
Amu: "This is no time to be impressed! And this has nothing to do with me, either!"
Tsuzumi: "But it does. You see..."
Tsuzumi: "Out of my own goodwill I, Onodera Tsuzumi, would like to invite you to become a member of my creative team!"
*Tsuzumi grins, elbows resting on the counter, her fingertips pressed together in a pose all too reminiscent of a mad scientist...*
Tsuzumi: "Fufu~ Isn't this exciting? It's like a plot device in one of your romance stories, isn't it?"
*Amu winces. It looks as though her defenses are crumbling.*
Tsuzumi: "And besides... I've already got this fine figure of a man on board, too~"
*With not a trace of irony in her voice, even though it's undoubtedly obvious she doesn't mean a single thing she says, Tsuzumi gestures towards me.*
Tsuzumi: "Think about it. I'm giving you an opportunity to spend more time with your childhood friend."
Tsuzumi: "A new relationship could bloom. Feelings, which before have gone unnoticed, could flourish overnight~ Who wouldn't want that?"
Amu: "W-Well I... Um..."
*Amu's face flushes.*
Amu: "It's not like I need an excuse to spend time with Atcchan! He'd want to come and see me regardless, because I'm so amazing! A-And anyway..."
Amu: "There's no way you could write manga! That must be some kind of joke!"
Tsuzumi: "Of course not. I never joke about business."
Tsuzumi: "I've been working on my newest release, but it's been difficult. My whole creative team quit on me, and I don't have anybody to help out. They said I was unapproachable and unreasonable - can you imagine that?"
Amu: "Oh no. I have no idea where they could've possibly got that impression from."
Tsuzumi: "I know, right?"
Tsuzumi: "All I have left on my team, other than that boy over there, is Paya - and she has about as much creativity as a dead jellyfish."
*Paya...?*
Tsuzumi: "She's good at doing the boring jobs, but her insight is no good at all! She couldn't come up with a decent story if it fell onto her head!"
Tsuzumi: "As such, I need to ask a few more people. You can see my dilemma, can't you?"
Amu: "And you don't have any other friends you can go ask?"
Tsuzumi: "I don't like people, other than my adorable little sister. I try to avoid them as much as possible - so, quite frankly, I don't. I don't have any friends, and I'm happy about it, too!"
Amu: "Whoa... You must lead quite a sad life. I'm almost starting to feel sorry for you, old woman."
*Tsuzumi surveys Amu archly, one eyebrow raised.*
Tsuzumi: "Life is whatever you make of it. Why should I try to act in a manner that suits your stipulations?"
Tsuzumi: "I am perfectly happy the way I am, thank you, and I would appreciate it if you could stop answering back. If I wanted to give somebody else the last word, I would buy a parrot."
*Amu sighs, shrugging her shoulders. It looks like she's finally given in.*
*Maybe she couldn't be bothered to keep arguing. Against Tsuzumi, victory may be impossible...*
Amu: "Okay, okay. Whatever. Have it your way."
Tsuzumi: "I will. I always do. Fufu~"
*Why does she look so smug...?*
Tsuzumi: "Any~way. I need some character designs for my new manga, and I need them as soon as possible! Get to work, you two!"
Atcchan: "Y-You mean... we're going to start right now?"
Tsuzumi: "Of course. There's no time like the present."
Atcchan: "But... B-But we don't even know what kind of manga you write. W-What kind of characters do you want?"
Tsuzumi: "Why? Isn't it obvious?"
*Tsuzumi smiles in a cloyingly sweet, saccharine manner which makes my teeth hurt. I think I just got a cavity...*
Tsuzumi: "Of course, a beautiful, charming, elegant girl like me would only write those kinds of stories~ Fufufu~"
Amu: "It's torture porn, isn't it? Really gross, anatomically incorrect torture porn. I can feel it in my bones."
Tsuzumi: "Of course not, silly Amu~ Kya~aa, saying something so embarrassing, I might blush! "
*I think her 'shy maiden' act would be more convincing if she wasn't snickering like that...*
Tsuzumi: "I'm a pretty young woman in the prime of her life... so, of course, I could only write one kind of story! Light, cute, fluffy stories, just like strawberry shortcake, filled with love and hope and happiness~! "
Amu: "Meaning?"
Tsuzumi: "I write romance stories, of course. Ehehe~ "
*I stare at Tsuzumi in shock. Amu does the same, her lips parted in a small 'o'.*
*The two of us turn to look at one another, our expressions equally disbelieving... and then we look back at Tsuzumi.*
*She's smiling so angelically, giggling into one hand like a refined princess from an all-girls school, that there might as well be a border of flowers blooming around her.*
*This is so completely at odds with her earlier character I can't help but gawp.*
Amu: "N-No way...! That's impossible!"
Atcchan: "Do you know much about manga, Amu?"
Amu: "Hm... I am quite partial to girls' manga, ehehe. Especially the ones with lots of hearts and sparkles!"
Atcchan: "Oh yeah..."
*I recall the glossy volume of manga she was flipping through back at the bookstore. I was surprised to see her so engrossed in something that looked so pink, so sweet, so decidedly un-Amu-like.*
*She's been a tomboy ever since I've known her, climbing up trees and scuffing her knees, catching bugs, and getting food all over herself while eating. I guess there's a side to her I don't know about, that she's never shown me before.*
*To be honest, I find it kind of endearing. Although I haven't read much romance manga myself, I have watched a lot of soap operas, which have similar kinds of storylines, don't they? They're both romances, at any rate.*
*Maybe Amu and I have more in common than I thought.*
Atcchan: "If you read a lot of romantic stories, shouldn't it be easy to design characters?"
Amu: "If only it were that simple..."
*Amu sighs.*
Amu: "I read a lot of the stories, but... I'm really bad at drawing."
Atcchan: "Ahaha... Same here."
*I laugh awkwardly, rubbing the back of my neck with one hand. I think Tsuzumi might have picked the wrong people for the job here.*
*I just hope, if we fail to produce anything worthwhile, she won't get too mad.*
*What if she tries to fillet us? I'm sure Amu would be able to protect me, but... I'd like to get something drawn onto this paper, just in case.*
*But I can't think of a single thing.*
*This is a lot harder than I thought it would be.*
*Maybe I should approach it from a different angle...*
Atcchan: "What kind of characters are you interested in?"
Amu: "Huh? What do you mean? You mean, like, my romantic preferences?"
Atcchan: "Um, well... N-Not really that, per say. M-More like, um... Let's start with the heroine."
Amu: "There's a heroine?"
Atcchan: "I... I assume so. Most of the TV dramas I watch have heroines..."
Amu: "Why not a hero? There are some romance stories with male main characters."
Atcchan: "But aren't the ones that follow men usually aimed at men?"
Amu: "Mm... You might be right."
*Amu nods her head, her ponytail bouncing.*
Amu: "Most of the romance series I've read have female protagonists."
Atcchan: "It's because they assume the reader will be female, so they want a main character the audience can relate to. Right?"
Amu: "That's right. So, for a main character... we want somebody relatable?"
Atcchan: "I guess so."
Amu: "But that's so vague!"
*Amu sighs, throwing her hands up in the air in defeat.*
Amu: "There are too many people in the world! Making a heroine that everyone can relate to is impossible!"
Atcchan: "Well, it really would be impossible to appeal to everyone... We shouldn't try to be so broad, I guess. Just focus on a common character archetype, maybe?"
Amu: "But if we make a character based on clichés, that'd be so boring. Who wants to read about some cute but shy, clumsy, homely girl who's good at cooking and sewing and never ever says 'no?'"
Atcchan: "T-There's nothing wrong with that kind of character... But I think they might be a little overdone."
*I frown, placing my thumb underneath my lower lip as I think.*
*In the TV dramas I've been watching lately, this kind of 'wholesome' female protagonist is very popular.*
*I don't find it too jarring, since I actually relate to that kind of character type (minus the highly accomplished housework skills, of course. I can't sew or cook to save my life), but...*
*I'm sure some people who don't fit those prerequisites would find it irritating to only see one type of character represented.*
*Since there aren't many male characters I feel I can relate to all that much, I naturally started to watch TV shows and movies aimed at women, with female main characters.*
*I found I related a lot more to the shy and self-conscious female heroines than I did to the cool, confident men who populate crime dramas and action movies - even though I'm not the target audience for those cheesy, melodramatic soaps.*
*What would the 'target audience' want, then? Maybe it's hard for me to come up with ideas since I'm a guy. I don't know.*
*I sigh.*
*I wonder... Just who is Tsuzumi's target audience, anyway? She said she wrote 'romances', but she never specified if they were for men or women, or what the characters should be like.*
Amu: "You know... there's no guarantee this is a romance story between a man and a woman, either."
Atcchan: "I was thinking the same. Tsuzumi didn't give us much information to work with."
Amu: "And, knowing Tsuzumi... this manga of hers could be really weird. Like, really, really weird."
Atcchan: "What do you mean, 'really, really weird?'"
Amu: "Well... I don't know. She's a pretty strange person, that's all."
Atcchan: "I... I guess that might be true. She is a little odd, I suppose."
Amu: "She's more than a 'little.' I have no idea what a woman like that would want to write about - and I'm not sure if I want to know, either."
*Amu and I look at one another, pencils in hand. Amu twirls hers about, spinning it as though performing some kind of circus trick. I almost feel like I should applaud her dexterity.*
*It's kind of impressive - even though the paper Tsuzumi gave us just as white and unblemished as before.*
Atcchan: "So... I guess we're back to square one, huh?"
Amu: "Yeah. I have no idea what to do."
Atcchan: "W-We could at least try to think of some characters, I guess?"
Amu: "We could try. Let's start with a female protagonist, then."
Atcchan: "R-Right! I'll do my best!"
*This shouldn't be too hard, should it? With our combined knowledge of girls' manga and TV dramas we should be able to come up with something!*
*... That is, of course, unless this project Tsuzumi's roped us into is more suspect than she's letting on.*
*As I stare down at my drawing, a heavy feeling begins to form in the pit of my stomach, as though I've swallowed an anchor.*
*I can't believe it. After almost two hours of discussion with Amu, designing and redesigning over and over again, this is all I have to show for it. This.*
*How could this be it, after such a long time? I-Is my creative vision really so weak? Do we really lack so much imagination?*
*If Tsuzumi sees this strange character we've concocted, she won't be happy. She won't be happy at all.*
*Amu and I tried to throw as many ideas into one character as possible but, instead of ending up a richly flavored and varied dish... it came out all wrong - like trying to make a curry with all the rancid leftovers lurking at the back of the fridge.*
*The end result is completely inedible.*
*This character has the long, straight black hair of a traditional romance heroine, with the same slender body... but Amu decided this wasn't adventurous enough, and decided to dress her up in some really outlandish clothes.*
*She's wearing some kind of military-style shirt, and then a light pink, ruffled skirt 'to add some cuteness!'*
*She's wearing the loose, white socks of a typical schoolgirl, and has a sailor style hat balanced on top of her head.*
*Our girl is complete with a patch over one eye - 'To add to that mysterious effect!' - and cat ears and a tail - 'Because they're popular!' - and also seems to be sporting vampire fangs.*
*Is our girl an army general? A vampire? A cat girl? A schoolgirl? A magical girl?*
*I don't know. I have no idea. The only certain thing is, this girl is suffering from a severe identity crisis, and I kind of feel sorry for her.*
*There are way too many elements in here for it to work. No character should look like this. The best place for her would not be between the pages of a manga, but in a paper shredder...*
Atcchan: "W-Well... at least we tried?"
Amu: "We... we really did try..."
Amu: "We did our very best, and therefore, nobody can criticize us! A-Ahaha..."
*And with this awkward laugh, her cheeks dusted light pink, Amu ruffles the back of her head, making her ponytail bounce.*
???: "Aaahn... This is incredible. It looks so awful...~"
Amu: "H-Huh?!"
Atcchan: "A-Ah...?"
*In almost perfect unison, Amu and I jump, as though electrocuted.*
*We were so busy examining our handiwork that we failed to hear the shop door being opened, the ding of the bell overhead, or the soft pad of footsteps sneaking up behind us, until it was too late...*
*It's the voice a girl, light and soft like silken tofu. I know, even before turning my head, that it definitely doesn't belong to Tsuzumi.*
*The girl - well, woman would be a more appropriate term - looks a good deal older than we are. Maybe she's in her mid twenties? It's hard to tell.*
*Her hair is light blond and cut roughly around her face, completely obscuring one of her eyes. She's fairly chubby, and dressed in a warm, woolen sweater.*
*Her skin is strangely dark - darker than I've ever seen outside of Hollywood movies. It's obvious, by a single glance, she isn't fully Japanese.*
*I don't know if I've ever seen a person who looks quite as obviously 'foreign' before. Not even in the city.*
*I worry I'm gawping. I don't want to gawp. That would be incredibly impolite, wouldn't it?*

Grandpa: "Mm! Your cooking is divine, Chiyo! You just can't beat it!"
